A ground generator or a generator of another plane anticommutes with both letters of $\omega_j$, hence commutes with their product. Pairwise commutation of the $\omega_j$ is the same parity count. The $\Omega_k$ statements follow: against $e_j$, exactly one factor ($\omega_j$) anticommutes.

t03-regenerated.title: Commuting copies
t03-regenerated.text:
Inside $T_k$, let $B_k$ be the subalgebra generated by the $2k$ plane generators $e_1, f_1, \dots, e_k, f_k$, and let $A_k$ be the subalgebra generated by the twisted base generators $x^{(k)} := x\,\omega_1 \omega_2 \cdots \omega_k$ for $x$ among the ground generators. Then: $B_k \cong \Cl(k,k) \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$; $A_k \cong \Cl(p,q)$ via $x \mapsto x^{(k)}$ (the twisted generators satisfy the ground Clifford relations); $A_k$ and $B_k$ commute elementwise; and multiplication $A_k \otimes B_k \to T_k$ is an isomorphism of algebras,
\[
\Cl(p{+}k, q{+}k) \;\cong\; \Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\R) \;=\; \Mat_{2^k}(\Cl(p,q)).
\]
The isomorphism is canonical given the ordered planes, and compatible with the tower embeddings up to the twist tracked in the section ``The CAR limit''.
t03-regenerated.proof:
\emph{$B_k \cong \Cl(k,k)$.} The $2k$ generators are orthonormal for the split form ($e_j^2 = 1$, $f_j^2 = -1$, pairwise orthogonal), so the universal property (\claimref{std-algebra.existence-uniqueness}) gives a surjection $\Cl(k,k) \to B_k$; it is injective because the $2^{2k}$ blades in the letters $e_1, f_1, \dots, e_k, f_k$ are part of the blade basis of $T_k$ (\claimref{std-algebra.blade-basis}), hence independent. \emph{$\Cl(k,k) \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$} by induction using the series' own results: $\Cl(0,0) = \R$, and $\Cl(j{+}1,j{+}1) \cong \Mat_2(\Cl(j,j))$ is Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial} with base $\Cl(j,j)$, the $(j{+}1)$-st plane carrying the outer index, so $\Cl(k,k) \cong \Mat_2(\Mat_2(\cdots)) = \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$.

\emph{$A_k \cong \Cl(p,q)$.} By Lemma \claimref{tower.volume-elements-planes}, $\Omega_k$ commutes with ground generators and $\Omega_k^2 = 1$, so for ground generators $x, y$:
\[
x^{(k)} y^{(k)} + y^{(k)} x^{(k)} = x \Omega_k y \Omega_k + y \Omega_k x \Omega_k = (xy + yx)\,\Omega_k^2 = 2B(x,y) .
\]
The universal property gives an algebra map $\Cl(p,q) \to A_k$, $x \mapsto x^{(k)}$; it sends the base blade $x_I$ to $x_I\,\Omega_k^{|I| \bmod 2}$, and these images are distinct nonzero blades (times a fixed invertible even element), hence independent: the map is an isomorphism onto $A_k$.

\emph{Commutation.} For a ground generator $x$ and any plane generator $g \in \{e_j, f_j\}$: $x$ anticommutes with $g$, and $\Omega_k$ anticommutes with $g$ (Lemma \claimref{tower.volume-elements-planes}), so $x^{(k)} g = x \Omega_k g = -x g \Omega_k = g x \Omega_k = g x^{(k)}$. Generators commute, hence the subalgebras do.

\emph{Multiplication is an isomorphism.} Commutation makes $A_k \otimes B_k \to T_k$ an algebra map. It is surjective: its image contains every plane generator, contains $\Omega_k \in B_k$, and therefore contains each ground generator $x = x^{(k)} \Omega_k$. Source and target both have dimension $2^n \cdot 2^{2k} = 2^{n + 2k}$, so a surjective linear map is an isomorphism. Finally $\Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\R) = \Mat_{2^k}(\Cl(p,q))$. Canonicity: the construction used only the ordered orthogonal planes and their volume elements, no basis choices in the ground algebra. The compatibility with $\iota_k$ is Lemma \claimref{tower.grade-twist-when-it-inner} below: under these identifications $\iota_k$ is the twisted diagonal, the twist being conjugation by $\Omega$-data that the section ``The CAR limit'' tracks.

t03-regenerated.text: Along the tower: the transport charge $d = p - q \bmod 8$ is constant; the division-ring type, simplicity class, and centre of every floor equal those of the ground floor; every floor is Morita equivalent to the ground floor; and the obstruction taxonomy of \cite{ButlerT1} is floor-independent: in particular a type-C obstruction (a central idempotent) never arises by transport from a simple ground algebra, at any height. t03-regenerated.title: Eight towers; signature change is tower change
t03-regenerated.text: The eight clock positions classify not stages of one tower but eight parallel towers, one per transport charge. t03-regenerated.title: Fock module; one qubit per rung
t03-regenerated.text: Let $W_k := \operatorname{span}\{v_1, \dots, v_k\}$, a maximal isotropic subspace of $H_1 \perp \cdots \perp H_k$. The Chevalley action ($v_j$ by wedge, $w_j$ by contraction against the pairing) makes the exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet W_k$, of dimension $2^k$, an irreducible module over $B_k \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$, with the vacuum $1 \in \Lambda^0$ annihilated by every $w_j$ and cyclic for the $v_j$. Each rung doubles the module: $\Lambda^\bullet W_{k+1} = \Lambda^\bullet W_k \otimes \Lambda^\bullet \R v_{k+1}$, one qubit per rung.
t03-regenerated.proof:
\emph{The action.} $W_k$ is isotropic (Proposition \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}) of dimension $k$, maximal since the split form $H_1 \perp \cdots \perp H_k$ has Witt index $k$ (\claimref{std-algebra.witt-decomposition}). Define, for $\xi \in \Lambda^\bullet W_k$,
\[
c(v_j)\,\xi = v_j \wedge \xi, \qquad c(w_j)\,\xi = \iota_{\varphi_j}\,\xi, \qquad \varphi_j := 2\langle w_j, \cdot\,\rangle|_{W_k} \in W_k^* ,
\]
so $\varphi_j(v_i) = \delta_{ij}$, and extend linearly to arbitrary vectors $\alpha = \sum_j (a_j v_j + b_j w_j)$.

\emph{The three anticommutator families,} elementary and proved outright. Wedge operators square to zero and pairwise anticommute, since $v \wedge v' = -v' \wedge v$ and $v \wedge v = 0$. The contraction $\iota_\varphi$ acts on monomials by
\[
\iota_\varphi(u_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge u_s) \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{s} (-1)^{i-1}\, \varphi(u_i)\; u_1 \wedge \cdots \widehat{u_i} \cdots \wedge u_s .
\]
Two contractions anticommute: in $\iota_\varphi \iota_\psi + \iota_\psi \iota_\varphi$ applied to a monomial, the term deleting $u_j$ then $u_i$ (with $i < j$) in the first composite carries the sign
\[
(-1)^{j-1}(-1)^{i-1},
\qquad \text{against} \qquad
(-1)^{i-1}(-1)^{j-2}
\]
for the matching term of the second composite, which deletes $u_i$ then $u_j$; the shift by one arises because removing $u_i$ first moves $u_j$ up a slot, and the opposite signs cancel the terms pairwise. The mixed anticommutator: the displayed expansion gives $\iota_\varphi(v \wedge \xi) = \varphi(v)\,\xi - v \wedge \iota_\varphi(\xi)$ (the $i = 1$ term, then the rest), so $\{v \wedge \cdot\,,\, \iota_\varphi\} = \varphi(v)\,\mathrm{id}$.

\emph{The Clifford relation, and the isomorphism.} Combining the three families,
\[
c(\alpha)^2 = \Bigl(\sum_j b_j \varphi_j\Bigr)\Bigl(\sum_i a_i v_i\Bigr)\,\mathrm{id} = \sum_j a_j b_j\,\mathrm{id} = Q(\alpha)\,\mathrm{id},
\]
since $Q(\alpha) = \sum_j 2 a_j b_j \langle v_j, w_j\rangle = \sum_j a_j b_j$. By the universal property (\claimref{std-algebra.existence-uniqueness}) $c$ extends to an algebra map $B_k \to \End(\Lambda^\bullet W_k)$. It is unital and nonzero with simple source ($B_k \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$, Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}), hence injective; source and target both have dimension $2^{2k} = (2^k)^2$, so it is an isomorphism, and the module is irreducible.

\emph{Vacuum, cyclicity, doubling.} The vacuum $1 \in \Lambda^0$ is sent to zero by every contraction and generates everything under wedges: $v_{i_1} \wedge \cdots \wedge v_{i_r} = c(v_{i_1}) \cdots c(v_{i_r})\,1$. The doubling statement is the exterior algebra of a direct sum.

So $m \leq$ the maximal totally isotropic dimension, which for a nondegenerate real form of signature $(p,q)$ is $\min(p,q)$: diagonalise, $V = P \perp N$ with $P$ positive definite of dimension $p$ and $N$ negative definite of dimension $q$; a totally isotropic $U$ meets $P$ trivially (a nonzero $v \in U \cap P$ would have $Q(v,v) > 0$ and $Q(v,v) = 0$ at once), so the projection $U \to N$ along $P$ is injective and $\dim U \leq q$; symmetrically $\dim U \leq p$; and $\min(p,q)$ is attained by the null spans of $\min(p,q)$ hyperbolic pairs (the classical bound, cf.\ [Lam2005, Ch.~I]).

\emph{Attainment.} Split off $\min(p,q)$ orthogonal hyperbolic planes from $(V, Q)$ (Witt decomposition) and take their normalised null pairs, as in Proposition 4.1. Along the tower, the form of signature $(p{+}k, q{+}k)$ has Witt index $\min(p,q) + k$, and each rung contributes its own plane to the attaining family.

t03-regenerated.text: The theorem is a prohibition as much as a count: no choice of vectors extracts $\min(p,q) + k + 1$ fermionic modes from floor $k$. t03-regenerated.title: The grade twist, and when it is inner
t03-regenerated.text: Under the isomorphism of Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}, the tower embedding $\iota_k$ becomes the twisted diagonal $a \mapsto \operatorname{diag}(a, \hat a)$ of \cite[Thm.~7.1]{ButlerT1} (in the corner identification of Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial}; in the twisted coordinates with $E_{11} = vw$ it reads $\operatorname{diag}(\hat a, a)$). If $p - q$ is even, $\Cl(p,q)$ is central simple over $\R$, the grade involution is an $\R$-algebra automorphism fixing the centre, and it is inner, implemented by the ground volume element $u$ (which anticommutes with vectors precisely when $n$ is even): $\hat a = u a u^{-1}$. Consequently $\operatorname{diag}(a, \hat a) = U \operatorname{diag}(a, a)\, U^{-1}$ with $U = \operatorname{diag}(1, u)$: the twist conjugates away at the level of the single step. (How the correction transports through the identifications of Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}, which is what the limit theorem needs, is Lemma \claimref{tower.compatibility-connecting-maps-transported}; the stagewise corrector is \emph{not} simply this $U$.) If $p - q$ is odd the grade involution acts nontrivially on the centre ($\R \oplus \R$ or $\C$) and is outer; no inner correction exists.
t03-regenerated.proof:
The matrix form of $\iota_k$ is Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial} applied with base $T_k$: the new plane's ladder pair supplies the matrix units, and the base embeds as $a \mapsto \operatorname{diag}(a, \hat a)$, the grade involution taken in $T_k$. Note the parity is stable: $\dim$ of floor $k$ is $n + 2k$, of the same parity as $n$, so ``even charge'' is a property of the whole tower.

Even charge: $n$ even makes $\Cl(p,q)$ (and every floor) central simple over $\R$ (its centre is $\R$, \claimref{primer.centre}) \cite{Porteous1995, Lounesto2001}. The grade involution is an $\R$-algebra automorphism fixing the centre $\R$ pointwise, so its innerness is an instance of the Skolem-Noether theorem \cite{Pierce1982}; nothing need be imported, because the implementing element is exhibited directly: the volume element $u = x_1 \cdots x_n$ of an orthogonal generator frame satisfies $u x = (-1)^{n-1} x u = -xu$ for each generator $x$ (\claimref{std-algebra.pseudoscalar-commutation}) (move $x$ through $n$ letters, one coincidence), and $u^2 = \pm 1$ is invertible; so $\Ad_u(x) = u x u^{-1} = -x = \hat x$ on generators, and two automorphisms agreeing on generators agree. The displayed conjugation is then the block computation $U \operatorname{diag}(a,a)\, U^{-1} = \operatorname{diag}(a, u a u^{-1})$ with $U = \operatorname{diag}(1, u)$, invertible in $\Mat_2(T_k)$.

Odd charge: the centre of each floor is $\R \oplus \R$ ($d \equiv 1 \bmod 4$) or $\C$ ($d \equiv 3 \bmod 4$), generated by $1$ and the volume element $\omega$, which is odd (its length $n + 2k$ is odd) and is therefore sent by the grade involution to $-\omega$: the involution exchanges the two central idempotents $\tfrac12(1 \pm \omega)$, respectively conjugates the central complex structure. An inner automorphism fixes the centre pointwise; the grade involution does not, so it is outer, and no unitary correction of the diagonal exists.

t03-regenerated.title: Compatibility: the connecting maps, transported
t03-regenerated.text:
Let $p - q$ be even, $A := \Cl(p,q)$, and let $\varphi_k : T_k \to A \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$ be the identifications of Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}, with every plane's matrix units labelled as in Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial} and the planes nested in order, the $(k{+}1)$-st plane carrying the outer index of $\Mat_{2^{k+1}} = \Mat_2(\Mat_{2^k})$. Write $\theta_k(z) := z \otimes 1_{2 \times 2}$ for block doubling in the outer index, $u_A \in A$ for the ground volume element, and $\overline\Omega_k \in \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$ for the image of $\Omega_k = \omega_1 \cdots \omega_k$. Then the transported connecting map $\psi_k := \varphi_{k+1} \circ \iota_k \circ \varphi_k^{-1}$ is
\[
\psi_k \;=\; \Ad(V_k) \circ \theta_k, \qquad
V_k \;:=\; \begin{pmatrix} u_A \otimes 1_{2^k} & 0 \\ 0 & 1_A \otimes \overline\Omega_k \end{pmatrix},
\]
with $V_k$ invertible ($u_A^2 = \pm 1$, $\Omega_k^2 = 1$). In this labelling and for $n = p + q \ge 1$, the corrector is \emph{not} the transported single-step corrector $\operatorname{diag}(1, u_{T_k})$ of Lemma \claimref{tower.grade-twist-when-it-inner}: transporting through $\varphi$ splits the correction across the two tensor legs, the ground volume acting in the first corner and the planes' volume in the second. The labelling convention of Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial} matters: with $vw$ and $wv$ exchanged for the new plane, the transported single-step corrector $\operatorname{diag}(1, u_{T_k})$ is the one that works and $V_k$ is not; for $n = 0$ the two coincide.
t03-regenerated.proof:
Both sides are unital algebra maps into $A \otimes \Mat_{2^{k+1}}$, so it suffices to check them on generators of $A \otimes \Mat_{2^k}$: the elements $x \otimes 1$ for ground generators $x$, and $1 \otimes b$ for $b$ the image of a plane generator $g \in \{e_j, f_j\}$, $j \leq k$.

\emph{Ground generators.} $\varphi_k^{-1}(x \otimes 1) = x^{(k)} = x\,\Omega_k$ (the twisted generator of \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}). In $T_{k+1}$, $\Omega_{k+1} = \Omega_k\, \omega_{k+1}$ and $\omega_{k+1}^2 = 1$ give $x^{(k)} = x^{(k+1)}\, \omega_{k+1}$. Under $\varphi_{k+1}$, $x^{(k+1)} \mapsto x \otimes 1_{2^{k+1}}$ by definition, and $\omega_{k+1} \mapsto 1_A \otimes \operatorname{diag}(-1_{2^k}, +1_{2^k})$ by Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial} for the outer plane. Hence
\[
\psi_k(x \otimes 1) \;=\; x \otimes \operatorname{diag}(-1_{2^k},\, +1_{2^k}).
\]
On the other side, $\theta_k(x \otimes 1) = x \otimes 1_{2^{k+1}}$, and conjugating cornerwise by $V_k$: the first corner gives $(u_A \otimes 1)(x \otimes 1)(u_A \otimes 1)^{-1} = u_A x u_A^{-1} \otimes 1 = -x \otimes 1$ (Lemma \claimref{tower.grade-twist-when-it-inner}, $n$ even), the second gives $(1 \otimes \overline\Omega_k)(x \otimes 1)(1 \otimes \overline\Omega_k)^{-1} = x \otimes 1$. The two sides agree.

\emph{Plane generators.} $\varphi_k^{-1}(1 \otimes b) = g$ and $\iota_k(g) = g \in B_{k+1}$. The nesting embeds $B_k$ into $\Mat_2(B_k)$ as the twisted diagonal of Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial} with base $B_k = \Cl(k,k)$: $g \mapsto \operatorname{diag}(g, \hat g)$, with $\hat{\cdot}$ the grade involution of $B_k$, which by Lemma \claimref{tower.volume-elements-planes} is implemented by $\Omega_k$ (it anticommutes with every plane generator and squares to one). Under $\varphi_{k+1}$ this reads
\[
\psi_k(1 \otimes b) \;=\; 1 \otimes \operatorname{diag}\bigl(b,\ \overline\Omega_k\, b\, \overline\Omega_k^{-1}\bigr),
\]
and conjugating $\theta_k(1 \otimes b) = 1 \otimes \operatorname{diag}(b, b)$ cornerwise by $V_k$ gives exactly the same: the first corner commutes with $u_A \otimes 1$, the second is conjugated by $\overline\Omega_k$. The two sides agree.

t03-regenerated.title: The algebraic limit, even charge

Let $p - q$ be even. The algebraic direct limit of the tower $(T_k, \iota_k)$ is canonically isomorphic to
\[
\varinjlim T_k \;\cong\; \Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^\infty}, \qquad \Mat_{2^\infty} := \varinjlim \Mat_{2^k}(\R) \ \ (m \mapsto \operatorname{diag}(m,m)),
\]

\]
with $V_k$ the split corrector displayed there. The comparison system is $(A \otimes \Mat_{2^k},\, \theta_k)$, whose limit is $A \otimes \Mat_{2^\infty}$ by definition. Intertwine the two systems stagewise: set $W_0 := 1$ and recursively $W_{k+1} := \theta_k(W_k)\, V_k^{-1}$, each $W_k$ an invertible element of $A \otimes \Mat_{2^k}$, and define $\lambda_k := \Ad(W_k)$. \[

\]

t03-regenerated.title: The *-structure of the tower, and its C*-norms
t03-regenerated.text: Fix the tower's frames: an orthogonal ground frame $x_1, \dots, x_n$ diagonalising $Q$, and the plane frames $e_j, f_j$. On each complexified floor $T_k^{\,\C}$ there is a unique conjugate-linear antiautomorphism $*$ with $x^* = x$ for every frame generator with $x^2 = 1$ and $x^* = -x$ for every frame generator with $x^2 = -1$. Under it: every frame generator, every blade in the frame, and every ground or plane volume element is unitary ($z^* z = 1$); the ladder pairs are mutually adjoint, $v_j^* = w_j$; the connecting maps $\iota_k$, the identifications $\varphi_k$ of Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}, the block doublings $\theta_k$, and the correctors $V_k$ and $W_k$ of Lemma \claimref{tower.compatibility-connecting-maps-transported} and Theorem \claimref{tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge} are all compatible with $*$ (the maps are *-homomorphisms, the correctors unitary). If moreover $p - q$ is even, each $T_k^{\,\C}$ is *-isomorphic to $\Mat_{2^{m/2}}(\C)$, $m := n + 2k$, with $*$ the conjugate transpose; consequently each floor carries a unique C*-norm, every unital *-monomorphism between floors is isometric, and the increasing union $\bigcup_k T_k^{\,\C}$ carries a unique C*-norm.
t03-regenerated.proof:
\emph{Existence and uniqueness.} Renormalise the $m$ frame generators of floor $k$ to $y_i := x_i$ when $x_i^2 = 1$ and $y_i := i\,x_i$ when $x_i^2 = -1$, so that $y_i^2 = 1$ and the $y_i$ pairwise anticommute. Reversal, the unique real antiautomorphism of a Clifford algebra fixing its generating vectors (the universal property applied to the opposite algebra; \claimref{std-algebra.involution-properties}), extends conjugate-linearly to $T_k^{\,\C}$; call the extension $*$. It is conjugate-linear and antimultiplicative by construction, fixes each $y_i$, and on the original generators unwinds to exactly the displayed values: for $x^2 = -1$, $x = -i\,y$ gives $x^* = \overline{(-i)}\, y^* = i\,y = -x$. Uniqueness holds because a conjugate-linear antiautomorphism is determined by its values on the generators.

\emph{Unitarity and adjoint pairs.} $y_i^* y_i = y_i^2 = 1$, and each original generator satisfies $x^* x = 1$ in both cases ($x^2 = 1$ gives $x^*x = x^2 = 1$; $x^2 = -1$ gives $x^*x = -x^2 = 1$). A product of unitaries is unitary by telescoping, $(z_1 \cdots z_s)^* (z_1 \cdots z_s) = z_s^* \cdots z_1^* z_1 \cdots z_s = 1$; blades, the ground volume $u_A$, the plane volumes $\omega_j$ and $\Omega_k$, hence the corners of $V_k$ (\claimref{tower.compatibility-connecting-maps-transported}), hence $V_k$ and recursively $W_k$ (\claimref{tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge}), are such products or diagonals of them. The ladder pairs: $v_j^* = \tfrac12(e_j + f_j)^* = \tfrac12(e_j - f_j) = w_j$. The maps: $\iota_k$ and $\theta_k$ send frame generators to frame generators or to $z \otimes 1$, so they intertwine the $*$'s; for $\varphi_k$ (\claimref{tower.commuting-copies}), equip $A \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\C)$ with the tensor $*$ (the ground $*$ on $A$, conjugate transpose on matrices) and check generators: $(x\,\Omega_k)^* = \Omega_k^*\, x^* = x^* \Omega_k$ since each $\omega_j^* = f_j^* e_j^* = (-f_j)(e_j) = e_j f_j = \omega_j$ and $\Omega_k$ commutes with ground generators, matching $(x \otimes 1)^* = x^* \otimes 1$; and the matrix units of Fact \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial} satisfy $E_{12}^* = v^* = w = E_{21}$ and $E_{11}^* = (vw)^* = w^* v^* = vw = E_{11}$, matching the conjugate transpose, nested stage by stage.

\emph{The even case is a matrix *-algebra.} Let $m$ be even and represent on $(\C^2)^{\otimes m/2}$ by the tensor-Pauli assignment
\[
Y_{2l-1} := \sigma_z^{\otimes (l-1)} \otimes \sigma_x \otimes 1^{\otimes (m/2 - l)}, \qquad
Y_{2l} := \sigma_z^{\otimes (l-1)} \otimes \sigma_y \otimes 1^{\otimes (m/2 - l)} ,
\]
Hermitian unitaries that pairwise anticommute and square to one; the universal property gives a unital homomorphism $\pi : T_k^{\,\C} \to \Mat_{2^{m/2}}(\C)$ with $\pi(y_i) = Y_i$, and $\pi$ is a *-homomorphism because $a \mapsto \pi(a^*)^*$ is again a homomorphism agreeing with $\pi$ on the generators. The $2^m$ blade images $Y_S := Y_{s_1} \cdots Y_{s_j}$ are, up to phase, distinct words in the Pauli basis, and distinct Pauli words are orthogonal for the trace form ($\operatorname{Tr}(Y_S^* Y_T) = 0$ for $S \neq T$), hence linearly independent: $\pi$ maps a basis to an independent set, so it is injective, and by the dimension count $2^m = (2^{m/2})^2$ it is a *-isomorphism onto the full matrix algebra, with $*$ the conjugate transpose.

\emph{Unique C*-norm, isometric inclusions.} In any C*-norm on $\Mat_N(\C)$, a self-adjoint $y$ has $\|y\| = \lim_j \|y^{2^j}\|^{1/2^j}$ (the C*-identity iterated) $=$ the spectral radius of $y$ (Gelfand's formula, valid in any finite-dimensional normed algebra), and then $\|x\|^2 = \|x^*x\| = \rho(x^* x)$ for every $x$: the norm is determined algebraically, hence unique. A unital *-monomorphism between floors pulls the target's C*-norm back to a C*-norm on the source, which by uniqueness is the source's own norm: the map is isometric. Finally, any C*-norm on $\bigcup_k T_k^{\,\C}$ restricts on each floor to a C*-norm, hence to the unique one, so the norm on the union is determined.

A product of unitaries is unitary by telescoping, $(z_1 \cdots z_s)^* (z_1 \cdots z_s) = z_s^* \cdots z_1^* z_1 \cdots z_s = 1$; blades, the ground volume $u_A$, the plane volumes $\omega_j$ and $\Omega_k$, hence the corners of $V_k$, hence $V_k$ and recursively $W_k$, are such products or diagonals of them. The ladder pairs: $v_j^* = \tfrac12(e_j + f_j)^* = \tfrac12(e_j - f_j) = w_j$. The maps: $\iota_k$ and $\theta_k$ send frame generators to frame generators or to $z \otimes 1$, so they intertwine the $*$'s; for $\varphi_k$, equip $A \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\C)$ with the tensor $*$ (the ground $*$ on $A$, conjugate transpose on matrices) and check generators: $(x\,\Omega_k)^* = \Omega_k^*\, x^* = x^* \Omega_k$ since each $\omega_j^* = f_j^* e_j^* = (-f_j)(e_j) = e_j f_j = \omega_j$ and $\Omega_k$ commutes with ground generators, matching $(x \otimes 1)^* = x^* \otimes 1$; and the matrix units of Fact 2.1 satisfy $E_{12}^* = v^* = w = E_{21}$ and $E_{11}^* = (vw)^* = w^* v^* = vw = E_{11}$, matching the conjugate transpose, nested stage by stage.

\emph{The even case is a matrix *-algebra.} Let $m$ be even and represent on $(\C^2)^{\otimes m/2}$ by the tensor-Pauli assignment
\[
Y_{2l-1} := \sigma_z^{\otimes (l-1)} \otimes \sigma_x \otimes 1^{\otimes (m/2 - l)}, \qquad
Y_{2l} := \sigma_z^{\otimes (l-1)} \otimes \sigma_y \otimes 1^{\otimes (m/2 - l)} ,
\]
Hermitian unitaries that pairwise anticommute and square to one; the universal property gives a unital homomorphism $\pi : T_k^{\,\C} \to \Mat_{2^{m/2}}(\C)$ with $\pi(y_i) = Y_i$, and $\pi$ is a *-homomorphism because $a \mapsto \pi(a^*)^*$ is again a homomorphism agreeing with $\pi$ on the generators. The $2^m$ blade images $Y_S := Y_{s_1} \cdots Y_{s_j}$ are, up to phase, distinct words in the Pauli basis, and distinct Pauli words are orthogonal for the trace form ($\operatorname{Tr}(Y_S^* Y_T) = 0$ for $S \neq T$), hence linearly independent: $\pi$ maps a basis to an independent set, so it is injective, and by the dimension count $2^m = (2^{m/2})^2$ it is a *-isomorphism onto the full matrix algebra, with $*$ the conjugate transpose.

\emph{Unique C*-norm, isometric inclusions.} In any C*-norm on $\Mat_N(\C)$, a self-adjoint $y$ has $\|y\| = \lim_j \|y^{2^j}\|^{1/2^j}$ (the C*-identity iterated) $=$ the spectral radius of $y$ (Gelfand's formula, valid in any finite-dimensional normed algebra), and then $\|x\|^2 = \|x^*x\| = \rho(x^* x)$ for every $x$: the norm is determined algebraically, hence unique. A unital *-monomorphism between floors pulls the target's C*-norm back to a C*-norm on the source, which by uniqueness is the source's own norm: the map is isometric. Finally, any C*-norm on $\bigcup_k T_k^{\,\C}$ restricts on each floor to a C*-norm, hence to the unique one, so the norm on the union is determined.

deposited.proof: The matrix-unit relations are the hyperbolic-pair identities (2) read off directly: $E_{12}E_{21} = ff^* = E_{11}$, $E_{21}E_{12} = f^*f = E_{22}$, $E_{12}^2 = f^2 = 0 = E_{21}^2$, $E_{11}E_{12} = ff^*f = f = E_{12}$, $E_{12}E_{11} = f\,ff^* = 0$, and so on; $E_{11} + E_{22} = 1$ is the pair's anticommutator. For the corner: using the displayed decomposition of $B$ and $ff^* a = a\, ff^*$ (evenness), one computes $ff^* (a_0 + a_1 f + a_2 f^* + a_3 ff^*)\, ff^* = (a_0 + a_3) ff^*$, since $ff^* \cdot f \cdot ff^* = f f^* f \cdot f f^* = f \cdot ff^* = f^2 f^* = 0$ and likewise the $f^*$ term vanishes, while the $1$ and $ff^*$ terms remain; so $E_{11}BE_{11} = A\,ff^*$. The map $a \mapsto a\,ff^*$ is an algebra isomorphism onto it: multiplicative since $(a\,ff^*)(b\,ff^*) = ab\,(ff^*)^2 = ab\,ff^*$, unital onto the corner unit $ff^*$, injective by the directness of the decomposition. The Peirce isomorphism of Lemma 5.4, whose proof uses only the matrix-unit relations, then gives $B \cong \Mat_2(A)$. The embedding: for $a \in A$, $\varphi(a)_{11} = E_{11} a E_{11} = a\,ff^*$ and $\varphi(a)_{22} = E_{12}\, a\, E_{21} = f a f^* = \hat{a}\, ff^*$, while the off-diagonal entries vanish ($E_{11} a E_{21} = a\, ff^*f^* = 0$, $E_{12} a E_{11} = \hat a\,f ff^* = 0$); under the corner identification this is $\mathrm{diag}(a, \hat{a})$, which is multiplicative since the grade involution is an automorphism. Morita-class preservation, and with it the invariance of the type-C diagnosis, is the statement $\Mat_2(A) \sim_{\text{Morita}} A$ together with the fact that the Wedderburn data of $\Mat_2(\Mat_m(D))$ (or of the split case, blockwise) is that of $A$ with $m$ doubled.

t04-regenerated.title: Introduction
t04-regenerated.text:
The root paper of this series operates at a single fibre. Given a real quadratic space of mixed signature, the null vectors of its Clifford algebra admit no equivariant element-level repair in any extension, while the space of points is repaired totally and uniquely by the Witt completion $\Cl(p,q) \to \Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$; the full taxonomy of zero-divisor obstructions, with the transport rule and minimality theorem belonging to each type, is settled in the same paper \cite{ButlerT1}. It treats one algebra at a time.

Geometry does not. In the gravitational application that motivates the series, the metric degenerates on a \emph{locus} $\Sig$ inside a manifold $M$: the algebra that needs completion is over $\Sig$, while the algebra away from $\Sig$ is nondegenerate and must be left unchanged. The natural demand is therefore a sheaf of Clifford algebras whose fibre is $\Cl(p,q)$ on the nondegenerate region and $\Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ over $\Sig$. Stated naively this is impossible, and the impossibility is instructive: $\Cl(p,q)$ has dimension $2^n$ and $\Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ has dimension $2^{n+2}$ (sixteen against sixty-four in the spacetime case), and the rank of a locally free sheaf is locally constant. The fibre dimension cannot jump. The subject of this paper is the resolution of that tension: the jump must be relocated into \emph{structure}, and there are exactly two natural places for it to go.

The first is a sheaf of constant rank $2^n$, the \emph{degeneration sheaf}: the Clifford sheaf of the degenerate cometric itself. Its fibres over $\Sig$ remain $2^n$-dimensional but degenerate as algebras, acquiring a canonical two-sided ideal that squares to zero. The singular locus registers as non-reducedness, in precise parallel with the appearance of nilpotents in the special fibres of algebraic-geometric degenerations, and the ideal is exactly the kind of object a blow-up is performed along: a canonical sheaf of ideals supported on the singular locus. The second is a sheaf of constant rank $2^{n+2}$, the \emph{ambient sheaf}, whose fibre is $\Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ at every point of the closed physical region; the metric-level description survives inside it as a distinguished subalgebra attached to a splitting, and on $\Sig$ it is the splitting, not the sheaf, that fails. Nothing jumps in the completion. The two sheaves are related by a global embedding, and the embedding is the localised transport.

Two further phenomena complete the picture, and both are theorems rather than constructions. First, a conservation law: the one-sided completion cannot be two-sided; no completion that is standard away from the wall is nondegenerate on both sides. The ambient form necessarily degenerates on a displaced hypersurface on the unphysical side, a \emph{shadow wall}, which for good couplings is itself a tame degeneration, so the completion iterates along an infinite wall sequence; degeneracy is moved, never destroyed. Second, an exceptional fibre: the anisotropic rescaling of the dying direction by $\sqrt{t}$ realises, fibrewise over $\Sig$, the deformation to the normal cone of algebraic geometry, and its special fibre is a genuine nondegenerate Clifford algebra whose metric in the dying direction is the \emph{rate} of the degeneration. The residue theorem then identifies the twist: the physical metric has a canonical simple pole at the wall, its residue induces an isomorphism $N^*\Sig \cong \shL^{\otimes 2}$ with $\shL$ the radical line bundle, so the dying line is a canonical square root of the conormal bundle and the Witt partner line adjoined by the completion, canonically $\shL^*$, is a canonical square root of the normal bundle. The new dimension is not adjoined arbitrarily; it is constructed tautologically from the dying direction and the geometry of its degeneration.

t04-regenerated.title: Prior art
t04-regenerated.text: Ambient constructions over conformal and degenerate structures have a substantial history, and this paper's ambient sheaf is a degenerate-locus-adapted relative of two of them. \emph{Tractor calculus}, going back to Thomas and formalised by Bailey, Eastwood and Gover \cite{BEG1994} with a modern treatment by Curry and Gover \cite{CurryGover2018}, packages a conformal manifold into a rank-$(n{+}2)$ bundle of signature $(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ with canonical connection; its almost-Einstein and boundary variants are the closest existing geometry to the completion of the section ``The ambient sheaf: one-sided completion''. The \emph{Fefferman-Graham ambient metric} \cite{FG1985, FG2012} realises the same increment $(+1,+1)$ as a nondegenerate metric on a thickened cone. The precise dictionary between those constructions and the present one is assembly-level material and is developed in the section ``Dictionary, choices, and scope'', per the series' practice of keeping the points of contact with existing structures in the text. The algebraic input, the Clifford algebra of a \emph{degenerate} symmetric form with its $2^n$-dimensional blade basis, is due to Chevalley \cite{Chevalley1997}; the structure theory of the nondegenerate fibres is classical \cite{Porteous1995, Lounesto2001, Lam2005}. On the geometric side, the blow-up along an ideal sheaf and the non-reducedness of special fibres are standard algebraic geometry \cite{Hartshorne1977}, and the deformation to the normal cone realised fibrewise in the section ``The exceptional algebra and the metric's residue'' is Fulton's \cite[Ch.~5]{Fulton1998}. Signature-change hypersurfaces and conformally regularised cosmological boundaries, the tame class's physical exemplars, appear throughout the literature on signature change and on Penrose's conformal cyclic cosmology \cite{Penrose2010}. None of these sources, to our knowledge, treats the degenerating \emph{Clifford} sheaf itself, its nilpotent ideal, or the conservation-of-degeneracy phenomenon; those, together with the residue identification of the twist, are the contributions claimed.

t04-regenerated.title: Contribution
t04-regenerated.text:
The paper proves eight clusters of results, at the standard of \cite{ButlerT1} (Tier A of the series: complete proofs, each theorem carrying its own hypotheses).

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{The degeneration sheaf} (the section ``The degeneration sheaf''). For a cometric of corank one along a tame hypersurface, the Clifford sheaf $\shA = \Cl(T^*M, G)$ is locally free of constant rank $2^n$ (Proposition \claimref{sheaf.local-freeness-constant-rank}, valid for arbitrary degeneracy); over the degenerate locus each fibre carries the canonical square-zero two-sided ideal generated by the radical line, with quotient the Clifford algebra of the induced nondegenerate form, and these ideals assemble into a coherent sheaf supported exactly on $\Sig$ (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.degeneration-sheaf}). Resolution is characterised ideal-theoretically: in any fibrewise nondegenerate Clifford completion the radical generates the \emph{unit} ideal (Proposition \claimref{sheaf.resolution-ideal-theoretically}); completion turns an infinitesimal into a dimension. The proof given needs no simplicity hypothesis, the hyperbolic partner exhibiting the unit directly, so the statement holds in the split signatures as well.
\item \textbf{One-sided completion} (the section ``The ambient sheaf: one-sided completion''). For walls with trivial radical line bundle (the twisted case is posed as a successor problem), a rank-$(n{+}2)$ ambient bundle with a coupled form $h$, equal to $G \perp H$ outside a collar of $\Sig$, is nondegenerate of constant signature $(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ on the closed physical side; the subalgebra generated by $T^*M$ is canonically the degeneration sheaf, globally; and the localised ladder pair exists exactly over $\Sig$.
\item \textbf{The shadow wall} (the section ``The shadow wall: conservation of degeneracy''). Conservation of degeneracy in two forms. Absolute: \emph{no} completion whatever that is standard outside a neighbourhood of the wall is nondegenerate everywhere, by a pure signature obstruction (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-absolute-form}), which is stronger than any ansatz-level statement. Located: within the coupling ansatz the degeneration lies exactly on the zero set of the determinant factor $F$, displaced to the unphysical side, with the signature passing from $(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ to $(p,q{+}2)$; for good couplings the shadow wall is itself tame and the infinite wall sequence iterates unconditionally (Lemma \claimref{sheaf.tame-wall-induction}, Corollary \claimref{sheaf.infinite-wall-sequence}). The cohomological wall-class question, and its relation to the conservation conjecture of \cite[\S7.4]{ButlerT1}, is posed precisely.
\item \textbf{The exceptional algebra and the residue} (the section ``The exceptional algebra and the metric's residue''). The $\sqrt{t}$-rescaled Clifford family through a tame wall converges to a nondegenerate special fibre built from normal-cone data, independent of all choices up to canonical isomorphism; the inverse cometric has a canonical simple pole at the wall whose residue is exactly the inverse of the invariant transversality datum of (T3), identifying $N^*\Sig \cong \shL^{\otimes 2}$: the dying line is a canonical square root of the conormal bundle, the partner line of the normal bundle. The identification fixes the direction of the twist (Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.direction-induced-twist}).
\item \textbf{Topology, dictionary and scope} (the section ``Dictionary, choices, and scope''). A topological corollary of the residue theorem: tame walls are always two-sided, since $N^*\Sig \cong \shL^{\otimes 2}$ makes the normal bundle's $w_1$ zero; the construction's global choices are itemised with their exact obstruction classes ($w_1(\shL)$ the only genuine invariant); the wall class is posed as a precise conjecture whose coarse half Theorem \claimref{sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-absolute-form} already proves; and the relation to tractor bundles and the Fefferman-Graham ambient metric is developed at assembly level and flagged as such, with the anisotropic, higher-codimension and BKL-weight questions stated as successor problems, the first instance of which the next item executes.
\item \textbf{The Schwarzschild composite} (the section ``The Schwarzschild composite''). The two failure modes that keep the Schwarzschild singularity outside the tame class, codimension three and anisotropy, are cleared together for the exact solution: the real oriented blow-up of the worldline absorbs the angular rates tautologically, and on a canonically weighted coframe module the residual degeneration is boundary-tame of corank one, with the Killing-time direction as its radical (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.schwarzschild-degeneration-boundary-tame}). The one-sided completion then ascends $\Cl(1,3) \to \Cl(2,4)$ on the whole blown-up manifold with the ladder pair supported exactly on the singular boundary and no shadow wall (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.one-sided-completion-singularity}); the weights that achieve this are forced, once the geometrically determined dying direction is named, and equal the Kasner exponents (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.weights-are-forced-are-kasner-exponents}), settling the Kasner-weights conjecture for Schwarzschild in the diagonal class.
\item \textbf{Uniqueness, the rain frame, the matching, and the anisotropic class} (the section ``Uniqueness of the weighted module''-the section ``The matching with the weighted limit'', the section ``The anisotropic class: variable weights and stability''). The weighted module is the \emph{unique} rain-bounded locally free extension of the interior cotangent module that is boundary tame, by a determinant argument whose hypothesis must be read on the dying eigenvalue, not the dying entry, and whose anchoring class cannot be dropped: two explicit modules separate the readings (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.uniqueness-weighted-module}, Examples \claimref{note.sheaf.eigenvalue-essential} and \claimref{note.sheaf.rain-boundedness-essential-null-mixing-extension}). Physically, the exceptional coframe is exactly the dual coframe of the infalling orthonormal frame, with exact Minkowski Gram at every radius, and the gauge field carries the flat radial null dyad onto a physical dyad with constant unit components in it (Propositions \claimref{sheaf.rain-duality}, \claimref{sheaf.chains-radial-dyad-rain-finite}): the weighted module is the $u$-smooth shadow of what the falling observer measures finitely. The weighted limit of \cite{ButlerT6} is then matched to the present construction, at the fibre and at the connection level: its adapted frame consists of exceptional-module sections, its rates are re-derived here exactly, its limit is the weight one-form of the exceptional bundle, and its surviving matrix is a unit boost precisely by the second Kasner relation (Proposition \claimref{sheaf.matching-fibre}, Theorem \claimref{sheaf.matching-connection-level}). Finally the whole package extends to position-dependent Kasner exponents, over a variable-order function algebra, stably under the relative error structure that velocity-dominated asymptotics deliver, with sharpness exhibited at relative order zero (Theorems \claimref{sheaf.variable-weight-boundary-tameness-completion-forced}, \claimref{sheaf.stability-reduction-strict-diagonal-case}); the smooth structure of that algebra is characterised exactly, variable-order polyhomogeneous with unavoidable logarithms measured by the derivative of the exponents (Theorems \claimref{sheaf.differential-closure-filtration-conormality}, \claimref{sheaf.exponent-ratios-are-invariant}); and the mixmaster boundary is closed at the algebraic level by the collision dichotomy: positive-pair collisions pass through the Schwarzschild triple and are interior to the theory, while ordering changes force Taub edges on which the wall ends and across which no weighted module continues (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.edge-wall}, Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.mixmaster-wall-complex}).
\item \textbf{Transversal independence, and the no-value theorem at the wall} (the section ``Transversal independence, and the no-value theorem at the wall''). The coupling uses a transversal, and the dependence is resolved exactly: a closed-form unipotent intertwiner identifies the completions built on any two transversals, the identifications compose (a cocycle), and the completion at the wall is canonically transversal-independent, preserving the form, the grading and the degeneration subalgebra though neither the frame nor the ladder pair (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.transversal-independence-wall}). On the same mechanism, the wall admits no equivariant classical value for the dying direction and no canonical ladder partner: the automorphisms of the completed structure translate the candidates freely (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.no-equivariant-value-wall}), so an analogue of the root paper's no-repair theorem holds at the wall itself, where that theorem's hypotheses fail. This is the boundary no-go the singularity paper imports verbatim.
\end{enumerate}

t04-regenerated.title: The objects
t04-regenerated.text:
Throughout, $M$ is a smooth manifold of dimension $n \geq 2$, all data are $C^\infty$, and a \emph{cometric} on $M$ is a smooth symmetric bilinear form $G$ on the cotangent bundle $T^*M$, i.e.\ a smooth section of $S^2 TM$. We work on the cotangent side because that is where the gravitational application delivers the data: in gauge theory gravity it is the gauge field's induced cometric that crosses the singular locus smoothly while metric components diverge. Nothing below depends on that origin, and the tangent-side theory is identical under $T^*M \leftrightarrow TM$.

At a point $x$, the \emph{radical} of $G_x$ is $\rad(G_x) = \{\alpha \in T^*_xM : G_x(\alpha, \cdot) = 0\}$, and the \emph{corank} of $G_x$ is its dimension. The degenerate locus of $G$ is $\Sig = \{x : \rad(G_x) \neq 0\}$. On $M \setminus \Sig$ the form is nondegenerate and its signature is locally constant.

\[

\]
for any spanning $k \in \shL(x)$, and the quotient is canonically the Clifford algebra of the induced form:
\[
A(x)/J(x) \;\cong\; \Cl\bigl(T^*_xM / \shL(x),\ \overline{G}_x\bigr),

\[
\shJ \;:=\; i_*\bigl(\shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL\bigr) \qquad (i : \Sig \hookrightarrow M)

is a finitely presented sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_M$-modules and of $\shA$-bimodules, supported exactly on $\Sig$, with fibre $J(x)$ at $x \in \Sig$ and fibre $0$ elsewhere. The associated ideal sheaf of $\shA$ is the kernel
\[
\shK \;:=\; \ker\bigl(\shA \longrightarrow i_*\bigl(\shA|_\Sig \,/\, \shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL\bigr)\bigr),
\]
a sheaf of two-sided ideals of $\shA$ whose restriction to $\Sig$ realises $J(x)$ fibrewise and whose quotient $\shA/\shK$ is the pushforward of the quotient bundle of (2).

\[

\[
\dim A(x) - \dim J(x) \;=\; 2^n - 2^{n-1} \;=\; 2^{n-1} \;=\; \dim \Cl(\overline{G}_x),
\]

t04-regenerated.title: Non-reducedness: the singularity registers as an infinitesimal
t04-regenerated.text: The interpretation deserves emphasis, because it is the central idea of the paper. In algebraic geometry, the special fibre of a degenerating family typically acquires nilpotents: the scheme becomes non-reduced, and the nilpotents record infinitesimal directions that no longer correspond to actual points \cite[Ch.~II]{Hartshorne1977}. Theorem \claimref{sheaf.degeneration-sheaf} exhibits the same phenomenon literally rather than by analogy: the direction along which the metric degenerated survives in the singular fibre only as an infinitesimal, an element all of whose products through the entire algebra square to zero. And $\shJ$ is the direct analogue of the object a blow-up is performed along: a canonical sheaf of ideals supported on the singular locus \cite[\S II.7]{Hartshorne1977}, transcribed from the structure sheaf to the Clifford sheaf. The ideal-theoretic characterisation of what resolution must accomplish is available in one line, and is the next proposition.

t04-regenerated.title: Conservation of degeneracy, absolute form
t04-regenerated.text: Let $M$ be connected, let $(M,G)$ be a tame corank-one degeneration whose two open sides $\Mp \setminus \Sig$ and $M \setminus \Mp$ are both nonempty, let $E \to M$ be \emph{any} vector bundle containing $T^*M$ as a subbundle, carrying \emph{any} smooth symmetric form $h$ which is \emph{standard} outside some neighbourhood $U$ of $\Sig$ with $M \setminus U$ meeting both sides: there, $h = G \perp K$ for a nondegenerate form $K$ on a complement, with $\operatorname{sig}(K)$ the same on both exterior regions. Then $h$ is not nondegenerate everywhere: every completion of a signature-change cometric that is standard, in this sense, outside a neighbourhood of the wall degenerates somewhere. Degeneracy can be displaced, never destroyed.
t04-regenerated.proof: The signature of a continuous nondegenerate symmetric form on a connected base is constant: the eigenvalues of its Gram matrix with respect to any auxiliary frame metric vary continuously and never vanish, so their sign counts are locally constant, and $M$ is connected. Suppose $h$ nondegenerate everywhere. On the physical exterior $h = G \perp K$ has signature $(p,q) + \operatorname{sig}(K)$; on the far exterior it has $(p{-}1, q{+}1) + \operatorname{sig}(K)$ (Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.coordinates-crossing-speed}, the wall being tame, \claimref{sheaf.tameness}), with the \emph{same} $\operatorname{sig}(K)$ by the standardness hypothesis. The two totals differ in the first entry by one; a single form of constant signature cannot have both, so nondegeneracy must fail somewhere in $U$. The constancy clause on $\operatorname{sig}(K)$ is necessary: $M \setminus U$ is disconnected (the two sides lie in different components of $M \setminus \Sig$), and a completion allowed to switch $K$'s signature across the wall, say from $(1,1)$ to $(2,0)$, could match the two totals; ``standard'' means one exterior model, not two.
t04-regenerated.label: Theorem

t04-regenerated.title: Tame wall induction
t04-regenerated.proof:
\emph{The monotone zone, and finiteness of $S$.} By Lemma \claimref{sheaf.determinant-identity-blow-up-expansion}(2), $s = 1/\lambda + b$ with $b$ smooth up to the wall, locally uniformly; so $s' = -\lambda'/\lambda^2 + b'$, and since $\lambda \to 0$ while $\lambda'$ is bounded away from zero near $\Sig$ (T3, \claimref{sheaf.tameness}) and $b'$ is bounded (compactness of $\Sig$ makes all these bounds uniform along the wall), there is a one-sided collar neighbourhood on which $|\lambda'|/\lambda^2 > |b'|$: the monotone zone. Its far-side complement within the collar has compact closure disjoint from $\Sig$, on which the smooth function $s$ is bounded: $S < \infty$.

(1) Outside the collar $F = 1$; on the far collar side outside the monotone zone, $|2\mu\nu\beta^2 s| \leq 2|\mu\nu| S < 1$, so $F > 0$: no zeros in either region, whatever $\beta$ does there. All far-side zeros therefore lie in the monotone zone. Approaching the wall $F \to -\infty$ (Lemma \claimref{sheaf.determinant-identity-blow-up-expansion}(2)) and at the zone's outer edge $F > 0$, so each transversal carries a zero; where $\beta \equiv 1$ (shrink the zone into the inner collar if necessary), $F = 1 + 2\mu\nu s$ is strictly monotone along each transversal with a single simple zero, and $dF = 2\mu\nu\, ds$ has nonvanishing transversal component $2\mu\nu s' \neq 0$: $\{F = 0\}$ is a regular level set, a smooth closed hypersurface $\Sig'$, and $\det h = \det G \cdot (-F)$ has a simple zero across it ($\det G \neq 0$ there).

(2) At a simple zero of $\det h = \prod_i \mu_i$ (eigenvalues with respect to the auxiliary metric), exactly one eigenvalue $\mu_1$ vanishes and to first order: two vanishing eigenvalues would force a second-order zero. For the smoothness of the radical line, no spectral theory is needed: the adjugate $\operatorname{adj}(h)$, polynomial in the entries of $h$, is smooth; at a point of corank one it has rank exactly one (some $(d{-}1)$-minor is nonzero, and $h \cdot \operatorname{adj}(h) = \det(h)\,1 = 0$ puts every column of $\operatorname{adj}(h)$ in $\ker h$, which is a line). A nonvanishing column of $\operatorname{adj}(h)$ is therefore a smooth local spanning section of the radical line along $\Sig'$.

(3) Jacobi's formula, $\partial_\tau \det h = \operatorname{tr}\bigl(\operatorname{adj}(h)\, \partial_\tau h\bigr)$ (differentiate the determinant column by column and expand each along its differentiated column), evaluated at a point of $\Sig'$: in an auxiliary-orthonormal eigenbasis there, $\operatorname{adj}(h) = \bigl(\prod_{i \geq 2} \mu_i\bigr)\, \tilde k\, \tilde k^{\mathsf T}$ with $\tilde k$ the unit kernel vector, so
\[
\partial_\tau \det h \;=\; \Bigl(\prod_{i \geq 2} \mu_i\Bigr)\, (\partial_\tau h)(\tilde k, \tilde k) .
\]
The left side is nonzero (the zero of $\det h$ is simple, by (1)) and the nonvanishing eigenvalues $\mu_i$, $i \geq 2$, are nonzero; hence $(\partial_\tau h)(\tilde k, \tilde k) \neq 0$. This is exactly the nonvanishing of the datum $\delta'$ of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.invariant-form-t3} for $(T, h)$ along $\Sig'$: for any extension of $\tilde k$, $d\,h(\tilde k, \tilde k)|_{\Sig'} = (\partial_\tau h)(\tilde k, \tilde k)\, d\tau$, the cross term vanishing because $\tilde k$ is radical on $\Sig'$, and the lemma's proof uses only the symmetric form and the radical, not the cotangent origin of the bundle. So (T3) holds, (T1) and (T2) being parts (1) and (2).

t04-regenerated.title: The infinite wall sequence
t04-regenerated.text: Let $\Sig$ be compact. For good couplings at every stage, there is an infinite sequence $\Sig = \Sig^{(0)}, \Sig^{(1)} = \Sig', \Sig^{(2)}, \dots$ of tame walls, each displaced from the last into the unphysical region, carrying Clifford sheaves of ranks $2^n, 2^{n+2}, 2^{n+4}, \dots$ whose physical-side fibres ascend the Witt tower $\Cl(p,q) \to \Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1) \to \Cl(p{+}2,q{+}2) \to \cdots$, one Rule-1 rung per wall. Degeneracy is conserved along the entire sequence: each completion resolves its wall and produces the next, displaced successively further from the physical region.
t04-regenerated.proof:
Induction on Lemma \claimref{sheaf.tame-wall-induction} via Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.setup-generalises-arbitrary-bundles}, choosing at each stage a good coupling (possible: each $\Sig^{(k)}$ is a closed subset of a compact collar of its predecessor, hence compact, so its $S$ is finite, and only an upper bound on $|\mu
u|$ is demanded). Each stage also needs its radical line trivial, so that collar data exist for the next coupling (Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.collar-data-coupling}); this is automatic, because the shadow wall's radical line carries an explicit global spanning section: writing $\alpha_0 := G^{-1}e$ for the metric dual of the transversal functional, so that $s = \alpha_0(u)$, the section
\[
x \;:=\; \alpha_0 \,+\, \mu eta s\, 
O \,+\, 
u eta s\, 
Inf
\]
satisfies $h(x, \alpha) = e(\alpha)\,(1 + 2\mu
u eta^2 s) = e(\alpha)\,F = 0$ on $\{F = 0\}$ for every $\alpha \in T^*M$, while $h(x, 
O) = 
u eta s - 
u eta s = 0$ and $h(x, 
Inf) = \mu eta s - \mu eta s = 0$: so $x$ spans $\ker h$ along $\Sig'$, globally and without zeros. A global transversal for the next stage is then any $u'$ with $x(u') = 1$, available from any bundle metric. The ranks and signatures are Theorem \claimref{sheaf.one-sided-completion} at each stage. a figure of the original displays the sequence.

t04-regenerated.title: The wall class, posed
t04-regenerated.text: Degeneracy is conserved: it can be pushed off the physical region, never annihilated globally. This is the first geometric instance of the conservation principle conjectured at the fibre level in \cite[Conj.~7.9]{ButlerT1} (obstructions are moved, never destroyed), and the sharpest open question this paper poses is its measure: to construct a cohomological invariant on $\Sig$, presumably a relative class built from the mod-8 residues of the two competing ascents on the two sides of the wall, whose nonvanishing forces the shadow wall's existence, and whose behaviour under the iteration of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.tame-wall-induction} advances the clock of \cite[\S7]{ButlerT1}. The precise formulation is given in the section ``Dictionary, choices, and scope'' among the successor problems.

t04-regenerated.title: The exceptional algebra: deformation to the normal cone
t04-regenerated.text: Fix $x \in \Sig$ and a transversal curve through $x$ with parameter $t$, so that $G(t) = G_0 + t\dot G + O(t^2)$ with radical of $G_0$ spanned by $k$ and $\dot G(k,k) \neq 0$ by (T3). Rescale anisotropically: fix a complement $V_1$ of the radical and send $k \mapsto k/\sqrt{t}$. Then the rescaled forms converge as $t \to 0^+$ to the nondegenerate form $\hat G := G_0|_{V_1} \perp \dot G(k,k)$ on $V_1 \oplus \R k$: the cross terms are suppressed by $\sqrt{t}$, and the dying direction re-enters with its rate of degeneration as its metric coefficient. On the physical side the limit has signature $(p, q)$. The rescaled Clifford family is therefore a continuous family of nondegenerate algebras through $t = 0$, and its special fibre $\shE(x) := \Cl(V_1 \oplus \R k, \hat G)$, the \emph{exceptional algebra} at $x$, is independent of the choice of complement and of the scales of $k$ and $t$ up to canonical isomorphism.
t04-regenerated.proof:
Compute the Gram matrix of the rescaled frame $(v_1, \dots, v_{n-1}, k/\sqrt{t})$, $v_i$ a basis of $V_1$, against $G(t)$:
\[
G(t)(v_i, v_j) = G_0(v_i,v_j) + t\dot G(v_i,v_j) + O(t^2) \;\longrightarrow\; G_0(v_i,v_j) ;
\]
\[
G(t)(v_i, k/\sqrt{t}) = \frac{G_0(v_i,k) + t\dot G(v_i,k) + O(t^2)}{\sqrt{t}} = \frac{0 + O(t)}{\sqrt{t}} = O(\sqrt{t}) \;\longrightarrow\; 0 ,
\]
using $G_0(v_i, k) = 0$ ($k$ is radical for $G_0$);
\[
G(t)(k/\sqrt{t},\, k/\sqrt{t}) = \frac{G_0(k,k) + t\dot G(k,k) + O(t^2)}{t} = \dot G(k,k) + O(t) \;\longrightarrow\; \dot G(k,k) \neq 0 .
\]
The inequality is (T3) of \claimref{sheaf.tameness}. The limit Gram is block-diagonal: $G_0|_{V_1}$, nondegenerate of signature $(p{-}1,q)$ (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.degeneration-sheaf}(2), via $V_1 \cong T^*_xM/\shL$), plus the $1 \times 1$ block $\dot G(k,k)$, positive on the physical side (Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.coordinates-crossing-speed}); so $\hat G$ is nondegenerate of signature $(p,q)$ there. All rescaled Gram entries are continuous functions of $\sqrt{t}$ on $[0, \varepsilon)$, and by Lemma \claimref{sheaf.blade-basis-degenerate-forms-included} the structure constants of the corresponding Clifford algebras are polynomial in them: the rescaled Clifford family is continuous through $t = 0$, with nondegenerate special fibre $\shE(x)$.

Independence. Changing the complement, $v \mapsto v + c(v)k$: the $V_1$-block entries change by $c(v)G_0(k, w) + c(w)G_0(v,k) + c(v)c(w)G_0(k,k) + O(t) = O(t)$, and the cross terms remain $O(\sqrt t)$, so the limit is unchanged, and the two limit forms are literally equal under the isomorphism $v + \R k \mapsto v' + \R k$ of $V_1 \oplus \R k$ with $V_1' \oplus \R k$ fixing $k$ and matching complements through the quotient $T^*_xM/\shL$. Rescaling $k \mapsto ck$ multiplies the diagonal limit entry by $c^2$ and the generator by $c$: the map $v_i \mapsto v_i$, $k \mapsto ck$ is an isometry of the two limit forms, inducing a canonical isomorphism of the Clifford algebras. Reparametrising $t \mapsto at$ ($a > 0$) multiplies $\dot G$ by $a$ and the rescaled generator $k/\sqrt{t}$ by $1/\sqrt{a}$; the two effects compose to the isometry $k \mapsto k/\sqrt a$ against the $a$-fold entry, again canonical. In each case the displayed isometry is built from the change of data alone, with no further choices, and the isomorphism of Clifford algebras it induces by functoriality is the canonical identification meant in the statement. (Uniqueness among all isometries fixing the $V_1$-part fails, $k \mapsto -k$ being another; canonicality here means choice-freeness of the displayed maps, not uniqueness.)

t04-regenerated.title: The metric's residue, and the square-root twist
t04-regenerated.text:
At a tame wall the physical metric (the inverse cometric) has a canonical simple pole: for any defining function $\tau$ of $\Sig$,
\[
O \;:=\; \lim_{\tau \to 0}\, \tau\, G^{-1} \;=\; \frac{k \otimes k}{\delta(k \otimes k)/d\tau} ,
\]
a nowhere-vanishing section of $\shL \otimes \shL$ depending on $\tau$ through the weight of a section of $\shL \otimes \shL \otimes N\Sig$; invariantly, the residue is $\delta^{-1}$, the inverse of the transversality datum of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.invariant-form-t3}, regarded as a section of $\shL \otimes \shL \otimes N\Sig = \operatorname{Hom}(N^*\Sig, \shL^{\otimes 2})$. It is a nondegenerate pairing between $\shL^* \otimes \shL^*$ and $N^*\Sig$, hence induces a canonical isomorphism
\[
N^*\Sig \;\cong\; \shL^{\otimes 2} :
\]
the conormal bundle is the square of the dying direction itself. Dually, $N\Sig \cong (\shL^*)^{\otimes 2}$: the Witt partner line adjoined by the completion, which the pairing normalisation $kk^* + k^*k = 1$ identifies with $\shL^*$, is a canonical square root of the \emph{normal} bundle, and the dying line $\shL$ is a canonical square root of the conormal bundle. (The reading of the blow-up rescaling $k \mapsto k/\sqrt{t}$ as the normalisation of a conormal square root is Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.blow-up-dictionary}.)
t04-regenerated.proof:
Work in the frame $(k, m_1, \dots, m_{n-1})$ of Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.coordinates-crossing-speed} along a transversal with parameter $\tau$, with Gram $G(\tau) = \begin{psmallmatrix} \lambda & b^{\mathsf T} \\ b & G_1 \end{psmallmatrix}$, $\lambda(0) = 0$, $b(0) = 0$, $G_1(0)$ invertible, and $\lambda'(0) =: T \neq 0$, so that $\delta(k \otimes k) = T\, d\tau$. The inverse cometric $G^{-1}$, a symmetric form on $TM$, has matrix $C := [\text{Gram}]^{-1}$ with respect to the covector basis, meaning $G^{-1} = \sum C_{ab}\, \kappa_a \otimes \kappa_b$ over the frame covectors $\kappa = (k, m)$. Block inversion:
\[
C_{00} = (\lambda - b^{\mathsf T} G_1^{-1} b)^{-1} = \frac{1}{T\tau}\bigl(1 + O(\tau)\bigr), \qquad
C_{0i} = -C_{00}\, (b^{\mathsf T} G_1^{-1})_i = O(1),
\]
since $b = O(\tau)$ makes $b^{\mathsf T} G_1^{-1} b = O(\tau^2)$ and $C_{00}\,O(\tau) = O(1)$; and the $m$-block of $C$ is $G_1^{-1} + G_1^{-1} b\, C_{00}\, b^{\mathsf T} G_1^{-1} = O(1)$. Multiplying by $\tau$ and letting $\tau \to 0$, every entry goes to zero except the top-left:
\[

t04-regenerated.title: Dictionary: tractors and the ambient metric
t04-regenerated.text:
The following correspondences are assembly-level: precise at the level of the structures named, with the differences stated, and with no claim of subsumption either way.

\emph{Tractor calculus} \cite{BEG1994, CurryGover2018} attaches to an $n$-dimensional conformal manifold of signature $(p,q)$ the standard tractor bundle $\mathcal{T}$, of rank $n + 2$ and signature $(p{+}1, q{+}1)$, with a composition series whose successive quotients are the density bundles $\Lambda^0[1]$, $T^*M[1]$, $\Lambda^0[-1]$, and a canonical (normal) tractor connection. The correspondences: the ambient bundle $T = T^*M \oplus \underline{\R}^2$ matches the underlying filtered bundle, with $\nO, \nInf$ the two weight lines (the ``point at zero'' and ``point at infinity'' slots of the conformal sphere model); the ambient form $h$ matches the tractor metric; the completion's increment $(p,q) \to (p{+}1,q{+}1)$ is the tractor increment. The differences: tractor calculus starts from a \emph{conformal class} on all of $M$ and its bundle carries a canonical connection; the present construction starts from a single \emph{degenerating} cometric, carries no distinguished connection (none is needed for the algebra), and its coupling is supported near the wall, where conformal rescaling is precisely what fails. The natural meeting point, flagged as a question rather than claimed: at a conformally regularised wall (the CCC picture \cite{Penrose2010}), the conformal class extends across $\Sig$ while the metric degenerates, and there the ambient sheaf should be canonically the tractor bundle of the extended class, with the coupling the almost-Einstein scale tractor; making that precise is successor work.

\emph{The Fefferman-Graham ambient metric} \cite{FG1985, FG2012} realises the same $(+1,+1)$ increment as a nondegenerate metric of signature $(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ on a thickening $\widetilde{M} \subset \R_+ \times M \times \R$ of the metric cone. The correspondence: the FG cone directions (the dilation and the transversal) match the hyperbolic plane $(\nO, \nInf)$; the FG normalisation (Ricci-flatness to infinite or determined order) plays the role that the coupling's collar normalisation plays here. The difference is categorical: FG produces a manifold with metric, this paper produces a bundle with form; the Clifford functor applied to the FG tangent bundle along the cone's zero section reproduces the fibres of the ambient sheaf, but the sheaf exists without any thickened manifold, which is what permits the degenerate locus to be handled at all.

t04-regenerated.title: The Schwarzschild composite
t04-regenerated.text:
The tame class stops short of the black hole on two separate counts, both recorded in Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.scope-tame-class}: the Schwarzschild singularity is a worldline, of codimension three, and its degeneration is anisotropic, different directions degenerating at different rates. the section ``Scope, and successor problems'' names the repairs: a geometric blow-up replacing the worldline by its normal sphere bundle, and direction-dependent weights in place of the single $\sqrt t$ rescaling, with the Kasner-weights conjecture that the correct weights are the Kasner exponents. This section executes the composite for exact Schwarzschild.

The finding that makes it tractable is that the two gaps are not independent obstacles to be cleared one after the other. The blow-up closes most of the anisotropy by itself: the two angular rates are exactly the tautological rescaling that the exceptional divisor of any blow-up carries (the normal sphere at parameter $r$ has radius $r$), so after the blow-up only \emph{one} direction still degenerates, and it does so at first order in the defining function. Anisotropy at codimension three, restricted to this case, is codimension-one tameness expressed in polar coordinates.

Three costs are incurred, and they are stated here. First, the wall is now a \emph{boundary} of the blown-up manifold rather than an interior hypersurface, so the tameness hypotheses need one-sided restatements; these turn out to make the completion easier, not harder, and to make the conservation theorem vacuous in a way that is itself instructive. Second, the corank-one structure lies on a \emph{weighted} coframe module $\shW$ rather than on the cotangent bundle; the module is not a choice, being characterised as the bounded-norm one-forms of the quasihomogeneous blow-up, and the weights it encodes are unique and are the Kasner exponents. Third, everything here is exact Schwarzschild; the general anisotropic class, and Kerr, remain open and are itemised at the end.

t04-regenerated.title: Variable-order algebra; strict diagonal data
t04-regenerated.text:
Let $E$ be a smooth $3$-manifold and $\Mt = [0,\varepsilon)_\tau \times E$. An \emph{admissible exponent family} is a countable family $\{e_j\}$ of smooth nonnegative functions on $E$ such that, on each compact $K \subseteq E$ and for each level $N$, only finitely many $e_j$ have $\inf_K e_j \leq N$. The \emph{variable-order algebra} $\mathcal{A}$ is the algebra of sums $\sum_j f_j(x,\tau)\,\tau^{e_j(x)}$ over admissible exponent families, with $f_j$ smooth up to $\tau = 0$; on each compact and each interval $[0, \tau_0]$, the terms below any level are finitely many and the remainder is $O(\tau^{N})$ locally uniformly, so the sums converge locally uniformly and the class is closed under products (exponent families add, and the sum family is again admissible). \[
\operatorname{diag}\bigl(1,\ -\tau^{-2p_1(x)}c_1,\ -\tau^{-2p_2(x)}c_2,\ -\tau^{-2p_3(x)}c_3\bigr),
\]
with $p_i$ smooth, $p_1 < 0 < p_2 \leq p_3$ pointwise, and $c_i(x,\tau)$ smooth and positive up to $\tau = 0$. The coupling of Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.collar-data-coupling} uses a transversal, and two questions were left open: whether the completion depends on the choice, and whether the wall admits an equivariant classical value for the dying direction at all, the no-repair theorem of \cite[Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT1} being proved where the ambient form is nondegenerate and the dying direction has a hyperbolic partner. Both are settled here, at the wall, with the collar constants $\mu, 
u$ and the bump held fixed. Throughout, computations are at a point of $\Sig$ on the inner collar, where $ eta = 1$ and the Gram $G$ of the coframe module has corank one with radical $\R k$; $\alpha$ ranges over covectors, $u, v, \lambda$ over vectors, and $\alpha(v)$ is the pairing. One term is fixed before anything is compared. The \emph{completed structure} at the point is the triple $(T, h_u, k)$: the ambient module with its form and the dying direction, carrying the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-grading of its Clifford algebra and the subalgebra generated by the coframe module (the fibre of the degeneration sheaf). The named frame $(
O, 
Inf)$ of Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.collar-data-coupling} and the ladder partner $k^* = 
O/2
u$ of Corollary \claimref{sheaf.localised-transport} are choices made inside that structure, not part of it; had the frame been retained as structure, the transversal would be recoverable from it, $\alpha(u) = 2h_u(\alpha, k^*)$ for $\alpha \in T^*M$, and Theorem \claimref{sheaf.no-equivariant-value-wall} would have nothing to say. What the theorem says is that neither choice is canonical. Every identity below is verified in exact rational arithmetic on the Schwarzschild data of the section ``The Schwarzschild composite'' at two masses (the section ``Machine verification'').

t04-regenerated.title: Base unipotents at the wall
t04-regenerated.text: For $\lambda \in \ker k := \{v : k(v) = 0\}$ define $g_\lambda(\alpha) := \alpha + \alpha(\lambda)\,k$ on $T^*M$ at the wall point. Then $g_\lambda$ is a $G$-isometry, fixes $k$, and $g_\lambda g_{\lambda'} = g_{\lambda+\lambda'}$; the dual action on vectors is $u' \mapsto u' - k(u')\lambda$, hence on transversals ($k(u') = 1$) the translation $u' \mapsto u' - \lambda$, a free and transitive action of $(\ker k, +)$.
t04-regenerated.proof: $G(g_\lambda\alpha, g_\lambda\alpha') = G(\alpha, \alpha')$, every correction term carrying a factor $G(\cdot, k) = 0$, $k$ spanning the radical; $g_\lambda(k) = k + k(\lambda)k = k$; the composition law is immediate. Dually, $(g_\lambda^{-1}\alpha)(u') = \alpha(u') - \alpha(\lambda)k(u') = \alpha(u' - k(u')\lambda)$; freeness and transitivity on transversals are affine-space statements over $\ker k$.

t04-regenerated.text: For every $v \in \ker k$ there is $\tilde v \in T^*M$ with $G(\alpha, \tilde v) = \alpha(v)$ for all $\alpha$, unique modulo $\R k$; and the normalisation $G(\tilde v, \tilde v) + 2\tilde v(u) = 0$ is met at exactly one gauge representative, the left side being affine in the gauge parameter with slope $2k(u) = 2$.
t04-regenerated.proof: The musical map $\alpha \mapsto G(\alpha, \cdot)$ has kernel $\R k$ and image inside the vectors annihilated by $k$; its rank equals $\dim\ker k$, so the image is exactly $\ker k$. O, 
Inf\}$, is an automorphism of the completed structure $(T, h_u, k)$: an $h_u$-isometry restricting to $g_\lambda$ on $T^*M$ and fixing $k$, hence an automorphism of the completed Clifford algebra preserving its grading and its degeneration subalgebra. t04-regenerated.title: Scope, and what this discharges
t04-regenerated.text: The statements are pointwise on $\Sig$, every formula rational in the collar data and hence smooth in the point, so they hold over every open piece of the wall; the collar constants and bump are held fixed, their variation being the rescaling of the section ``Dictionary, choices, and scope''. Off the wall the two ambient forms $h_u$ and $h_{u+v}$ need not be isometric, and Theorem \claimref{sheaf.transversal-independence-wall} does not say they are: by Lemma \claimref{sheaf.determinant-identity-blow-up-expansion}, $\det h = \det G \cdot (-(1 + 2\mu\nu\beta^2 s))$ with $s = G^{-1}(e,e)$ depending on the transversal, so the shadow wall of the section ``The shadow wall: conservation of degeneracy'' moves with the transversal, and on a far-side collar point one form can be degenerate while the other is not, or both nondegenerate with different signatures (the script exhibits both, on the model data $G = \operatorname{diag}(\lambda, 1, -1, -1)$ with $\mu\nu = 1$). The transversal independence proved here is a statement at the wall, and nothing off the wall is needed: the value question is a question at the wall. What Theorem \claimref{sheaf.no-equivariant-value-wall} discharges downstream is the boundary case that the singularity paper recorded as open in the scope of its no-repair import \cite{ButlerT5}: with the theorem in place, no classical value repairs the dying direction on the approach or at the boundary itself.

t04-regenerated.title: Position in the series
t04-regenerated.text: This paper is T4 of the series. It uses two predecessors and supplies four successors. It uses the language and fibre computations of the primer T0 \cite{ButlerT0} and the fibre theory of the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1}: the Witt completion, the zero-divisor taxonomy with its transport rules, and the minimality theorem, all used here one fibre at a time. It supplies, downstream: the localised transport (Corollary \claimref{sheaf.localised-transport}) is the structure the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} imports when it applies the transport principle at the black hole, and the section ``The Schwarzschild composite'' extends that import from tame walls to the Schwarzschild boundary itself; the wall package of the section ``The ambient sheaf: one-sided completion'' and the section ``The shadow wall: conservation of degeneracy'' is what the iteration corollary of the tower paper T3 \cite{ButlerT3} climbs; the support statement, that the ladder pair is supported exactly on the singular locus, is the geometric input behind the no-attic and no-echo arguments of the entropy paper T8 \cite{ButlerT8}; and the tractor-level route to the same singularity, reached here at sheaf level, is the subject of the interior paper T6 \cite{ButlerT6}, whose weighted limit the section ``The matching with the weighted limit'' identifies as a connection on this paper's exceptional bundle, and whose admissibility class is assigned the analytic half of the anisotropic theory that the section ``The anisotropic class: variable weights and stability'' closes at the algebraic level. Two further exports go to the singularity paper alone: the no-value theorem at the wall (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.no-equivariant-value-wall}), which it reproduces verbatim as its boundary no-go, and the function-linearity principle (Proposition \claimref{sheaf.function-linearity-tame-constructions}), the class-membership input of its hopping exclusion \cite[Facts B.3, B.4]{ButlerT5}.

t04-regenerated.title: Machine verification
t04-regenerated.text:
Every computational identity in this paper has been checked by computer, in exact rational arithmetic, in the manner of the verifications deposited with \cite{ButlerT1}. The script \texttt{verify\_T04.py}, deposited with this paper alongside the series' shared exact-arithmetic library \texttt{GA.py}, \cite{ButlerVerifyT04}, performs two hundred and ninety-six checks and reports each. Three exact computational routines are implemented directly: the basis-blade Clifford product over the rationals with degenerate generators; an exterior-algebra model of the Clifford action for \emph{arbitrary} rational Gram matrices, non-diagonal and degenerate included, whose faithfulness is the symbol-map triangularity in the proof of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.blade-basis-degenerate-forms-included}; and a rational-function routine in a formal collar parameter $\tau$, with exact polynomial GCD reduction, so that identities are verified as identities of rational functions rather than at samples. The coverage: the blade-basis independence of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.blade-basis-degenerate-forms-included} for a degenerate non-orthogonal Gram matrix, together with the Clifford relation of the exterior model on every basis state; the full degeneration-sheaf package of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.degeneration-sheaf} at the physical wall fibre (anticommutation, $ka = \hat a k$, $\dim J = 8$ by exact rank, $J^2 = 0$ over all $64$ ideal products, and the quotient's structure constants against $\Cl(0,3)$); the unit-ideal identity of Proposition \claimref{sheaf.resolution-ideal-theoretically} in $\Cl(1,1)$ and in the spacetime ascent $\Cl(2,4)$; the wall Gram of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.wall-gram} (block determinant $-2\mu\nu$, both block signatures, the orthocomplement vector $w$, and the full wall signatures for $(1,3)$ and $(2,1)$ under both coupling signs); the determinant identity of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.determinant-identity-blow-up-expansion} as an exact rational-function identity in $\tau$, with nonzero $b(\tau)$, $\tau$-dependent tangential block and two bump values, plus the blow-up expansion $(\tau s)(0) = 1/\lambda'(0)$; the one-sided completion sampled at exact rational collar points ($F \geq 1$, signature $(2,4)$); the localised ladder pair of Corollary \claimref{sheaf.localised-transport} verified \emph{on} the wall in the full coupled six-dimensional Gram via the exterior model ($c(k)c(k^*) + c(k^*)c(k) = \mathrm{id}$ on all $64$ states); the located conservation of Proposition \claimref{sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-located} with the shadow wall found at the exact rational point $\tau' = -2\mu\nu$, its crossing simple, its corank exactly one, and the signatures $(2,4)$ and $(1,5)$ on the two sides; the rescaled Gram limits, complement-independence and $c^2$ weight of Proposition \claimref{sheaf.exceptional-algebra-deformation-normal-cone} as polynomials in $\sqrt t$; and the residue of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.metrics-residue-square-root-twist}, all sixteen entries of $\tau G^{-1}$ at $\tau = 0$ with $b \neq 0$, the scale-freeness under $k \mapsto 2k$, and the weight $a$ under $\tau \mapsto a\tau$.

The Schwarzschild composite of the section ``The Schwarzschild composite'' is covered by seventy further checks, all identities in the radial variable being verified as identities of rational functions in $u = \sqrt r$ (exact polynomial GCD reduction), not at samples, with the mass entering as $2M = m^2$. t04-regenerated.title: The cones fold
t04-regenerated.text:
Track the null directions of the $(t,r)$ plane in the metric $g(a,b) \;=\; \hb^{-1}(a) \cdot \hb^{-1}(b)$, $g(a,a) = \hb^{-1}(a)^{2}$ with $\hb^{-1} = 1 + \beta P$: for $a = \et + \lambda\,\er$,
\[
\hb^{-1}(a) = \et + (\lambda + \beta)\,\er, \qquad g(a,a) = 1 - (\lambda + \beta)^2 ,
\]
so $a$ is $g$-null exactly when $\lambda = -\beta \pm 1$: the physical cone's two null directions are $\et + (-\beta \pm 1)\er$, the radial null curves $dr/dt = -\beta \pm 1$ of the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand line element of the section ``The metric of the gauge field, and its static form''. At the horizon ($\beta = 1$) they are $\lambda = 0$, the hovering ray, and $\lambda = -2$, an ingoing one. Normalising each by its $\er$-coefficient and letting $r \to 0$ (so $\beta \to \infty$),
\[
\tfrac{1}{-\beta \pm 1}\,\et + \er \;\longrightarrow\; \er :
\]
both branches of the light cone collapse onto the single direction $\er$, both tipping towards $-\er$, inward, on the way. Simultaneously $g(\et, \et) = 1 - \beta^2 \to -\infty$: no rescaling of the classical field stays finite and nondegenerate. The degeneration is through a null kernel direction in the exact sense of Proposition \claimref{singularity.degeneration-exactly}, and it is not removable by gauge choice (Proposition \claimref{singularity.non-removability-invariant-argument}).

t04-regenerated.title: The degeneration, exactly
t04-regenerated.text:
As $r \to 0$, exactly and with every identity holding at finite $\beta$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (The map.) $\beta^{-1}\hb = \beta^{-1}\,\mathrm{id} - P$, so $\beta^{-1}\hb \to -P$: a rank-one map with image $\R\,\er$ and kernel $\et^{\perp} = \operatorname{span}(\er, e_\vartheta, e_\varphi)$.
\item (The metric.) $\beta^{-2} g(a,b) = -(a\cdot\et)(b\cdot\et) + \beta^{-1}\bigl[(a\cdot\et)(b\cdot\er) + (b\cdot\et)(a\cdot\er)\bigr] + \beta^{-2}(a \cdot b)$, so $\beta^{-2}g \to \hat g$ with
\[
\hat g(a,b) \;=\; -(a\cdot\et)(b\cdot\et) :
\]
a form of rank one and signature $(0,1,3)$, whose radical is $\et^{\perp}$, the kernel of the limit map.
\item (The null direction, located.) The folded direction $\er$ of Proposition \claimref{singularity.cones-fold} lies in the radical of $\hat g$ and is $\hat g$-null, while $g(\er,\er) = -1$ at every finite radius: the nullity of the degenerate direction is a property of the limit form, not of the flat background, and this is the exact content of the phrase ``degeneration through a null kernel direction''. It is the datum Step 2 uses.
\end{enumerate}

t04-regenerated.title: The solution, and where the divergence lies
t04-regenerated.text:
The pair $(\hb, \Omega)$ of $\hb(a) \;=\; a - \beta\,(a \cdot \et)\,\er \;=\; (1 - \beta P)(a), \qquad \beta(r) = \sqrt{2M/r}, \qquad P(a) := (a \cdot \et)\,\er$ and Proposition \claimref{singularity.connection-bivector-computed} solves the vacuum field equations $\mathcal{R}(a) - \tfrac12\, a\, \mathcal{R} \;=\; 8\pi\, T(a), \qquad D \wedge \hb(a) \;=\; \hb(\nabla \wedge a)$ at every $r > 0$, and the divergence of the classical description resides in $\Omega$ and in the curvature, not in $\hb$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (The radial curvature, from the gauge field alone.) On the radial plane both connection values are multiples of the single bivector $\sigma_r$, so the commutator term of the field strength the relation displayed with \claimref{singularity.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations} vanishes identically and nothing depends on $t$; hence, in two lines,
\[
\mathcal{R}(\partial_t \wedge \partial_r)
\;=\; \partial_t\,\Omega(\partial_r) - \partial_r\,\Omega(\partial_t) + \Omega(\partial_t)\times\Omega(\partial_r)
\;=\; -\,\partial_r\Bigl(\frac{M}{r^2}\Bigr)\sigma_r
\;=\; \frac{2M}{r^3}\,\sigma_r :

the radial plane is an eigenplane of the curvature with eigenvalue of magnitude $2M/r^3$, derived without leaving the gauge formalism.

\item (Unimodularity.) $\det \hb = 1$ exactly, at every radius, horizon included: $P$ is rank-one nilpotent, so $1 - \beta P$ is unipotent as a matrix.
