In the parallel frame of Lemma \claimref{interior.exact-parallelism-convergence-rate}, write $B_i := e_0 \wedge e_i$ for the three boost bivectors and $R_{ij} := e_i \wedge e_j$ for the rotations. The rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ of the interior gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}: the torsion-free connection, whose reading on the derived metric is its Levi-Civita connection), evaluated on the unit tangential physical directions (through $A \cdot D = D_{\hb(A)}$, so that $\Omega(e_c)$ stands for $\Omega(\hb(e_c))$), is exactly
\[
\Omega(e_1) = -\sigma_1 B_1, \qquad
\Omega(e_2) = -\sigma_2 B_2, \qquad
\Omega(e_3) = -\sigma_3 B_3 + \frac{\cot\theta}{r}\,R_{23},
\]
and $\Omega(e_0) = 0$, in the sign of the Definition, $D_a M = a \cdot \nabla M + \Omega(a) \times M$, in which the Cartan forms $\omega^{i}{}_{0} = \sigma_i\,\theta^i$ assemble to $-\sigma_i B_i$. The rotation coefficient is the connection induced by $D$ on the round two-spheres of fixed $(\tau, t)$, of radius $r$: in any local orthonormal frame on an $S^2$ coordinate patch its coefficients are $O(1/r)$.
t06-regenerated.proof: The computation below is written for the derived metric of the interior gravitational field; by Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(ii) its Levi-Civita connection forms, evaluated on the frame and assembled into bivectors, are the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ on the physical frame vectors, so it computes $\Omega$ directly. With orthonormal coframe $\theta^0 = d\tau$, $\theta^i = a_i dx^i$, dual to the frame of \claimref{interior.exact-parallelism-convergence-rate}, the first structure equation $d\theta^a = -\omega^a{}_b \wedge \theta^b$ determines the connection uniquely (torsion-free, metric). Computing: $d\theta^1 = (\partial_\tau a_1)\,d\tau \wedge dt = \sigma_1\,\theta^0 \wedge \theta^1$, and likewise for $\theta^2$; while $d\theta^3 = \partial_\tau(a_3)\,d\tau\wedge d\varphi\,+\,\partial_\theta(r\sin\theta)\,d\theta \wedge d\varphi = \sigma_3\,\theta^0\wedge\theta^3 + \frac{\cot\theta}{r}\,\theta^2 \wedge \theta^3$. The last sentence is the standard statement that the induced connection on the constant-$\tau$ spheres is that of $S^2$ of radius $r$, whose coefficients in an orthonormal frame scale as $1/r$; the $\cot\theta$ divergence at the poles is an artifact of the spherical frame, removable by a change of patch.

Inf \wedge W$, $
O \wedge W$, or $\R(

t06-regenerated.proof:
Containment is immediate: $B_i \in \Lambda^2 W$ and $\Lambda^2 W$ is a subalgebra (brackets of operators preserving $W$ and annihilating $W^\perp$ do the same). For fullness, compute with $(u \wedge v)(w) \;=\; \ip{v}{w}\,u - \ip{u}{w}\,v$, the action of bivectors on vectors as the orthogonal Lie algebra (\claimref{std-algebra.bivector-lie-algebra}): for $u,v,u',v'$ orthogonal frame vectors,
\[
[\,u\wedge v,\ v\wedge w\,] \;=\; Q(v)\; u\wedge w ,
\]
and brackets of wedges with no shared factor vanish. Hence $[B_1, B_2] = [e_0\wedge e_1,\, e_0 \wedge e_2]$: rewriting $B_1 = -e_1\wedge e_0$, this is $-Q(e_0)\, e_1\wedge e_2 = -R_{12}$, and cyclically for the other pairs: all three rotations appear. The verification script performs the generation exactly: starting from the three boosts as antisymmetric matrices over $\mathbb{Q}$ preserving the $(2,4)$ form, it closes under commutators and confirms the resulting span has dimension six and lies in $\Lambda^2 W$.

t06-regenerated.title: Weighted blow-up, Hubble normalisation, and the admissible class
t06-regenerated.text:
Blow up the interior along the singular locus by adjoining the exceptional boundary $\{\tau = 0\}$ to the collar $(0,\tau_0] \times \mathcal{B}$, $\mathcal{B} := \R_t \times S^2$, \emph{with direction-dependent weights} $(p_1, p_2, p_3)$: the boundary is probed by the rescaled (Hubble-normalised) data
\[
\widehat\Omega_\tau \;:=\; \tau\,\Omega\big|_{\text{unit tangential directions at time } \tau},
\]
the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ in the $D$-parallel physical frame, evaluated on the unit vectors of the $\tau$-slice and multiplied by $\tau$; a tangential direction carries weight $p_i$ in the sense that its unit vector contracts by the factor $\tau^{p_i}$ relative to the coordinate vector, which is exactly what the frame normalisation implements. A gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on the collar (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), in a synchronous gauge and with derived metric singular at $\tau = 0$, is \emph{admissible} (Einstein velocity-dominated) if it is Einstein, $\mathcal{R}(a) = \Lambda a$ with $\Lambda$ constant (in the store's sign, so that the derived metric has $\Ric_{ab} = \Lambda\, g_{ab}$; the field-equation hypothesis the tractor clauses of Theorem \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem} consume; the Levi-Civita clauses, those about $\Omega$, use only the decay conditions), and in some $D$-parallel orthonormal physical frame, with boosts $B_i = e_0 \wedge e_i$, the Hubble-normalised connection satisfies $\widehat\Omega_\tau = -\sum_i p_i B_i \otimes \hat\theta^i + E_\tau$ with constants $p_i \neq 0$ (the sign is that of Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}, $D_a M = a \cdot \nabla M + \Omega(a) \times M$, in which the Cartan forms $\omega^{i}{}_{0} = (p_i/\tau)\,\theta^i$ of a Kasner field assemble to $-\sum_i p_i B_i$) satisfying the Kasner-type constraint $\sum_i p_i^2 = 1$ (the Schwarzschild exponents $(-\tfrac13, \tfrac23, \tfrac23)$ satisfy it, Lemma \claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior}; the constraint is what Theorem \claimref{interior.transport-level-convergence-along-tangential-curves} uses, through Cauchy-Schwarz, to bound the model generator on unit directions by $1$) and an error $E_\tau$ which tends to zero as $\tau \to 0$ and for which $\|E_\tau\|/\tau$ is integrable on $(0, \tau_0]$, both locally uniformly on $\mathcal{B}$. A synchronous metric is called admissible when it is the derived metric of an admissible gravitational field. Two boundary objects are part of the same data. The \emph{boundary bundle} is the trivial extension of the parallel trivialisation: the tractor fibre in the parallel tractor frame, extended over $\{\tau = 0\} \times \mathcal{B}$ as a product, so that a section defined for $\tau > 0$ extends to the boundary exactly when its components in that frame converge. The \emph{boundary holonomy algebra} is the Lie subalgebra of $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$ generated by the limiting values of the Hubble-normalised connection on unit tangential directions, over all boundary points: a values-level definition, which is what the theorem computes; along the directions where the connection is abelian it agrees with the transport-level reading (Theorem \claimref{interior.weighted-limit-theorem}, final clause). By Lemmas \claimref{interior.exact-parallelism-convergence-rate} and \claimref{interior.interior-connection-exactly} the Schwarzschild interior ($\Lambda = 0$) is admissible, with $\|E_\tau\| = O(\tau^{2/3}) + O(\tau/r) = O(\tau^{1/3})$ tending to zero and $\|E_\tau\|/\tau = O(\tau^{-2/3})$ integrable at $0$. On the sphere factor the frame, and with it the display, is taken patchwise (no global orthonormal frame on $S^2$ exists); admissibility and the limiting values are patch-independent statements, the values transforming by the constant rotation between patches.

\[
\mathfrak M \;=\; -M\,\chi^{-3}
\]
with $\chi = r - Ia\cos\theta$ the Killing-spinor scale of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-walker-penrose-killing-spinor} in the same normalisation. t06-regenerated.title: The perturbed Cauchy horizon
t06-regenerated.text: Exact Kerr was never the hard part of the test. Since Kerr is Ricci-flat, Theorem \claimref{interior.covariant-form-vacuum-equations} applies verbatim on the whole vacuum region, inner horizons included: the parallel null tractor exists globally, and exact Kerr passes the covariance test outright. The physical question is what survives perturbation, because the Cauchy horizon is known to be unstable. The established results are imported with provenance and then read.

t06-regenerated.title: The filtration at the Cauchy horizon, read from the literature
t06-regenerated.text:
In the framework's language, Fact \claimref{interior.imported-mass-inflation-stability} yields three findings; each is a reading of the imported statements, and the one-step translation carrying each reading is proved below.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Obstruction type:} the degeneration at the perturbed Cauchy horizon is of type N (null kernel direction), in the degenerate-radical reading the series fixes at the Schwarzschild centre \cite[Prop.~3.1]{ButlerT5}, which extends T1's taxonomy \cite[Def.~3.1]{ButlerT1} to radical directions through \cite[Thm.~4.4, Cor.~4.5]{ButlerT4}: the same class as at the centre, realised on a null hypersurface rather than at a point.
\item \emph{Filtration by derivative level:} a $C^0$ derived metric $g(a,b) = \hb^{-1}(a) \cdot \hb^{-1}(b)$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) determines a $C^0$ conformal class (pointwise multiplication by a positive function preserves continuity, and the class map $g \mapsto [g]$ is continuous), so point-level structure, metric and conformal alike, extends continuously across the Cauchy horizon, while connection-level structure, the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ (whose reading on $g$ is the Levi-Civita connection) and the tractor connection alike (on flat spacetime the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}, whose $\nO$ summand carries the Schouten map, two derivatives of $g$), generically fails: proved in spherical symmetry by Fact \claimref{interior.imported-mass-inflation-stability}(ii$'$), expected for Kerr. The ordering is by derivative level; a strict separation of the conformal description from the metric one at fixed derivative level is not among the imports, and is exactly the open transport question of the section ``Scope, and successor problems''.
\item \emph{Filtration:} in a physical frame adapted to the horizon generators, the divergent components of the field strength $\mathcal{R}(B)$ are those of extreme boost weight, the top of the parabolic filtration attached to the null direction: the divergence occupies the nilpotent slots, as in every previous instance of the obstruction.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The Cauchy horizon, as the boundary of the maximal development, and the extension of the field across it are global and are not carried by a single gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime; the statements above that hold on the invertible region (the type and kernel of the degeneration, the regularity of the derived metric and of $\Omega$ along the approach, the boost weights of the divergent components) are in Gauge Theory Gravity, and the Cauchy horizon and the extension across it are read on the manifold assembled from the derived metric's charts.

At connection level the two descriptions succeed or fail together: the tractor connection \claimref{interior.imported-tractor-connection} carries the Levi-Civita action and the Schouten tensor, first and second derivatives of $g$, so the generic failure of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-mass-inflation-stability}(ii$'$) reaches it exactly where it reaches the metric connection; no separation between the descriptions is claimed, or available, from the imports. (3) is the boost-weight structure of weak null singularities as established in the works cited in Fact \claimref{interior.imported-mass-inflation-stability}: the blow-up is in the transversal derivative components, which carry extreme weight under the boost fixing the horizon generator; we import the analytic statement and observe only that extreme boost weight is precisely the nilradical slot of the parabolic fixing the null direction (Proposition \claimref{interior.stabilisers-flat-model}(3)).

t06-regenerated.title: The conclusion, and two cautions
t06-regenerated.text: Proposition \claimref{interior.filtration-cauchy-horizon-read-literature}(2) is a filtration statement, and it is read as exactly that: survival at the perturbed Cauchy horizon is ordered by derivative level, with the divergence in the nilpotent slots, which is the structure the framework predicts. What the literature does not supply is a strict separation of the conformal from the metric description at fixed derivative level: the framework's central claim, that the ascended description persists where the metric one fails, therefore rests at the Cauchy horizon on the open transport question of successor problem (1), not on a finished theorem. The Kerr test is passed at the level the imports reach, and no further. Two cautions make the conclusion more precise, both recorded as scope. First, generic perturbations destroy type-D rigidity: the exact shape factorisations of Propositions \claimref{interior.exact-scale-decoupling} and \claimref{interior.complex-factorisation-location-ring} are properties of the exact family, and robust statements off it must be made at the level of the boost-weight filtration rather than the fixed operator $S$. Second, what the framework most needs, a quantitative transport theorem (convergence of tractor parallel transport along causal curves crossing the Cauchy horizon), needs integrability of the connection along such curves: a property strictly between the established $C^0$ metric extension and the $C^1$ statement whose generic failure is proved in spherical symmetry and expected for Kerr, and not currently available in either direction. It is the sharpest open problem the test leaves, and it is registered in the section ``Scope, and successor problems''.

\emph{Which state?} the section ``The state input: the I-state'' proves the I-state theorem, the I-state being the series' name for the framework's distinguished equilibrium state $\omega_I$: among the quasi-free states of the CAR algebra of the boundary modes there is exactly one that is KMS for the geometry's boost at the Hawking temperature, and the KMS identity forces its two-point data outright, the pairing to zero and the symbol to Fermi-Dirac (Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state}). \emph{Which algebra carries the mode continuum?} the section ``The mode continuum'' extends the single-mode statements over the tower's CAR limit \cite{ButlerT3}: the finite-window statements are exact theorems, the inductive-limit results are imported as Facts with provenance, and the result is free-fermion thermal field theory as the algebra carrying the near-horizon boundary modes.

In $\Cl(1,1)$, by \claimref{std-algebra.vector-squares}: $v^*v = \tfrac14(e_0 - e_1)(e_0 + e_1) = \tfrac14(e_0^2 - e_1^2 + e_0e_1 - e_1e_0) = \tfrac14(1 + 1 + 2e_0e_1) = \tfrac12(1 + e_0e_1)$, so $\sigma = v^*v - vv^* = e_0e_1$ in this orientation; relabelling the pair reverses it. (2) From $vv^*v = v$ and the vanishing squares, $\sigma v = (v^*v - vv^*)v = -vv^*v = -v$ and $v\sigma = v(v^*v - vv^*) = vv^*v = +v$. Since $\sigma^2 = 1$, $e^{-\lambda\sigma} = \cosh\lambda - \sigma\sinh\lambda$ (\claimref{std-algebra.bivector-exponential}), and the second relation collapses it on the left factor: $v\,e^{-\lambda\sigma} = v(\cosh\lambda - \sinh\lambda) = e^{-\lambda}v$. The $v^*$ computation is the mirror image, with both signs reversed. (3) $\tfrac12(1 + \sigma) = \tfrac12(1 + v^*v - vv^*) = \tfrac12(v^*v + vv^* + v^*v - vv^*) = v^*v$, and likewise for the complement. (4) In the two-dimensional Fock module ($v^* = $ creation, $v = $ annihilation, $N = v^*v$): $\tfrac12\sigma = \tfrac12(v^*v - vv^*) = \tfrac12(N - (1 - N)) = N - \tfrac12$. t07-regenerated.title: The boundary-mode algebra, windows, and the boost dynamics
t07-regenerated.text: Fix a countable mode set $J$ with Schwarzschild frequencies $\omega_j > 0$ ($j \in J$), the frequencies the geometry assigns to the boundary modes (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-modular-descent-premises-geometric-normalisation}). \emph{Provenance of $J$:} the boundary modes are the ladder pairs of the blown-up singular boundary, one per point, aggregated over the s-wave channels into the countable array of Theorem \claimref{singularity.bosonisation-bridge-s-wave-sector}, an identification the singularity paper makes and flags. By convention here (it is in neither the singularity paper nor the thermality paper, and reconciles the array's weights $\kappa k$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, with $\omega_j > 0$), the modes below the level enter $J$ through their particle-hole conjugates, so that every frequency is positive, and the one zero-frequency mode of the array lies outside $J$; the bookkeeping is filed alongside (synthesis.s-wave-array-is-a-boundary-mode-set). The tower of iterated completions is the algebra's model, not the source of its countability: its limit is the CAR algebra with the adjoined null pairs as modes (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-car-algebra}), while on the physical closure one ascent completes the description and further rungs lie on shadow walls outside the physical region (Corollary \claimref{tower.answers-iteration-question}). The \emph{boundary-mode algebra} $\mathfrak{A}$ is the CAR algebra over $\ell^2(J)$ (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-car-algebra}), the C*-inductive limit of the \emph{window algebras} $\mathfrak{A}_F$, $F \subset J$ finite, each $\mathfrak{A}_F \cong \End(\Lambda^\bullet \C^F)$ of dimension $4^{|F|}$. The \emph{boost dynamics} is the one-parameter group $\tau_t$ acting on generators by $\tau_t(a_j) = e^{-i\omega_j t}\,a_j$, with $t$ Schwarzschild time: the quasi-free flow whose one-particle Hamiltonian is $h = \mathrm{diag}(\omega_j)$; it preserves every window. In rapidity $\lambda = \kappa t$ the same flow has boost weights $\omega_j/\kappa$ and modular temperature $2\pi$ (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-modular-descent-premises-geometric-normalisation}); in Schwarzschild time the inverse temperature is $\beta = 1/\TH = 2\pi/\kappa$, and this normalisation is used throughout.

t07-regenerated.title: Gibbs states are KMS, and conversely, in finite dimensions
t07-regenerated.text:
Let $\mathfrak{B} = \End(\C^m)$, let $H$ be diagonal in the basis $(\xi_a)$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_a$, all distinct or not, let $\alpha_t = \mathrm{Ad}(e^{itH})$, and $\beta \in \R$. Then the Gibbs state $\omega_G(x) := \tr(e^{-\beta H}x)/\tr(e^{-\beta H})$ satisfies the KMS identity
\[
\omega_G(x\,y) \;=\; \omega_G\bigl(y\,\alpha_{i\beta}(x)\bigr), \qquad \alpha_{i\beta}(x) := e^{-\beta H}x\,e^{\beta H},
\]
for all $x, y$; and it is the \emph{unique} $\alpha$-KMS state at $\beta$ on $\mathfrak{B}$, degenerate spectrum included.
t07-regenerated.proof:
The identity is cyclicity of the trace:
\[
\omega_G\bigl(y\,\alpha_{i\beta}(x)\bigr) = \tr\bigl(e^{-\beta H}y\,e^{-\beta H}x\,e^{\beta H}\bigr)/Z = \tr\bigl(e^{-\beta H}xy\bigr)/Z = \omega_G(xy),
\]
the trailing $e^{\beta H}$ moved around the trace to cancel the inner factor. Conversely write $\omega(x) = \tr(\rho x)$ and evaluate the KMS identity on matrix units $x = E_{ab}$, $y = E_{cd}$: since $\alpha_{i\beta}(E_{ab}) = e^{-\beta(\lambda_a - \lambda_b)}E_{ab}$ and $\tr(\rho\,E_{ab}E_{cd}) = \delta_{bc}\,\rho_{da}$, the identity reads
\[
\delta_{bc}\,\rho_{da} \;=\; e^{-\beta(\lambda_a - \lambda_b)}\,\delta_{da}\,\rho_{bc}
\qquad \text{for all } a, b, c, d.
\]
Taking $c = b$ and $d = a$ gives $\rho_{aa} = e^{-\beta(\lambda_a - \lambda_b)}\rho_{bb}$: Gibbs ratios between all diagonal entries. Taking $c = b$ and $d \neq a$ gives $\rho_{da} = 0$ (the right side carries $\delta_{da} = 0$), for every pair $d \neq a$, degenerate eigenvalues included: $\rho$ is diagonal. So $\rho = e^{-\beta H}/Z$, and the KMS state is unique. The verification script performs the solve symbolically for the mode algebra $\Mat_2$ with $H = \omega N$ and confirms both clauses as identities of rational functions in the Boltzmann factor.
t07-regenerated.label: Lemma

t07-regenerated.text: If $\omega$ is $\alpha$-KMS at $\beta$ on $\mathfrak{B}$ and $\mathfrak{C} \subseteq \mathfrak{B}$ is a unital subalgebra with $\alpha_t(\mathfrak{C}) = \mathfrak{C}$, then $\omega|_{\mathfrak{C}}$ is KMS at $\beta$ for $\alpha|_{\mathfrak{C}}$.

t07-regenerated.text: For every operator $A$ on $\ell^2(J)$ with $0 \le A \le 1$ (the \emph{symbol}) there is a unique gauge-invariant state $\omega_A$ on $\mathfrak{A}$ with two-point function $\omega_A(a^\dagger(f)\,a(g)) = \ip{g}{Af}$ and all higher truncated functions zero (Wick determinants). t07-regenerated.title: The I-state
t07-regenerated.text:
Consider the boundary-mode algebra with its boost dynamics (Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics}) at inverse temperature $\beta = 1/\TH = 2\pi/\kappa$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Existence, exactly on windows.)} The quasi-free state $\omega_I$ with the Fermi-Dirac symbol
\[
A_I \;=\; \bigl(1 + e^{\beta h}\bigr)^{-1}, \qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad n_j = \frac{1}{e^{\omega_j/\TH} + 1},
\]
restricts on every window to the Gibbs state of $H_F = \sum_{j \in F}\omega_j N_j$ and is KMS there, exactly (Lemma \claimref{hawking.gibbs-states-are-kms-conversely-finite}); it is the unique quasi-free extension of these window states, and it is $\tau$-KMS at $\beta$ on the full algebra by Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-kms-passes-inductive-limits}.
\item \emph{(Gauge invariance is forced.)} If a quasi-free state of $\mathfrak{A}$ is $\tau$-KMS at $\beta$, its pairing vanishes: the state is gauge-invariant automatically.
\item \emph{(The symbol is derived.)} Its symbol then satisfies the operator identity $A(1 + e^{-\beta h}) = e^{-\beta h}$, equivalently $A = e^{-\beta h}(1 - A)$, whence $A = A_I$: within the quasi-free class, the state whose modular clock is the geometry's clock is unique, and its two-point data are forced.
\end{enumerate}
t07-regenerated.proof:
(1) On a window $F$, the quasi-free state with diagonal symbol is the product state of Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-algebra} with $n_j = (1 + e^{\beta\omega_j})^{-1}$, which is exactly the Gibbs density matrix of $H_F$: $e^{-\beta H_F} = \bigotimes_j \mathrm{diag}(1, e^{-\beta\omega_j})$, normalised; the script builds the two sides independently and confirms the identity in exact arithmetic. Lemma \claimref{hawking.gibbs-states-are-kms-conversely-finite} gives the KMS identity on the window, exactly; the script verifies it on a three-mode window at rational Boltzmann factors, on a spanning set of pairs. The windows are nested with dense union and the dynamics preserves each, so Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-kms-passes-inductive-limits} passes the KMS property to $\mathfrak{A}$.
(2) Apply the KMS identity to the pair $x = a^\dagger(f)$, $y = a^\dagger(g)$, with $f, g$ supported in windows (so that $\alpha_{i\beta}(a^\dagger(f)) = a^\dagger(e^{-\beta h}f)$ is again a generator):
\[
P(f, g) \;=\; \omega\bigl(a^\dagger(f)\,a^\dagger(g)\bigr) \;=\; \omega\bigl(a^\dagger(g)\,a^\dagger(e^{-\beta h}f)\bigr) \;=\; P(g,\, e^{-\beta h}f).
\]
Antisymmetry of creation operators gives $P(f, g) = -P(g, f)$, so $P(g, (1 + e^{-\beta h})f) = 0$ for all $f, g$ in the dense span of the windows; $1 + e^{-\beta h}$ is bounded with bounded inverse and preserves that span, so $P = 0$.
(3) Apply the KMS identity to the pair $x = a^\dagger(f)$, $y = a(g)$:
\[
\omega\bigl(a^\dagger(f)\,a(g)\bigr) \;=\; \omega\bigl(a(g)\,a^\dagger(e^{-\beta h}f)\bigr)
\;=\; \ip{g}{e^{-\beta h}f} - \omega\bigl(a^\dagger(e^{-\beta h}f)\,a(g)\bigr),
\]
using the CAR $\{a(g), a^\dagger(f')\} = \ip{g}{f'}$. In symbols: $\ip{g}{Af} = \ip{g}{e^{-\beta h}f} - \ip{g}{Ae^{-\beta h}f}$ for all $f, g$ supported in windows, i.e.\ $A(1 + e^{-\beta h}) = e^{-\beta h}$ on the dense span, i.e.\ $A = e^{-\beta h}(1+e^{-\beta h})^{-1} = (1 + e^{\beta h})^{-1} = A_I$ (all four operators bounded, $h \ge 0$ here). By (2) and Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-algebra}, the state is determined by its two-point data, which are forced, so $\omega = \omega_I$. The mode-diagonal scalar identity $n = e^{-\beta\omega}(1-n)$, equivalently the detailed balance $n/(1-n) = e^{-\beta\omega}$, is checked by the script as an exact identity of rational functions.
t07-regenerated.label: Theorem

Lemma 3.1 gives the KMS identity on the window, exactly; the script verifies it on a three-mode window at rational Boltzmann factors, on a spanning set of pairs. The windows are nested with dense union and the dynamics preserves each, so Fact 3.4 passes the KMS property to $\mathfrak{A}$.
(2) Apply the KMS identity to the pair $x = a^\dagger(f)$, $y = a^\dagger(g)$, with $f, g$ supported in windows (so that $\alpha_{i\beta}(a^\dagger(f)) = a^\dagger(e^{-\beta h}f)$ is again a generator):
\[
P(f, g) \;=\; \omega\bigl(a^\dagger(f)\,a^\dagger(g)\bigr) \;=\; \omega\bigl(a^\dagger(g)\,a^\dagger(e^{-\beta h}f)\bigr) \;=\; P(g,\, e^{-\beta h}f).
\]
Antisymmetry of creation operators gives $P(f, g) = -P(g, f)$, so $P(g, (1 + e^{-\beta h})f) = 0$ for all $f, g$ in the dense span of the windows; $1 + e^{-\beta h}$ is bounded with bounded inverse and preserves that span, so $P = 0$.
(3) Apply the KMS identity to the pair $x = a^\dagger(f)$, $y = a(g)$:
\[
\omega\bigl(a^\dagger(f)\,a(g)\bigr) \;=\; \omega\bigl(a(g)\,a^\dagger(e^{-\beta h}f)\bigr)
\;=\; \ip{g}{e^{-\beta h}f} - \omega\bigl(a^\dagger(e^{-\beta h}f)\,a(g)\bigr),
\]

By (2) and Fact 3.3, the state is determined by its two-point data, which are forced, so $\omega = \omega_I$. The mode-diagonal scalar identity $n = e^{-\beta\omega}(1-n)$, equivalently the detailed balance $n/(1-n) = e^{-\beta\omega}$, is checked by the script as an exact identity of rational functions.

t07-regenerated.title: The current commutator, exactly, with its edge split
t07-regenerated.text:
In the finite window, exactly and as an operator identity,
\[
[\,a_m,\, a_m^\dagger\,] \;=\; B_m - T_m, \qquad
B_m := \sum_{k=1}^{m} N_k, \qquad T_m := \sum_{k=L-m+1}^{L} N_k ,
\]
with $N_k = \psi_k^\dagger\psi_k$: the deviation from the infinite-volume central value is a difference of \emph{edge operators}, supported on the lowest and highest $m$ modes. Consequently, for $2m \le L$, on every state in which the bottom $m$ levels are filled and the top $m$ levels are empty (an \emph{edge-clean} state), $[a_m, a_m^\dagger]$ acts as the scalar $m$: the free-boson relation holds exactly, not asymptotically, on the edge-clean subspace. Moreover $[a_m, a_{m'}] = 0$ for all $m, m'$, exactly; and for $m \neq m'$ the cross commutator $[a_m, a_{m'}^\dagger]$ is a difference of bilinears supported on the lowest and highest $\max(m, m')$ modes, which annihilates every state that is edge-clean at depth $\max(m, m')$.
t07-regenerated.proof:
The fermionic bilinear commutator is $[\psi_a^\dagger\psi_b,\ \psi_c^\dagger\psi_d] = \delta_{bc}\,\psi_a^\dagger\psi_d - \delta_{ad}\,\psi_c^\dagger\psi_b$, an instance of the CAR (\claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car}). With $a_m^\dagger = \sum_{l=1}^{L-m}\psi_{l+m}^\dagger\psi_l$:
\[
[a_m, a_m^\dagger] = \sum_{k,l=1}^{L-m}\bigl(\delta_{k+m,\,l+m}\,\psi_k^\dagger\psi_l - \delta_{k l}\,\psi_{l+m}^\dagger\psi_{k+m}\bigr)
= \sum_{k=1}^{L-m} N_k - \sum_{k=m+1}^{L} N_k ,
\]
after shifting the index of the second sum. The shared middle range cancels pairwise: for $2m \le L$ the terms $k = m{+}1, \dots, L{-}m$ appear in both sums and cancel, leaving $B_m - T_m$; for $2m > L$ the two sums instead share the empty middle and the overlap $k = L{-}m{+}1, \dots, m$ of $B_m$ and $T_m$ cancels on the right-hand side, so the identity $\sum_{1}^{L-m} N_k - \sum_{m+1}^{L} N_k = B_m - T_m$ holds in both regimes. On an edge-clean state (which requires $2m \le L$ to be non-vacuous), $B_m$ acts as $m$ (each bottom mode occupied) and $T_m$ as $0$. For the cross commutators, the same computation gives
\[
[a_m, a_{m'}] = \sum_{k}\psi_k^\dagger\psi_{k+m+m'} - \sum_{k}\psi_k^\dagger\psi_{k+m+m'} = 0
\]
exactly, both surviving sums running over the same range $1 \le k \le L - m - m'$; and, for $m > m'$,
\[
[a_m, a_{m'}^\dagger] = \sum_{k=1}^{m'}\psi_k^\dagger\psi_{k+m-m'} \;-\; \sum_{k=L-m+1}^{L-m+m'}\psi_k^\dagger\psi_{k+m-m'},
\]
every surviving index within $\max(m,m')$ of an edge. Each bottom term annihilates an edge-clean state because its target level $k$ is occupied; each top term because its source level $k + m - m'$ lies in the empty top band. The case $m < m'$ follows by taking adjoints, $[a_m, a_{m'}^\dagger] = [a_{m'}, a_m^\dagger]^\dagger$, with the same band support; it annihilates edge-clean states by the mirrored argument (creation onto an occupied bottom level, lowering of an empty top level). t07-regenerated.title: Successor problems
t07-regenerated.text:
Six problems for the series' list of open directions.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{State selection from geometry.} Formulate the geometric-modular-action axiom for a net of boundary-mode algebras over the horizon and derive the boost dynamics, the temperature entering through the net's geometric normalisation rather than as an algebra-intrinsic quantity, which T5's rate-rigidity theorem shows it cannot be \cite[Thm.~7.16]{ButlerT5}. Proposition \claimref{hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair}(5) fixes the single-atom orbits, and T5's factor-level analysis (its condition (G), rejected as over-determining) records what is already established.
\item \emph{The lift beyond assembly.} Derive joint J3, the partial-wave identification, from the emergent transverse geometry (the fuzzy sphere of the counting programme), converting the helicity lift (Assembly \claimref{hawking.helicity-lift-joints-itemised}) from assembly to theorem; shared with the entropy paper T8 \cite{ButlerT8} and the action paper T10 \cite{ButlerT10}.
\item \emph{The Kerr continuum.} Superradiant channels make the rotating analogue of Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state-continuum} genuinely different (no global KMS state at fixed angular velocity for all modes); formulate the correct rotating statement.
\item \emph{The $\ell_P^2/A$ correction, per observable.} Refine Remark \claimref{note.hawking.p-2-correction-interpreted} into a table of leading finite-$L$ corrections for named observables (spectrum distortion, correlator deficits), with the $\ell_P^2/A$ scaling proved rather than dimensional.
\item \emph{The cosmological state.} Connect the equilibrium I-state to the non-equilibrium state of the descent.
\item \emph{Helicity counting per boundary mode.} Decide whether one boundary mode of the near-horizon theory carries one helicity channel of the lift or both helicities of a massless species. The two answers differ downstream by a factor of two in the capacity per boundary mode ($\ln 2$ against $2\ln 2$) and so in the entropy paper's calibration residue, $\kappa_c = 1/(4\ln 2)$ against $1/(8\ln 2)$ \cite[Prop.~4.12]{ButlerT8}. In this paper the question sits at joint J3 of Assembly \claimref{hawking.helicity-lift-joints-itemised}, the partial-wave identification of each $(\omega, \ell, m, s)$ channel with a two-dimensional mode, which is modelling; joints J1 and J2 place the two helicities at distinct homogeneities but do not say how many channels one boundary mode registers. T8 takes the one-helicity reading, at the tier of that joint; settling it is part of converting J3 to a theorem (problem 2).
\end{enumerate}

t07-regenerated.title: Position in the series
t07-regenerated.text:
This paper is T7 of the series. \emph{It relies on six predecessors:} the primer T0 \cite{ButlerT0} and the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1} for the completed-pair language and the transport principle; the tower paper T3 \cite{ButlerT3} for the CAR limit that makes the boundary modes an algebra (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-car-algebra}); the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} for modular descent under its premises (P) and (R), the bosonisation bridge under (Q), and the surface gravity $\kappa = 1/4M$ (Facts \claimref{hawking.imported-modular-descent-premises-geometric-normalisation} and \claimref{hawking.imported-s-wave-bosonic-sector}); the interior paper T6 \cite{ButlerT6} for the exterior exactness that greybody inheritance rests on (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-exterior-exactly-general-relativity}); and the twistor paper T9 \cite{ButlerT9} for the ordering shift from which Proposition \claimref{hawking.homogeneity-ordering-shift} is promoted.

\emph{Papers that rely on this one:} the entropy paper T8 \cite{ButlerT8} imports the single-mode modular structure, the quasi-free calculus, and the finite-window identities; the action paper T10 \cite{ButlerT10} imports the finite-window quantification of the current algebra; the standard-model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} imports the helicity identification of Proposition \claimref{hawking.homogeneity-ordering-shift}; and the capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17} tabulates this paper's claims at their tiers.

t07-regenerated.title: Machine verification
t07-regenerated.text:
The computational identities asserted in this paper are verified by the script deposited with it, \texttt{verify\_T07.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT7}. The script imports the series' shared exact-arithmetic library \texttt{GA.py}, runs entirely in exact arithmetic (rational numbers and rational functions in a formal Boltzmann variable, no floating point anywhere), and so certifies each check as an identity, or as an exactly evaluated inequality, rather than an approximation. Twenty-five checks pass. Not scripted, and stated as such where they occur: the imported Facts, certified by their source papers' scripts or by the literature; the continuum passage beyond its window content; the assembly joints of the section ``The four-dimensional lift''; the classical Penrose transform; and the geometric inputs $\kappa = 1/4M$ and $\TH = \kappa/2\pi$, proved and scripted in T5.

The coverage, section by section.

\begin{description}
\item[the section ``Setting and imports'', the single mode (Proposition \claimref{hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair}).] All five clauses in the basis-blade arithmetic over $\Cl(1,1)$: the null pair's squares and anticommutator, $\sigma = e_0e_1$ with $\sigma^2 = 1$, the one-sided weight relations, the finite conjugation at the rational rotor $R = \tfrac53 + \tfrac43\,\sigma$ (that is, $\cosh(\lambda/2) = \tfrac53$) with scale factors $\tfrac19$ and $9$, the projector identities, and the one-dimensionality of the bivector space; plus the Fock identity $\tfrac12\sigma = N - \tfrac12$.
\item[the section ``The state input: the I-state'', the state (Lemma \claimref{hawking.gibbs-states-are-kms-conversely-finite}, Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state}).] The Gibbs KMS identity on all sixteen matrix-unit pairs of the mode algebra, as identities of rational functions in the formal Boltzmann factor; the uniqueness solve, performed symbolically, the KMS constraints on an arbitrary density matrix having a one-dimensional kernel spanned by the Gibbs matrix. Then the symbol itself: the Fermi-Dirac detailed-balance identity $n/(1-n) = e^{-\beta\omega}$; the Fermi-Dirac product state on a three-mode window confirmed equal to the Gibbs matrix of $H_F$, the two sides built independently, then confirmed KMS on all $4096$ matrix-unit pairs; and, on a two-mode window, the full KMS constraint system solved for an arbitrary density matrix against independently supplied dynamics, with one-dimensional kernel, vanishing pairing, and the Fermi-Dirac symbol.
\item[the section ``The mode continuum'', the continuum.] No separately computable identity: its exact content is the window case, scripted under Section 3, and its remaining steps are the imported calculus of Facts \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-kms-reduces-two} and \claimref{hawking.imported-ideal-fermi-gas-uniqueness}, certified by their sources.
\item[the section ``The four-dimensional lift'', the lift (Proposition \claimref{hawking.homogeneity-ordering-shift}).] The operator identity $q(\id) = -\hbar(\Upsilon + 2)$ on all twistor monomials of degree at most three, and the homogeneity table $-2s-2 \mapsto (-4, 0, -6, +2)$ at $s = \pm 1, \pm 2$.
\item[the section ``The finite boundary mode space, and the $\ell_P^2/A$ correction'', the finite window (Propositions \claimref{hawking.current-commutator-exactly-edge-split} and \claimref{hawking.bose-einstein-occupancy-quantified-window-corrections}).] The edge identity $[a_m, a_m^\dagger] = B_m - T_m$ as an operator identity on all $256$ states of an eight-mode window for $m = 1, 2, 3$; the exact free-boson relation on every edge-clean state; the exact vanishing of $[a_m, a_{m'}]$ and the vanishing of the cross commutator on edge-clean states. Then the ladder: the detailed-balance identity of Proposition \claimref{hawking.bose-einstein-occupancy-quantified-window-corrections}(1) in the formal $x^{-k}$ at three values of $x^{-m}$, with the Bose-Einstein form $\bar n/(1 + \bar n) = e^{-\beta\omega}$ of the clause-(2) occupancy, at $\omega = \epsilon m$ on the ladder; the window sums' approach to the exact Planck factor from below, within the proven tail bound, as exact rational inequalities at two temperatures and three $m$; and the Wick formula checked against the direct density-matrix expectation on the full $256$-state window, the ladder in the paper's occupancy convention.
\end{description}

The script exits nonzero on any failure and prints one line per check, tagged by the statement it certifies.

t07-regenerated.title: The Clifford side of the ordering shift
t07-regenerated.text:
Let $(v, v^*)$ be a null pair of $V$ with $\ip{v}{v^*} = 1$ (an adjoined ladder pair), and let $E := v\wedge v^* \in \mathfrak{so}(2,4)$ be the grading element of the corresponding hyperbolic plane. In the Fock model, the spinor action of $E$ is
\[
\rho(E) \;=\; \tfrac12\,c(v)\,c(v^*) - \tfrac12 \;=\; N - \tfrac12 ,
\]
where $N$ is the occupation number operator of the mode created by $v$ (eigenvalue $1$ on states containing that mode, $0$ otherwise). The generator of the adjoined plane's boost is the mode's number operator shifted by one half.

t07-regenerated.title: The Fock model of the complexified ascended algebra
t07-regenerated.text:
Let $W \subset V_\C$ be a maximal totally isotropic subspace ($\dim_\C W = 3$) and $W'$ a complementary maximal isotropic subspace, dual to $W$ under the $\C$-bilinear form (such a pair exists, and any two such pairs are conjugate under $O(V_\C)$). On the exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet W$ ($\dim_\C = 2^3 = 8$) define
\[
c(w) := \sqrt2\; w \wedge (\cdot) \quad (w \in W),
\qquad
c(w') := \sqrt2\; \iota_{w'} \quad (w' \in W'),
\]
with $\iota$ contraction through the pairing. Then $c(u)^2 = Q(u)\,\id$ for every $u \in W \oplus W' = V_\C$, so $c$ extends to an algebra map $\Cl(V_\C) \to \End(\Lambda^\bullet W)$; this map is an isomorphism, and $\Lambda^\bullet W$ is the unique irreducible module of $\Cl(2,4)_\C$: the Dirac spinors of the completion. Vectors act oddly, so the even and odd halves
\[
\CS := \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}} W, \qquad \CSm := \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}} W,
\]
each of complex dimension 4, are modules of the even subalgebra $\Cl^0(2,4)_\C \cong \End(\CS) \oplus \End(\CSm)$: the two chiralities, the conformal spinor space $\CS$ and its opposite $\CSm$ (twistor and dual twistor space).

t07-regenerated.title: The bosonisation bridge, s-wave sector
t07-regenerated.text:
Let $\{\psi_k, \psi^\dagger_k\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be the boundary modes, as fermion operators on the filled-sea Fock space (the infinite filled-sea array whose algebraic model is the completed tower limit of \cite[Thm.~5.6]{ButlerT3}, cited for the structure; its provenance here is the s-wave aggregation declared above, not a tower, the mod-8 clock having stopped after one ascent), and define the currents $a_m := \sum_k :\psi^\dagger_k\,\psi_{k+m}:$ with $:\;:$ normal ordering at the sea level; with the sea filled below the level, $a_m$ annihilates the sea for $m > 0$ and $a_{-m} = a_m^{\dagger}$ creates particle-hole pairs. (The opposite index convention flips the sign of the central term; the verification script fixes the convention by computation.) Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Current algebra.) $[a_m, a_n] = m\,\delta_{m+n,0}\,\id$ on the infinite array; on a finite window the commutator equals $m\,\delta_{m+n,0}\,\id$ plus an \emph{exactly identified} edge operator ($B_m - T_m - m$ in the proof's notation), supported on the bottom and top $m$ sites and vanishing on all bulk states: the number-conserving bilinears satisfy the canonical commutation relations of a free boson. A boson is a pair of the pair.
\item (KMS restriction.) Each bilinear $\psi^\dagger_k\psi_{k+m}$ carries a definite boost weight, fixed by the difference $\omega_{k+m} - \omega_k$ of its two modes' weights. Under (Q)'s weight clause, $\omega_k = \kappa k$, that difference is $\kappa m$ for every $k$, so each current $a_m$ is itself a weight vector and the current subalgebra is globally invariant under the modular flow of Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-structure-completed-pair}; for weights that are not affine in $k$ the summands of $a_m$ rotate at different rates and the span of the currents need not be invariant, so this invariance uses (Q). Under (Q) the joint state is KMS for that flow, and a KMS state restricted to a flow-invariant subalgebra is KMS at the same temperature for the restricted flow. Without (Q) no joint KMS state is available: (R) is imposed on the marginals alone, and Theorem \claimref{singularity.exact-equilibrium-over-determines-boundary-modes} is the reason its joint form is rejected elsewhere in the chain.
\item (The Planck factor.) Under (Q), with the marginal occupancies $n_k = (e^{\beta\omega_k} + 1)^{-1} = (e^{\beta\kappa k} + 1)^{-1}$ at the premise's linear weights, the current occupancy is, exactly,
\[
\langle a_{-m} a_m \rangle \;=\; \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} n_{k+m}\,(1 - n_k) \;=\; \frac{m}{e^{\beta\kappa m} - 1} \qquad (m > 0) ,
\]
with no vacuum piece in this convention ($a_m$ annihilates the sea): Bose-Einstein occupancy at exactly $\TH$. The Planck spectrum of the bosonic Hawking flux is derived, not conjectured, for the s-wave sector, in the equilibrium reading (Q) fixes; for a general member of the chain's state class the left side acquires the connected correlators (Q) sets to zero, and no exact spectrum is claimed.
\end{enumerate}
The single assembly-level ingredient in the section is the charge-zero Fock isomorphism (the charge-zero sector of the fermionic Fock space is canonically the bosonic Fock space, with fermions recovered as vertex operators), cited to \cite{PressleySegal1986} and used only for the completeness statement that the two descriptions are one algebra; parts (1)-(3) are proved outright.

t07-regenerated.title: $\kappa = 1/4M$, computed
t07-regenerated.text:
For the Schwarzschild gravitational field of the section ``The metric of the gauge field, and its static form'' (the stored field $\hb = 1 - \beta P$ on flat spacetime, Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), the static Killing field $K = \hb^{-1}(e_t)$ has $Q(K) = f = 1 - 2M/r$, and the static observers, of velocity $v = K/\sqrt f$, have redshifted proper acceleration $\sqrt f\,\sqrt{-Q((v \cdot D)v)} = f'(r)/2$ at every $r > 2M$, so the surface gravity of the horizon locus $r = 2M$ is
\[
\kappa \;=\; \lim_{r \to 2M} \frac{f'(r)}{2} \;=\; \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{2M}{(2M)^2} \;=\; \frac{1}{4M} .
\]

t07-regenerated.title: The descended form is state independent
t07-regenerated.text:
Let $\varrho$ be the density matrix of \emph{any} state on the boundary mode space, and $\varrho_k$ its marginal at mode $k$. Then $E_k(\varrho_k)$ is diagonal in that mode's number basis, and therefore
\[
E_k(\varrho_k) \;=\; \frac{e^{-\beta_k \omega_k N_k}}{Z_k}
\]
for a unique $\beta_k \in [-\infty, +\infty]$, determined by $\beta_k\omega_k = \log\bigl(p_k/(1-p_k)\bigr)$ with $p_k$ the descended vacancy probability. (Stated for $\omega_k \neq 0$: at a zero-weight mode the right side is $\tfrac12\,\mathrm{id}$ for every $\beta_k$, so uniqueness always fails there, and existence fails unless $p_k = \tfrac12$.) The descended single-mode state is a Gibbs state of the boost generator $K_k$ whatever the ascended state was: no hypothesis on the state is used.
t07-regenerated.provenance: Transport Lab claim singularity.descended-form-state-independent, version 4 (T05 Thm 7.6)

t07-regenerated.title: The Euclidean section, and its period
t07-regenerated.text:
Let $t_s = -i\tau$ in the static gauge of the Schwarzschild gravitational field on flat spacetime (the section ``The metric of the gauge field, and its static form''; Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}). The Wick-rotated field lives on the flat Euclidean background, and its derived metric is the Riemannian metric $f\,d\tau^{2} + f^{-1}dr^{2} + r^{2}d\Omega^{2}$ on $r > 2M$; let $\varrho(r) := \int_{2M}^{r} f^{-1/2}\,dr'$ be proper radial distance from the horizon locus. Then, with $F := \sqrt f$ regarded as a function of $\varrho$,
\[
f\,d\tau^{2} + f^{-1}dr^{2} \;=\; d\varrho^{2} + F(\varrho)^{2}\,d\tau^{2}, \qquad F(0) = 0, \qquad \frac{dF}{d\varrho}\Big|_{\varrho = 0} \;=\; \frac{f'(2M)}{2} \;=\; \kappa \;=\; \frac{1}{4M} ,
\]
so that near $\varrho = 0$ the $(\varrho, \tau)$ plane carries the metric $d\varrho^{2} + \kappa^{2}\varrho^{2}d\tau^{2} + O(\varrho^{4})\,d\tau^{2}$. If $\tau$ is periodic with period $p$, the section is a smooth Riemannian manifold at $\varrho = 0$ (the tip of the section, the two-sphere where the Euclidean Killing flow has its fixed points, the Euclidean counterpart of the bifurcation sphere) if and only if
\[
\kappa\,p \;=\; 2\pi, \qquad \text{i.e.} \qquad p \;=\; \frac{2\pi}{\kappa} \;=\; 8\pi M ;
\]
for any other period the origin of the $(\varrho, \tau)$ plane is a conical point of total angle $\kappa p$. The period of imaginary Killing time is therefore fixed by the gravitational field, at the horizon locus, and it is the conversion factor of Proposition \claimref{singularity.plane-rate} read in imaginary time. The regularity condition is local: it lives in a polar chart about the tip of the Wick-rotated flat background; the Lorentzian bifurcation surface itself lies beyond one flat chart and is not used.

t07-regenerated.label: Fact (imported)

t07-regenerated.title: The matching: Steps 4b and 4c join by equation
t07-regenerated.text:
Realise the hyperbolic atom of Lemma \claimref{singularity.pseudo-inverse-identities-hyperbolic-atom} on the radial plane, $e_0 = \hat e_t$, $e_1 = \hat e_r$. Where this realisation lies must be stated, because it is available exactly where the ascent is not needed: at every $r > 0$ the physical radial plane has signature $(1,1)$ and carries a CAR pair inside $\Cl(1,3)$ with no ascent at all, but at $r = 0$ the radial plane itself degenerates, its radical the dying direction $k$ (corank one in the forced weighting, Remark \claimref{note.singularity.corank-limit-weighted-answer} and Fact \claimref{sheaf.schwarzschild-degeneration-boundary-tame}(2); Proposition \claimref{singularity.degeneration-exactly}'s uniform rescaling degenerates the whole form), so no CAR pair supported on the radial plane survives there, even though the weighted module still contains hyperbolic planes (Fact \claimref{sheaf.schwarzschild-degeneration-boundary-tame}(2): $V_1$ carries $\mathrm{diag}(m^2, -1, -1)$). On $E$ the atom is carried by $\operatorname{span}(k, \nO/2\nu)$, one leg the dying direction itself and one adjoined (Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-one-sided-completion-singularity}, Remark \claimref{note.singularity.metric-level-parity-even-level}): the odd sector is not a pre-existing grading of $\Cl(1,3)$ precisely because one of its legs lies outside. Nor is the matching an identification of two coexisting copies, Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-one-sided-completion-singularity}'s pair existing exactly over $E$: the two constructions share the leg $k$. At every $r > 0$ the radial plane contains $k^{\sharp} = -\sqrt r\,\er$ (Proposition \claimref{singularity.transport-schwarzschild-fibre}(4)), the plane degenerates onto $\R k$ as $r \to 0$, and the completion re-attaches $\nO/2\nu$ to that same $k$. What is shared is the direction and the degeneration onto it, not a null leg of the atom: $k^{\sharp}$ is spacelike at every $r > 0$ while the atom's legs are null, and the $E$-atom's bivector $k \wedge \nO/2\nu$ is not $\sigma_r$. The identification of the modular bivector with the curvature-selected plane is therefore made at $r > 0$, where Theorem \claimref{singularity.curvature-gauge-field-exact-shape-decoupling} holds, and \emph{transported} to $E$ along the degeneration; that transport is the matching's residual step, stated as such rather than absorbed into the shared direction, and the two-level computations of Steps 4c through 6b concern the abstract atom, whichever realisation carries it. Then the modular bivector of Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-structure-completed-pair},
\[
\sigma \;=\; v^*v - vv^* \;=\; e_0 e_1 ,
\]
spans the radial plane and satisfies the pair of equations
\[
S(\sigma) = -2\,\sigma, \qquad \sigma^2 = +1 ,
\]
and this pair characterises $\sigma$ up to sign among the unit frame bivectors: the eigenvalue equation confines $\sigma$ to $\{\sigma_r, I\sigma_r\}$ (Theorem \claimref{singularity.curvature-gauge-field-exact-shape-decoupling}), and the square excludes the dual, for which $(I\sigma_r)^2 = -1$. The bivector that generates Step 4c's modular flow, the phase flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{it\sigma/2})$, whose real rotor flow is $\exp(\lambda\sigma/2)$, is therefore the same object Step 4b's curvature distinguishes, identified by equation rather than by name; the residual sign is the orientation of the boost, the labelling of outgoing against ingoing, which is exactly the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ that Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-structure-completed-pair}(2) attaches to the weights of $v$ and $v^*$. And by the localisation theorem \cite[Thm.~4.4, Cor.~4.5]{ButlerT4} the pair, hence the atom, hence $\sigma$, is at the degenerate radial direction, which is where Proposition \claimref{singularity.degeneration-exactly} located the division: the plane the curvature selects, the plane the completed pair lies in, and the plane through which division fails are one plane. One plane, not one locus: the curvature selects it at every $r > 0$, the calibration reads it at the horizon (Proposition \claimref{singularity.plane-rate}), the ladder inhabits it on $E$, and Proposition \claimref{singularity.why-calibration-cannot-be-internal} records that the calibration locus and the singular locus do not meet; what carries the identification across them is the frame-robustness of the plane (Remark \claimref{note.singularity.frame-made-explicit}) and the radius-independence of its selection, not a claim that the loci coincide.

t07-regenerated.title: Modular descent
t07-regenerated.text:

t08-regenerated.title: Scheme robustness of the cutoff
t08-regenerated.text: The stretched singularity is robust at order one against the choice of Planck criterion: the curvature-eigenvalue condition $2M/r^3 = 1$, the Kretschmann condition $48M^2/r^6 = 1$, and the unit-proper-time condition $\tau(r) = 1$ (with $\tau = \tfrac23 r^{3/2}(2M)^{-1/2}(1 + O(r/2M))$ the proper time to the singularity) all yield $r_c = c_0\,M^{1/3}\lP^{2/3}$ with order-one constants: $c_0 = 2^{1/3}$, $48^{1/6}$, and $(3/2)^{2/3}\,2^{1/3}$ respectively. The surface where the algebra requires completion is, at this order, unambiguous.
t08-regenerated.proof: Each condition is solved exactly for $r$. Curvature eigenvalue: $r^3 = 2M$, so $r_c = (2M)^{1/3} = 2^{1/3}M^{1/3}$. Kretschmann: $r^6 = 48M^2$, so $r_c = 48^{1/6}M^{1/3}$. Proper time: from the exact interior integral $\tau(r) = \int_0^r \sqrt{u/(2M - u)}\,du = \tfrac{2}{3}\,r^{3/2}(2M)^{-1/2}(1 + O(r/2M))$ (the leading term of the series proved in \cite[Lem.~5.1]{ButlerT6} (\claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior}), rescaled to $2M \neq 1$), setting $\tau = 1$ gives $r_c = (3/2)^{2/3}(2M)^{1/3}(1 + O(r_c/M))$. All three are $M^{1/3}$ times constants $2^{1/3} \approx 1.26$, $48^{1/6} \approx 1.91$, $(3/2)^{2/3}2^{1/3} \approx 1.65$: order one. The script checks the three exponent computations and the constants exactly (as exact powers of rationals).

t08-regenerated.title: The slice volume is exactly $8\pi M$ per unit Killing time, at leading order in $r_c/2M$
t08-regenerated.text:
For the Schwarzschild field in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand gauge field $\hb = 1 - \beta P$, $\beta = \sqrt{2M/r}$, of Fact \claimref{sheaf.gauge-field-cometric}, the induced geometry of the background slice $r = r_c$ inside the horizon, read from $\hb^{-1}$ on its tangent vectors ($Q(\hb^{-1}(e_t)) = -f$), is $ds_3^2 = f\,dt^2 + r_c^2\,d\Omega^2$ with $f = 2M/r_c - 1$, so the three-volume per unit Killing time $t$ is $4\pi r_c^2\sqrt{f}$. With the curvature cutoff $r_c = (2M)^{1/3}$ and to leading order in $r_c/2M$ (i.e.\ $f \approx 2M/r_c$),
\[
4\pi\,r_c^2\,\sqrt{2M/r_c} \;=\; 4\pi\,\sqrt{2M}\;r_c^{3/2} \;=\; 4\pi\,\sqrt{2M}\,\sqrt{2M} \;=\; 8\pi M
\]
\emph{exactly}: the cutoff radius combines with the anisotropic stretch of the $t$-direction to give an exactly linear dependence on the mass. A cutoff radius independent of $M$ would give $M^{1/2}$ instead.
t08-regenerated.proof:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity: the metric below is the derived metric of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), and the manifold is its invertible region.

Inside the horizon $r$ is timelike and $t$ spacelike; the static metric restricted to $r = r_c$ gives the displayed induced metric with $f = 2M/r_c - 1 > 0$. The volume element is $\sqrt{f}\,r_c^2\sin\theta\,dt\,d\theta\,d\varphi$; integrating the sphere gives $4\pi r_c^2\sqrt f$ per unit $t$. The display is the exponent identity $r_c^{3/2} = ((2M)^{1/3})^{3/2} = (2M)^{1/2}$, checked exactly by the script; the neglected factor is $\sqrt{1 - r_c/2M} = 1 + O(M^{-2/3})$, subleading at large $M$ and quantified as such.

t08-regenerated.title: Uniqueness of the internal scaling
t08-regenerated.text: Call a timescale \emph{admissible} when the Schwarzschild geometry supplies it without tuning: the light-crossing, causal-epoch, and modular scales, $\Delta t \propto M$ up to logarithmic dressings, and the evaporation lifetime, $\Delta t \propto M^3$. Write the count as $N \propto M^p\,\Delta t$ with $p$ determined by the cutoff scheme. Then $p = 1$, produced by the framework's own curvature cutoff, is the \emph{unique} power for which an admissible timescale of order $M$ delivers the area law $N \propto M^2$: a sphere-only count (cells of the $r_c$-sphere, no $t$-stretch) gives $4\pi r_c^2 \propto M^{2/3}$, hence $p = 2/3$ and $N \sim M^{5/3}$; a fixed (mass-independent) cutoff radius gives volume per unit time $\propto \sqrt{M}$, hence $p = 1/2$ and $N \sim M^{3/2}$; and no admissible infrared choice repairs either: matching $M^{p + q} = M^2$ with $p \in \{2/3, 1/2\}$ requires $q \in \{4/3, 3/2\}$, and no admissible timescale has those exponents (a logarithmic dressing changes no exponent). The scaling test could have failed and did not.
t08-regenerated.proof: The three exponent computations: (i) internal cutoff, Proposition \claimref{scrambling.slice-volume-exactly-per-unit-killing}: $p = 1$, and $q = 1$ (the causal epoch) gives $N \propto M^2$, the area law, with the exact coefficient handled by Proposition \claimref{scrambling.area-law-test}. (ii) Sphere-only: $4\pi r_c^2 = 4\pi(2M)^{2/3}$, so $p = 2/3$. (iii) Fixed radius $r_0$: volume per unit time $4\pi r_0^2\sqrt{2M/r_0} \propto M^{1/2}$, so $p = 1/2$. The matching arithmetic is displayed; the admissible set is the statement's hypothesis, its exponents are $1$ and $3$, and neither $4/3$ nor $3/2$ is among them, a logarithmic dressing changing no exponent. The script checks all exponent arithmetic exactly as rational-exponent identities.

t08-regenerated.title: The density factor $\nu$, stated in full
t08-regenerated.text:
Two normalisations enter $
u$, and their statuses differ. The corank is settled: under the weights the geometry forces, the anisotropic Schwarzschild singularity carries exactly one ladder pair per point of the blown-up singular locus \cite[\S 8.9]{ButlerT4}, the resolution T5 records in passing the count to this paper \cite[\S 10]{ButlerT5}. What remains open is the \emph{cell calibration}: how many Planck cells of slice volume one localised pair accounts for, the conversion from per-point to per-cell. The weighted completion supplies the geometry at the exceptional set on which that conversion is to be read (Fact \claimref{tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity}), and its analysis is closed at Schwarzschild, so no analytic step of the geometry programme stands between it and $
u$; what blocks the calibration is one dimensionless number, the residue $\kappa_c$ of the section ``The calibration factorised, and the quarter examined'', and deriving it is this paper's task, carried as its first successor problem (the section ``Scope, and successor problems''). The $M$-scaling of Theorem \claimref{scrambling.mode-count} is independent of it, the coefficient is not, and the section ``The epoch is the modular period'' converts the requirement into that single number. Separately, the per-mode entropy normalisation is $\ln 2$ for a maximally mixed fermionic mode: T5 compares the capacity $C = N\ln 2$, not the bare count, with $\SBH$, so the area-law condition of Proposition \claimref{scrambling.area-law-test} reads $
u\Delta t = M/2$ in the 1-nat convention used here and $
u\Delta t = M/(2\ln 2)$ in T5's capacity convention, a factor of $\ln 2$ (31 per cent) that is stated rather than absorbed into an approximation sign.

t08-regenerated.title: The clock inventory of the boundary modes
t08-regenerated.proof: (i) is the algebra's own inventory: a one-parameter group of inner automorphisms of a Clifford algebra preserving the vector grade is generated by an even element whose commutator preserves grade one, i.e.\ by a bivector (the commutator of a vector with a grade-$2k$ element has grade $2k - 1$, so only $k = 1$ preserves the vector space; a mixed even generator $A_2 + A_4 + \cdots$ reduces to its bivector part, since grade preservation forces $[A_{2k}, v] = 0$ for every vector $v$ when $k \geq 2$, making each higher $A_{2k}$ central, and an even central element is a scalar; scalars generate nothing). The single-pair clause of (ii) is the import, proved in \cite[Prop.~2.1]{ButlerT7} (\claimref{hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair}), unique up to reparametrisation and orientation: the algebra fixes the orbits, not the speed, and the geometric normalisation of \cite[App.~A]{ButlerT5} is what fixes the speed, converting rapidity, and only rapidity, to Schwarzschild time at $\kappa = 1/4M$, so a rescaled generator traverses the same orbits and defines the same clock, not a faster one. For (iii): the flow a bivector $X$ generates acts on the mode operators by $\operatorname{ad}_X$, which is insensitive to a central shift ($\operatorname{ad}_{E_{ii}} = \operatorname{ad}_{E_{ii} - 1/2}$), so it is the adjoint spectrum and not the one-particle spectrum that the classification must read. From the canonical anticommutation relations of the mode operators (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix}), $[E_{ij}, \psi_k^\dagger] = \delta_{jk}\psi_i^\dagger$ and $[E_{ij}, \psi_k] = -\delta_{ik}\psi_j$. Hence $\operatorname{ad}_{E_{ii}}$ has eigenvalues $\pm 1$ on $(\psi_i^\dagger, \psi_i)$ and $0$ elsewhere, and the atom's boost bivector $\sigma_i = 2(\hat n_i - \tfrac12)$ (Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-modes-modular-inventory}) generates that same flow in the rotor convention $e^{\sigma_i t/2}(\cdot)\,e^{-\sigma_i t/2}$: unit rapidity. The equal-coefficient sum $\sum_i E_{ii}$ gives $\pm 1$ on every mode, the simultaneous boost of all $n$ atoms and the statement's common clock; what is compact here is the phase circle $e^{i\theta \hat n}$, whose generator is $i$ times a bivector, which the real Clifford algebra of the boundary modes excludes, its centre being scalar, so the phase circle is not an intrinsic flow in the sense of (i); the single-atom instance of the exclusion is published as \cite[Prop.~7.21(3)]{ButlerT5} (\claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies}). For $i \neq j$, $\operatorname{ad}_{E_{ij} + E_{ji}}$ has eigenvectors $\psi_i^\dagger \pm \psi_j^\dagger$ with eigenvalues $\pm 1$, and $E_{ij} + E_{ji} = \hat n_+ - \hat n_-$ exactly in the rotated modes $(\psi_i \pm \psi_j)/\sqrt{2}$: again unit rapidity. The antisymmetric $E_{ij} - E_{ji}$ has adjoint eigenvalues $\pm i$ and is compact; the single $E_{ij}$ with $i \neq j$ is nilpotent, generating a unipotent shear; neither carries a rapidity. A diagonal $\sum_i c_i E_{ii}$ has adjoint eigenvalues $\pm c_i$, so unequal $|c_i|$ leave no common rapidity and admit no single conversion. The pairing sector is classified by one product: from the CAR, $\operatorname{ad}$ of $c\,\psi_i^\dagger\psi_j^\dagger + d\,\psi_j\psi_i$ maps $\psi_i^\dagger \mapsto d\,\psi_j$, $\psi_j \mapsto c\,\psi_i^\dagger$, $\psi_j^\dagger \mapsto -d\,\psi_i$, $\psi_i \mapsto -c\,\psi_j^\dagger$, two $2 \times 2$ blocks each with eigenvalues $\pm\sqrt{cd}$: hyperbolic for $cd > 0$, where unequal coefficients rescale the common rapidity rather than remove it ($2\psi_i^\dagger\psi_j^\dagger + \tfrac12\psi_j\psi_i$ is a clock at unit rapidity outright); compact for $cd < 0$, eigenvalues $\pm i\sqrt{|cd|}$; nilpotent for $cd = 0$. Every clock in the inventory is therefore hyperbolic with unit rapidity after normalisation, hence by the Witt-extension clause of (iii), in the split space of the $n$ hyperbolic pairs of \claimref{tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity}, $O(n,n)$-conjugate to a sum of standard atom boosts, and the geometric normalisation converts them all at the one $\kappa$. What is unique is the rate, not the flow. Normalisation sets the nonzero adjoint eigenvalues to $\pm 1$, so the continuation of any clock to imaginary rapidity acts on the mode operators by $e^{\pm i\theta}$ and has conjugation period exactly $2\pi$, the atom's period of Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-modes-modular-inventory} (\cite[Prop.~7.21(1)]{ButlerT5}); at the geometric rate $\kappa$ that period is the Schwarzschild span $2\pi/\kappa = \beta$.

The pairing sector is classified by one product: from the CAR, $\operatorname{ad}$ of $c\,\psi_i^\dagger\psi_j^\dagger + d\,\psi_j\psi_i$ maps $\psi_i^\dagger \mapsto d\,\psi_j$, $\psi_j \mapsto c\,\psi_i^\dagger$, $\psi_j^\dagger \mapsto -d\,\psi_i$, $\psi_i \mapsto -c\,\psi_j^\dagger$, two $2 \times 2$ blocks each with eigenvalues $\pm\sqrt{cd}$: hyperbolic for $cd > 0$, where unequal coefficients rescale the common rapidity rather than remove it ($2\psi_i^\dagger\psi_j^\dagger + \tfrac12\psi_j\psi_i$ is a clock at unit rapidity outright); compact for $cd < 0$, eigenvalues $\pm i\sqrt{|cd|}$; nilpotent for $cd = 0$. Every clock in the inventory is therefore hyperbolic with unit rapidity after normalisation, hence by the Witt-extension clause of (iii) $O(n,n)$-conjugate to a sum of standard atom boosts, and the geometric normalisation converts them all at the one $\kappa$. What is unique is the rate, not the flow. Normalisation sets the nonzero adjoint eigenvalues to $\pm 1$, so the continuation of any clock to imaginary rapidity acts on the mode operators by $e^{\pm i\theta}$ and has conjugation period exactly $2\pi$, the atom's period of Fact 2.2 ([ButlerT5, Prop.~7.21(1)]); at the geometric rate $\kappa$ that period is the Schwarzschild span $2\pi/\kappa = \beta$.

deposited.statement:
Along the rain geodesics of the interior, the radial infall lines with unit energy at infinity that are the worldlines of the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand frame of Section 2, $|dt/dr| = \sqrt{r/2M}\;r/(2M - r)$, so the span of Killing time between crossing $r = 2M(1 - \varepsilon)$ and reaching the singularity is
\[
\Delta t(\varepsilon) \;=\; \int_0^{2M(1-\varepsilon)} \sqrt{\frac{r}{2M}}\,\frac{r\,dr}{2M - r}
\;=\; 4M\Bigl(\tfrac12\ln\frac{1+u}{1-u} - u - \tfrac{u^{3}}{3}\Bigr)\Big|_{u = \sqrt{1-\varepsilon}}
\;=\; 2M\Bigl(\ln\tfrac{1}{\varepsilon} - \tfrac83 + 2\ln 2\Bigr) + O(\varepsilon) :
\]
of order $M$ for any fixed regulator $\varepsilon$, with only logarithmic sensitivity to the horizon-crossing cutoff, the coefficient $2M$ of the logarithm being independent of the geodesic's energy. The informal estimate ``$\Delta t \sim M$ up to a logarithm'' is exactly this statement, with the logarithm identified.
deposited.proof: For a radial geodesic of the static metric with conserved energy $\mathcal{E} = f\,dt/d\lambda$ per unit mass, the normalisation gives $(dr/d\lambda)^{2} = \mathcal{E}^{2} - f$, so $dt/dr = \mathcal{E}/\bigl(f\sqrt{\mathcal{E}^{2} - f}\bigr)$; at $\mathcal{E} = 1$, $\sqrt{1 - f} = \sqrt{2M/r}$ and $|dt/dr| = \sqrt{r/2M}\,\bigl|r/(r - 2M)\bigr|$, which is the stated integrand for $r < 2M$. Substituting $r = 2Mu^{2}$ turns the integral into $4M\int_0^{\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}} u^{4}/(1 - u^{2})\,du$, and the integrand identity $u^{4}/(1 - u^{2}) = -u^{2} - 1 + 1/(1 - u^{2})$ gives the antiderivative $-u^{3}/3 - u + \tfrac12\ln\frac{1+u}{1-u}$, checked by differentiation; the closed form follows. For the expansion, $u = \sqrt{1 - \varepsilon} = 1 - \varepsilon/2 + O(\varepsilon^{2})$ gives $\tfrac12\ln\frac{1+u}{1-u} = \tfrac12\ln\frac{4}{\varepsilon} + O(\varepsilon) = \tfrac12\ln\tfrac1\varepsilon + \ln 2 + O(\varepsilon)$ and $u + u^{3}/3 = \tfrac43 + O(\varepsilon)$, so $\Delta t = 2M\ln\tfrac1\varepsilon + 4M(\ln 2 - \tfrac43) + O(\varepsilon)$. Near the horizon $dt/dr \approx 1/f$ for every $\mathcal{E}$, which is why the logarithm's coefficient is universal. Both the integrand identity and the substitution are verified exactly in the deposited script, as identities of rational functions, and the closed form is checked against the integral by exact rational Riemann bounds at the rational endpoint $\varepsilon = 1999 \cdot 10^{-6}$.

deposited.statement: For any nondegenerate real quadratic space $(V, Q)$, the maximal number of pairwise-anticommuting fermionic mode pairs realisable by \emph{vectors} of $\Cl(V, Q)$ (families $(a_i, b_i)$ of vectors satisfying the displayed CAR of Proposition 4.1) is exactly the Witt index $\min(p,q)$ of $Q$. Along the tower the Witt index is $\min(p,q) + k$: each rung raises the algebra's mode capacity by exactly one, and by no more.
deposited.proof:
\emph{Upper bound.} Let $(a_i, b_i)_{i \leq m}$ be vectors satisfying the CAR. Reading the relations through the Clifford relation on vectors: $\langle a_i, a_j \rangle = 0$ for all $i, j$ (including $i = j$), and $\langle a_i, b_j \rangle = \tfrac12 \delta_{ij}$. The span of the $a_i$ is therefore totally isotropic, and the $a_i$ are independent: a vanishing combination $\sum c_i a_i = 0$ pairs against $b_j$ to give $c_j/2 = 0$. So $m \leq$ the maximal totally isotropic dimension, which for a nondegenerate real form of signature $(p,q)$ is $\min(p,q)$: diagonalise, $V = P \perp N$ with $P$ positive definite of dimension $p$ and $N$ negative definite of dimension $q$; a totally isotropic $U$ meets $P$ trivially (a nonzero $v \in U \cap P$ would have $Q(v,v) > 0$ and $Q(v,v) = 0$ at once), so the projection $U \to N$ along $P$ is injective and $\dim U \leq q$; symmetrically $\dim U \leq p$; and $\min(p,q)$ is attained by the null spans of $\min(p,q)$ hyperbolic pairs (the classical bound, cf.\ [Lam2005, Ch.~I]).

\emph{Attainment.} Split off $\min(p,q)$ orthogonal hyperbolic planes from $(V, Q)$ (Witt decomposition) and take their normalised null pairs, as in Proposition 4.1. Along the tower, the form of signature $(p{+}k, q{+}k)$ has Witt index $\min(p,q) + k$, and each rung contributes its own plane to the attaining family.

t09-regenerated.title: Introduction
t09-regenerated.text:
The transport principle \cite{ButlerT1} resolves division by zero in the spacetime algebra $\Cl(1,3)$ by a forced minimal completion into $\Cl(2,4)$, and the series has so far exploited the completion's vector side: the fibre quadric whose points resolve the division \cite{ButlerT1}, the sheaf of completions over a degenerating metric \cite{ButlerT4}, the tower of iterated completions and its CAR limit \cite{ButlerT3}, the vacuum equations as a parallel ideal point of the quadric \cite{ButlerT6}, and T5's chain from the Schwarzschild gauge field to the Page curve \cite{ButlerT5}. This paper develops the completion's \emph{spinor} side, and finds there a formalism that has existed since 1967: Penrose's twistor theory.

The correspondence is not an analogy, and the paper's task is to prove it as a set of theorems and then apply it in both directions. In one direction, the series gains: fifty years of twistor technology (the Klein correspondence, the incidence geometry, local twistor transport, the twistor description of massless fields) becomes available to the transport programme with an explicit dictionary. In the other direction, the series contributes: the completion explains \emph{why} the twistorial objects are what they are. The two distinguished skew lines of projective twistor space are the null pair adjoined by the Witt completion; the incidence relation is the completion's chart, re-derived rather than postulated; and the palatial programme's noncommutative twistor algebra is exactly one quantisation above the completion's ladder pairs, with the conformal algebra as the shared core.

Let $W \subset V_\C$ be a maximal totally isotropic subspace ($\dim_\C W = 3$) and $W'$ a complementary maximal isotropic subspace, dual to $W$ under the $\C$-bilinear form (such a pair exists, and any two such pairs are conjugate under $O(V_\C)$). On the exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet W$ ($\dim_\C = 2^3 = 8$) define
\[
c(w) := \sqrt2\; w \wedge (\cdot) \quad (w \in W),
\qquad
c(w') := \sqrt2\; \iota_{w'} \quad (w' \in W'),
\]
with $\iota$ contraction through the pairing. \[

\]
each of complex dimension 4, are modules of the even subalgebra $\Cl^0(2,4)_\C \cong \End(\CS) \oplus \End(\CSm)$: the two chiralities, the conformal spinor space $\CS$ and its opposite $\CSm$ (twistor and dual twistor space).

Existence of the isotropic pair: in the orthonormal basis of the section ``Setting and imports'' take
\begin{align*}
w_1 &:= a_1 + b_1, & w_2 &:= a_2 + b_2, & w_3 &:= b_3 + i\,b_4,\\
w_1' &:= \tfrac12(a_1 - b_1), & w_2' &:= \tfrac12(a_2 - b_2), & w_3' &:= -\tfrac12(b_3 - i\,b_4).
\end{align*}
The first two isotropic vectors pair a plus direction with a minus direction and are real; the third pairs two minus directions and is complex, $Q(b_3 + ib_4) = -1 + 1 = 0$; and $\ip{w_j}{w_k'} = \delta_{jk}$, $\ip{w_j}{w_k} = \ip{w_j'}{w_k'} = 0$ by inspection. This is the basis the verification script uses, over the Gaussian rationals. Conjugacy: two dual pairs $(W, W')$ and $(U, U')$ with dual bases $w_j, w_j'$ and $u_j, u_j'$ have the same Gram matrix $\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} 0 & I \\ I & 0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$, so the linear map $w_j \mapsto u_j$, $w_j' \mapsto u_j'$ is an isometry of $V_\C$ carrying one pair to the other. \[

\]

\[

\]

Fix bases $\pi_1, \pi_2$ of $\Spi$ and $e_1, e_2$ of $\Som$ with $\pi_1\wedge\pi_2 = N_0$ and $e_1 \wedge e_2 = N_\infty$. For a linear map $A: \Spi \to \Som$ let $L_A := \{A\pi + \pi : \pi \in \Spi\}$ be its graph line and
\[
P(A) \;:=\; (A\pi_1 + \pi_1)\wedge(A\pi_2 + \pi_2) \;\in\; \Lambda^2\T
\]
its Pl\"ucker bivector, normalised by $P(0) = N_0$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Expansion.)} $P(A) = N_0 + \varphi(A) + (\det A)\, N_\infty$, where $\varphi(A) := A\pi_1\wedge\pi_2 + \pi_1\wedge A\pi_2$ lies in the mixed slot $\Som\wedge\Spi$ and $\det$ is taken in the chosen bases.
\item \emph{(The chart, term by term.)} $\varphi$ is a linear isomorphism onto the mixed slot $= \{\nO,\nInf\}^\perp \otimes \C$, and satisfies $\ip{\varphi(A)}{\varphi(A)} = -2\det A$. Writing $m(A) := \varphi(A)$ as a vector of $\{\nO,\nInf\}^\perp\otimes\C$, the Pl\"ucker bivector is exactly the completion's point embedding, complexified:
\[
P(A) \;=\; \nO \,+\, m(A)\,-\,\tfrac12\,\ip{m(A)}{m(A)}\,\nInf \;=\; X\bigl(m(A)\bigr).
\]
In particular every $P(A)$ is null, as a Pl\"ucker bivector must be, and the nullity of $P(A)$ is equivalent to the identity $\det A = -\tfrac12\ip{m(A)}{m(A)}$: the quadratic term of the chart is a determinant.
\item \emph{(Coverage.)} $A \mapsto L_A$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}(\Spi, \Som)$ onto the lines of $\PT$ skew to $L_\infty$, and $[P(A)]$ ranges exactly over the points of the Klein quadric with $\ip{P}{\nInf} \neq 0$: the affine chart of the complexified conformal compactification, with the lines meeting $L_\infty$ as the points at infinity; the real locus is cut out in Proposition 4.5(5).
\item \emph{(Consequences.)} (i) The null pair adjoined by the Witt completion is the pair of skew lines $(L_\infty, L_0)$ (Proposition 4.1). (ii) The splitting of a twistor into its $(\omega, \pi)$ parts along $\T = \Som\oplus\Spi$ is the Witt completion seen at spinor level: the same datum in a third language. (iii) Penrose's incidence relation $\omega = ix\pi$ is the case $A = i\hat x$ of the chart map, with $\hat x$ Hermitian for the twistor form (Proposition 4.5(5)). (iv) The stabiliser of the infinity line $L_\infty$ in $\mathfrak{so}(V_\C)$ is the stabiliser of the ray of $\nInf$: the Poincar\'e parabolic, with its Levi factor acting on $\Som \oplus \Spi$ as the two chiral $2$-dimensional representations, one plane the doublet of each $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)$ factor of the complexified Lorentz algebra and trivial for the other (Lemma 4.4(1)).
\end{enumerate}
deposited.proof:
(1) Expand bilinearly. The $\pi_1\wedge\pi_2$ term is $N_0$. The cross terms give $\varphi(A)$, manifestly in $\Som\wedge\Spi$. The top term is $A\pi_1\wedge A\pi_2$, a bivector of the $2$-plane $\Som$, hence a multiple of $e_1\wedge e_2$; writing $A\pi_i = \sum_j A_{ji}e_j$, the multiple is $A_{11}A_{22} - A_{21}A_{12} = \det A$.
(2) $P(A)$ is decomposable by construction, hence null (Theorem 3.4(2)). Expanding its norm with Proposition 4.1 (the mixed slot is orthogonal to the hyperbolic plane):
\[
0 \;=\; \ip{P(A)}{P(A)} \;=\; \ip{\varphi(A)}{\varphi(A)} + 2\det A\,\ip{N_0}{N_\infty}
 \;=\; \ip{\varphi(A)}{\varphi(A)} + 2\det A ,
\]
which is the displayed norm identity, and equivalently $\det A = -\tfrac12\ip{m(A)}{m(A)}$; substituting back into (1) yields $P(A) = X(m(A))$ exactly, in the chart normalisation of Section 2. Injectivity of $\varphi$: if $\varphi(A) = 0$ then $P(A) = N_0 + (\det A)N_\infty$ is decomposable, but $(N_0 + cN_\infty)\wedge(N_0 + cN_\infty) = 2c\,N_0\wedge N_\infty$, so $\det A = 0$ and $P(A) = N_0$, forcing $L_A = L_0$ and $A = 0$. Since $\dim \operatorname{Hom}(\Spi,\Som) = 4 = \dim(\Som\wedge\Spi)$, $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.
(3) A $2$-plane $U$ satisfies $U \cap \Som = 0$ if and only if the projection $U \to \Spi$ along $\Som$ is injective, hence bijective, if and only if $U$ is the graph of a unique $A: \Spi \to \Som$; and $U \cap \Som = 0$ is exactly skewness of $\mathbb{P}(U)$ and $L_\infty$. For the quadric statement: for decomposable $P = u_1\wedge u_2$, $\ip{P}{N_\infty} = \varepsilon(u_1\wedge u_2\wedge e_1\wedge e_2)$ vanishes exactly when the four vectors are dependent, i.e.\ when the planes meet; and $\ip{P(A)}{N_\infty} = \varepsilon(N_0\wedge N_\infty) = 1$. Rescaling any quadric point with $\ip{P}{\nInf} \neq 0$ to pairing $1$ places it in the chart, uniquely.
(4) (i) and (ii) are Proposition 4.1 applied to the pair $(\nInf, \nO)$; (iii) is Proposition 4.5(5). (iv): by equivariance of $\Psi$, a spin transformation stabilises the line $L_\infty$ (the plane $\Som$) if and only if it stabilises the ray of the bivector $N_\infty = \Psi(\nInf)$, i.e.\ the ray of $\nInf$ in $V_\C$. That stabiliser is computed in the flat model of [ButlerT6]: the parabolic with Levi factor $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)\oplus\R$ and nilradical the translations, imported here as Fact 4.3 below. The Levi factor preserves both $\Som$ and $\Spi$ (it stabilises both rays), and the assignment of the two $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)$ factors of $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)_\C$ to the two planes is Lemma 4.4(1). The verification script checks all eleven parabolic basis elements preserve $\Som$, that the complementary four do not, and the chiral assignment itself.

t09-regenerated.title: The chiral planes, and the summand spaces
t09-regenerated.proof:
Two preliminaries. First, $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)$ is simple: with the standard basis $e, h, f$, an ideal containing $x = ae + bh + cf \neq 0$ contains $[e,[e,x]] = -2c\,e$ and $[f,[f,x]] = -2a\,f$, so it contains $e$ or $f$ unless $a = c = 0$, in which case it contains $h$ and then $[h,e] = 2e$; and from any one of $e, f, h$ the brackets $[e,f] = h$, $[h,e] = 2e$, $[h,f] = -2f$ produce the other two. Second, the ideals of $\mathfrak{l} = \mathfrak{g}^+\oplus\mathfrak{g}^-$ are $0$, $\mathfrak{g}^+$, $\mathfrak{g}^-$, $\mathfrak{l}$: if an ideal $I$ is not contained in $\mathfrak{g}^-$, its projection to $\mathfrak{g}^+$ is a nonzero ideal of $\mathfrak{g}^+$, hence all of $\mathfrak{g}^+$, and then $\mathfrak{g}^+ = [\mathfrak{g}^+, \mathfrak{g}^+] = [\mathfrak{g}^+, I] \subseteq I$ (the $\mathfrak{g}^-$-components of $I$ commute with $\mathfrak{g}^+$, by \claimref{correspondence.chirality-split-ordering-insensitivity-asd-sector}(1)); symmetrically for $\mathfrak{g}^-$.

(1) The Levi factor stabilises the rays of $\nO$ and $\nInf$, so by equivariance of $\Psi$ it preserves the planes $\Spi$ and $\Som$, and $\mathfrak{l}$ acts on both. The map $\omega\otimes\pi \mapsto \omega\wedge\pi$ is equivariant for the induced action on $\Lambda^2\CS$ (the action for which $\Psi$ is equivariant) and surjective onto the four-dimensional mixed slot $\Som\wedge\Spi = \Psi(W_\C)$ (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.skew-lines-splittings-hyperbolic-planes-one}), so by dimension $\Som\otimes\Spi \cong W_\C$ as $\mathfrak{l}$-modules. The action of $\mathfrak{l}$ on $W_\C$ is faithful (bivectors act on vectors as $\so(V)$, \claimref{std-algebra.bivector-lie-algebra}, read over $\C$): the bivector $e_i\wedge e_j$ of an orthonormal pair acts as $\pm$ the elementary antisymmetric matrix, and the six are linearly independent. Let $\mathfrak{k}_\omega, \mathfrak{k}_\pi \subseteq \mathfrak{l}$ be the kernels of the actions on $\Som$, $\Spi$: ideals. Each is nonzero, since $\dim\mathfrak{l} = 6 > 4 = \dim\mathfrak{gl}(2,\C)$. Neither is $\mathfrak{l}$: if $\mathfrak{l}$ annihilated $\Spi$ it would act on $W_\C \cong \Som\otimes\Spi$ through $\Som$ alone, with image of dimension at most $4 < 6$, contradicting faithfulness; likewise for $\Som$. So $\mathfrak{k}_\omega, \mathfrak{k}_\pi \in \{\mathfrak{g}^+, \mathfrak{g}^-\}$, and they are different, since a common kernel would annihilate $\Som\otimes\Spi = W_\C$. Say $\mathfrak{k}_\pi = \mathfrak{g}^a$ and $\mathfrak{k}_\omega = \mathfrak{g}^b$ with $\{a, b\} = \{+,-\}$.
