A faithful action of $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)$ on a $2$-plane $S$ is an isomorphism onto $\mathfrak{sl}(S)$: the image is three-dimensional and consists of traceless operators, because $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C) = [\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C), \mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)]$ and commutators are traceless, and $\dim\mathfrak{sl}(S) = 3$. An $\mathfrak{l}$-equivariant map $f: W_\C\otimes\Spi \cong \Som\otimes\Spi\otimes\Spi \to \Som$ is therefore a linear map that commutes with $\mathfrak{sl}(\Som)$ acting on the first factor (through $\mathfrak{g}^a$, which acts trivially on the $\Spi$ factors) and is annihilated by $\mathfrak{sl}(\Spi)$ acting as a derivation on the last two factors (through $\mathfrak{g}^b$, trivial on $\Som$). Regard $f$ as a bilinear map $\Spi\times\Spi \to \End(\Som)$, $(\pi,\pi') \mapsto (\omega \mapsto f(\omega\otimes\pi\otimes\pi'))$. Its values commute with $\mathfrak{sl}(\Som)$, hence are scalars (an operator commuting with $E_{12}$, $E_{21}$ and $E_{11} - E_{22}$ is scalar), so $f$ is a bilinear form $\beta$ on $\Spi$ with $\beta(X\pi, \pi') + \beta(\pi, X\pi') = 0$ for all $X \in \mathfrak{sl}(\Spi)$. So $\beta$ is a multiple of the determinant form, which is invariant; the space is one-dimensional. The other case is the same with the roles of the planes exchanged.

Write $v \mapsto \bar v$ for the real structure of $V_\C$ with real points $V$, and $J$ for the antilinear map on $\Lambda^\bullet W$ that conjugates coefficients in the monomial basis built on the isotropic basis of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.fock-model-complexified-ascended-algebra}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item (\emph{The conjugation.}) With $\Gamma$ the parity operator ($+1$ on $\CS$, $-1$ on $\CSm$) and $b_4$ the fourth negative basis vector of the section ``Setting and imports'',
\[
\kappa := \Gamma\, c(b_4)\, J
\]
is an antilinear bijection of $\Lambda^\bullet W$ with $\kappa\, c(v) = c(\bar v)\, \kappa$ for all $v \in V_\C$; every antilinear map with this property is a complex multiple of $\kappa$; $\kappa$ swaps the chiralities, $\kappa(\CS) = \CSm$; and $\kappa^2 = -\id$.
\item (\emph{The invariant Hermitian form.}) $\Sigma(Z_1, Z_2) := B(\kappa Z_1, Z_2)$ (the twistor form; on the conformal spinor space $\CS$ it corresponds to the reversion form) is a nondegenerate sesquilinear form on $\CS$ with $\Sigma(Z_2, Z_1) = \lambda\,\overline{\Sigma(Z_1, Z_2)}$ for a constant $\lambda$ of modulus one, so that a rescaling of $\kappa$ by a phase makes $\Sigma$ Hermitian; for the $\kappa$ of (1), $\lambda = 1$ and $\Sigma$ is Hermitian as it stands. The real bivectors act $\Sigma$-anti-Hermitianly, so $\Sigma$ is $\mathrm{Spin}(2,4)$-invariant.
\item (\emph{Null planes.}) For every real null vector $v$ the plane of $\Psi(v)$ is $\Sigma$-null. In particular $\Som$ and $\Spi$ are $\Sigma$-null.
\item (\emph{Signature.}) $\Sigma$ has signature $(2,2)$.
\item (\emph{Reality of the chart, and the factor $I_6$.}) The conformal pseudoscalar $I_6$ acts on $\CS$ as its complex unit (the factor $i$). Let $\sigma(\omega, \pi) := \Sigma(\omega, \pi)$ be the resulting perfect pairing $\Som\times\Spi \to \C$, and call $\hat x: \Spi\to\Som$ \emph{$\sigma$-Hermitian} if $\sigma(\hat x\pi, \pi') = \overline{\sigma(\hat x\pi', \pi)}$ for all $\pi, \pi' \in \Spi$. For $A \in \operatorname{Hom}(\Spi, \Som)$ the following are equivalent: (a) the chart point $m(A)$ of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart} is real, $m(A) \in W_{1,3}$; (b) the line $L_A$ is $\Sigma$-null; (c) $A = I_6\hat x$ with $\hat x$ $\sigma$-Hermitian. Consequently the real points of the affine chart are exactly the $\Sigma$-null lines skew to $L_\infty$, the incidence relation of a real point reads $\omega = I_6\hat x\pi$ with $\hat x$ $\sigma$-Hermitian, and on real points the chart norm is $Q(m) = -2\det A = 2\det\hat x$ in the bases of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart}.

\[

Let $[g]$ be the conformal class of the derived metric of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), on its invertible region. \[
\nabla_a(\sigma, \mu_b, \rho) = \bigl(\nabla_a\sigma - \mu_a,\;\; \nabla_a\mu_b + g_{ab}\rho - \mathrm{P}_{ab}\sigma,\;\; \nabla_a\rho + \mathrm{P}_a{}^b\mu_b\bigr),
\]
with $\mathrm{P}$ the Schouten tensor. \[
\nabla^{\mathrm{LT}}_a(\omega^B, \pi_{B'}) \;=\; \bigl(\nabla_a \omega^B + i\,\varepsilon_A{}^B\,\pi_{A'},\;\; \nabla_a\pi_{B'} + i\,\mathrm{P}_{AA'BB'}\,\omega^B\bigr),
\]
in the index conventions of \cite[Vol.~2, Ch.~6]{PenroseRindler86}, where the factor $i$ acts on $\CS$ as the conformal pseudoscalar $I_6$; under conformal rescaling $\omega$ is invariant and $\pi$ shifts, so the $\pi$-plane $\{\omega = 0\}$ (the kernel in $\CS$ of the point's null vector) is the canonical subbundle. \emph{Provenance:} (i) \cite{BEG1994, CurryGover2018}, in the conventions of \cite[Fact 4.1, eq.~(3)]{ButlerT6}; (ii) \cite{PenroseMacCallum73, Dighton74}; the statement that (ii) is the spin representation of (i), that is, that the conformal spinor connection is the tractor connection acting on $\CS$, is standard in the tractor literature \cite{BEG1994, CurryGover2018}, and is \emph{proved} rather than imported below, since the proof is short in the present framework.

t09-regenerated.title: The conformal spinor connection is Penrose's local twistor transport
t09-regenerated.text:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be the tractor bundle of \cite[\S 4]{ButlerT6} and $\CS M$ its spin bundle, the conformal spinor bundle: the rank-four complex bundle with fibre the conformal spinor space $\CS$, carried by the fibrewise Fock model of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.fock-model-complexified-ascended-algebra}, associated to a lift of the $SO(2,4)$ tractor bundle to $\mathrm{Spin}(2,4)$. We assume the conformal manifold is spin, so that the lift exists globally (on the invertible region of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), an open subset of flat spacetime, it does); every statement below is local, and locally a lift always exists. At a point, write $X_p$ for the canonical (tautological) null direction of $\mathcal{T}_p$, and, in a scale, $u_p$ for the null direction with $\ip{X_p}{u_p} = 1$ singled out by the splitting. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the connection of Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}(i) decomposes, in the scale, as
\[
\nabla_a \;=\; \nabla^{g}_a \;-\; u_p \wedge e_a \;+\; X_p \wedge \mathrm{P}(e_a),
\]
(for a gravitational field on flat spacetime, with $u_p = \nInf$, $X_p = \nO$ and $e_a = \hb^{-1}(a)$, this is the gauge field $\Omega_{T}(a) = \Omega(a) - \nInf \wedge \hb^{-1}(a) + \nO \wedge \Sch(\hb^{-1}(a))$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}, $\nabla^{g}$ being $\Omega(a)$), where $\nabla^g$ couples the Levi factor only: the soldering summand is valued in $u_p\wedge W_\C$ and the Schouten summand in $X_p \wedge W_\C$, with $W_\C = (W_{1,3})_\C$ the complexified Minkowski complement, the latter in the nilradical of the parabolic stabilising $X_p$;
\item on the spinor bundle, with $\Spi$ the plane of $\Psi(X_p)$ (the point's own line: the canonical subbundle) and $\Som$ the plane of $\Psi(u_p)$, the grading element $E := u_p\wedge X_p$ acts with eigenvalue $+\tfrac12$ on $\Som$ and $-\tfrac12$ on $\Spi$; consequently the soldering summand ($E$-weight $+1$) maps $\Spi \to \Som$ and annihilates $\Som$, and the Schouten summand ($E$-weight $-1$) maps $\Som \to \Spi$ and annihilates $\Spi$;
\item the induced spinor connection therefore has, in the scale splitting $Z = (\omega, \pi)$ with $\omega \in \Som$, $\pi \in \Spi$, the form
\[
\nabla^{\CS M}_a(\omega, \pi) = \bigl(\nabla^g_a\omega + \sigma_a\pi,\ \nabla^g_a\pi + \tau_a\omega\bigr),
\]
where $\sigma_a := \rho(-u_p\wedge e_a)|_{\Spi\to\Som}$ is the soldering summand and $\tau_a := \rho(X_p\wedge\mathrm{P}(e_a))|_{\Som\to\Spi}$ the Schouten summand.
The summands are Levi-equivariant in the direction $e_a$, so by Lemma \claimref{correspondence.chiral-planes-summand-spaces}(2) each is the unique map of its type up to a scalar: under Levi-equivariant identifications of $\Som$, $\Spi$ with Penrose's $S^B$, $S_{B'}$, and the \emph{metric-normalised} identification of $W_\C$ with $S^B\otimes S^{B'}$ (the one under which $g_{ab}$ corresponds to $\varepsilon_{AB}\varepsilon_{A'B'}$, Penrose and Rindler's own, fixed up to sign), with $a = AA'$ and $c = CC'$ in the convention of Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}(ii), $\sigma_a$ is the $\varepsilon$-contraction $\pi_{A'} \mapsto \varepsilon_A{}^B\pi_{A'}$ times a constant $c_1$ and $\tau_a$ is the Schouten contraction $\omega^B \mapsto \mathrm{P}_{AA'BB'}\omega^B$ times a constant $c_2$. The constants depend on the relative scale of the two spinor identifications, which multiplies $c_1$ by $\lambda$ and $c_2$ by $\lambda^{-1}$ (the sign freedom of the third flips both, so it changes neither their product nor anything not already realised by $\lambda = -1$), so their product is invariant and is fixed by the composite of the summands on $\Som$:
\[
\sigma_a\,\tau_c \;=\; \tfrac12\,c(e_a)\,c(\mathrm{P}(e_c))\big|_{\Som} \;=\; \tfrac12\,\mathrm{P}_{ac}\,\id_{\Som} + \rho\bigl(e_a\wedge\mathrm{P}(e_c)\bigr)\big|_{\Som} .
\]
Penrose's local twistor transport (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}(ii)) has the same form, with summand composite $\omega^B \mapsto -\varepsilon_A{}^B\,\mathrm{P}_{CC'DA'}\,\omega^D$. Hence Penrose's local twistor bundle is the conformal spinor bundle $\CS M$ and his local twistor transport is the conformal spinor connection, the spinor square root of the tractor connection, exactly when the two composites agree, which is a single convention this identification imports: the sign and normalisation of $\mathrm{P}_{AA'BB'}$ in \cite{PenroseRindler86} relative to the Schouten tensor of Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}(i) (Remark \claimref{note.correspondence.one-imported-convention-local-twistor-identification}).
\end{enumerate}

t09-regenerated.title: The palatial relation: two quantisations, one core
t09-regenerated.text:
Palatial twistor theory \cite{Penrose15} is Penrose's current approach to the full Einstein equations: it replaces holomorphic functions on twistor space by a \emph{noncommutative} algebra of twistor operators, with $\bar Z$ realised as a derivative and the googly data expected to reside in ordering ambiguities. The transport framework independently produces noncommutative pair structure, the completed ladder pairs with their CAR relations, as the mandatory replacement for classical values at the singular locus \cite{ButlerT1}. It is natural to conjecture that the two structures are the same object. This section proves that the naive form of that conjecture is \emph{false}, for a reason of statistics that admits a one-line proof, and then proves the corrected picture: the two algebras are the two storeys of one tower, meeting at the conformal algebra.

Throughout, the \emph{palatial algebra} $\mathcal{P}$ is the unital associative $\C$-algebra with generators $Z^\alpha, \bar Z_\beta$ ($\alpha, \beta = 1, \dots, 4$) and relations
\[
[Z^\alpha, Z^\beta] = 0, \qquad [\bar Z_\alpha, \bar Z_\beta] = 0, \qquad [Z^\alpha, \bar Z_\beta] = \hbar\,\delta^\alpha_\beta ,
\]
the twistor canonical commutation relations of \cite{Penrose15} (there realised by $\bar Z_\beta = \hbar\,\partial/\partial Z^\beta$ on holomorphic functions); $\hbar \neq 0$ is a fixed constant.

t09-regenerated.title: Symmetrised quadratics of the palatial algebra
t09-regenerated.proof:
(1) $[Z^\alpha\bar Z_\beta, Z^\gamma] = Z^\alpha[\bar Z_\beta, Z^\gamma] = -\hbar\,\delta^\gamma_\beta Z^\alpha$, and the same for the reversed ordering, so $[q(M), Z^\gamma] = -\hbar\sum_\alpha M^\gamma{}_\alpha Z^\alpha$; likewise $[Z^\alpha \bar Z_\beta, \bar Z_\gamma] = \hbar\,\delta^\alpha_\gamma\,\bar Z_\beta$ gives the second display.
(2) $\operatorname{ad}_{q(M)}$ is a derivation, so by (1),
\[
[q(M), q(N)] = \tfrac12\sum N^\beta{}_\alpha\Bigl(\,[q(M),Z^\alpha]\bar Z_\beta + Z^\alpha[q(M),\bar Z_\beta] + [q(M),\bar Z_\beta]Z^\alpha + \bar Z_\beta[q(M),Z^\alpha]\Bigr),
\]
and collecting coefficients of the symmetrised monomials gives $-\hbar\,q(NM) + \hbar\,q(MN) = \hbar\,q([M,N])$. Injectivity: the adjoint action (1) recovers $M$. The verification script confirms (2) in the polynomial realisation $Z^\alpha = z_\alpha$, $\bar Z_\beta = -\hbar\,\partial_\beta$ (the sign that realises $[Z^\alpha, \bar Z_\beta] = +\hbar\delta^\alpha_\beta$, checked as an operator identity), where both sides are operators determined by their action on polynomials of degree $\le 2$, checked exactly on that finite basis.

t09-regenerated.title: The Clifford side of the ordering shift
t09-regenerated.text:
Let $(v, v^*)$ be a null pair of $V$ with $\ip{v}{v^*} = 1$ (an adjoined ladder pair), and let $E := v\wedge v^* \in \mathfrak{so}(2,4)$ be the grading element of the corresponding hyperbolic plane. In the Fock model, the spinor action of $E$ is
\[
\rho(E) \;=\; \tfrac12\,c(v)\,c(v^*) - \tfrac12 \;=\; N - \tfrac12 ,
\]
where $N$ is the occupation number operator of the mode created by $v$ (eigenvalue $1$ on states containing that mode, $0$ otherwise). The generator of the adjoined plane's boost is the mode's number operator shifted by one half.
t09-regenerated.proof: The bivector element of $\Cl(V_\C)$ attached to $a\wedge b$ is $\tfrac12 c(a)c(b) - \tfrac12\ip{a}{b}$ (the product of two vectors is $\ip{a}{b}$ plus half their commutator, \claimref{std-algebra.vector-squares}): its commutator with vectors is the bivector action for any $a, b$, orthogonal or not, as in Proposition \claimref{correspondence.spin-representation}. Take $v = w_1$, $v^* = w_1'$ in an adapted model, and write $A_1 := w_1\wedge(\cdot)$, $B_1 := \iota_{w_1'}$, so $c(v)c(v^*) = 2\,A_1 B_1$. On a basis monomial containing $w_1$, $A_1B_1$ removes and restores the $w_1$-factor: eigenvalue $1$; on a monomial without $w_1$, $B_1$ annihilates it: eigenvalue $0$. So $\tfrac12 c(v)c(v^*) = N$ and $\rho(E) = N - \tfrac12$. The script checks the full $8\times 8$ eigenvalue table. The eigenvalues $\pm\tfrac12$ on the two chirality-plane pairs are the grading weights used in Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}.
t09-regenerated.label: Proposition

t09-regenerated.title: The shared core, and the ordering dictionary

(2) is Proposition \claimref{correspondence.spin-representation}. (3) Compose: $\beta \mapsto \rho(\beta) \in \mathfrak{sl}(\CS) \subset \mathfrak{gl}(\CS) \mapsto q(\rho(\beta))/\hbar$; both maps are injective Lie homomorphisms (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.spin-representation}, Lemma \claimref{correspondence.symmetrised-quadratics-palatial-algebra}(2)), and Lemma \claimref{correspondence.symmetrised-quadratics-palatial-algebra}(1) says the adjoint action on the generator span is $\rho(\beta)$ again (in the dual pair of slots). t09-regenerated.title: The two-storey picture
t09-regenerated.text: The corrected relationship is a proved structure, drawn in a figure of the original. The Clifford (fermionic) quantisation turns ambient directions into conformal spinor (twistor) \emph{states}: first quantisation, forced at the singular locus (Remark \claimref{note.correspondence.point-contact-planes-tower}). The Weyl (bosonic) quantisation of the palatial programme turns conformal spinor states into the noncommutative algebra of quantised conformal spinors: second quantisation, one storey up, and provably not the first storey under another name (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.statistics-no-go}). The conformal algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$ is the invariant core of both storeys (Theorem \claimref{correspondence.shared-core-ordering-dictionary}), and the ordering shift of a half per dimension recurs at each. What survives of the naive conjecture is its corrected form: the framework's operator-valued completion and Penrose's noncommutative holomorphic geometry are opposite ends of one tower rather than of one identification, meeting at the conformal algebra. Read against the tower paper \cite{ButlerT3}, the completion's ladder pairs supply the states on which the palatial storey acts.

t09-regenerated.text: The correspondence proved so far is flat-model and connection-level. t09-regenerated.title: Imported: the nonlinear graviton
t09-regenerated.text: For a complex $4$-manifold with anti-self-dual (half-flat) vacuum conformal structure, the $\alpha$-plane distribution defined fibrewise by the ruling of the Klein quadric is integrable; the leaf space of the resulting foliation is a complex $3$-manifold, the \emph{curved twistor space}; spacetime points reappear as rational curves with normal bundle $\mathcal{O}(1)\oplus\mathcal{O}(1)$; and the conformal structure is recovered from curve intersection. Conversely such a curved twistor space determines the half-flat spacetime. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Penrose76}. In the language of this paper: half-flatness is exactly the condition under which the completion's point space, the fibrewise Klein quadric of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.spinor-identification}, globalises to a deformed projective spinor space with the incidence dictionary of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart} intact. \emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The complex four-manifold with its half-flat conformal structure, and the curved twistor space as the leaf space of its $\alpha$-plane foliation, are global and are not carried by a single gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}). Even the pointwise condition needs the complex setting: the Weyl map $\mathcal{W}$ of a real field is linear over $\{1, I\}$ with $I^{2} = -1$, so a nonzero $\mathcal{W}$ of one handedness only exists for a complexified field, and the statement is read on the complex manifold, whose half-flatness is that condition on the Weyl part of its curvature.

t09-regenerated.title: No real Lorentzian vacuum is half-flat
t09-regenerated.text: Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), $\mathcal{W}$ the Weyl map of its field strength on physical bivectors, and $\Lambda^{\pm}$ the duality halves, the eigenspaces of multiplication by the pseudoscalar $I$ (the Hodge star) on the complexified bivectors $\Lambda^{2}_{\C}$, with the scalar $i$ kept distinct from $I$. At every point of the invertible region, if either duality half of $\mathcal{W}$ vanishes, $\mathcal{W}$ vanishes: a real half-flat field has a conformally flat derived metric. The statement is pointwise; equivalently, on an oriented Lorentzian $4$-manifold, if either duality half of the Weyl tensor vanishes, the Weyl tensor vanishes: a real Lorentzian half-flat metric is conformally flat. In particular no real Lorentzian black hole is half-flat: the Weyl maps of the Schwarzschild and Kerr fields are nonzero (a nonzero curvature scale times a nonzero type-D bivector off the singular locus, the locus where $\hb$ fails, imported from \cite[Prop.~3.3, Fact 6.3]{ButlerT6}).

\begin{gather*}
[A^{(1)}_i, A^{(1)}_j] = \tfrac14\,\epsilon_{ijk}\bigl(R_k + iB_k + iB_k + R_k\bigr) = \epsilon_{ijk}A^{(1)}_k,\\
[A^{(1)}_i, A^{(2)}_j] = \tfrac14\,\epsilon_{ijk}\bigl(R_k - iB_k + iB_k - R_k\bigr) = 0,
\end{gather*}

(2) (a) Two orderings of a word $q(\rho(P_1))\cdots q(\rho(P_r))$, $P_s \in \mathfrak{g}^-$, differ by a sequence of adjacent transpositions, each of which changes the word by the word with the adjacent pair $q(\rho(P_s))q(\rho(P_t))$ replaced by $[q(\rho(P_s)), q(\rho(P_t))] = \hbar\,q(\rho([P_s, P_t]))$ (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.symmetrised-quadratics-palatial-algebra}(2) and Proposition \claimref{correspondence.spin-representation}); since $[P_s, P_t] \in \mathfrak{g}^-$ by (1), the result is $\hbar$ times a word in elements of $q(\rho(\mathfrak{g}^-))$, an element of $\hbar\,\mathcal{A}^-$; for $r = 2$ it is the single commutator displayed. This paper is T9 of the series. \emph{It relies on four predecessors:} the primer T0 \cite{ButlerT0} for the Clifford conventions (the section ``Setting and imports''); the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1} for the forced completion, its fibre quadric, the real ladder pairs and the transvection no-go (Facts \claimref{correspondence.imported-forced-completion-fibre-quadric}, \claimref{correspondence.imported-ladder-pairs-fock-modules-over}, \claimref{correspondence.imported-stabilisers-flat-model}); the tower paper T3 \cite{ButlerT3} for the iterated ascent whose rungs are the ladder pairs of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.twistors-are-states-three-ladder-pairs} (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-ladder-pairs-fock-modules-over}, Remark \claimref{note.correspondence.point-contact-planes-tower}); the interior paper T6 \cite{ButlerT6} for the flat-model stabilisers, the scale tractor and the vacuum equations, the tractor connection, and the Kerr Killing spinor (Facts \claimref{correspondence.imported-stabilisers-flat-model}, \claimref{correspondence.imported-vacuum-equations-scale-tractor}, \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}, Remark \claimref{note.correspondence.boundary-stated-plainly}). No result is imported from the spectrum paper T7 \cite{ButlerT7}, which is named in successor problem (4) as the paper that proves its homogeneity half from this paper's ordering shift; the sheaf paper T4 \cite{ButlerT4} is named in the introduction and in successor problem (3), and the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} as context.

\emph{Papers that rely on this one:} the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} assigns the twistor restatement of its spectrum condition to this paper's setting; the interior paper T6 \cite{ButlerT6} cites the twistor reading of the completion's spinor module as a point of contact; the spectrum paper T7 \cite{ButlerT7} imports the ordering shift of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.shared-core-ordering-dictionary}(4); the action paper T10 \cite{ButlerT10} imports nothing from this paper: the summand decomposition of Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}(1) reappears there, in the frozen point's scale, as its own Lemma 2.5(iii), proved directly; the mass paper T11 \cite{ButlerT11} imports the pure-spinor identification of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.twistors-are-states-three-ladder-pairs}, the chart normalisation of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart}, and the palatial quadratics of Lemma \claimref{correspondence.symmetrised-quadratics-palatial-algebra}; the standard-model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} imports the spinor identification, the pure-spinor theorem and the shared core (Theorems \claimref{correspondence.spinor-identification}, \claimref{correspondence.twistors-are-states-three-ladder-pairs}, \claimref{correspondence.shared-core-ordering-dictionary}); the dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14} imports the Witt-flag reading of the ladder pairs; the synthesis paper T16 \cite{ButlerT16} imports the point embedding and the Fock-vacuum reading; and the capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17} tabulates this paper's claims at their tiers.

t09-regenerated.title: Machine verification
t09-regenerated.text:
Every computational identity asserted in this paper is verified by the deposited script \texttt{verify\_T09.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT9}, which imports the series' shared exact-arithmetic library \texttt{GA.py} and runs entirely in exact arithmetic over the Gaussian rationals $\mathbb{Q}(i)$: no floating point appears anywhere, so every check is an identity, not an approximation. The script works with $C(v) = c(v)/\sqrt2$ (the section ``Setting and imports''), so that $\{C(u), C(v)\} = \ip{u}{v}$ and $C(u)^2 = Q(u)/2$, and with the isotropic basis of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.fock-model-complexified-ascended-algebra}, which is Gaussian rational. Sixty-nine checks pass. Three reusable routines developed for this paper were promoted into \texttt{GA.py} per the series' practice, append-only and backward compatibly: an exact Gaussian-rational field class, generic-field linear algebra (rank, solve) usable over any exact field, and a kernel routine over any exact field.

The coverage, by section. \emph{The Fock model} (Theorem \claimref{correspondence.fock-model-complexified-ascended-algebra}): the CAR relations of the three wedge and contraction pairs $w_j\wedge$, $\iota_{w_j'}$ (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.clifford-side-ordering-shift}, there written $A_1$, $B_1$) and all anticommutators on the full state basis; $\{C(u), C(v)\} = \ip{u}{v}$ on all thirty-six basis pairs and $C(u)^2 = Q(u)/2$ on non-null, complex, and null instances; linear independence of the sixty-four ordered generator products in $\End(\Lambda^\bullet W)$ (rank $64$: simplicity, surjectivity and irreducibility at once); oddness of vectors; the even subalgebra of dimension exactly $32$. \emph{The Chevalley pairing} (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.chevalley-pairing}): parity vanishing, perfection of the $\T'\times\T$ block, antisymmetry on all sixty-four pairs, $B$-self-transposedness of all six basis vectors, and invariance under all fifteen antisymmetrised bivectors. \emph{The spinor identification} (Theorem \claimref{correspondence.spinor-identification}, Example \claimref{note.correspondence.isomorphism-witt-pair}): antisymmetry of $G_v$; rank six of $\Psi$; the norm correspondence on all twenty-one pairs with the computed constant ($-1$ for the $C$-normalised $\Psi$, i.e.\ $-2$ in the paper's normalisation); the exact values $\Psi_C(w_1) = -t_2\wedge t_3$, $\Psi_C(w_1') = t_0 \wedge t_1$ and their planes; the Pfaffian nullity criterion on null and non-null instances; equivariance $\Psi(\beta v) = \beta\cdot\Psi(v)$ for all fifteen bivectors on all six basis vectors (ninety identities). \emph{Incidence} (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.skew-lines-splittings-hyperbolic-planes-one}, Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart}, Proposition \claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor}): the hyperbolic pair; the expansion, norm identity, chart identification $P(A) = X(m(A))$ and simplicity for four sample maps $A$ (identity, Gaussian-rational, singular, and $i$ times a Hermitian matrix); the sign flip $-2\det(i\hat x) = +2\det\hat x$ on a sample map; the coverage pairing. \emph{Reality} (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor}): the real orthonormal basis and its relation to the isotropic one; the conjugation as the reflection in $b_4$ composed with coordinate conjugation; $\kappa\,C(v) = C(\bar v)\,\kappa$ on every basis state for the six basis vectors and their $i$-multiples; $\kappa^2 = -\tfrac12$ (the $C$-normalised $-1$) and the parity swap; the constant $\lambda_0 = \lambda = 1$ on the full basis, and the general relation $\Sigma(Z_2,Z_1) = \lambda\,\overline{\Sigma(Z_1,Z_2)}$ with its phase repair tested on $\kappa$ rescaled by $(3+4i)/5$, where $\lambda \neq 1$; $\Sigma$ Hermitian and of rank four; $\Som$ and $\Spi$ both $\Sigma$-null; the signature $(2,2)$ read off $\Sigma$ through its real form; all fifteen real bivectors $\Sigma$-anti-Hermitian; four $\sigma$-Hermitian $\hat x$ with $m(i\hat x)$ real and spanning $W_{1,3}$, and $m(\hat x)$ not real. \emph{Chiral planes and summands} (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.chiral-planes-summand-spaces}, Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}(3)): each chirality factor annihilates exactly one of $\Som$, $\Spi$ and acts faithfully on the other, the two factors on different planes; the summand composite equals $C(e_a)C(\mathrm{P}(e_c))$, the $C$-form of $\tfrac12 c(e_a)c(\mathrm{P}(e_c))$, on $\Som$ for all sixteen pairs of mixed directions. \emph{Stabilisers and local twistors} (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-stabilisers-flat-model}, Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}, Proposition \claimref{correspondence.clifford-side-ordering-shift}): the commutator identity $[\beta, C(w)] = C(\beta w)$ for all fifteen bivectors; trace-freeness and linear independence of the fifteen spinor actions (the $\mathfrak{sl}(\T)$ isomorphism); the stabiliser census $10 + 1 + 4$ of the infinity direction and the exact match with preservation of the plane $\Som$; both summand actions on all four mixed directions; the full eigenvalue table of $\rho(v\wedge v^*) = N - \tfrac12$. \emph{Twistors as states} (Theorem \claimref{correspondence.twistors-are-states-three-ladder-pairs}): the annihilator of the vacuum; purity (dimension three, total isotropy) of a generic even and a generic odd spinor; the joint-kernel line; generation of the whole module from a vacuum by its dual system; the CAR relations of the generic twistor's own pair system, built on its annihilator and the dual complement constructed in the proof. \emph{The palatial algebra} (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.symmetrised-quadratics-palatial-algebra}, Theorem \claimref{correspondence.shared-core-ordering-dictionary}): the relations $[Z^\alpha, \bar Z_\beta] = \hbar\delta$ in the realisation $\bar Z = -\hbar\,\partial$; the homogeneity identity $q(\mathrm{id}) = -(h+2)\hbar$ (the $-2s-2$ point of contact) on all monomials of degree $\le 3$; $[q(M), q(N)] = \hbar\,q([M,N])$ and the adjoint action for explicit Gaussian-rational $M, N$, checked on the determining monomial basis; The script exits nonzero on any failure and prints one line per check, tagged by the statement it certifies.

Inf$ be the pure-scale section of $\mathcal{T}$ in the scale $g$. For the tractor connection, which in Gauge Theory Gravity is the $\Cl(2,4)$ rotation-gauge field $D^{T}_{a} = a \cdot 
abla + \Omega_{T}(a)	imes$, $\Omega_{T}(a) = \Omega(a) -

Inf + \mu + ho
O$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}), with slots in the splitting of $g$,
\[

abla_a I_g =  igl(0,\; -\Sch_{ab},\; 0 igr), \qquad	ext{that is}\qquad D^{T}_{a}
Inf = -\Sch igl(\hb^{-1}(a) igr),
\]
so $I_g$ is parallel if and only if $\Sch = 0$, if and only if $g$ is Ricci-flat, if and only if (Fact \claimref{interior.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations}) the GTG vacuum field equations hold. A non-constant rescaling $e^{2\omega}g$ already keeps the parallel section while losing the field equations.) t09-regenerated.title: Exact scale decoupling
t09-regenerated.text:
In the conventions of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-schwarzschild-curvature-spectrum}, the Schwarzschild curvature operator is, exactly and at every radius,
\[
R(B) \;=\; -\,\frac{M}{r^3}\,S(B), \qquad
S \;:=\; 1 - 3\Pi \;=\; -\tfrac12\bigl(B \mapsto B + 3\,\sigma_r B \sigma_r\bigr),
\]
where the shape operator $S$ satisfies the algebraic identity
\[
S^2 + S = 2 ,
\]
has spectrum $(-2, -2, 1, 1, 1, 1)$, and is trace-free. The factorisation is exact: $S$ depends on neither $M$ nor $r$, and the entire approach to the singularity changes only the conformal prefactor $-M/r^3$.

t09-regenerated.title: Imported: the Kerr curvature
t09-regenerated.text:
In the conventions of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-schwarzschild-curvature-spectrum}, which are the store's curvature sign of Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}, the curvature operator of the Kerr gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (its field strength, a linear map on physical bivectors) is
\[
\mathcal{R}(B) \;=\; \frac{M}{2}\,\bigl(r - I a\cos\theta\bigr)^{-3}\,\bigl(B + 3\,\sigma_r B\sigma_r\bigr),
\]
where $\sigma_r$ is the unit bivector of the principal planes (the plane pair singled out by the two principal congruences of physically null vectors), $I$ is the pseudoscalar of $\Cl(1,3)$, the inverse cube is taken in the commutative subalgebra $\R \oplus \R I$, and $(r,\theta)$ are oblate spheroidal coordinates on the flat background in which the singular set is the ring $r = 0$, $\theta = \pi/2$, where $\hb$ is undefined (it is unimodular wherever it is defined) and the field strength diverges. \emph{Provenance:} Doran-Lasenby \cite[Ch.~14]{DoranLasenby2003}; the type-D form is classical \cite{Carter1968}.

I_g \;:=\; \Bigl(1,\; 0,\; \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\Bigr) \;=\; \nInf + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\,\nO

in the scale $g$. Then $I_g$ is parallel, and every parallel section of the form $(1, 0, \rho)$ arises this way: $(1,0,\rho)$ is parallel if and only if $\rho$ is constant and $g$ is Einstein with $\Lambda = 6\rho$. The norm is

t09-regenerated.title: The Clifford algebra exists and is unique
t09-regenerated.text: For every real quadratic space $(V, Q)$ a Clifford algebra exists: $\Cl(V, Q) = T(V) / I_Q$, the tensor algebra modulo the two-sided ideal generated by $\{v \otimes v - Q(v)\,1 : v \in V\}$, with $\iota$ the inclusion of $V = T^{1}(V)$ followed by the quotient map. Any two Clifford algebras of $(V, Q)$ are isomorphic by a unique isomorphism compatible with the maps from $V$. t09-regenerated.title: Minimality
t09-regenerated.text:
Let $(\mathbb{W}, f)$ be any null-lift completion of $(\mathbb{V}, Q)$. Then $\mathbb{W}$ contains at least one direction of positive square and one of negative square; in particular $\dim \mathbb{W} \geq 2$, and enlargements of signature increment $(+k, 0)$ or $(0, +k)$ are excluded for every $k$. A single hyperbolic plane suffices, and any two-dimensional $\mathbb{W}$ admitted by the definition is a hyperbolic plane; hence the minimal completion is
\[
\Cl(p,q) \;\longrightarrow\; \Cl(p{+}1, q{+}1),
\]
with the adjoined space unique up to isometry, and the signature increment is $(+1,+1)$ in every signature.

\[
\omega_k = \kappa\bigl(k + \tfrac12\bigr), \qquad k \in \Z ,
\]

t10-regenerated.title: Introduction
t10-regenerated.text:
The geometry paper of this series proves that the vacuum field equations are exactly the covariant constancy of a distinguished section of the completion's ambient bundle, the \emph{frozen point}, null for $\Lambda = 0$ and of squared norm $\Lambda/3$ otherwise \cite{ButlerT6}. That was kinematics: the equations restated. This paper is dynamics: what is gravity's action principle, in the framework's terms, and what does it permit one to do?

The answers arrange themselves around one construction. MacDowell and Mansouri showed in 1977 that gravity's action can be written as the curvature-squared functional of an (anti-)de Sitter gauge connection \cite{MacDowellMansouri1977}, broken to Lorentz symmetry, in Stelle and West's form \cite{StelleWest1980}, by an internal vector of fixed norm whose covariant derivative is the tetrad; the geometric identity of that vector has remained an interpretive puzzle for fifty years. The framework supplies the identity in two steps, and the frozen point is the first step, not the vector itself. The frozen point is parallel: that is what the vacuum equations say. So it cannot be the Stelle-West vector, whose derivative is the tetrad. What the frozen point does is reduce the ambient $SO(2,4)$-structure to the de Sitter group $SO(1,4)$, the group MacDowell and Mansouri gauge, and then, inside the de Sitter fibre, select the Stelle-West vector canonically: the canonical tractor projected orthogonally to the frozen point (Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point}, Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}). The projected vector has squared norm $-3/\Lambda$, the square of the de Sitter radius with the sign of its fibre direction, and its covariant derivative is exactly the soldering form. Gravity's dynamical principle then reads: extremise the square of the curvature as seen from the point at infinity, the frozen point supplying the reduction and the prefactor, the point at infinity's own tractor supplying the Stelle-West slot.

Five consequences, at declared levels, organise the paper. \emph{Polynomiality} (the section ``The action of the frozen point''): the functional contains no inverse metric, so it is defined wherever the ambient bundle and connection are, in particular across the singular locus where the sheaf paper's structure continues; and its curvature-squared presentation degenerates as $\Lambda \to 0$, because the prefactor is the inverse norm of the frozen point, so the presentation exists precisely because $\Lambda \neq 0$. What survives the limit, after a topological subtraction, is the Einstein-Cartan functional: the boundary is a boundary of the presentation, not of gravity's action principle, and the paper says so. \emph{Vacating} (the section ``What the equations vacate, and what cannot evolve''): at a corank-one wall of the soldering form the field equations, which polynomiality keeps meaningful there, are strictly weaker than on the invertible region, and the paper computes exactly how much weaker, at the level of the torsion, the connection and the propagation: the equations determine the connection up to one symmetric bilinear form on the wall's tangent space, which they never propagate across the wall and which, on the flat model, they constrain by a single scalar relation (the wall's Hamiltonian constraint, with the form entering as a second extrinsic curvature); the curved-wall count is posed. The sheaf paper's wall turns out to be the dual degeneration, a cometric with a radical, at which the soldering form has a pole rather than a radical; there the wall opens exactly one new gauge generator, and that generator is the boost of the completion's ladder pair. At the Schwarzschild wall the paper then computes what the frozen-point datum does: its connection has a simple pole with the Kasner residue, the field equations reach the wall as the Kasner relations on that residue, the residues are exactly the weights the sheaf paper's completion is built from, and the curvature-squared value of the action diverges through its topological term alone, a divergence a local wall counterterm removes without touching the equations; the cosmological constant leaves the residue unchanged, and the statement holds pointwise for variable exponents. The equations do not permit or demand the completion; their singularity supplies its data. \emph{Dark energy} (the section ``What the equations vacate, and what cannot evolve''): on the vacuum region the frozen point is parallel and its norm cannot evolve, $w = -1$ exactly, a maximally rigid stance registered against the DESI record; off the vacuum region the identification needs a definition the paper does not yet have, and the registration is conditional on it. \emph{Two kinds of action} (the section ``What the equations vacate, and what cannot evolve''): the MacDowell-Mansouri mechanism does not extend to the internal factors by either of its two natural routes (the ninth refutation, shared with the Standard-Model paper): the internal forces are conformal-level, gravity alone is pre-metric, and what crosses the singularity is gravity and the $\theta$-terms. \emph{One way to grip} (the section ``One way to grip: the acoustic no-go''-the section ``The engineering conclusion, and scope''): in the neutral thermal sector of the s-wave current algebra of T5, the graviton mode is the Sugawara stress tensor and nothing outside the stress-energy sector couples to it at first order; the $(I,V)$-sector is pure gauge (the point at infinity has no physical fluctuation); the four-dimensional lift inherits the orthogonality at assembly level, the sphere's operators being boundary-mode bilinears by the counting paper's theorem, conditional on that paper's Indifference premise; and the engineering conclusion holds on either reading of the graviton's ontology, by derivation inside the framework and, at leading order, by Weinberg's soft theorem outside it.

t10-regenerated.title: The Stelle-West vector of the frozen point
t10-regenerated.text:
Let a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) be Einstein with $\Lambda \neq 0$ on its invertible region, and work in the scale $g$ of its derived metric determined by the frozen point, so that $I = (1, 0, \Lambda/6) = \nInf + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\nO$ and $\nabla I = 0$ (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}). Let $X := (0, 0, 1) = \nO$ be the canonical tractor, and define
\[
V \;:=\; X - \frac{\ip{X}{I}}{Q(I)}\, I \;=\; X - \frac{3}{\Lambda}\, I \;=\; \Bigl(-\frac{3}{\Lambda},\; 0,\; \frac12\Bigr),
\qquad
W \;:=\; \frac{V}{Q(V)} \;=\; \Bigl(1,\; 0,\; -\frac{\Lambda}{6}\Bigr) \;=\; \nInf - \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\nO .
\]
Write $e_a$ for the tractor $(0, g_{ab}, 0)$, the unit vector of the $\mu_a$ slot: on flat spacetime the physical frame vector $\hb^{-1}(a)$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $Q(X) = 0$, $\ip{X}{I} = 1$, $\ip{V}{I} = 0$, and $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda = -\ell^2$.
\item[(ii)] $\nabla_a X = e_a$, the soldering form, and $\nabla_a V = e_a$ as well; $\ip{e_a}{I} = 0$.
\item[(iii)] On a tractor with no $\mu$-component the connection \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} acts as $\nabla_a = \partial_a + e_a\wedge W$; on a general tractor it is the Levi-Civita connection on the $\mu$-slot plus the same bivector: $\nabla_a = D_a + e_a\wedge V/Q(V)$. On flat spacetime this is the $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field $\Omega_{T}(a) = \Omega(a) + \hb^{-1}(a) \wedge W$: the rotation-gauge field plus the soldering bivector built from the physical frame, with Schouten map $\tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\,\mathrm{id}$.
\item[(iv)] $[\,e_a\wedge W,\; e_b\wedge W\,] = -Q(W)\; e_a\wedge e_b = (\Lambda/3)\, e_a\wedge e_b$.
\end{enumerate}
t10-regenerated.proof:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity: the metric $g$ below is the derived metric of the gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime, the manifold is the invertible region, and the tractor connection is a flat-space $\Cl(2,4)$ gauge field, the rotation-gauge field plus the soldering bivector; the index computation below is its reading in the splitting of $g$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}).

(i) From $\ip{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)}{(\sigma',\mu',\rho')} \;=\; g(\mu,\mu') + \sigma\rho' + \rho\sigma'$: $Q(X) = 2\cdot 0\cdot 1 = 0$; $\ip{X}{I} = 0\cdot(\Lambda/6) + 1\cdot 1 = 1$; $\ip{V}{I} = \ip{X}{I} - (3/\Lambda)Q(I) = 1 - (3/\Lambda)(\Lambda/3) = 0$; $Q(V) = Q(X) - 2(3/\Lambda)\ip{X}{I} + (9/\Lambda^2)Q(I) = 0 - 6/\Lambda + 3/\Lambda = -3/\Lambda$. The formula for $W$ is then $V\cdot(-\Lambda/3) = (1, 0, -\Lambda/6)$.
(ii) Put $(\sigma,\mu,\rho) = (0,0,1)$ in \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}: $\nabla_a X = (0 - 0,\; 0 + g_{ab}\cdot 1 - P_{ab}\cdot 0,\; 0 + 0) = (0, g_{ab}, 0) = e_a$, whatever $P_{ab}$ is. In the scale, $\ip{X}{I} = 1$ and $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ are constants and $\nabla I = 0$, so $\nabla_a V = \nabla_a X = e_a$. Finally $\ip{e_a}{I} = g_{ab}\,\mu_I^b = 0$ because $\mu_I = 0$.
(iii) For $u = (\sigma,\mu,\rho)$: $\ip{W}{u} = \rho - (\Lambda/6)\sigma$ and $\ip{e_a}{u} = \mu_a$, so
$(e_a\wedge W)u = \ip{W}{u}\,e_a - \ip{e_a}{u}\,W = \bigl(-\mu_a,\; (\rho - (\Lambda/6)\sigma)\,g_{ab},\; (\Lambda/6)\,\mu_a\bigr)$,
which is exactly the non-derivative part of \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} with $P_{ab} = (\Lambda/6)g_{ab}$; the derivative part is $\partial_a$ on the $\sigma$ and $\rho$ slots and the Levi-Civita $D_a$ on the $\mu$ slot. Since $W = V/Q(V)$ the bivector is $e_a\wedge V/Q(V)$.
(iv) For any four fibre vectors, the action convention gives $[a\wedge b, c\wedge d] = \ip{b}{c}\,a\wedge d - \ip{b}{d}\,a\wedge c - \ip{a}{c}\,b\wedge d + \ip{a}{d}\,b\wedge c$, by expanding both products on a test vector $w$ and collecting the four terms. With $a = e_a$, $b = d = W$, $c = e_b$, and $\ip{e_a}{W} = \ip{e_b}{W} = 0$, $W\wedge W = 0$, only the second term survives: $-Q(W)\,e_a\wedge e_b$, and $Q(W) = 2\cdot 1\cdot(-\Lambda/6) = -\Lambda/3$. The script confirms (i), (ii) and (iv) in exact arithmetic, and (iii) by comparing the two sides of \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry} on a basis.

t10-regenerated.title: Point of contact: why the form, not the value
t10-regenerated.text: Per the series' practice the meeting point with the cosmological-constant problem is stated where it occurs, with its limits. Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(2) answers a narrower question than the one usually asked: not what value $\Lambda$ takes, and not why it is nonzero, but what its being nonzero yields. When $\Lambda \neq 0$ the frozen point has length, the ambient structure reduces to a reductive group, and gravity's action is a single curvature-squared invariant seen from the point at infinity. When $\Lambda = 0$ the frozen point is null, the prefactor $3/Q(I)$ poles, and what remains is the Einstein-Cartan functional: an action principle still, but one that no longer reads as a curvature squared and no longer sees the point at infinity. The delimiters: this is a statement about the form of the action, not about its existence; it gives no value and no smallness, and the smallness problem is not addressed and is declared so in the section ``The engineering conclusion, and scope''. That the boundary of the curvature-squared form is itself a division by zero (normalisation by a null vector, $1/Q(I)$) is, given this series' founding subject, worth recording; whether it is more than a coincidence is not something this paper can decide.

t10-regenerated.title: The wall's free sector

\item[(a)] \emph{(Torsion.)} Regarded as linear conditions on the $24$ components of the torsion, the connection equation has rank $24$ on the invertible region and rank $18$ at the point: three of its components are identities $0 = 0$ and six torsion components are freed, all tangential to the wall (every component with a leg along $r$, and the cokernel component $n_dT^d$, are forced to vanish). \]

\[

\]

\[

The remaining open item, that the four-dimensional lift might introduce a coupling invisible to the s-wave sector, is addressed by covering the spacetime in two pieces, with one step upgraded. The steps, each with its provenance:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Partial waves (exact, kinematic).} Near the horizon the four-dimensional two-point function between the graviton mode and any probe decomposes over partial waves, and the angular integration is diagonal in $\ell$ by spherical-harmonic orthogonality.
\item \emph{Near-horizon reduction (assembly, at the level it carries in T5).} Each fixed-$\ell$ sector reduces, at the horizon where the potential barrier vanishes, to a two-dimensional copy of the setting of the current algebra, in which the $\ell$-th component of the graviton mode is the $\ell$-th $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-harmonic of the current bilinears. Which operator is the stress tensor in the $\ell$-th copy is fixed by step (4), not assumed.
\item \emph{Exterior exactness (imported theorem).} On any region where the gauge-theoretic metric is invertible, the horizon included, the description coincides exactly with classical general relativity, by the geometry paper's import of gauge-theory gravity from Lasenby, Doran and Gull \cite[Fact~2.1]{ButlerT6}, whose couplings to the metric are stress-energy alone. The two pieces overlap and cover the spacetime.
\item \emph{The sphere step (conditional on the entropy paper's Indifference premise; then proved by covariance).} By the sphere theorem (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}, \cite[Thm.~5.5]{ButlerT8}, conditional on \cite[Principle~5.4]{ButlerT8}) every angular operator of the lift is a boundary-mode bilinear of definite spin under the adjoint $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, of spin $\ell \geq 1$ for every non-trivial harmonic, while the s-wave stress tensor $T$ is an $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ singlet. In an $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-invariant state the symmetry orthogonality of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} applies verbatim: nonzero spin, zero overlap. Orthogonality by dimension would \emph{not} do here, the bilinears having dimension two like $T$; it is the spin that separates them. The lift inherits the no-go because the sphere is built from the same correlations to which the no-go applies, and those correlations carry spin.
\end{enumerate}
With Propositions \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} and \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} and these steps, the acoustic programme is closed at the mixed level of its inputs: the metric-forming correlations admit exactly one coupling sector, its weakness is dimensional, its leading nonlinearity is Gertsenshtein's, and its Goldstones are eaten. Step (2), the near-horizon reduction, is at assembly level, its promotion shared with T5 and T7; step (4) is conditional on the entropy paper's Indifference premise, and the closure of the acoustic programme inherits that condition.

t10-regenerated.title: Kasner form of the interior
t10-regenerated.text:
In the interior, with $A(r) := 2M/r - 1 > 0$, the Schwarzschild gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), taken in a synchronous position gauge, has derived metric of diagonal form
\[
ds^2 \;=\; d\tau^2 - A\,dt^2 - r^2\,d\Omega^2,
\qquad
\tau(r) \;=\; \int_0^r A(u)^{-1/2}\,du ,
\]
where $\tau$ is proper time along the radial timelike worldlines ruling the interior, whose velocity $\hb^{-1}(x')$ is $D$-parallel (the geodesics of the derived metric), normalised so that the singularity is $\tau = 0$. In units $2M = 1$,
\[
\tau(r) \;=\; \tfrac23\, r^{3/2}\bigl(1 + \tfrac{3}{10}\,r + O(r^2)\bigr),
\qquad
r \;=\; R\,\bigl(1 - \tfrac15 R + O(R^2)\bigr), \quad R := (3\tau/2)^{2/3},
\]
and the scale factors obey $\sqrt{A} \propto \tau^{-1/3}$ and $r \propto \tau^{2/3}$ to leading order: the Kasner exponents of the approach are
\[
(p_1, p_2, p_3) \;=\; \bigl(-\tfrac13,\ \tfrac23,\ \tfrac23\bigr),
\qquad
p_1 + p_2 + p_3 \;=\; 1, \qquad p_1^2 + p_2^2 + p_3^2 \;=\; 1 .
\]

t10-regenerated.title: The Schwarzschild $\varphi$-lines, exactly
t10-regenerated.text:
For the Schwarzschild interior in units $2M = 1$, along a $\varphi$-coordinate line at fixed $(r, \theta)$ the Hubble-normalised generator is constant along the line,
\begin{align*}
G \;&=\; -\bigl(\tfrac23 + \delta(r)\bigr) B_{3} + \varepsilon(r)\, R_{23}, \\
\delta(r) \;&=\; \tau\sigma_{3} - \tfrac23 \;=\; -\tfrac{2}{15}\,r - \tfrac{8}{105}\,r^{2} - \tfrac{16}{315}\,r^{3} - \cdots, \\

t10-regenerated.title: The degeneration sheaf
t10-regenerated.text:
Let $(M, G)$ be a tame corank-one degeneration (Hypotheses \claimref{sheaf.tameness}), $\shA = \Cl(T^*M, G)$, and write $A(x)$ for the fibre at $x$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Over $\Mo$, each fibre $A(x)$ is isomorphic to the nondegenerate Clifford algebra of the local signature; on the interior of $\Mp$ this is $\Cl(p,q)$, on the far side $\Cl(p{-}1,q{+}1)$. In the physical case these are $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat_2(\HH)$ and $\Cl(0,4) \cong \Mat_2(\HH)$.
\item Over $x \in \Sig$, the two-sided ideal $J(x)$ of $A(x)$ generated by the radical line $\shL(x)$ is
\[
J(x) \;=\; A(x)\,k \;=\; k\,A(x), \qquad J(x)^2 = 0, \qquad \dim_\R J(x) = 2^{n-1},
\]
for any spanning $k \in \shL(x)$, and the quotient is canonically the Clifford algebra of the induced form:
\[
A(x)/J(x) \;\cong\; \Cl\bigl(T^*_xM / \shL(x),\ \overline{G}_x\bigr),
\]
where $\overline{G}_x$ is nondegenerate of rank $n-1$ and signature $(p{-}1, q)$.
\item The fibrewise ideals assemble: the multiplication map $\shA|_\Sig \otimes \shL \to \shA|_\Sig$ has image a smooth subbundle $\shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL$ of rank $2^{n-1}$, and its pushforward
\[
\shJ \;:=\; i_*\bigl(\shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL\bigr) \qquad (i : \Sig \hookrightarrow M)
\]
is a finitely presented sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_M$-modules and of $\shA$-bimodules, supported exactly on $\Sig$, with fibre $J(x)$ at $x \in \Sig$ and fibre $0$ elsewhere. The associated ideal sheaf of $\shA$ is the kernel
\[
\shK \;:=\; \ker\bigl(\shA \longrightarrow i_*\bigl(\shA|_\Sig \,/\, \shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL\bigr)\bigr),
\]
a sheaf of two-sided ideals of $\shA$ whose restriction to $\Sig$ realises $J(x)$ fibrewise and whose quotient $\shA/\shK$ is the pushforward of the quotient bundle of (2).
\end{enumerate}

t10-regenerated.text:
The question the paper ends by pointing at can itself be classified. The classification has four parts, of which the first contains a proved statement and a reading, the second is an import, the third is conditional on the first two, on Observation \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent} and on a decision the fourth names, and the fourth is imported from the action paper; the levels are marked clause by clause.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Kinematic.)} Proved: under $\Lambda \to s^{2}\Lambda$ at fixed $M_{P}$, that is $I \to sI$ on the frozen point with the conformal class unchanged, $H \to sH$ and $N \to N/s$, while every discrete invariant this paper derives (the algebra and its dimension twelve, the global form and its $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$, the dimension four, the content and the hypercharges, and under (S) the ratio $3/8$) is unchanged, since each is computed from the conformal class, the pair structure and the group alone, none of which the rescaling affects. Reading, at observation level: since the conformal class and the pair structure carry no scale, no construction from them alone can fix $N$, which lies in the ratio of the frozen point's norm to the Planck scale; on this reading the kinematic layer determines all discrete invariants and no continuous modulus, and $N$ and the weight spectrum are its only continuous moduli.
\item \emph{(Non-dynamical, imported.)} $\Lambda$ is the norm of the frozen point, and the norm is not a field: it is fixed by a constraint, the fluctuations of the frozen point are pure gauge, and the action carries no equation of motion for it (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-norm-frozen-point-not-field}).
\item \emph{(Initial data, conditional.)} If the alternatives kinematic, dynamical and initial-data are exhaustive, then by (1) and (2) $N$ is initial data, and Observation \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent}(ii) locates the boundary that carries it at the origin. \end{enumerate}

The action paper of this series builds the internal vector of gravity's MacDowell-Mansouri functional from the completion's frozen point, the parallel scale tractor $I$ whose squared norm is $\Lambda/3$: the Stelle-West vector is $V = X - (3/\Lambda)I$, made from $I$ and the canonical tractor $X$ \cite{ButlerT10}. No representation of the principal or complementary series has $m^{2} < 0$; the exceptional (discrete) series, which also contains scalar members at $\Delta = 3 + k$, $k = 1, 2, \dots$, with $m^{2} = -k(k+3)H^{2}$, is not used in this paper. \emph{Provenance:} the classification of the unitary representations is Dixmier's \cite[\S\S3--4]{Dixmier1961}; the $\Delta$-parametrisation and the mass formula for the scalar series of $SO(N,1)$ are the modern presentation, for which see \cite{Higuchi1987}. The Casimir normalisation here is the field-theoretic one on a scalar module. The de Sitter Casimir $C_{2}(I_{\Lambda}^{\perp})$ of Proposition \claimref{mass.casimir-form-join}, a quadratic form on the moment components of a composite, is in this same normalisation, with no shift between the two. What differs from the de Sitter mass is that Proposition's grip: by its clause (1) the grip equals the de Sitter mass plus $Q(I_{\Lambda}) = H^{2}$ times the composite's conformal Casimir $C_{2}(\Lambda^{2}\CS)$. Used to read Corollary \claimref{mass.weight-polynomial-two-series}, which proves the algebra of $-w(w+3)$ and imports the names of the series from here.

t11-regenerated.title: Invariant forms on a simple Lie algebra
t11-regenerated.text: On a finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra over $\C$, any two nonzero invariant symmetric bilinear forms are proportional.
t11-regenerated.proof: Let $B_{1}$ be the Killing form, nondegenerate by Cartan's criterion \cite[\S5.1]{Humphreys1972}, and $B_{2}$ invariant. Then $B_{2}(A, \cdot) = B_{1}(\phi A, \cdot)$ defines a linear $\phi$, and invariance of both forms makes $\phi$ commute with the adjoint action; the adjoint representation of a simple algebra is irreducible, so $\phi$ is a scalar by Schur's lemma \cite[\S6.1]{Humphreys1972}. Used in Proposition \claimref{mass.casimir-form-join}.
t11-regenerated.label: Lemma

t11-regenerated.title: The mass-weight dictionary
t11-regenerated.text:
Let $\sigma$ be a density of conformal weight $w$ on a vacuum Einstein background with frozen point $I$, and impose the coupling
\[
I \cdot D\sigma = 0.
\]
Then, in the scale of $I$, $\sigma$ obeys the Klein-Gordon equation $(\Box + m^{2})\sigma = 0$ with
\begin{equation}
m^{2} = -\,w(w+n-1)\,Q(I), \qquad\text{in } n = 4:\quad m^{2} = -\,w(w+3)\,\frac{\Lambda}{3} = -\,w(w+3)\,H^{2}.
\end{equation}
The mass of a field is its conformal weight, read in the units the frozen point provides, and every mass in the theory is $\sqrt{\Lambda}$ times a factor fixed by the weight.
t11-regenerated.proof:
Pair $I = (1, 0, \rho_{I})$ with $D\sigma$ (Fact \claimref{mass.imported-thomas-operator}) in the metric $\ip{(\sigma,\mu,\rho)}{(\sigma',\mu',\rho')} = \sigma\rho' + \rho\sigma' + g(\mu,\mu')$. The middle slots contribute nothing since $I$ has $\mu = 0$, leaving the two hyperbolic cross terms:
\[
I \cdot D\sigma = 1 \cdot \bigl(-(\Box\sigma - wJ\sigma)\bigr) + \rho_{I} \cdot w(n+2w-2)\,\sigma .
\]
Substituting $\rho_{I} = J/n$ from Fact \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection} and collecting the $\sigma$-terms:
\[
I \cdot D\sigma = -\Box\sigma + wJ\sigma + \frac{J}{n}\,w(n+2w-2)\,\sigma
= -\Box\sigma + \frac{wJ}{n}\bigl[n + (n+2w-2)\bigr]\sigma
= -\Box\sigma + \frac{2wJ}{n}(n+w-1)\,\sigma .
\]
Setting this to zero gives $\Box\sigma = \tfrac{2wJ}{n}(n+w-1)\,\sigma$, that is $(\Box + m^{2})\sigma = 0$ with
\[
m^{2} = -\frac{2J}{n}\,w(n+w-1) = -\,w(w+n-1)\,Q(I),
\]
the last step by $Q(I) = 2J/n$ (Fact \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection}). In $n = 4$ with $J = 2\Lambda/3$: $m^{2} = -w(w+3)\Lambda/3$. The script forms the pairing slot by slot from the two Facts, with $\sigma$ and $\Box\sigma$ as formal coordinates, and reads $m^{2}$ off the resulting Klein-Gordon equation, on a rational grid in $(w, n, J)$ and as an identity of rational functions in a formal $\Lambda$; as a consequence, the opposite sign fails the same pairing wherever $m^{2} \neq 0$, which the script also records.

t11-regenerated.title: What the dictionary does and does not yield
t11-regenerated.text: The natural conjecture, that coupling to the frozen point explains the observed masses, fails quantitatively, and the failure is the finding. The unit is $H \approx 1.5 \times 10^{-33}\,\mathrm{eV}$, so the fields with real weight in $[-3,0]$, the complementary series with its endpoints, end at $m = 3H/2$, below every known massive particle. Every known massive field is in the principal series, with $\mathrm{Re}\,w = -\tfrac32$ and $\mathrm{Im}\,w = \nu \approx m/H$, about $3 \times 10^{38}$ for the electron. The dictionary does not remove the hierarchy problem; it restates it: the hierarchy is the question of why the imaginary parts of the conformal weights of matter are so large in Hubble units. What the dictionary does yield: a single origin for mass and dark energy, both couplings to $I$; the de Sitter representation theory of matter as its $w$-classification, with the $-\tfrac32$ of the principal series read as the universal real part of every weight; and, together with the area formula of the section ``Mass as symplectic area'', a two-scale structure for the matter programme: the frozen point supplies the unit, the spinor bracket supplies the compositeness, and the internal symmetry of the multi-spinor system (many conformal spinors) is where the forces arise, taken up by the standard-model paper \cite{ButlerT12}.

t11-regenerated.title: Point of contact: the dictionary in plain words
t11-regenerated.text: The universe, in this framework, has exactly one built-in scale: the length of the point at infinity, which is the cosmological constant under another name. The theorem says that mass is how strongly a field is coupled to that one scale: each field carries a number, its weight, and its mass is that number read against that single scale. A massless field is one whose weight gives zero mass against that scale. Against the data the natural conjecture fails: the scale is the Hubble scale, whose length is cosmological, so a field whose weight is an ordinary real number is lighter than anything ever observed, and everyday particles must carry weights whose imaginary part is extremely large. The mechanism does not explain why matter is so heavy compared to dark energy; it converts that question into a new one, which is the old hierarchy problem restated. The next section adds the other half of the account from the conformal spinor side, and the section ``The exact join'' joins the two halves.

t11-regenerated.title: The de Sitter scale and its frozen point
t11-regenerated.text:
Let $\eta$ be the fixed product of flat spacetime, the chart of Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}, $Q(x) = \eta(x,x)$, and $\sigma(x) := 1 - \Lambda Q(x)/12$; on the region $\sigma \neq 0$ let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be the gravitational field with $\hb(a) = \sigma\,a$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), whose derived metric is $g = \sigma^{-2}\eta$. Write tractors in the flat scale as the vectors $\sigma\,n_{\infty} + \mu + \rho\,n_{0}$ of $\Cl(2,4)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scale tractor of $\sigma$ in the flat scale is
\[
I_{\sigma} = \bigl(\sigma,\; \nabla\sigma,\; -\tfrac14\Box\sigma\bigr) = \Bigl(1 - \frac{\Lambda Q}{12},\; -\frac{\Lambda}{6}\,x_{a},\; \frac{\Lambda}{6}\Bigr),
\]
it is parallel for the connection \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection} of $\eta$, and $\ip{I_{\sigma}}{I_{\sigma}} = \Lambda/3$ identically. Hence the derived metric $g = \sigma^{-2}\eta$ is Einstein with cosmological constant $\Lambda$, on the region $\sigma \neq 0$: the gravitational field $\hb = \sigma$ is de Sitter space on flat spacetime, and $I_{\sigma}$ is its frozen point.
\item The constant ambient vector whose scale function is $\sigma$ is
\[
I_{\Lambda} := n_{\infty} + \frac{\Lambda}{6}\, n_{0},
\]
and it is the only one: $\ip{X(x)}{n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}} = 1 - \lambda Q(x)/2$, which equals $\sigma$ iff $\lambda = \Lambda/6$, and the points $X(x)$ span the ambient space. The vector $n_{0} + \lambda n_{\infty}$, of the same norm, has scale function $\lambda - Q/2$: the inverted chart, not this one.
\item $\ip{I_{\Lambda}}{I_{\Lambda}} = 2 \cdot \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\ip{n_{\infty}}{n_{0}} = \Lambda/3$, in agreement with (1). At $\Lambda = 0$, $I_{\Lambda} = n_{\infty}$: the frozen point of flat space is the point at infinity $n_{\infty}$ of the conformal model (the infinity twistor), and, read through the Klein correspondence as a bivector, it becomes non-simple exactly when $\Lambda \neq 0$.
\end{enumerate}
t11-regenerated.proof:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity: the metric below is the derived metric of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), and the manifold is its invertible region.

\emph{(1) The scale tractor.} By Fact \claimref{mass.imported-thomas-operator} at $w = 1$ with $J = 0$ for the flat scale, the scale tractor of $\sigma$ is $\tfrac14 D\sigma = (\sigma, \nabla\sigma, -\tfrac14\Box\sigma)$. With $\nabla_{a}Q = 2x_{a}$ and $\Box Q = 2\eta^{ab}\eta_{ab} = 8$,
\[
\nabla_{a}\sigma = -\tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\,x_{a}, \qquad \Box\sigma = -\tfrac{2\Lambda}{3}, \qquad -\tfrac14\Box\sigma = \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}.
\]
\emph{Parallelism}, slot by slot in \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection} with $P = 0$: the first slot is $\nabla_{a}\sigma - \mu_{a} = 0$ by construction; the second is $\nabla_{a}\mu_{b} + \eta_{ab}\rho = -\tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\eta_{ab} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\eta_{ab} = 0$; the third is $\nabla_{a}\rho = 0$ since $\rho$ is constant. \emph{The norm:}
\[
2\sigma\rho + \eta^{ab}\mu_{a}\mu_{b} = 2\Bigl(1 - \frac{\Lambda Q}{12}\Bigr)\frac{\Lambda}{6} + \frac{\Lambda^{2}}{36}Q = \frac{\Lambda}{3}.
\]
\emph{Einstein.} The tractor metric and parallelism are scale-independent, so in the scale $\sigma$ itself, where the density is the constant $1$ and the section therefore reads $(1, 0, \rho')$ by Fact \claimref{mass.imported-thomas-operator} (its middle slot is $n\nabla 1 = 0$), with $2\rho' = \Lambda/3$, Fact \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection} gives that $g = \sigma^{-2}\eta$ is Einstein with $P_{ab} = \rho' g_{ab}$, that is with cosmological constant $6\rho' = \Lambda$.

\emph{(2) The flat-model dictionary.} In the form used here it is elementary. A section $(\sigma, \mu_{b}, \rho)$ is parallel for \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection} with $P = 0$ iff the three slot equations $\nabla_{a}\rho = 0$, $\nabla_{a}\mu_{b} = -\eta_{ab}\rho$, $\nabla_{a}\sigma = \mu_{a}$ hold; integrating them in turn,
\[
\rho = \text{const}, \qquad \mu_{b} = v_{b} - \rho\, x_{b}, \qquad \sigma = \alpha + \ip{v}{x} - \tfrac12\rho\, Q(x),
\]

The first conclusion is the chart form of \cite[Prop.~4.5(2)]{ButlerT9} (\claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor}), which states that the real bivectors act $\Sigma$-anti-Hermitianly; here it is the chart computation, in four steps. The second conclusion is this paper's.

\emph{Step 1, the criterion.} In the block form of Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}, $\Sigma = \left(\begin{smallmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, so for $A = \left(\begin{smallmatrix} A_{11} & A_{12} \\ A_{21} & A_{22}\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ the matrix $\Sigma A = \left(\begin{smallmatrix} A_{21} & A_{22} \\ A_{11} & A_{12}\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is anti-Hermitian iff $A_{12}^{\dagger} = -A_{12}$, $A_{21}^{\dagger} = -A_{21}$ and $A_{22} = -A_{11}^{\dagger}$.

\emph{Step 2, the grading and the translations.} The grading element has $A_{11} = -\tfrac12$, $A_{22} = \tfrac12$, $A_{12} = A_{21} = 0$, and satisfies the criterion. For $x$ in the slice \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}, $x = \tfrac{i}{\sqrt2}K\varepsilon$ with $K$ Hermitian, the translation block of Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}(2) is $b_{x} = x\varepsilon = \tfrac{i}{\sqrt2}K\varepsilon^{2} = -\tfrac{i}{\sqrt2}K$, anti-Hermitian.

\emph{Step 3, the special conformal generators.} The block of Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}(3) is $c_{x} = -x^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon = \tfrac{i}{\sqrt2}\,\varepsilon K^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon$ (using $\varepsilon^{\mathsf T} = -\varepsilon$), whose adjoint is $-\tfrac{i}{\sqrt2}\,\varepsilon^{\dagger}\bar{K}\varepsilon^{\dagger} = -\tfrac{i}{\sqrt2}\,\varepsilon K^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon = -c_{x}$, since $\bar K = K^{\mathsf T}$ and $\varepsilon^{\dagger} = -\varepsilon$: anti-Hermitian.

\emph{Step 4, the Lorentz generators.} For two rotations $R_{U\wedge V}(Z) = \ip{U}{Z}V - \ip{V}{Z}U$, expanding both sides on a vector $Z$ gives
\[
[R_{U\wedge V}, R_{W\wedge Y}] = \ip{U}{W}R_{V\wedge Y} - \ip{U}{Y}R_{V\wedge W} - \ip{V}{W}R_{U\wedge Y} + \ip{V}{Y}R_{U\wedge W}
\]
(the four terms are $R_{U\wedge V}R_{W\wedge Y}Z = \ip{W}{Z}\,R_{U\wedge V}Y - \ip{Y}{Z}\,R_{U\wedge V}W$ minus the same with the pairs exchanged, regrouped by which of $U, V, W, Y$ carries $Z$). For $U = x$, $V = n_{\infty}$, $W = x'$, $Y = n_{0}$ with $x, x'$ in the slice, $\ip{n_{\infty}}{x'} = \ip{x}{n_{0}} = Q(n_{\infty}) = 0$ and $\ip{n_{\infty}}{n_{0}} = 1$ leave $[R_{x\wedge n_{\infty}}, R_{x'\wedge n_{0}}] = \ip{x}{x'}R_{n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0}} + R_{x\wedge x'}$. Hence $A(x\wedge x') = [A(x\wedge n_{\infty}), A(x'\wedge n_{0})] - \ip{x}{x'}A(n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0})$ lies in $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)$, a Lie algebra, because $\ip{x}{x'}$ is real.

\emph{The span, and the grip.} The pairs $n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0}$ (one), $x\wedge n_{\infty}$ (four), $x\wedge n_{0}$ (four) and $x\wedge x'$ (six) span $\Lambda^{2}V_{\R}$, of dimension $15$, so every $A(U\wedge V)$ with $U, V \in V_{\R}$ is in $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)$, and $M_{A}$ is real there because $\Sigma A$ anti-Hermitian makes $\bar{Z}\cdot AZ$ imaginary. Then $\ip{P}{U} = M_{U\wedge I}$ is real for every $U \in V_{\R}$, and since the pairing restricted to $V_{\R}$ is a real nondegenerate form (the form of signature $(2,4)$ of Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}; in the basis $n_{\infty}, n_{0}$ and the slice \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes} its Gram matrix is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{smallmatrix}\right) \oplus \operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$), $P \in V_{\R}$. The last clause is $P \perp I_{\Lambda}$ with Fact \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection}. The script checks the commutator identity on the real points, the anti-Hermiticity of the generators for real pairs on four real points, and the reality of the pairings of $P$ with a real basis of $V_{\R}$.

t11-regenerated.title: The exact join
t11-regenerated.proof:
Conventions: the chart's complex unit, written $i$ below, is $I_{6}$, the complex unit of the conformal spinor space $\CS$, and the bar is the conjugation that reverses it; $\Som$ and $\Spi$ are the halves of $\CS$ spanned by $e_{1}, e_{2}$ and by $e_{3}, e_{4}$, the $E = -1$ and $E = +1$ eigenspaces.

(1) Expand $Z^{1}\wedge Z^{2} = (\omega^{1} + \pi^{1})\wedge(\omega^{2} + \pi^{2})$ into four terms. Pairing against $n_{\infty} = e_{1}\wedge e_{2}$ annihilates every term with an $\omega$ factor (the wedge repeats a vector of $\Som$), leaving $\varepsilon(e_{1}\wedge e_{2}\wedge\pi^{1}\wedge\pi^{2}) = \varepsilon_{a'b'}\pi_{1}^{a'}\pi_{2}^{b'}\,\varepsilon(e_{1}\wedge e_{2}\wedge e_{3}\wedge e_{4}) = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}$; pairing against $n_{0} = e_{3}\wedge e_{4}$ likewise leaves $\varepsilon(e_{3}\wedge e_{4}\wedge\omega^{1}\wedge\omega^{2}) = [\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]\,\varepsilon(e_{3}\wedge e_{4}\wedge e_{1}\wedge e_{2}) = [\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]$, the permutation being even. Linearity in $I_{\Lambda}$ gives \claimref{mass.exact-join}; at $\Lambda = 0$ the frozen point is $n_{\infty}$ (the infinity twistor) (Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}(3)).

(2) \emph{Slots of the grip.} $M_{U\wedge I}$ is linear in $U \wedge I$, so with $I_{\Lambda} = n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}$ the grip is $P = P_{\infty} + \lambda P_{0}$, where $P_{\infty} := M(n_{\infty})$ and $P_{0} := M(n_{0})$. Put $d := M_{n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0}}$, and for $x$ in the $x$-slot $p(x) := M_{x\wedge n_{\infty}}$, $k(x) := M_{x\wedge n_{0}}$, three linear forms in $x$. Then $\ip{P}{n_{\infty}} = M_{n_{\infty}\wedge I_{\Lambda}} = \lambda M_{n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0}} = \lambda d$, $\ip{P}{n_{0}} = M_{n_{0}\wedge n_{\infty}} = -d$, and $\ip{P}{x} = p(x) + \lambda k(x)$. Writing $P = \alpha n_{\infty} + \beta n_{0} + v$ with $v$ in the $x$-slot, $\alpha = \ip{P}{n_{0}} = -d$, $\beta = \ip{P}{n_{\infty}} = \lambda d$, and $\ip{v}{x} = p(x) + \lambda k(x)$ for all $x$. Hence
\[
Q(P) = 2\alpha\beta + Q(v) = -2\lambda d^{2} + Q(p) + 2\lambda\, p\cdot k + \lambda^{2}\, Q(k),
\]
where $f \cdot g$ denotes the dual metric on linear forms on the $x$-slot. By Remark \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes} the metric matrix on the $x$-slot, in the components $x^{aa'}$, is $G = -\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon$; since $\varepsilon^{2} = -1$, $G^{2} = (\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)^{2} = \varepsilon^{2}\otimes\varepsilon^{2} = 1$, so $G^{-1} = G$ and $f\cdot g = -\varepsilon_{ab}\varepsilon_{a'b'}f_{aa'}g_{bb'}$ with the same numerical symbols. Below, $u\cdot v$ for two $2$-component objects is the plain sum $\sum_{a}u_{a}v_{a}$ of products of components.

\emph{The three forms in components.} By Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}(2), $A(x\wedge n_{\infty})Z = b_{x}\pi \in \Som$, so by the relation displayed with \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism} and $M_{A}(Z^{1}, \dots, Z^{N}) := i\sum_{i=1}^{N} \bar{Z}^{i}\cdot(A Z^{i}), \qquad A \in \mathfrak{sl}(\T)$, $p(x) = i\sum_{i}\hp{\pi^{i}}{b_{x}\pi^{i}} = i\sum_{i} x^{aa'}\,\overline{\pi^{i}_{a}}\,(\varepsilon\pi^{i})_{a'}$, where $(\varepsilon\pi)_{a'} := \varepsilon_{a'b'}\pi^{b'}$ and $\overline{\pi^{i}_{a}}$ is the conjugate of the component of $\pi^{i}$ paired with $e_{a}$ by $\Sigma$. Thus $p = \sum_{i}p^{i}$ with $p^{i}_{aa'} = i\,\overline{\pi^{i}_{a}}\,(\varepsilon\pi^{i})_{a'}$. By Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}(3), $A(x\wedge n_{0})Z = c_{x}\omega \in \Spi$, so $k(x) = i\sum_{i}\overline{\hp{c_{x}\omega^{i}}{\omega^{i}}} = i\sum_{i}\sum_{a'}(c_{x}\omega^{i})^{a'}\,\overline{\omega^{i}_{a'}} = -i\sum_{i}x^{ba'}\varepsilon_{ba}\omega^{i\,a}\,\overline{\omega^{i}_{a'}}$; thus $k = \sum_{i}k^{i}$ with $k^{i}_{aa'} = -i\,(\varepsilon\omega^{i})_{a}\,\overline{\omega^{i}_{a'}}$, where $(\varepsilon\omega)_{a} := \varepsilon_{ab}\omega^{b}$. By Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}(1), $A(n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0})Z = (-\tfrac12\omega, \tfrac12\pi)$, so $\bar{Z}\cdot AZ = -\tfrac12\hp{\pi}{\omega} + \tfrac12\overline{\hp{\pi}{\omega}} = -i\,\mathrm{Im}\hp{\pi}{\omega}$ and $d = \sum_{i}\mathrm{Im}\,t_{ii} = \mathrm{Im}\tr t$.

\emph{The three pairings.} Using $\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon = 1$, $\varepsilon^{2} = -1$ and $\det\varepsilon = 1$ for the $2\times 2$ symbol:
\begin{align*}
p^{i}\cdot p^{l} &= -\varepsilon_{ab}\varepsilon_{a'b'}\,(i)^{2}\,\overline{\pi^{i}_{a}}\,\overline{\pi^{l}_{b}}\,(\varepsilon\pi^{i})_{a'}(\varepsilon\pi^{l})_{b'}
= \overline{\br{\pi^{i}\pi^{l}}}\;\br{\varepsilon\pi^{i},\varepsilon\pi^{l}} = |\br{\pi^{i}\pi^{l}}|^{2},\\
k^{i}\cdot k^{l} &= -\varepsilon_{ab}\varepsilon_{a'b'}\,(-i)^{2}\,(\varepsilon\omega^{i})_{a}(\varepsilon\omega^{l})_{b}\,\overline{\omega^{i}_{a'}}\,\overline{\omega^{l}_{b'}}
= [\varepsilon\omega^{i},\varepsilon\omega^{l}]\;\overline{[\omega^{i}\omega^{l}]} = |[\omega^{i}\omega^{l}]|^{2},\\
p^{i}\cdot k^{l} &= -\varepsilon_{ab}\varepsilon_{a'b'}\,(i)(-i)\,\overline{\pi^{i}_{a}}\,(\varepsilon\omega^{l})_{b}\,(\varepsilon\pi^{i})_{a'}\,\overline{\omega^{l}_{b'}}
= -\bigl(-\overline{\pi^{i}}\cdot\omega^{l}\bigr)\bigl(\pi^{i}\cdot\overline{\omega^{l}}\bigr) = t_{il}\,\overline{t_{il}} = |t_{il}|^{2},
\end{align*}
where in the last line $\varepsilon_{ab}u_{a}(\varepsilon v)_{b} = u^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon\varepsilon v = -u\cdot v$ and $\varepsilon_{a'b'}(\varepsilon u)_{a'}v_{b'} = u^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon v = u\cdot v$. Summing over $i, l$: $Q(p) = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2}$ (the diagonal terms vanish, and this is Proposition \claimref{mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula} again), $Q(k) = 2|[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]|^{2}$, and $p\cdot k = \sum_{i,l}|t_{il}|^{2}$. Therefore
\[
Q(P) = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2} + 2\lambda^{2}|[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]|^{2} + 2\lambda\Bigl(\sum_{i,l}|t_{il}|^{2} - (\mathrm{Im}\tr t)^{2}\Bigr).
\]

\emph{The comparison.} $2|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2} + 2\lambda^{2}|[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]|^{2} + 4\lambda\,\mathrm{Re}\bigl(\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\,\overline{[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]}\bigr)$. The matrix $t$ is the product of the matrix with rows $\overline{\pi^{1}}, \overline{\pi^{2}}$ and the matrix with columns $\omega^{1}, \omega^{2}$, so $\det t = \overline{\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}}\,[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]$ and $\mathrm{Re}\det t = \mathrm{Re}\bigl(\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\overline{[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]}\bigr)$. It remains to show
\[
\sum_{i,l}|t_{il}|^{2} - (\mathrm{Im}\tr t)^{2} - 2\,\mathrm{Re}\det t \;=\; C .
\]
With $h_{11} = 2\,\mathrm{Re}\,t_{11}$, $h_{22} = 2\,\mathrm{Re}\,t_{22}$, $h_{12} = t_{12} + \overline{t_{21}}$, the right side is $(\mathrm{Re}\,t_{11} - \mathrm{Re}\,t_{22})^{2} + |t_{12}|^{2} + |t_{21}|^{2} + 2\,\mathrm{Re}(t_{12}t_{21})$, and the left side is $|t_{11}|^{2} + |t_{22}|^{2} + |t_{12}|^{2} + |t_{21}|^{2} - (\mathrm{Im}\,t_{11} + \mathrm{Im}\,t_{22})^{2} - 2\,\mathrm{Re}(t_{11}t_{22}) + 2\,\mathrm{Re}(t_{12}t_{21})$. Their difference is
\[
|t_{11}|^{2} + |t_{22}|^{2} - (\mathrm{Im}\,t_{11} + \mathrm{Im}\,t_{22})^{2} - 2\,\mathrm{Re}(t_{11}t_{22}) - (\mathrm{Re}\,t_{11} - \mathrm{Re}\,t_{22})^{2},
\]
and writing $t_{jj} = r_{j} + i s_{j}$ this is $(r_{1}^{2} + s_{1}^{2} + r_{2}^{2} + s_{2}^{2}) - (s_{1} + s_{2})^{2} - 2(r_{1}r_{2} - s_{1}s_{2}) - (r_{1} - r_{2})^{2} = 0$. Hence $Q(P) = 2|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} + 2\lambda C$, and $2\lambda = Q(I_{\Lambda}) = \Lambda/3$ by Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}(3). The identities for $C$ in the relation displayed with \claimref{mass.grip-real} are the $2\times 2$ identities $\tr(h_{0}^{2}) = \tr h^{2} - \tfrac12(\tr h)^{2}$ and $\tr h^{2} = (\tr h)^{2} - 2\det h$.

(3) At $\lambda = 0$ the formula reduces to its first term, and (1) identifies $B_{0}$ with $\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}} = \ip{n_{\infty}}{Z^{1}\wedge Z^{2}}$.

(4) In the chart of Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity} the line of $x$ is the graph $L_{x} = \{\mu_{x}\pi + \pi : \pi \in \Spi\}$ of the map $\mu_{x}: \Spi \to \Som$, $(\mu_{x}\pi)^{a} = x^{aa'}\varepsilon_{b'a'}\pi^{b'}$, that is $\mu_{x} = -b_{x}$ in the notation of Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism} \cite[Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT9} (\claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart}); indeed $(\mu_{x}e_{3} + e_{3})\wedge(\mu_{x}e_{4} + e_{4}) = n_{0} + \mu_{x}e_{3}\wedge e_{4} + e_{3}\wedge\mu_{x}e_{4} + \det(\mu_{x})\,n_{\infty} = n_{0} + x^{a4}e_{a}\wedge e_{4} + x^{a3}e_{a}\wedge e_{3} + \det(x^{aa'})\,n_{\infty} = X(x)$, since $\det\mu_{x} = \det(x^{aa'}) = -\tfrac12 Q(x)$ by Remark \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}. Two conformal spinors on $L_{x}$ are $Z^{i} = \mu_{x}\pi^{i} + \pi^{i}$, and bilinearity with antisymmetry gives $Z^{1}\wedge Z^{2} = \pi_{1}^{a'}\pi_{2}^{b'}\,(\mu_{x}e_{a'} + e_{a'})\wedge(\mu_{x}e_{b'} + e_{b'}) = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\,(\mu_{x}e_{3} + e_{3})\wedge(\mu_{x}e_{4} + e_{4}) = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\,X(x)$. Then $B_{\Lambda} = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\ip{I_{\Lambda}}{X(x)} = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\,\sigma(x)$ by Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}(2).

(5) Both terms of \claimref{mass.exact-join} are nonnegative for $\Lambda > 0$, and $C = 0$ iff $h_{11} = h_{22}$ and $h_{12} = 0$. For $Z^{2} = Z^{1}$: $Z\wedge Z = 0$ gives $B_{\Lambda} = 0$; $h = h_{11}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ gives $C = \tfrac14\cdot 0 + h_{11}^{2}$. For the example, $\omega^{1} = e_{1}$, $\pi^{1} = e_{4}$, $\omega^{2} = \alpha e_{1}$, $\pi^{2} = \beta e_{4}$: both brackets vanish, so $B_{\Lambda} = 0$; every $t_{il} = \hp{\pi^{i}}{\omega^{l}}$ pairs a multiple of $e_{4}$ (which $\Sigma$ identifies with $e_{2}$) against a multiple of $e_{1}$ and vanishes, so $h = 0$; and $Z^{1}\wedge Z^{2} = (\beta - \alpha)\,e_{1}\wedge e_{4} \neq 0$. The script builds $P$ from the exact spin isomorphism and the moment map, on ten spinor pairs, and confirms (2) as an identity in $\lambda$ (all three coefficients of the quadratic in $\lambda$), the assembled values $Q(P_{\infty})$, $Q(P_{0})$ and $\ip{P_{\infty}}{P_{0}}$ against their closed forms with $p\cdot k$, $d$ and $\det t$ formed from the components of the proof, (3), the wedge identity and the factor $\sigma(x)$ of (4), and both parts of (5).
