where $f \cdot g$ denotes the dual metric on linear forms on the $x$-slot. By Remark 5.2 the metric matrix on the $x$-slot, in the components $x^{aa'}$, is $G = -\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon$; since $\varepsilon^{2} = -1$, $G^{2} = (\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)^{2} = \varepsilon^{2}\otimes\varepsilon^{2} = 1$, so $G^{-1} = G$ and $f\cdot g = -\varepsilon_{ab}\varepsilon_{a'b'}f_{aa'}g_{bb'}$ with the same numerical symbols. Below, $u\cdot v$ for two $2$-component objects is the plain sum $\sum_{a}u_{a}v_{a}$ of products of components.

\emph{The three forms in components.} By Lemma 5.3(2), $A(x\wedge n_{\infty})Z = b_{x}\pi \in \Sc$, so by (7) and (8), $p(x) = i\sum_{i}\hp{\pi^{i}}{b_{x}\pi^{i}} = i\sum_{i} x^{aa'}\,\overline{\pi^{i}_{a}}\,(\varepsilon\pi^{i})_{a'}$, where $(\varepsilon\pi)_{a'} := \varepsilon_{a'b'}\pi^{b'}$ and $\overline{\pi^{i}_{a}}$ is the conjugate of the component of $\pi^{i}$ paired with $e_{a}$ by $\Sigma$. Thus $p = \sum_{i}p^{i}$ with $p^{i}_{aa'} = i\,\overline{\pi^{i}_{a}}\,(\varepsilon\pi^{i})_{a'}$. By Lemma 5.3(3), $A(x\wedge n_{0})Z = c_{x}\omega \in \Sc'$, so $k(x) = i\sum_{i}\overline{\hp{c_{x}\omega^{i}}{\omega^{i}}} = i\sum_{i}\sum_{a'}(c_{x}\omega^{i})^{a'}\,\overline{\omega^{i}_{a'}} = -i\sum_{i}x^{ba'}\varepsilon_{ba}\omega^{i\,a}\,\overline{\omega^{i}_{a'}}$; thus $k = \sum_{i}k^{i}$ with $k^{i}_{aa'} = -i\,(\varepsilon\omega^{i})_{a}\,\overline{\omega^{i}_{a'}}$, where $(\varepsilon\omega)_{a} := \varepsilon_{ab}\omega^{b}$. By Lemma 5.3(1), $A(n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0})Z = (-\tfrac12\omega, \tfrac12\pi)$, so $\bar{Z}\cdot AZ = -\tfrac12\hp{\pi}{\omega} + \tfrac12\overline{\hp{\pi}{\omega}} = -i\,\mathrm{Im}\hp{\pi}{\omega}$ and $d = \sum_{i}\mathrm{Im}\,t_{ii} = \mathrm{Im}\tr t$.

\emph{The three pairings.} Using $\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon = 1$, $\varepsilon^{2} = -1$ and $\det\varepsilon = 1$ for the $2\times 2$ symbol:
\begin{align*}
p^{i}\cdot p^{l} &= -\varepsilon_{ab}\varepsilon_{a'b'}\,(i)^{2}\,\overline{\pi^{i}_{a}}\,\overline{\pi^{l}_{b}}\,(\varepsilon\pi^{i})_{a'}(\varepsilon\pi^{l})_{b'}
= \overline{\br{\pi^{i}\pi^{l}}}\;\br{\varepsilon\pi^{i},\varepsilon\pi^{l}} = |\br{\pi^{i}\pi^{l}}|^{2},\\
k^{i}\cdot k^{l} &= -\varepsilon_{ab}\varepsilon_{a'b'}\,(-i)^{2}\,(\varepsilon\omega^{i})_{a}(\varepsilon\omega^{l})_{b}\,\overline{\omega^{i}_{a'}}\,\overline{\omega^{l}_{b'}}
= [\varepsilon\omega^{i},\varepsilon\omega^{l}]\;\overline{[\omega^{i}\omega^{l}]} = |[\omega^{i}\omega^{l}]|^{2},\\
p^{i}\cdot k^{l} &= -\varepsilon_{ab}\varepsilon_{a'b'}\,(i)(-i)\,\overline{\pi^{i}_{a}}\,(\varepsilon\omega^{l})_{b}\,(\varepsilon\pi^{i})_{a'}\,\overline{\omega^{l}_{b'}}
= -\bigl(-\overline{\pi^{i}}\cdot\omega^{l}\bigr)\bigl(\pi^{i}\cdot\overline{\omega^{l}}\bigr) = t_{il}\,\overline{t_{il}} = |t_{il}|^{2},
\end{align*}
where in the last line $\varepsilon_{ab}u_{a}(\varepsilon v)_{b} = u^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon\varepsilon v = -u\cdot v$ and $\varepsilon_{a'b'}(\varepsilon u)_{a'}v_{b'} = u^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon v = u\cdot v$. Therefore
\[
\ip{P}{P} = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2} + 2\lambda^{2}|[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]|^{2} + 2\lambda\Bigl(\sum_{i,l}|t_{il}|^{2} - (\mathrm{Im}\tr t)^{2}\Bigr).
\]

The matrix $t$ is the product of the matrix with rows $\overline{\pi^{1}}, \overline{\pi^{2}}$ and the matrix with columns $\omega^{1}, \omega^{2}$, so $\det t = \overline{\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}}\,[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]$ and $\mathrm{Re}\det t = \mathrm{Re}\bigl(\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\overline{[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]}\bigr)$. It remains to show
\[
\sum_{i,l}|t_{il}|^{2} - (\mathrm{Im}\tr t)^{2} - 2\,\mathrm{Re}\det t \;=\; C .
\]
With $h_{11} = 2\,\mathrm{Re}\,t_{11}$, $h_{22} = 2\,\mathrm{Re}\,t_{22}$, $h_{12} = t_{12} + \overline{t_{21}}$, the right side is $(\mathrm{Re}\,t_{11} - \mathrm{Re}\,t_{22})^{2} + |t_{12}|^{2} + |t_{21}|^{2} + 2\,\mathrm{Re}(t_{12}t_{21})$, and the left side is $|t_{11}|^{2} + |t_{22}|^{2} + |t_{12}|^{2} + |t_{21}|^{2} - (\mathrm{Im}\,t_{11} + \mathrm{Im}\,t_{22})^{2} - 2\,\mathrm{Re}(t_{11}t_{22}) + 2\,\mathrm{Re}(t_{12}t_{21})$. Their difference is
\[
|t_{11}|^{2} + |t_{22}|^{2} - (\mathrm{Im}\,t_{11} + \mathrm{Im}\,t_{22})^{2} - 2\,\mathrm{Re}(t_{11}t_{22}) - (\mathrm{Re}\,t_{11} - \mathrm{Re}\,t_{22})^{2},
\]
and writing $t_{jj} = r_{j} + i s_{j}$ this is $(r_{1}^{2} + s_{1}^{2} + r_{2}^{2} + s_{2}^{2}) - (s_{1} + s_{2})^{2} - 2(r_{1}r_{2} - s_{1}s_{2}) - (r_{1} - r_{2})^{2} = 0$. Hence $\ip{P}{P} = 2|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} + 2\lambda C$, and $2\lambda = \ip{I_{\Lambda}}{I_{\Lambda}} = \Lambda/3$ by Lemma 5.1(3). The identities for $C$ in (9) are the $2\times 2$ identities $\tr(h_{0}^{2}) = \tr h^{2} - \tfrac12(\tr h)^{2}$ and $\tr h^{2} = (\tr h)^{2} - 2\det h$.

(3) At $\lambda = 0$ the formula reduces to its first term, and (1) identifies $B_{0}$ with $\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}} = \ip{n_{\infty}}{Z^{1}\wedge Z^{2}}$.

(4) In the chart of Fact 2.3 the incidence line of $x$ is the graph $L_{x} = \{\mu_{x}\pi + \pi : \pi \in \Sc'\}$ of the map $\mu_{x}: \Sc' \to \Sc$, $(\mu_{x}\pi)^{a} = x^{aa'}\varepsilon_{b'a'}\pi^{b'}$, that is $\mu_{x} = -b_{x}$ in the notation of Lemma 5.3 [ButlerT9, Thm.~4.2]; indeed $(\mu_{x}e_{3} + e_{3})\wedge(\mu_{x}e_{4} + e_{4}) = n_{0} + \mu_{x}e_{3}\wedge e_{4} + e_{3}\wedge\mu_{x}e_{4} + \det(\mu_{x})\,n_{\infty} = n_{0} + x^{a4}e_{a}\wedge e_{4} + x^{a3}e_{a}\wedge e_{3} + \det(x^{aa'})\,n_{\infty} = X(x)$, since $\det\mu_{x} = \det(x^{aa'}) = -\tfrac12 Q(x)$ by Remark 5.2. Then $B_{\Lambda} = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\ip{I_{\Lambda}}{X(x)} = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\,\sigma(x)$ by Lemma 5.1(2).

(5) Both terms of (11) are nonnegative for $\Lambda > 0$, and $C = 0$ iff $h_{11} = h_{22}$ and $h_{12} = 0$. For $Z^{2} = Z^{1}$: $Z\wedge Z = 0$ gives $B_{\Lambda} = 0$; $h = h_{11}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ gives $C = \tfrac14\cdot 0 + h_{11}^{2}$. The script builds $P$ from the exact spin isomorphism and the moment map, on ten twistor pairs, and confirms (2) as an identity in $\lambda$ (all three coefficients of the quadratic in $\lambda$), the assembled values $\ip{P_{\infty}}{P_{\infty}}$, $\ip{P_{0}}{P_{0}}$ and $\ip{P_{\infty}}{P_{0}}$ against their closed forms with $p\cdot k$, $d$ and $\det t$ formed from the components of the proof, (3), the wedge identity and the factor $\sigma(x)$ of (4), and both parts of (5).

t11-regenerated.title: The Casimir form of the join
t11-regenerated.proof:
Conventions: the chart's complex unit, written $i$ below, is $I_{6}$, the complex unit of the conformal spinor space $\CS$, and the bar is the conjugation that reverses it.

(1) Take a basis $e_{1}, \dots, e_{5}$ of $I^{\perp}$ and $e_{6} = I$; then $g^{a6} = 0$ for $a \le 5$ and $g^{66} = 1/Q(I)$. In $\tfrac12 g^{\alpha\alpha'}g^{\beta\beta'}M_{\alpha\beta}M_{\alpha'\beta'}$ the terms with no index equal to $6$ sum to $C_{2}(I^{\perp})$; the terms with exactly one $6$ in $(\alpha,\beta)$ need exactly one $6$ in $(\alpha',\beta')$ in the matching position, giving $\tfrac12\bigl(g^{ab}g^{66}M_{a6}M_{b6} + g^{66}g^{ab}M_{6a}M_{6b}\bigr) = g^{66}g^{ab}M_{a6}M_{b6}$; terms with $\alpha = \beta = 6$ vanish since $M_{66} = 0$. Now $M_{a6} = M_{e_{a}\wedge I} = \ip{P}{e_{a}}$, and $P \in I^{\perp}$, so $g^{ab}\ip{P}{e_{a}}\ip{P}{e_{b}} = Q(P)$. Hence $C_{2}(\Lambda^{2}\CS) = C_{2}(I^{\perp}) + Q(P)/Q(I)$.

(2) \emph{The moment element.} Let $\mathsf{M} := i\sum_{i}Z^{i}\otimes(\bar{Z}^{i}\cdot\,)$ be the endomorphism $W \mapsto i\sum_{i}Z^{i}\,(\bar{Z}^{i}\cdot W)$ of $\CS$, so that $M_{A} = \tr(\mathsf{M}A)$ by $M_{A}(Z^{1}, \dots, Z^{N}) := i\sum_{i=1}^{N} \bar{Z}^{i}\cdot(A Z^{i}), \qquad A \in \mathfrak{sl}(\T)$, and let $\mathsf{M}_{0}$ be its traceless part; since every $A_{\alpha\beta} := A(e_{\alpha}\wedge e_{\beta})$ is traceless, $M_{\alpha\beta} = \tr(\mathsf{M}_{0}A_{\alpha\beta})$.

\emph{An invariant form.} Put
\[
\Phi(A, B) := \tfrac12\, g^{\alpha\alpha'}g^{\beta\beta'}\,\tr(AA_{\alpha\beta})\,\tr(BA_{\alpha'\beta'})
\]
on $\mathfrak{sl}(\CS)$, so that $C_{2}(\Lambda^{2}\CS) = \Phi(\mathsf{M}_{0}, \mathsf{M}_{0})$. It is symmetric, and invariant: under $A \mapsto \gamma A\gamma^{-1}$ the matrices $A_{\alpha\beta}$ transform by the rotation of the ambient basis induced by $\gamma$ (Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}), and the contraction with $g^{\alpha\alpha'}g^{\beta\beta'}$ is invariant under rotations of the basis. By Lemma \claimref{mass.invariant-forms-simple-lie-algebra}, $\Phi(A,B) = \kappa\tr(AB)$ for a constant $\kappa$.

\emph{The constant.} Evaluate at $A = B = \mathsf{E} := A(n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0}) = \operatorname{diag}(-\tfrac12,-\tfrac12,\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$, the grading element, in the basis $n_{\infty}, n_{0}$, $x$-slot. For a translation or special conformal generator $\tr(\mathsf{E}A_{\alpha\beta}) = 0$, the blocks being off-diagonal (Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}). For a rotation of the $x$-slot: it annihilates $n_{\infty}$ and $n_{0}$, and an $A$ with $A\cdot n_{\infty} = 0$ has no $\Som \to \Spi$ block (the mixed component of $Ae_{1}\wedge e_{2} + e_{1}\wedge Ae_{2}$ is that block applied to $e_{1}, e_{2}$) and traceless $\Som$-block (the $n_{\infty}$-component is $\tr_{\Som}A$), and likewise from $n_{0}$; so $\tr(\mathsf{E}A_{\alpha\beta}) = -\tfrac12\tr_{\Som}A + \tfrac12\tr_{\Spi}A = 0$. Finally $\tr(\mathsf{E}\,A(n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0})) = \tr \mathsf{E}^{2} = 1$ and $\tr(\mathsf{E}\,A(n_{0}\wedge n_{\infty})) = -1$. With $g^{\infty 0} = g^{0\infty} = 1$ and $g^{\infty\infty} = g^{00} = 0$ the only surviving terms of $\Phi(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E})$ are $(\alpha\beta, \alpha'\beta') = (\infty 0, 0\infty)$ and $(0\infty, \infty 0)$, each contributing $-1$, so $\Phi(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}) = -1 = \kappa\tr \mathsf{E}^{2} = \kappa$.

\emph{The value.} Hence $C_{2}(\Lambda^{2}\CS) = -\tr(\mathsf{M}_{0}^{2})$. Now $\tr\mathsf{M} = i\sum_{i}\bar{Z}^{i}\cdot Z^{i} = i\tr h$ and $\tr\mathsf{M}^{2} = -\sum_{i,l}(\bar{Z}^{i}\cdot Z^{l})(\bar{Z}^{l}\cdot Z^{i}) = -\tr(h^{2})$ ($h$ is Hermitian), so $-\tr(\mathsf{M}_{0}^{2}) = -\tr\mathsf{M}^{2} + \tfrac14(\tr\mathsf{M})^{2} = \tr(h^{2}) - \tfrac14(\tr h)^{2}$.

(3) Combine (1), (2) and \claimref{mass.exact-join}: $C_{2}(I_{\Lambda}^{\perp}) = \tr h^{2} - \tfrac14(\tr h)^{2} - C - 6|B_{\Lambda}|^{2}/\Lambda$, and $\tr h^{2} - \tfrac14(\tr h)^{2} - C = \tfrac12\tr h^{2} = \tfrac14(\tr h)^{2} + C$ by the relation displayed with \claimref{mass.grip-real}. The script forms both Casimirs from the exact moment components in adapted bases and confirms (1), (2) and (3) on four pairs, together with $\tr\mathsf{E}^{2} = 1$.

t11-regenerated.title: The five broken generators
t11-regenerated.text: Let $\Omega_{I}(u,v) := \ip{I}{u\wedge v}$ be the $2$-form on the conformal spinor space $\CS$ (twistor space) of an ambient vector $I$; it is nondegenerate iff $I$ is non-simple iff $Q(I) \neq 0$. For such $I$, the elements $A \in \mathfrak{sl}(\CS)$ with $\Omega_{I}A$ symmetric form the stabiliser of $I$, of dimension $10$ (six conditions on $\mathfrak{gl}(\CS)$, none of which is the trace); the elements with $\Omega_{I}A$ antisymmetric form a $6$-dimensional complement in $\mathfrak{gl}(\CS)$, cut to $5$ by the trace; and the five generators $A(e_{a}\wedge I)$, $e_{a}$ a basis of $I^{\perp}$, are an independent basis of that $5$-dimensional complement. On the real form, for the frozen point with $\Lambda > 0$, the stabiliser is $\mathfrak{so}(1,4)$ and the five are the de Sitter translations, the $I$-half of the nine Goldstone modes of the action paper \cite[Prop.~5.4]{ButlerT10}.
t11-regenerated.proof:
The components of $\Omega_{I}$ are $\varepsilon(I\wedge e_{k}\wedge e_{l})$, the Hodge dual of $I$, and its Pfaffian is a nonzero multiple of $\varepsilon(I\wedge I) = Q(I)$; so $\Omega_{I}$ is nondegenerate iff $Q(I) \neq 0$, which is the non-simplicity of $I$ (Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}(3)). For $A \in \mathfrak{gl}(\CS)$ put $\beta_{A}(u,v) := \Omega_{I}(u, Av) = u^{\mathsf T}\Omega_{I}Av$; since $\Omega_{I}^{\mathsf T} = -\Omega_{I}$, $\Omega_{I}(Au,v) = -\beta_{A}(v,u)$, so $\Omega_{I}(Au,v) + \Omega_{I}(u,Av) = \beta_{A}(u,v) - \beta_{A}(v,u)$, and $A$ preserves $\Omega_{I}$ iff $\beta_{A}$, that is the matrix $\Omega_{I}A$, is symmetric. By invariance of the pairing under the action of $\mathfrak{sl}(\CS)$ (Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}), $\ip{I}{A\cdot(u\wedge v)} = -\ip{A\cdot I}{u\wedge v}$, so $\Omega_{I}(Au,v) + \Omega_{I}(u,Av) = -\Omega_{A\cdot I}(u,v)$: preserving $\Omega_{I}$ is the same as stabilising $I$, and the antisymmetric part of $\beta_{A}$ is $-\tfrac12\Omega_{A\cdot I}$. Symmetry of a $4\times 4$ matrix is six conditions, so the stabiliser is $10$-dimensional; it is $\mathfrak{sp}(\Omega_{I}) \cong \mathfrak{so}(I^{\perp})$, whose elements are traceless. Antisymmetry is ten conditions, leaving the $6$-dimensional space $\{A : \Omega_{I}A \text{ antisymmetric}\}$, on which $A \mapsto A\cdot I$ is injective (an antisymmetric $\beta_{A}$ equal to $-\tfrac12\Omega_{A\cdot I}$ vanishes iff $A\cdot I = 0$, and then $A = 0$ by nondegeneracy), hence a bijection onto $\Lambda^{2}\CS$; $\mathfrak{gl}(\CS)$ is the direct sum of the two parts. The identity lies in the antisymmetric part ($\beta_{1} = \Omega_{I}$) and has trace $4$, so the trace cuts that part to a $5$-dimensional complement of the stabiliser inside $\mathfrak{sl}(\CS)$.

For $U \in I^{\perp}$, $A(U\wedge I)$ is not in the stabiliser, since $R_{U\wedge I}(I) = \ip{U}{I}I - Q(I)U = -Q(I)U \neq 0$, and $U \mapsto A(U\wedge I)$ is linear and injective on $I^{\perp}$. Its image lies in the antisymmetric part by equivariance: under the stabiliser $\mathfrak{so}(I^{\perp})$, $I^{\perp}$ is the $5$-dimensional vector representation and the stabiliser itself is the $10$-dimensional adjoint representation, irreducible and non-isomorphic, while $\mathfrak{gl}(\CS) = \mathfrak{sp}(\Omega_{I}) \oplus \{\text{antisymmetric part}\}$ is a decomposition into $\mathfrak{so}(I^{\perp})$-submodules (both conditions are invariant under conjugation by the stabiliser); the map $U \mapsto A(U\wedge I)$ is $\mathfrak{so}(I^{\perp})$-equivariant, so by Schur's lemma its component in $\mathfrak{sp}(\Omega_{I})$ vanishes. Since the five images are traceless (all of $A(\cdot)$ is), they span the $5$-dimensional traceless antisymmetric part. The real-form statement is Fact \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection}'s stabiliser together with the count $15 - 10 = 5$; the action paper's Proposition 5.4 counts nine broken generators for the pair $(I, V)$, of which the five directions of $I^{\perp}$ are the $I$-half. The script confirms the dimensions $10$, $6$ and $5$ by exact rank at $\Lambda = 3$ and checks directly that the five matrices $A(e_{a}\wedge I_{\Lambda})$ are traceless, independent, and have $\Omega A$ antisymmetric.

deposited.statement: Let $\Omega_{I}(u,v) := \ip{I}{u\wedge v}$ be the $2$-form on $\T$ of an ambient vector $I$; it is nondegenerate iff $I$ is non-simple iff $\ip{I}{I} \neq 0$. For such $I$, the elements $A \in \mathfrak{sl}(\T)$ with $\Omega_{I}A$ symmetric form the stabiliser of $I$, of dimension $10$ (six conditions on $\mathfrak{gl}(\T)$, none of which is the trace); the elements with $\Omega_{I}A$ antisymmetric form a $6$-dimensional complement in $\mathfrak{gl}(\T)$, cut to $5$ by the trace; and the five generators $A(e_{a}\wedge I)$, $e_{a}$ a basis of $I^{\perp}$, are an independent basis of that $5$-dimensional complement. On the real form, for the frozen point with $\Lambda > 0$, the stabiliser is $\mathfrak{so}(1,4)$ and the five are the de Sitter translations, the $I$-half of the nine Goldstone modes of the action paper [ButlerT10, Prop.~5.4].
deposited.proof:
The components of $\Omega_{I}$ are $\varepsilon(I\wedge e_{k}\wedge e_{l})$, the Hodge dual of $I$, and its Pfaffian is a nonzero multiple of $\varepsilon(I\wedge I) = \ip{I}{I}$; so $\Omega_{I}$ is nondegenerate iff $\ip{I}{I} \neq 0$, which is the non-simplicity of $I$ (Lemma 5.1(3)). For $A \in \mathfrak{gl}(\T)$ put $\beta_{A}(u,v) := \Omega_{I}(u, Av) = u^{\mathsf T}\Omega_{I}Av$; since $\Omega_{I}^{\mathsf T} = -\Omega_{I}$, $\Omega_{I}(Au,v) = -\beta_{A}(v,u)$, so $\Omega_{I}(Au,v) + \Omega_{I}(u,Av) = \beta_{A}(u,v) - \beta_{A}(v,u)$, and $A$ preserves $\Omega_{I}$ iff $\beta_{A}$, that is the matrix $\Omega_{I}A$, is symmetric. By invariance of the pairing, $\ip{I}{A\cdot(u\wedge v)} = -\ip{A\cdot I}{u\wedge v}$, so $\Omega_{I}(Au,v) + \Omega_{I}(u,Av) = -\Omega_{A\cdot I}(u,v)$: preserving $\Omega_{I}$ is the same as stabilising $I$, and the antisymmetric part of $\beta_{A}$ is $-\tfrac12\Omega_{A\cdot I}$. Symmetry of a $4\times 4$ matrix is six conditions, so the stabiliser is $10$-dimensional; it is $\mathfrak{sp}(\Omega_{I}) \cong \mathfrak{so}(I^{\perp})$, whose elements are traceless. Antisymmetry is ten conditions, leaving the $6$-dimensional space $\{A : \Omega_{I}A \text{ antisymmetric}\}$, on which $A \mapsto A\cdot I$ is injective (an antisymmetric $\beta_{A}$ equal to $-\tfrac12\Omega_{A\cdot I}$ vanishes iff $A\cdot I = 0$, and then $A = 0$ by nondegeneracy), hence a bijection onto $\Lambda^{2}\T$; $\mathfrak{gl}(\T)$ is the direct sum of the two parts. The identity lies in the antisymmetric part ($\beta_{1} = \Omega_{I}$) and has trace $4$, so the trace cuts that part to a $5$-dimensional complement of the stabiliser inside $\mathfrak{sl}(\T)$.

For $U \in I^{\perp}$, $A(U\wedge I)$ is not in the stabiliser, since $R_{U\wedge I}(I) = \ip{U}{I}I - \ip{I}{I}U = -\ip{I}{I}U \neq 0$, and $U \mapsto A(U\wedge I)$ is linear and injective on $I^{\perp}$. Its image lies in the antisymmetric part by equivariance: under the stabiliser $\mathfrak{so}(I^{\perp})$, $I^{\perp}$ is the $5$-dimensional vector representation and the stabiliser itself is the $10$-dimensional adjoint representation, irreducible and non-isomorphic, while $\mathfrak{gl}(\T) = \mathfrak{sp}(\Omega_{I}) \oplus \{\text{antisymmetric part}\}$ is a decomposition into $\mathfrak{so}(I^{\perp})$-submodules (both conditions are invariant under conjugation by the stabiliser); the map $U \mapsto A(U\wedge I)$ is $\mathfrak{so}(I^{\perp})$-equivariant, so by Schur's lemma its component in $\mathfrak{sp}(\Omega_{I})$ vanishes. Since the five images are traceless (all of $A(\cdot)$ is), they span the $5$-dimensional traceless antisymmetric part. The real-form statement is Fact 2.1's stabiliser together with the count $15 - 10 = 5$; the action paper's Proposition 5.4 counts nine broken generators for the pair $(I, V)$, of which the five directions of $I^{\perp}$ are the $I$-half. The script confirms the dimensions $10$, $6$ and $5$ by exact rank at $\Lambda = 3$ and checks directly that the five matrices $A(e_{a}\wedge I_{\Lambda})$ are traceless, independent, and have $\Omega A$ antisymmetric.

t11-regenerated.title: Point of contact: what gravity is, and why everything falls the same way
t11-regenerated.text: Assembling this paper with the action paper gives the following account, each claim at its declared level. First: mass is coupling to the frozen point, at theorem level for fields (Theorem \claimref{mass.mass-weight-dictionary}) and, for composites, by Definition \claimref{obj.mass.grip-mass-composite} with the closed form of Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join}; and gravity's action is the MacDowell-Mansouri functional of the frozen point (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}, whose action clause rests on an identity imported at assembly level). So matter and gravity are two relations to the same object: a massive field couples to $I$; gravity is the dynamics of $I$. Second, a structural reading of the equivalence principle: every mass term in the theory is a coupling to the one frozen point whose dynamics is the gravitational field, so the universality of gravitation, that gravitational and inertial mass coincide and everything falls alike, reads as the statement that the theory contains a single scale-giving object. Fields differ in how strongly they couple to $I$ (their weight), never in what they couple to. This is a reading, not a theorem: it rests on the two theorem-level ends and on the uniqueness of the scale-giving object, and it is entered in the levels of the results below at that level. Third, imported from the action paper at the levels it assigns: the action paper leaves the graviton's ontology open and states its engineering conclusion on either reading; on the reading in which the graviton is a collective mode of the boundary mode space, the acoustic no-go gives that conclusion at the mixed level of its inputs, one step conditional on the entropy paper's premise \cite[\S\S5--6]{ButlerT10}. Last, at the level of flagged speculation: a massive body is a multi-spinor composite (a composite of many conformal spinors), misaligned within (Proposition \claimref{mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula}) and coupled to $I$ through its grip (Definition \claimref{obj.mass.grip-mass-composite}, Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join}), and its gravitational field is the response of the boundary mode space to that disturbance. In one sentence: gravity, at the quantum level, is the collective dynamics of the frozen point, coupling to which defines every mass, and everything falls the same way because there is only one point at infinity to couple to.

\emph{Part A: the dictionary.} The pairing $I \cdot D\sigma$ is formed slot by slot from Facts \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection} and \claimref{mass.imported-thomas-operator}, with $\sigma$ and $\Box\sigma$ as formal coordinates, and $m^{2}$ is read off the resulting Klein-Gordon equation: $m^{2} = -w(w+n-1)Q(I)$ on a $144$-point rational grid in $(w, n, J)$, with a separate check that the opposite sign fails at every grid point where $m^{2} \neq 0$; in $n = 4$, $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $\rho_{I} = \Lambda/6$ and $m^{2} = -w(w+3)\Lambda/3$ as rational-function identities in a formal $\Lambda$. \emph{Part B: the area.} On exact Gaussian-rational spinor instances: a single twistor's momentum is null; $p^{2} = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2}$ on all ten pairs with the imaginary part identically zero; aligned spinors give a null composite.

\emph{Part C: the chart and the de Sitter scale.} The chart on $\Lambda^{2}\C^{4}$: $\ip{n_{0}}{n_{\infty}} = +1$ with both null; $Q(x) = -2\det x$ and the orthogonality of the slots; $Q(X_{c}) = Q(1+2c)$ with $c$ undetermined (Remark \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}). c(w') := \sqrt2\; \iota_{w'} \quad (w' \in W'),

t11-regenerated.text:
Fix bases $\pi_1, \pi_2$ of $\Spi$ and $e_1, e_2$ of $\Som$ with $\pi_1\wedge\pi_2 = N_0$ and $e_1 \wedge e_2 = N_\infty$. For a linear map $A: \Spi \to \Som$ let $L_A := \{A\pi + \pi : \pi \in \Spi\}$ be its graph line and
\[
P(A) \;:=\; (A\pi_1 + \pi_1)\wedge(A\pi_2 + \pi_2) \;\in\; \Lambda^2\CS
\]
its Pl\"ucker bivector, normalised by $P(0) = N_0$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Expansion.)} $P(A) = N_0 + \varphi(A) + (\det A)\, N_\infty$, where $\varphi(A) := A\pi_1\wedge\pi_2 + \pi_1\wedge A\pi_2$ lies in the mixed slot $\Som\wedge\Spi$ and $\det$ is taken in the chosen bases.
\item \emph{(The chart, term by term.)} $\varphi$ is a linear isomorphism onto the mixed slot $= \{\nO,\nInf\}^\perp \otimes \C$, and satisfies $Q(\varphi(A)) = -2\det A$. Writing $m(A) := \varphi(A)$ as a vector of $\{\nO,\nInf\}^\perp\otimes\C$, the Pl\"ucker bivector is exactly the completion's point embedding, complexified:
\[
P(A) \;=\; \nO \,+\, m(A)\,-\,\tfrac12\,Q(m(A))\,\nInf \;=\; X\bigl(m(A)\bigr).
\]
In particular every $P(A)$ is null, as a Pl\"ucker bivector must be, and the nullity of $P(A)$ is equivalent to the identity $\det A = -\tfrac12Q(m(A))$: the quadratic term of the chart is a determinant.
\item \emph{(Coverage.)} $A \mapsto L_A$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}(\Spi, \Som)$ onto the lines of $\PCS$ skew to $L_\infty$, and $[P(A)]$ ranges exactly over the points of the Klein quadric with $\ip{P}{\nInf} \neq 0$: the affine chart of the complexified conformal compactification, with the lines meeting $L_\infty$ as the points at infinity; the real locus is cut out in Proposition \claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor}(5).

t12-regenerated.title: Introduction
t12-regenerated.text:
The mass paper of this series proves that mass first exists at two twistor constituents: a single twistor is null, and a two-twistor composite's mass is set by the symplectic area of its constituents' misalignment \cite{ButlerT11}. This paper asks what symmetries such composites carry, and finds that the question answers most of particle physics. The internal mixings of an $n$-twistor system form exactly $U(n)$; the minimal \emph{massive} hierarchy, two twistors of three ladder pairs each, is $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$; and the automorphisms of that tensor structure have Lie algebra $\su(2) \oplus \su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$, dimension $4 + 9 - 1 = 12$: the Standard Model's, exactly. The global group comes out $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, the full $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$ quotient, the smallest of the Standard Model's global forms; and conversely (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.four-dimensions-forces-converse}(2)) the Standard Model algebra is the automorphism algebra of a two-factor hierarchy only for a two-by-three one. The fermion content is the quark doublet at the pair level, unconditionally, as the cells of the hierarchy's own state space, and the lepton doublet one level higher in the hierarchy under one declared hypothesis, that the twistor slots are fermionic modes like the pairs; without it the state space contains no lepton at all, and the paper proves that too. Under that hypothesis the object carrying the states has a thirteen-dimensional automorphism algebra, one abelian generator more than the twelve; in the action the state space carries, the extra generator is anomaly-free, the $U(1)_{X}$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, and the right-handed neutrino's Majorana mass breaks it (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}(3)): the twelve are what survives below that scale. Colour neutrality of the lepton is then the exact statement that a lepton is a complete twistor, its pair system full, while a quark is a fractional one. Hypercharge is the weight of the global form's own abelian generator, and pair counting reads it off: one pair has weight one unit, so the quark doublet is at $Y = 1/6$; the single-twistor Fock space, listed by one handedness, gives the four singlets at $Y = 0, -2/3, 1/3, 1$ (a computation on that Fock space, which is not a subspace of the tensor state space; under the hypothesis it is the state space's slot-free row); and under the slot-statistics hypothesis a slot with its pair system full has weight minus three, so the lepton doublet is at $Y = -1/2$. Three anomaly conditions then hold as identities, the fourth confirms the orientation, and, given that content, they admit no other spectrum. Chirality is the handedness of the two halves of the single-twistor spinor module $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, and under the hypothesis the parity of the five-mode state space, whose even half is the generation as the half-spinor of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}). The connection is forced, not chosen. And the numerical layer compresses. The mixing angle at the unification scale, over that generation, is $\sin^{2}\theta_{W} = 3/8$, a value that rests on the hypothesis with the lepton (without the lepton the ratio is $9/26$); the one-loop run from the scale where the couplings meet (the structural scale, $M_{U}$ below) refutes the desert and demands that the running between the scales change, either by partner-like content or by a gauge symmetry enlarged at an intermediate scale, and the composite's split between slots and pairs supplies the second (the section ``An intermediate symmetry: the slot/pair split''); and the framework's three smallness problems are powers of the single largeness $N = M_{P}/H$, which the paper's closing trichotomy classifies: under the action as written, with the frozen point's norm fixed before variation, $N$ is a parameter of the laws (an import from the action paper); under the promotion of that norm to a Lagrange-multiplier field, a decision the series records open, it is initial data of the descent, a state-count fixing the universe's own boundary-mode count (about $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$) rather than a coupling. The exhaustiveness of the alternatives is not proved.

Seven of this paper's results began as natural conjectures that failed and were refuted into better questions, and each failure is carried as a result that makes precise the question the next result answers. The refutation narrative itself belongs to the capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17}, which numbers these seven as the sixth, seventh, eighth, tenth, eleventh, twelfth and fourteenth of the series; here the results are stated neutrally and the remarks say which conjecture each one refuted. The paper is Tier B for its unconditional results: the algebra, the quark doublet, the singlet spectrum, the anomaly arithmetic given a content, the run and the compressions are proved or derived at the series' standard from named premises; the identification of the derived structures with the observed forces is declared at observation level wherever it occurs; and the registered stances (the $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$ charge lattice, the refutation of the desert) are flagged with their falsification conditions. The results that rest on the slot-statistics hypothesis, the lepton doublet, the common handedness of doublets and singlets, the $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ spinor and the values $3/8$ and $3/4$, are proved from that hypothesis at the same standard and carry its level, that of a declared and underived structural premise: until the hypothesis is derived or registered with refutation conditions (successor problem (6)), those results are conditional, and the list of levels in the section ``The levels of the results, and successor problems'' sets them apart.

t12-regenerated.text:
For finite-dimensional complex vector spaces $A$ and $B$ and every $k$,
\[
\Lambda^{k}(A \otimes B) \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{|\lambda| = k} S_{\lambda}A \otimes S_{\lambda'}B
\]
as $GL(A) \times GL(B)$-modules, the sum over partitions $\lambda$ of $k$ with $\lambda'$ the conjugate partition and $S_{\lambda}$ the Schur functor; $S_{\lambda}A = 0$ when $\lambda$ has more parts than $\dim A$. For $\dim A = 2$: $S_{(1,1)}A = \Lambda^{2}A = \det$, $S_{(2,1)}A \cong A \otimes \det$, $S_{(3)}A = S^{3}A$ of dimension four. For $\dim B = 3$: $\Lambda^{2}B \cong B^{*} \otimes \det$, $S_{(2,1)}B \cong \mathfrak{sl}(B) \otimes \det$, the eight-dimensional adjoint, $S_{(2,2)}B \cong S^{2}B^{*} \otimes \det^{2}$; and in general $\Lambda^{k}B \cong (\Lambda^{n-k}B)^{*} \otimes \det$ for $n = \dim B$, equivalently $(\Lambda^{k}B)^{*} \cong \Lambda^{n-k}B \otimes \det^{-1}$. Under $SU(A) \times SU(B)$ the determinant characters are trivial. For a direct sum, $\Lambda^{n}(A \oplus B) \cong \bigoplus_{j+k=n}\Lambda^{j}A \otimes \Lambda^{k}B$ as $GL(A) \times GL(B)$-modules. \emph{Provenance:} the Cauchy formula is \cite[I, \S 4, (4.3$'$)]{Macdonald1995} and \cite[Ex.~6.11]{FultonHarris1991}; the small identifications are the standard dimension-two and dimension-three cases of \cite[\S 6.1, \S 15.3]{FultonHarris1991}; the direct-sum formula is \cite[App.~B.2]{FultonHarris1991}.

Then the pair count per twistor is $(n+2)/2$ (Lemma 2.12), the minimal massive hierarchy is $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{(n+2)/2}$, and its automorphism algebra is $\su(2) \oplus \su((n+2)/2) \oplus \uu(1)$ by the argument of Theorem 4.1, which for $m \neq k$ uses the Segre lemma and the tensor factorisation only, and which at $n = 2$, where $m = k = 2$, still applies because an automorphism is defined as a map of the form $A \otimes B$, so that the swap of factors is excluded by definition, as in (2). This equals the Standard Model algebra if and only if $n = 4$. If, therefore, the gauge algebra of matter is the automorphism algebra of its minimal massive compositeness, four dimensions is a consequence: four is the dimension in which the pair count is three. The identification premise is Theorem 4.1's reading, the mass-begins-at-two hypothesis in dimension $n \neq 4$ is a hypothesis (the mass paper proves it in dimension four only), and both conditionalities are declared.

(2) Conversely, with no hypothesis on $n$: for every two-factor hierarchy $\C^{m} \otimes \C^{k}$ with $m, k \ge 1$ the automorphism algebra is $\su(m) \oplus \su(k) \oplus \uu(1)$, of dimension $m^{2} + k^{2} - 1$, and it is isomorphic to the Standard Model algebra if and only if $\{m, k\} = \{2, 3\}$ as an unordered pair. So the gauge algebra, once identified, forces the hierarchy to be a two-by-three, and one further input orders it: given that mass begins at two constituents ($m = 2$), the pair count is three, hence four dimensions by Lemma 2.12; given four dimensions ($k = 3$), the constituents number two. Under Theorem 4.1's reading, each of the two framework inputs is a consequence of the observed forces together with the other, not only consistent with them; the algebra alone does not distinguish two twistors of three pairs from three twistors of two.

(1) $\su((n+2)/2) = \su(3)$ iff $(n+2)/2 = 3$ iff $n = 4$, and for $n \neq 4$ the dimensions $3 + ((n+2)/2)^{2} - 1 + 1$ and $12$ differ, so the algebras are not isomorphic; the $\su(2)$ factor is dimension-independent because the two-ness of the minimal massive composite is the hypothesis, not the pair count.

(2) The kernel computation of Theorem 4.1 used nothing about $m$ and $k$: the pairs $(A, B) \in U(m) \times U(k)$ with $A \otimes B = 1$ are the scalars $(\lambda I_{m}, \lambda^{-1}I_{k})$, so the algebra is $(\uu(m) \oplus \uu(k))/\uu(1) = \su(m) \oplus \su(k) \oplus \uu(1)$, of dimension $(m^{2} - 1) + (k^{2} - 1) + 1 = m^{2} + k^{2} - 1$, for every $m, k \ge 1$ (with $\su(1) = 0$; for $m = k$ the factor swap is excluded by the definition of an automorphism of the hierarchy, as in Section 4's preamble). Isomorphic Lie algebras have equal dimension, so $m^{2} + k^{2} = 13$, whose only solutions in positive integers are $\{m, k\} = \{2, 3\}$ (since $13 - 1, 13 - 4, 13 - 9$ are $12, 9, 4$, of which only $9$ and $4$ are squares, and $13 - 16 < 0$). \begin{enumerate}
\item The one-generation spectrum of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency},
\[
Q \oplus L \oplus u^{c} \oplus d^{c} \oplus e^{c} \oplus \nu^{c}
\;=\; (2,3)_{1/6} \oplus (2,1)_{-1/2} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{-2/3} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{1/3} \oplus (1,1)_{1} \oplus (1,1)_{0},
\]
is exactly the even part $\Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}(\C^{2} \oplus \C^{3})$, sixteen-dimensional, with $\nu^{c}$, $u^{c}$, $Q$, $L$, $e^{c}$, $d^{c}$ at $(j, k) = (0,0), (0,2), (1,1), (1,3), (2,0), (2,2)$; and the odd part $\Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}(\C^{2} \oplus \C^{3})$ is its dual, the antiparticles, with the doublet of the empty conformal spinor (the empty-twistor doublet) $(2,1)_{1/2}$ at $(1,0)$. The mass bracket's slot factor $\Lambda^{2}\C^{2}$, $(1,1)_{1}$, is the even component $(2,0)$, the same representation as $e^{c}$.
\item The five-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus \C^{3}) = \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ is the spinor module of $\Cl(10)$, its two parities are the two half-spinor representations of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, and the automorphisms of the five-mode state space's canonical anticommutation relations induced by orthogonal maps of its ten Majorana generators form $O(10)$, implemented on the Fock space by $\mathrm{Pin}(10)$, with the connected part $SO(10)$ implemented by $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-representation-clifford-algebra-bogoliubov}). \[

\]
the pair-number form of the operator $B - L$ of Fact \claimref{families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch}, and it takes the values $-\tfrac52$ on $\nu^{c}$, $-\tfrac12$ on $Q$, $u^{c}$, $e^{c}$ and $\tfrac32$ on $L$, $d^{c}$: the $U(1)_{X}$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$. t12-regenerated.title: One number to explain
t12-regenerated.text: The gravitational action of the action paper carries, in its curvature-squared presentation, a single dimensionless combination of scales, $G\Lambda$, the relative coefficient of its Einstein-Hilbert and Gauss-Bonnet terms (\cite[Thm.~3.1(2)]{ButlerT10}; reading that coefficient as \emph{the} dimensionless coupling is this paper's, not the action paper's). Let $N = M_{P}/H$, the number the dictionary of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-frozen-point-dictionary} attaches to the Planck mass, about $1.0 \times 10^{61}$. Then, as an exact exponent computation, the framework's well-known smallness problems are all powers of $N$: the cosmological-constant problem is $G\Lambda = 3N^{-2}$; the weakness of gravity relative to a dimension-one matter coupling, evaluated at the Hubble scale, is $N^{-2}$; and the mass hierarchy is the statement that the imaginary weight of a mass $m$ is $\operatorname{Im} w = (m/M_{P})\,N$. The numerical layer of the programme therefore reduces to a single question: why is $N$ large? That question this framework does not answer; what it has done is ensure there is only one of it. The computation is exact and script-checked; the choice of $H$ as the comparison scale for gravity's weakness, and the reading of the three problems as one, are conventions, which is why this is an Observation. The reading has a limit the computation shows. The first two problems are one number by the definition of $N$: both are $(H/M_{P})^{2}$, the first times $3$. The third is not a power of $N$, and not exact as written: $\operatorname{Im} w = (m/M_{P})\,N$ holds to relative order $H^{2}/m^{2}$ for $m > 3H/2$ (exactly, the weight's Casimir is $-w(w+3) = (m/M_{P})^{2}N^{2}$, Proposition \claimref{synthesis.smallness-monomials-exact-hierarchy-casimir}), and it carries a second ratio, $m/M_{P}$, which for the weak scale is the rung unit $v/M_{P} \approx 2.0 \times 10^{-17}$, between $N^{-0.28}$ and $N^{-0.27}$; it is invariant under the rescaling of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}(1) and so kinematically not a function of $N$ (Proposition \claimref{families.why-kinematic-attacks-had-fail}, at the level of its observation-level invariance premise). One number is to be explained for the cosmological-constant problem and gravity's weakness; the mass hierarchy adds the second continuous modulus that Proposition \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}(1) lists beside $N$, the weight spectrum.

\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] The even half (total mode number even) has sixteen states and the odd half sixteen.
\item[(2)] The even half's hypercharge multiset is the derived generation's, $\tfrac16$ six times, $-\tfrac12$ twice, $-\tfrac23$ and $\tfrac13$ three times each, $1$ and $0$ once, and the odd half's is its negative: the halves are the $16$ and the $\overline{16}$.

The Chevalley action makes $\Lambda^{\bullet}\operatorname{span}(v_{1}, \ldots, v_{k})$ an irreducible $B_{k}$-module, one qubit per rung. On each complexified floor there is a conjugate-linear antiautomorphism $*$ under which the ladder pairs are mutually adjoint, $v_{j}^{*} = w_{j}$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thms.~3.2, 4.2]{ButlerT3} (\claimref{tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung}, \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}); proved there.

t12-regenerated.title: The two-rung module; sectors; slot components
t12-regenerated.text:
Let $R_{2} = \operatorname{span}(v_{4}, v_{5})$ be the span of the two rungs' creation modes over $\C$ and $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus R_{2})$ the Fock module of the five mode pairs, three of $W$ and two of $R_{2}$, with the Hermitian structure induced by $*$ of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module} on the rung factor and by a fixed $\mathrm{Spin}(2,4)$-invariant Hermitian form on the pair factor. The \emph{sector} $(j, k)$ is $\Lambda^{j}R_{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$, $j$ the rung (slot) number and $k$ the pair number; the \emph{slot-singlet sectors} are $j \in \{0, 2\}$ and the \emph{slot-doublet sectors} $j = 1$. For an orthonormal basis $(e_{a})$ of $\Lambda^{j}R_{2}$, the \emph{slot components} of a state $\Psi_{j} = \sum_{a} e_{a} \otimes \psi_{a}$ in rung sector $j$ are the $\psi_{a} \in \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, $\binom{2}{j}$ of them. A \emph{product form} on the module is a Hermitian form with $\ip{e_{a} \otimes \psi}{e_{b} \otimes \varphi} = \ip{e_{a}}{e_{b}}_{R}\,\ip{\psi}{\varphi}_{W}$; the structure just described is one. The \emph{moment} of a bivector $X \in \Lambda^{2}V_{\C}$ on a state $\Psi$ is $M_{X}(\Psi) = \ip{\Psi}{X\Psi}$, and for $I \in V$ the grip and the mass-squared of $\Psi$ are Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-grip-area-casimir-form}(i) with this moment.
In the same module write the mode operators $v_{a}$ (creation) and $w_{a}$ (annihilation), $a = 1, \ldots, 5$, modes $1, 2, 3$ those of $W$ and $4, 5$ those of $R_{2}$; \emph{the ten} is their span, the complexified transported ambient space $V_{\C} \oplus R_{2} \oplus \overline{R}_{2}$; \emph{rung vectors} are $v_{4}, v_{5}, w_{4}, w_{5}$ and \emph{pair vectors} $v_{1}, v_{2}, v_{3}, w_{1}, w_{2}, w_{3}$. The hypercharge generator is $y = 3N_{R} - 2N_{W}$ and $2T_{3} = N_{4} - N_{5}$ in occupation numbers.

t12-regenerated.title: The module factorises, and even ground elements act on the pair factor
t12-regenerated.proof: By Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module}, $T_{2} \cong \Cl(2,4) \otimes \mathrm{M}_{4}(\R)$, so $T_{2} \otimes \C \cong \mathrm{M}_{8}(\C) \otimes \mathrm{M}_{4}(\C) = \mathrm{M}_{32}(\C)$, whose irreducible module is unique up to isomorphism and is the Fock module of any five anticommuting mode pairs; the three pairs of $W$ with $\overline{W}$ and the two rung pairs $(v_{a}, w_{a})$ are such a set, and their Fock module is $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus R_{2}) = \Lambda^{\bullet}W \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}R_{2}$ by the direct-sum formula for exterior algebras \cite[App.~B.2]{FultonHarris1991} (\claimref{standard-model.imported-cauchy-decomposition-exterior-power}). Realise the mode operators in the Jordan-Wigner form on the occupation basis, modes $1, 2, 3$ of $W$ before modes $4, 5$ of $R_{2}$: the creation and annihilation operators of mode $i$ carry the sign $(-1)^{\#\{\text{occupied modes below } i\}}$. For $i \le 3$ that sign involves pair modes only, so the operator is $x_{W} \otimes 1$; for $i \in \{4, 5\}$ it involves all three pair modes, giving $(-1)^{N_{W}} \otimes y_{R}$. This is (1) for vectors, and products of two vectors of $V_{\C}$ are products of operators of the form $x_{W} \otimes 1$, hence $X_{W} \otimes 1$; the even ground subalgebra is spanned by such products. (2): $(x_{W} \otimes 1)((-1)^{N_{W}} \otimes y_{R}) = -((-1)^{N_{W}} \otimes y_{R})(x_{W} \otimes 1)$ since a vector of $V_{\C}$ changes the pair number by one and so anticommutes with $(-1)^{N_{W}}$; two rung vectors give $((-1)^{N_{W}})^{2} \otimes Y_{R} = 1 \otimes Y_{R}$. (3) follows: operators of the forms $X_{W} \otimes 1$ and $1 \otimes Y_{R}$ commute, and $N_{R}$ and the $v_{a}w_{b}$ are of the second form. The untwisted bivectors used here are the twisted ones of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module} up to sign, since $x\omega_{1}\omega_{2}\,y\omega_{1}\omega_{2} = \pm xy\,(\omega_{1}\omega_{2})^{2} = \pm xy$, so (3) is also the statement that $A_{2}$ and $B_{2}$ commute, read on the even part. The script builds the $32$-dimensional module exactly and checks: the Clifford relations of the five pairs; that every one of the fifteen bivectors of $V_{\C}$ has the block form $X_{W} \otimes 1_{4}$ (the same $8 \times 8$ block on each of the four rung states, no element between rung states); that every vector of $V_{\C}$ has that form and no rung vector does; that vectors of the two kinds anticommute; and that every bivector of $V_{\C}$ commutes with $N_{R}$, with the four $v_{a}w_{b}$, and with every bivector of the rung plane.

t12-regenerated.title: The moment map, the grip and the mass are insensitive to the slots
t12-regenerated.proof: $A(U \wedge I)$ is a bivector of $V_{\C}$, so by Proposition \claimref{standard-model.module-factorises-even-ground-elements-act}(1) it acts as $A_{W} \otimes 1$. For a product form and states $e_{a} \otimes \psi$, $e_{b} \otimes \varphi$ with $e_{a}, e_{b}$ in rung sectors $j, j'$: $\ip{e_{a} \otimes \psi}{(A_{W} \otimes 1)(e_{b} \otimes \varphi)} = \ip{e_{a}}{e_{b}}_{R}\ip{\psi}{A_{W}\varphi}_{W}$, which vanishes for $j \ne j'$ (different rung numbers are orthogonal under the rung Fock form) and for $a \ne b$ within a sector (orthonormality). The families paper T13 \cite{ButlerT13} locates that factor in the module, in the operator $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ of Fact \claimref{families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch} at the end of this section, imported there with its provenance: with $B - L := 1 - \tfrac23 N_{W}$ and $\chi := -(-1)^{N_{R}}$ the rung parity, $T_{\mathrm{GJ}} = w_{4}(B - L)\chi$ is pure grade five, its mass form is the $126$ component, and its Clebsches have ratio $|y_{e}/y_{d}| = 3$, Georgi-Jarlskog's. The script recomputes the closed form, the grade and the Clebsches before using them. Three theorems then say, on the one-generation module, that the family structure cannot supply the factor, that the frozen point and its lifts cannot, and that the mass bracket cannot either; for an odd element $T$ of the Clifford algebra of the ten the \emph{mass form} is $Y_{T}(\psi, \varphi) = B(\psi, T\varphi)$ on the sixteen, symmetrised.

t12-regenerated.title: Family no-go: a vev in the $10$ cannot separate the charged leptons from the down quarks
t12-regenerated.proof: The Clebsch computation is Theorem \claimref{standard-model.yukawa-pattern-two-rung-module}'s, recomputed: for $x = w_{4}$ the form $Y_{x}$ is nonzero exactly on the species pairs $(L, e^{c})$ and $(Q, d^{c})$, the species named by (S) (\claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}), symmetric, with every nonzero entry $\pm 1$ (the script enumerates all $16 \times 16$ basis pairs); so $|y_{e}| = |y_{d}| = 1$. t12-regenerated.title: The space of symmetric doublet mass forms is two-dimensional
t12-regenerated.text: Under Hypothesis (S), on the sixteen of one generation, the symmetric bilinear forms $Y_{T}(\psi, \varphi) = B(\psi, T\varphi)$ with $T$ an odd colour-singlet element of the Clifford algebra of the ten carrying hypercharge $-\tfrac12$ and $T_{3} = -\tfrac12$ span exactly a two-dimensional space, spanned by the form of the $10$ direction $w_{4}$ (Clebsch ratio $|y_{e}/y_{d}| = 1$) and the form of $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ (ratio $3$). Then the unital associative algebra generated by $\{I, c_{4}, c_{5}\}$ is eight-dimensional, spanned by $1, I, c_{4}, c_{5}, Ic_{4}, Ic_{5}, c_{4}c_{5}, Ic_{4}c_{5}$, its odd part is $\mathrm{span}\{I, c_{4}, c_{5}, Ic_{4}c_{5}\}$, and of these $c_{4}$ and $c_{5}$ are grade one (the $10$) while $I$ and $Ic_{4}c_{5}$ carry a pair-mode index and are not colour singlets. The odd products are the four listed. Colour: the $\su(3)$ generator $v_{1}w_{2}$ has nonzero commutator with $I$ and with $Ic_{4}c_{5}$ (script), because each contains the mode-one operators $v_{1}, w_{1}$ once; $c_{4}, c_{5}$ commute with all of $\su(3)$ (script), and are vectors: $c_{5} = -w_{5}$ has hypercharge $-\tfrac12$, and $c_{4} = -w_{4} + \lambda v_{4}$ is a combination of the hypercharge $-\tfrac12$ and $+\tfrac12$ vectors $w_{4}, v_{4}$, not a hypercharge eigenvector for $\lambda \ne 0$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point}(i)). Finally the script adjoins $\sum_{i}v_{i}\wedge w_{i}$ to the eight products and finds the rank rise to nine.

t12-regenerated.title: The coefficient cannot come from the frozen point
t12-regenerated.text: No polynomial in the frozen point and its lifts produces the $126$ doublet direction, so the Georgi-Jarlskog coefficient cannot be derived from the transported frozen point alone, however many rungs it is lifted through: the lifts add rung vectors, and rung vectors wedge to grade at most one per rung, never to the pair-sector bivector. The mass mechanism can produce the coefficient only if the pair sector enters it, through $\sum_{i}v_{i}\wedge w_{i}$, which is the $B - L$ generator and, in the correspondence paper's language, the charge of the conformal spinor storey (the twistor storey). The weight programme's first deliverable is therefore restated more precisely once more: not ``a pair-number-dependent rung coupling'' in general, but specifically a coupling of the rung vector to the pair-sector $u(1)$ current, and the object in the series that already couples to that current is the mass bracket, whose direction Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-bracket-direction-charged-not} located in $120 \oplus 126$; its charge is wrong for a vev, but its $B - L$ structure is the right kind. Whether a neutral composite of bracket and rung vector reaches $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ is the next computation, and it is a computation, not a decision.

t12-regenerated.title: The bracket composite lands on the $10$
t12-regenerated.text:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be the unital algebra generated, inside the endomorphisms of the five-mode module, by the frozen point $I = av_{1} + bw_{1}$, its lifted rung components $c_{4}$ and $c_{5}$, the bracket $b = v_{4}v_{5}$ and its conjugate $b^{\dagger} = w_{5}w_{4}$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $\dim \mathcal{A} = 32$, and $\mathcal{A} = \Cl_{R} \oplus I\,\Cl_{R}$ where $\Cl_{R} \cong \Cl(2,2)_{\C}$ is the sixteen-dimensional algebra of the two rung modes.
\item[(ii)] The colour-singlet part of $\mathcal{A}$, the commutant of $\su(3)$ acting on the pair modes, is exactly $\Cl_{R}$.
\item[(iii)] The odd elements of $\Cl_{R}$ of hypercharge $-\tfrac12$ and $T_{3} = -\tfrac12$ form the two-dimensional space spanned by $w_{4}$ and $w_{4}N_{5}$.
\item[(iv)] The mass form of $w_{4}N_{5}$ is one half the mass form of $w_{4}$. Hence every symmetric doublet mass form produced by $\mathcal{A}$ is a multiple of the $10$ form, with $|y_{e}| = |y_{d}|$ under Hypothesis (S), which names the species; in particular the neutral composite $b^{\dagger}v_{5} = -w_{4} + w_{4}N_{5}$ has mass form $-\tfrac12$ times the $10$ form.
\item[(v)] The $126$ direction $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ is not in the span of the forms $\mathcal{A}$ produces, and the pair bivector $\sum_{i} v_{i} \wedge w_{i}$ is not in $\mathcal{A}$.
\end{enumerate}
t12-regenerated.proof: (i) $I$ anticommutes with every rung vector (distinct modes) and $I^{2} = ab$ is a scalar, so every word in the generators reduces to $X$ or $IX$ with $X$ a word in $v_{4}, w_{4}, v_{5}, w_{5}$; the sixteen ordered monomials in those four operators are independent, and $I\Cl_{R} \cap \Cl_{R} = 0$ since $I$ carries pair-mode charge. The script closes the generating set under products and finds rank $32$. (ii) An element $IX$ has $[v_{1}w_{2}, IX] \ne 0$ because $I$ has a $v_{1}$ or $w_{1}$ component and $X$ commutes with the pair modes; an element of $\Cl_{R}$ commutes with every $\su(3)$ generator. The script computes the kernel of the joint commutator map on a basis of $\mathcal{A}$ and finds dimension $16$. (iii) The odd monomials in the rung operators with $[Y, M] = -\tfrac12 M$ and $[T_{3}, M] = -\tfrac12 M$ are $w_{4}$, $w_{4}v_{5}w_{5}$ and $w_{4}v_{4}w_{4} = w_{4}$; the script enumerates all sixteen monomials, filters by the two weights and by parity, and finds rank two with $\{w_{4}, w_{4}N_{5}\}$ a basis. (iv) Direct computation of $B(\psi, X\varphi)$ on all $16 \times 16$ pairs for $X = w_{4}$ and $X = w_{4}N_{5}$, symmetrised: the second is one half the first, and both couple only $(L, e^{c})$ and $(Q, d^{c})$, the species named by (S) (\claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}), with equal magnitudes. The composite identity is $w_{5}w_{4}v_{5} = -w_{4}w_{5}v_{5} = -w_{4}(1 - v_{5}w_{5})$. (v) The forms of $w_{4}$ and $w_{4}N_{5}$ have rank one and adjoining $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$'s form raises it to two; adjoining $\sum v_{i} \wedge w_{i}$ to a basis of $\mathcal{A}$ raises the rank from $32$ to $33$.

t12-regenerated.title: what this settles and what it leaves open
t12-regenerated.text: Corollary \claimref{standard-model.coefficient-cannot-come-frozen-point} asked whether the bracket's composites with the rung vectors land on $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ with a fixed coefficient. t12-regenerated.title: what the chain decides, and what it leaves
t12-regenerated.text: Three measured couplings fix $M_{I}$, $M_{U}$ and $\alpha_{U}$, so on this route $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}$ is an input that fixes $M_{I}$, not a prediction. The route passes the tests it can be held to: $M_{I} < M_{U}$, and the proton condition, which the chain with the $(15,2,2)$ meets by a factor of six in $M_{U}$. The $(15,2,2)$ is the Pati-Salam home of the $126$'s electroweak doublets (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pati-salam-representation-theory-survival}(a)), and so of the Georgi-Jarlskog direction of Fact \claimref{families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch}: if that direction is to contribute to a mass at the weak scale, a $(15,2,2)$ doublet must be light, and by Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pati-salam-representation-theory-survival}(b) the multiplet then sits at $M_{I}$, which is the chain with the $(15,2,2)$. The vev along $T$ sets both $M_{I}$, through the mass of the $\su(2)_{R}$ gauge bosons, and the right-handed neutrino's Majorana mass (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}). A derived relation in the neutrino sector would therefore fix $M_{I}$ and turn the input into a prediction; this is successor problem (7). Left-right symmetric unification with left-right parity broken at the unification scale is Chang, Mohapatra and Parida's \cite{ChangMohapatraParida1984}; the chains are of the class surveyed by Bertolini, Di Luzio and Malinsky \cite{BertoliniDiLuzioMalinsky2009}.

Let $\Delta$ be the largest $|d\ln O/d\ln p|$ for $O = m_{3}$ and $O = m_{3}/m_{2}$ over the Lagrangian couplings $p$, with (EW) held exact. Representative fits:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lllll@{}}
\toprule
couplings & factor $3$ of the second family & largest $|M_{\nu}|$ entry & $m_{1}$ & $\Delta$ \\

t12-regenerated.title: Successor problems
t12-regenerated.text: Eight, ordered by exactness within the running programme and then by structure. (1) \emph{The rung unit, and the rung component as a field:} the partner sector's question, which tower and which content, is answered in the section ``The partner sector quantified'' and the section ``The module's mass mechanism and the rung doublet'': this tower, split content cutting across the $SU(5)$ pieces, and the split is the rung/ground split of the transported ambient space. What remains is a single number, the weak scale as the size of the rung's algebraic unit, the rung unit $v/M_{P} \approx 2 \times 10^{-17}$, which nothing in the series fixes and which is rescaling-invariant and so not kinematically an instance of $N$ (in Hubble units $v/H = N\,v/M_{P} \approx 10^{44}$ inherits $N$); and the promotion of the rung component of a parallel section from a constant background to a dynamical field with a connection on the rung plane, a potential and a quantum (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.what-derived-what-not}). (2) \emph{Two loops at two thresholds:} Proposition \claimref{standard-model.supersymmetric-row-two-loops} decides the supersymmetric row at one common threshold; extend it to the split families of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.four-supersymmetric-splits}, which needs the two-loop coefficients of partial supersymmetric content with the gaugino Yukawas included below the heavy threshold, the generic formula alone being shown not to suffice; the target is that this decides the supersymmetric row's splits and nothing else, the other rows' conclusions standing at one loop. (3) \emph{The weight assignments, now with a specific form:} the Georgi-Jarlskog term is one grade-five element, three factors, all present in the series, and the section ``What the pattern cannot do: three no-go theorems'' proves that neither the family structure, nor the frozen point and its lifts, nor the bracket and its composites reach it; what would is a coupling of the rung vector to the pair-sector $\uu(1)$ current, which is what the colour label carries and what Hypothesis (S) would have to produce. The family breaking is the second step, acting on the resulting two-term structure, and belongs to the families paper T13 \cite{ButlerT13}. (4) \emph{The orientation:} the particle-antiparticle orientation, shown underivable from the kinematics and identified with the descent's one bit in the dark-matter paper T14 \cite[Prop.~5.2]{ButlerT14}; here it is the choice of which parity the one-handed listing keeps, and the sign of the hypercharge generator. (5) \emph{The descent measure, behind the promotion decision:} the one object the trichotomy says the framework needs and does not possess; the action paper's fourth alternative (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}, clause (4)) makes the measure a measure over theories unless the Henneaux-Teitelboim promotion is adopted, and only then is ``why this $\Lambda$'' a question within one theory; its physics is the first event's, and the capstone carries the survey of what would count as progress. (6) \emph{Hypothesis (S), slot statistics, and the label-copy theorem:} decide whether the twistor slots of a composite are fermionic modes on the same footing as its pairs, so that the composite's state space is $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ with chirality the parity of the mode number. This is the decision on which the lepton doublet, the common handedness of doublets and singlets, the singlet sector's membership in one object with the quark doublet, the status of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, and the values $3/8$ and $3/4$ all turn (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(2), Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency}, Propositions \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}, \claimref{standard-model.weak-angle-over-derived-generation}, Remark \claimref{note.standard-model.point-contact-grand-unification-what-hypothesis}), and on which every result of the section ``The partner sector quantified'' and the section ``The module's mass mechanism and the rung doublet'' that names a species rests; without it the tensor state space contains no lepton, and the paper has proved that. Adopting it costs a state space that does not record which pairs belong to which slot; the thirteenth abelian generator it also brings is anomaly-free (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}(3)), lies inside the Pati-Salam algebra of the section ``An intermediate symmetry: the slot/pair split'', and is broken with it at the intermediate scale (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}), so it is not a cost. the section ``The two flags, resolved'' and the section ``What the pattern cannot do: three no-go theorems'' make precise what a proof would have to supply: the module's own pair mixing cannot serve as colour (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.pair-mixing-not-colour}), so the missing theorem must produce the label copy of the pair space that the hierarchy bundle carries, not identify the two, and the pair-sector current the $126$ coefficient needs is exactly what that copy would carry. Two further things are known about it. The transport principle cannot prove it: $n$ twistors generate nothing outside $V_{\C}$, three of them span an $\alpha$-plane of their own, and the completion invites one plane whatever $n$. And the tower reading applied literally at three constituents gives the $32$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(12)$, one generation and its conjugate, not three families, a tension with the families paper's account that any constituent-is-a-rung principle must stop at two constituents or resolve. The outcomes are five. (S) adopted as a structural premise of the series, the tier declaration saying so. A weaker constituent hypothesis adopted, that a constituent is a slot vector times a Dirac state with the slot mixing acting on the slot once, the row $j = 1$ of (S) with its chirality bit fixed by the anomalies, which yields the lepton and the common handedness but not the five-mode state space, hence not $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ and not $3/8$. (S) restated as a hypothesis about the transport tower, that the composite's internal state space is the spinor module of the twice-transported completion, which is (S) in the tower's language once slots are identified with rungs, and which no theorem of the series yet derives. (S) registered as a Tier C premise with quantified refutation conditions, the nearest of which, the one-loop miss of the supersymmetric row, Proposition \claimref{standard-model.supersymmetric-row-two-loops} removes. Or (S) rejected, in which case this paper derives the algebra, the global form, the quark doublet and the singlet spectrum and no lepton, and the families and neutrino papers T13 \cite{ButlerT13} and T15 \cite{ButlerT15} must re-examine what they import. A derivation of the lepton inside the two-level hierarchy is not among the outcomes: the negative clause of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(2) shows that any such derivation would have to change the state space, and a reading of the state space's operators, rather than its states, as the elementary fermions comes with no principle selecting one operator among the many representations the endomorphism algebra contains. (7) \emph{The intermediate scale:} on the Pati-Salam route $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}$ is an input that fixes $M_{I}$, at $1.9 \times 10^{10}$ GeV on the chain with the $(15,2,2)$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.chain}). (8) \emph{The family coupling of the grade-three direction:} the untuned row of Observation \claimref{standard-model.fits-record-level} needs the direction $w_{4}(B - L)$ of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.grade-three-georgi-jarlskog-direction} coupled antisymmetrically between the second and third families, with a neutrino coefficient independent of its charged-lepton and down-quark ones; deriving that coupling from the family structure of the families paper T13 \cite{ButlerT13} would say where the second family's factor $3$ comes from.

Every computational identity asserted in this paper has been verified in exact arithmetic by the script \texttt{verify\_T12.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT12}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py}: exact rationals, Gaussian rationals with exact linear algebra over them, and arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic; the one field the library does not provide, the cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{6})$, is realised in the script in a few dozen lines. No floating point is used anywhere except in the lines marked RECORD (the GeV conversions, the proton lifetimes, and the two-loop integrations of Propositions \claimref{standard-model.supersymmetric-row-two-loops} and \claimref{standard-model.chain}, printed as records rather than checked) and in the checks marked CONTROL; two hundred and forty-three checks, all passing (two hundred and thirty-four exact, nine floating-point controls), organised in thirteen parts keyed to statement tags.

\emph{Part A: the ladder.} The polarisation step of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder} at $n = 3$: the nine rank-one constraints $v^{\dagger}Mv = 0$ span the nine-dimensional real space of Hermitian forms on $\C^{3}$, so only $M = 0$ survives; and the nine products $\pi^{j}\bar\pi^{k}$ of an explicit three-twistor configuration have rank four, not nine, the dependence the proof must avoid (the $n = 2$ configuration has rank four of four). Exact rational unitaries (one real, one complex) are confirmed to preserve the total momentum; and the mass bracket is confirmed to transform by $\det(U)$ exactly on both, and to carry abelian weight $6$, hypercharge $+1$, under the generator of the section ``Content, charges, chirality'' (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.mass-bracket-charged-singlet}).

\emph{Part B: the algebra and the global form.} The action of an explicit $13$-generator basis of $\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)$ on $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$ has image of rank exactly $12$ by exact Gaussian-rational rank (the diagonal-phase kernel), and $\uu(3) \oplus \uu(3)$ on $\C^{3} \otimes \C^{3}$ has image rank $17$: the two dimension claims of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}. The coset rescaling law $\lambda^{2}\lambda^{-3} = \lambda^{-1}$ is confirmed on a unit-modulus Gaussian rational. In $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{6})$: $\zeta_{6}$ has order exactly six, the second isomorphism $(a, b, \lambda) \mapsto (\lambda^{3}a, \lambda^{-2}b)$ evaluated on each of the six elements $(\zeta^{-3j}I_{2}, \zeta^{2j}I_{3}, \zeta^{j})$ returns the identity with $a$, $b$ of determinant one, and evaluated on $(I_{2}, I_{3}, \zeta)$ does not (that nothing else lies in the kernel is the determinant argument of the proof); and the lattice residue $2t + 3\delta + q \bmod 6$ vanishes on every representation of the section ``Content, charges, chirality'', the hypercharge-zero singlet included, and does not vanish on a colour singlet of hypercharge $1/3$. The pair count $(n+2)/2$ equals three at $n = 4$ and at no other even $n$ in the tested range, and the algebra dimension $((n+2)/2)^{2} + 3$ equals twelve only there (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.four-dimensions-forces-converse}(1)); $m^{2} + k^{2} - 1 = 12$ has exactly the solutions $\{2, 3\}$ for $1 \le m, k \le 12$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.four-dimensions-forces-converse}(2)).

\emph{Part C: content and charges.} The graded dimensions $1, 6, 15, 20, 15, 6, 1$ and both Cauchy splits of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.raw-representation-content-state-space} are confirmed (the splits from the Schur-functor dimensions), together with the degree-two and degree-three Cauchy identities as identities of symmetric functions at rational diagonal instances; and, exhaustively over the ten partitions of the two-by-three box with the Schur-functor dimensions from the hook-content formula, the summands total $64$, no summand is $(2,1)$ (the two-dimensional $S_{\lambda}(\C^{2})$ occur at $\lambda = (1), (2,1), (3,2)$, whose conjugates give $3, 8, \bar{3}$), the $SU(3)$ singlets occur only at $\lambda = (), (3), (3,3)$, and no summand has a one-dimensional $S_{\lambda}(\C^{2})$ against a three-dimensional $S_{\lambda'}(\C^{3})$, so neither $(1,3)$ nor $(1,\bar{3})$ occurs in any degree; every cell has weight $+1$ under the generator, so the state space has no state of negative weight, against the single-twistor weights $0, -2, -4, -6$. The hypercharge generator $\mathsf{y} = (3iI_{2}, -2iI_{3})$ is built as an exact matrix on $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$, on $\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{0}$ and $\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{3}$, and on each $\Lambda^{k}\C^{3}$, and acts as the scalar $iq$ with $q = 1$; $3$ and $-3$; $0, -2, -4, -6$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}). The negative clause of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(2): five unipotent images of a filled row of the tensor state space, expanded in the wedge basis of $\Lambda^{3}\C^{6}$, have rank exactly four, and the Lie-algebra generator of the unipotent applied three times to the filled row is $6\,e_{01} \wedge e_{02} \wedge e_{03} \neq 0$ (four times, zero), so the four-dimensional span is a single Jordan block, irreducible: the row-filling states are the quadruplet $(4,1)$ and not $2 \oplus 2$. Proposition \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}(4): $d(N^{2})/d\Lambda = -3M_{P}^{2}/\Lambda^{2}$ as a rational-function identity, and on the flat model $N^{2}$ read from the chart's norm scales as $\Lambda^{-1}$ across three pairs of values and is distinct at distinct $\Lambda$.

\emph{Parts F to J: the section ``The partner sector quantified'' and the section ``The module's mass mechanism and the rung doublet''.} \emph{Part F} (the section ``The partner sector quantified''): the one-loop coefficients of the derived and the supersymmetric listings from component tables (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-coefficient-sum-indices}); t12-regenerated.title: The Fock model of the complexified ascended algebra
t12-regenerated.text:
Let $W \subset V_\C$ be a maximal totally isotropic subspace ($\dim_\C W = 3$) and $W'$ a complementary maximal isotropic subspace, dual to $W$ under the $\C$-bilinear form (such a pair exists, and any two such pairs are conjugate under $O(V_\C)$). On the exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet W$ ($\dim_\C = 2^3 = 8$) define
\[
c(w) := \sqrt2\; w \wedge (\cdot) \quad (w \in W),
\qquad
c(w') := \sqrt2\; \iota_{w'} \quad (w' \in W'),
\]
with $\iota$ contraction through the pairing. Then $c(u)^2 = Q(u)\,\id$ for every $u \in W \oplus W' = V_\C$, so $c$ extends to an algebra map $\Cl(V_\C) \to \End(\Lambda^\bullet W)$; this map is an isomorphism, and $\Lambda^\bullet W$ is the unique irreducible module of $\Cl(2,4)_\C$: the Dirac spinors of the completion. Vectors act oddly, so the even and odd halves
\[
\CS := \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}} W, \qquad \CSm := \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}} W,
\]
each of complex dimension 4, are modules of the even subalgebra $\Cl^0(2,4)_\C \cong \End(\CS) \oplus \End(\CSm)$: the two chiralities, the conformal spinor space $\CS$ and its opposite $\CSm$ (twistor and dual twistor space).

t12-regenerated.title: Imported: the tractor connection, and the conformal spinor connection (local twistor transport)
t12-regenerated.text:
Let $[g]$ be the conformal class of the derived metric of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), on its invertible region. (i) $[g]$ carries a canonical connection on the rank-six tractor bundle, whose fibre is the vector space of $\Cl(2,4)$ and which on flat spacetime is the rotation-gauge field $D^{T}_{a} = a \cdot \nabla + \Omega_{T}(a)\times$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}; its expression in a scale $g$ is
\[
\nabla_a(\sigma, \mu_b, \rho) = \bigl(\nabla_a\sigma - \mu_a,\;\; \nabla_a\mu_b + g_{ab}\rho - \mathrm{P}_{ab}\sigma,\;\; \nabla_a\rho + \mathrm{P}_a{}^b\mu_b\bigr),
\]
with $\mathrm{P}$ the Schouten tensor. (ii) The conformal class likewise carries the classical bundle of conformal spinors (the \emph{local twistor} bundle), fibrewise the conformal spinor space $\CS = \Cl^+(2,4)P$, a $4$-dimensional module over the complex unit $I_6$, with the scale splitting $Z = (\omega^B, \pi_{B'})$ into the halves $\Som \oplus \Spi$, and its transport, the conformal spinor connection (local twistor transport),
\[
\nabla^{\mathrm{LT}}_a(\omega^B, \pi_{B'}) \;=\; \bigl(\nabla_a \omega^B + i\,\varepsilon_A{}^B\,\pi_{A'},\;\; \nabla_a\pi_{B'} + i\,\mathrm{P}_{AA'BB'}\,\omega^B\bigr),
\]
in the index conventions of \cite[Vol.~2, Ch.~6]{PenroseRindler86}, where the factor $i$ acts on $\CS$ as the conformal pseudoscalar $I_6$; under conformal rescaling $\omega$ is invariant and $\pi$ shifts, so the $\pi$-plane $\{\omega = 0\}$ (the kernel in $\CS$ of the point's null vector) is the canonical subbundle. \emph{Provenance:} (i) \cite{BEG1994, CurryGover2018}, in the conventions of \cite[Fact 4.1, eq.~(3)]{ButlerT6}; (ii) \cite{PenroseMacCallum73, Dighton74}; the statement that (ii) is the spin representation of (i), that is, that the conformal spinor connection is the tractor connection acting on $\CS$, is standard in the tractor literature \cite{BEG1994, CurryGover2018}, and is \emph{proved} rather than imported below, since the proof is short in the present framework.

t12-regenerated.title: The conformal spinor connection is Penrose's local twistor transport
t12-regenerated.text:
Let $\mathcal{T}$ be the tractor bundle of \cite[\S 4]{ButlerT6} and $\CS M$ its spin bundle, the conformal spinor bundle: the rank-four complex bundle with fibre the conformal spinor space $\CS$, carried by the fibrewise Fock model of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.fock-model-complexified-ascended-algebra}, associated to a lift of the $SO(2,4)$ tractor bundle to $\mathrm{Spin}(2,4)$. We assume the conformal manifold is spin, so that the lift exists globally (on the invertible region of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), an open subset of flat spacetime, it does); every statement below is local, and locally a lift always exists. At a point, write $X_p$ for the canonical (tautological) null direction of $\mathcal{T}_p$, and, in a scale, $u_p$ for the null direction with $\ip{X_p}{u_p} = 1$ singled out by the splitting. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the connection of Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}(i) decomposes, in the scale, as
\[
\nabla_a \;=\; \nabla^{g}_a \;-\; u_p \wedge e_a \;+\; X_p \wedge \mathrm{P}(e_a),
\]
(for a gravitational field on flat spacetime, with $u_p = \nInf$, $X_p = \nO$ and $e_a = \hb^{-1}(a)$, this is the gauge field $\Omega_{T}(a) = \Omega(a) - \nInf \wedge \hb^{-1}(a) + \nO \wedge \Sch(\hb^{-1}(a))$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}, $\nabla^{g}$ being $\Omega(a)$), where $\nabla^g$ couples the Levi factor only: the soldering summand is valued in $u_p\wedge W_\C$ and the Schouten summand in $X_p \wedge W_\C$, with $W_\C = (W_{1,3})_\C$ the complexified Minkowski complement, the latter in the nilradical of the parabolic stabilising $X_p$;
\item on the spinor bundle, with $\Spi$ the plane of $\Psi(X_p)$ (the point's own line: the canonical subbundle) and $\Som$ the plane of $\Psi(u_p)$, the grading element $E := u_p\wedge X_p$ acts with eigenvalue $+\tfrac12$ on $\Som$ and $-\tfrac12$ on $\Spi$; consequently the soldering summand ($E$-weight $+1$) maps $\Spi \to \Som$ and annihilates $\Som$, and the Schouten summand ($E$-weight $-1$) maps $\Som \to \Spi$ and annihilates $\Spi$;
\item the induced spinor connection therefore has, in the scale splitting $Z = (\omega, \pi)$ with $\omega \in \Som$, $\pi \in \Spi$, the form
\[
\nabla^{\CS M}_a(\omega, \pi) = \bigl(\nabla^g_a\omega + \sigma_a\pi,\ \nabla^g_a\pi + \tau_a\omega\bigr),
\]
where $\sigma_a := \rho(-u_p\wedge e_a)|_{\Spi\to\Som}$ is the soldering summand and $\tau_a := \rho(X_p\wedge\mathrm{P}(e_a))|_{\Som\to\Spi}$ the Schouten summand.
The summands are Levi-equivariant in the direction $e_a$, so by Lemma \claimref{correspondence.chiral-planes-summand-spaces}(2) each is the unique map of its type up to a scalar: under Levi-equivariant identifications of $\Som$, $\Spi$ with Penrose's $S^B$, $S_{B'}$, and the \emph{metric-normalised} identification of $W_\C$ with $S^B\otimes S^{B'}$ (the one under which $g_{ab}$ corresponds to $\varepsilon_{AB}\varepsilon_{A'B'}$, Penrose and Rindler's own, fixed up to sign), with $a = AA'$ and $c = CC'$ in the convention of Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}(ii), $\sigma_a$ is the $\varepsilon$-contraction $\pi_{A'} \mapsto \varepsilon_A{}^B\pi_{A'}$ times a constant $c_1$ and $\tau_a$ is the Schouten contraction $\omega^B \mapsto \mathrm{P}_{AA'BB'}\omega^B$ times a constant $c_2$. The constants depend on the relative scale of the two spinor identifications, which multiplies $c_1$ by $\lambda$ and $c_2$ by $\lambda^{-1}$ (the sign freedom of the third flips both, so it changes neither their product nor anything not already realised by $\lambda = -1$), so their product is invariant and is fixed by the composite of the summands on $\Som$:
\[
\sigma_a\,\tau_c \;=\; \tfrac12\,c(e_a)\,c(\mathrm{P}(e_c))\big|_{\Som} \;=\; \tfrac12\,\mathrm{P}_{ac}\,\id_{\Som} + \rho\bigl(e_a\wedge\mathrm{P}(e_c)\bigr)\big|_{\Som} .
\]
Penrose's local twistor transport (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}(ii)) has the same form, with summand composite $\omega^B \mapsto -\varepsilon_A{}^B\,\mathrm{P}_{CC'DA'}\,\omega^D$. Hence Penrose's local twistor bundle is the conformal spinor bundle $\CS M$ and his local twistor transport is the conformal spinor connection, the spinor square root of the tractor connection, exactly when the two composites agree, which is a single convention this identification imports: the sign and normalisation of $\mathrm{P}_{AA'BB'}$ in \cite{PenroseRindler86} relative to the Schouten tensor of Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}(i) (Remark \claimref{note.correspondence.one-imported-convention-local-twistor-identification}).
\end{enumerate}
