t12-regenerated.title: Reality: the conjugation, the invariant Hermitian form, and the factor $I_6$
t12-regenerated.text:
Write $v \mapsto \bar v$ for the real structure of $V_\C$ with real points $V$, and $J$ for the antilinear map on $\Lambda^\bullet W$ that conjugates coefficients in the monomial basis built on the isotropic basis of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.fock-model-complexified-ascended-algebra}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item (\emph{The conjugation.}) With $\Gamma$ the parity operator ($+1$ on $\CS$, $-1$ on $\CSm$) and $b_4$ the fourth negative basis vector of the section ``Setting and imports'',
\[
\kappa := \Gamma\, c(b_4)\, J
\]
is an antilinear bijection of $\Lambda^\bullet W$ with $\kappa\, c(v) = c(\bar v)\, \kappa$ for all $v \in V_\C$; every antilinear map with this property is a complex multiple of $\kappa$; $\kappa$ swaps the chiralities, $\kappa(\CS) = \CSm$; and $\kappa^2 = -\id$.
\item (\emph{The invariant Hermitian form.}) $\Sigma(Z_1, Z_2) := B(\kappa Z_1, Z_2)$ (the twistor form; on the conformal spinor space $\CS$ it corresponds to the reversion form) is a nondegenerate sesquilinear form on $\CS$ with $\Sigma(Z_2, Z_1) = \lambda\,\overline{\Sigma(Z_1, Z_2)}$ for a constant $\lambda$ of modulus one, so that a rescaling of $\kappa$ by a phase makes $\Sigma$ Hermitian; for the $\kappa$ of (1), $\lambda = 1$ and $\Sigma$ is Hermitian as it stands. The real bivectors act $\Sigma$-anti-Hermitianly, so $\Sigma$ is $\mathrm{Spin}(2,4)$-invariant.
\item (\emph{Null planes.}) For every real null vector $v$ the plane of $\Psi(v)$ is $\Sigma$-null. In particular $\Som$ and $\Spi$ are $\Sigma$-null.
\item (\emph{Signature.}) $\Sigma$ has signature $(2,2)$.
\item (\emph{Reality of the chart, and the factor $I_6$.}) The conformal pseudoscalar $I_6$ acts on $\CS$ as its complex unit (the factor $i$). Let $\sigma(\omega, \pi) := \Sigma(\omega, \pi)$ be the resulting perfect pairing $\Som\times\Spi \to \C$, and call $\hat x: \Spi\to\Som$ \emph{$\sigma$-Hermitian} if $\sigma(\hat x\pi, \pi') = \overline{\sigma(\hat x\pi', \pi)}$ for all $\pi, \pi' \in \Spi$. For $A \in \operatorname{Hom}(\Spi, \Som)$ the following are equivalent: (a) the chart point $m(A)$ of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart} is real, $m(A) \in W_{1,3}$; (b) the line $L_A$ is $\Sigma$-null; (c) $A = I_6\hat x$ with $\hat x$ $\sigma$-Hermitian. Consequently the real points of the affine chart are exactly the $\Sigma$-null lines skew to $L_\infty$, the incidence relation of a real point reads $\omega = I_6\hat x\pi$ with $\hat x$ $\sigma$-Hermitian, and on real points the chart norm is $Q(m) = -2\det A = 2\det\hat x$ in the bases of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart}.
\end{enumerate}

t12-regenerated.title: Towers are residues, and the single-clock filter
t12-regenerated.text:
The residue $r = p - q \pmod 8$ is invariant along every tower: the eight parallel towers are the eight residues, their parallelism derived rather than described. Call a signature $(p,q)$ \emph{causal} if $\min(p,q) = 1$: exactly one direction of the minority sign, the timelike one, whichever sign convention carries time. Labelling this world $(1,3)$, residue $6$, fixes the convention time $=$ plus, and the mirror residue $2$ reads $(3,1)$; under the opposite convention the two labels swap and the causal sort is unchanged, but every attribution of a Clifford type to a member of the reversal pair passes to the other member, since $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat(2,\mathbb{H})$ and $\Cl(3,1) \cong \Mat(4,\R)$ are not isomorphic. That attribution is fixed by a labelling convention Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} declares indexical, and is so read below. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Census; proved.)} Every residue contains causal signatures once the dimension is free: the lowest are $(1,1)$ at $r = 0$, $(2,1)$ at $r = 1$, $(3,1)$ at $r = 2$, $(4,1)$ at $r = 3$, $(1,5)$ or $(5,1)$ at $r = 4$, $(1,4)$ at $r = 5$, $(1,3)$ at $r = 6$, $(1,2)$ at $r = 7$. The residue alone therefore sorts nothing; a representative must be chosen.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The sort under P3; proved given the premise.)} Under Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} the representatives are $(1,3)$ at $r = 6$, this world; $(3,1)$ at $r = 2$, a mirror Minkowski with real (Majorana-type) spinors; $(2,2)$ at $r = 0$, two times; $(4,0)$ or $(0,4)$ at $r = 4$, none; $(2,1)$ and $(1,2)$ at $r = 1, 7$, three-dimensional; $(4,1)$ and $(1,4)$ at $r = 3, 5$, five-dimensional. Exactly two are sterile, $r = 0$ and $r = 4$ (a figure of the original), and they are the fixed points of the mirror map $r \mapsto -r$: under P3 the towers without a single time are the towers that are their own mirrors.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Sensitivity; proved.)} The sterile set is a function of the window. With any dimension up to five allowed, only $r = 4$ is sterile ($(1,1)$ is a causal signature for $r = 0$); with dimensions three to six, only $r = 0$ ($(1,5)$ is one for $r = 4$); with the upper bound removed, nothing is ($(1,9)$ is one for $r = 0$ at ten); and the literal lowest-dimensional representative of every residue, with no lower bound, is definite for $r = 6$ itself, namely $(0,2)$: without a lower bound the criterion would sterilise this world.
\end{enumerate}
Six admit matter: this one and five dark. Which of the six the descent populated is a further question, answered for the mirror by P2 and for the odd towers only by the record (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}). Structural level given P3; the two-time exclusion at $r = 0$ imports the standard instability of two-time dynamics, flagged, and the flag does not remove it (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.flag-insensitive-residue-no-flag-level}).

t12-regenerated.title: The alignment computed: the thirteenth refutation, democracy, and one heavy family
t12-regenerated.text:
Four statements, the first a refutation, the rest its redirection, each at the level marked.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The thirteenth refutation, by magnitude; a dimensional estimate.)} The source term of Proposition \claimref{families.source-term-linear-tilt-mass-functional} is $\Lambda$-suppressed, so the condensate it can induce is $\delta b \sim \Lambda\,\Omega_{\mathrm{vac}}$ with $\Omega_{\mathrm{vac}}$ a length; for any vacuum length between the Planck and Hubble scales, $\Lambda\Omega_{\mathrm{vac}}$ lies between $H^{2}/M_{P} \approx 10^{-94}$ eV and $H \approx 10^{-33}$ eV, that is between roughly $10^{-105}$ and $10^{-44}$ of the weak scale $10^{11}$ eV: the tilt cannot reach $10^{2}$ GeV, the natural conjecture that the vacuum $\omega$-area sets the weak scale is refuted, and the weak scale falls back to the weight question, where the hierarchy has remained since the mass paper's fifth refutation.
\item \emph{(The redirection.)} Alignment requires only a nonzero tilt, and directions are ratios, $\Lambda$-independent; so what the vacuum $\omega$-area does determine is its \emph{direction} in the three-dimensional face space of Conjecture \claimref{families.three-generations-faces-maximal-composite}, which carries the family ordering and the mixing. The magnitude was never the physical content; the direction is, and the direction is computable from symmetry where the magnitude was not.
\item \emph{(The direction, at structural level, under the Gram-square reading.)} The kinematic vacuum cannot break $S_{3}$ before its own source exists: a face-anisotropic vacuum would be uncaused structure, forbidden by the indifference instrument (Fact \claimref{families.imported-indifference-instrument}). The source therefore lies on the democratic line, spanned by $u = (1,1,1)/\sqrt{3}$. If the leading mass form is the Gram square of the source, $Y_{0} \propto u' u'^{\mathsf{T}}$ with $u' = (1,1,1)$, the democratic mass matrix of \cite{HHW1978} (the reading the section ``The Gaussian theorems'' realises at operator level and successor problem (2) asks to derive in general), then $Y_{0}$ has spectrum $(3, 0, 0)$ times the condensate scale: one heavy family and two light ones at leading order, the third generation's dominance as structure rather than fit; and Conjecture \claimref{families.three-generations-faces-maximal-composite} is refined rather than replaced: the physical families are the \emph{eigenvectors} of the face-space mass form, at leading order the democratic vector (heavy) and its orthogonal plane (light), the faces up to the rotation the vacuum performs.
\item \emph{(The residue, named.)} The second-order breaking $S_{3} \to S_{2} \to 1$, the anisotropic corrections that lift the two light families and convert the CKM shape into CKM numbers: the family programme's next computable target, confronted in the section ``The Koide geometry''-the section ``The Gaussian theorems''. Everything in this proposition past the magnitude refutation is at the structural and observation levels stated.
\end{enumerate}

t12-regenerated.text:
On functions on the conformal spinor space $\CS$ (twistor functions), realise the palatial relation of Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-twistor-storey-ordering-shift} by $\bar Z_\nu = -\hbar\,\partial/\partial Z^\nu$ (the realisation with the palatial sign $[Z^\mu, \bar Z_\nu] = +\hbar\,\delta^\mu_\nu$), let $\Upsilon := Z^\mu \partial_\mu$ be the homogeneity (Euler) operator, its eigenvalue written $\mathsf{h}$ in sans serif to keep it clear of the one-particle Hamiltonian $h$, and let the helicity operator be one half the distinguished charge, $\mathsf{s} := \tfrac12\, q(\id)$, the standard helicity operator on $\CS$ (twistor helicity) \cite{Penrose1969, EPW1981} in the symmetric ordering that Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-twistor-storey-ordering-shift} forces storey-wide. Then, as an operator identity,
\[
q(\id) \;=\; -\hbar\,(\Upsilon + 2),
\]
so a function on $\CS$ homogeneous of degree $\mathsf{h}$ is an eigenfunction of $\mathsf{s}$ with eigenvalue $s\hbar$ if and only if
\[
\mathsf{h} \;=\; -2s - 2.
\]
The $-2$ is exactly the ordering shift: without the symmetric-ordering shift of $-\hbar/2$ per complex dimension (over the complex unit $I_6$) the offset would vanish. Combined with Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-penrose-transform}, the classification parameter of the Penrose transform is the completion's own $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ charge, its offset supplied by the ordering. t12-regenerated.title: The de Sitter scale and its frozen point
t12-regenerated.text:
Let $\eta$ be the fixed product of flat spacetime, the chart of Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}, $Q(x) = \eta(x,x)$, and $\sigma(x) := 1 - \Lambda Q(x)/12$; on the region $\sigma \neq 0$ let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be the gravitational field with $\hb(a) = \sigma\,a$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), whose derived metric is $g = \sigma^{-2}\eta$. Write tractors in the flat scale as the vectors $\sigma\,n_{\infty} + \mu + \rho\,n_{0}$ of $\Cl(2,4)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scale tractor of $\sigma$ in the flat scale is
\[
I_{\sigma} = \bigl(\sigma,\; \nabla\sigma,\; -\tfrac14\Box\sigma\bigr) = \Bigl(1 - \frac{\Lambda Q}{12},\; -\frac{\Lambda}{6}\,x_{a},\; \frac{\Lambda}{6}\Bigr),
\]
it is parallel for the connection \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection} of $\eta$, and $\ip{I_{\sigma}}{I_{\sigma}} = \Lambda/3$ identically. Hence the derived metric $g = \sigma^{-2}\eta$ is Einstein with cosmological constant $\Lambda$, on the region $\sigma \neq 0$: the gravitational field $\hb = \sigma$ is de Sitter space on flat spacetime, and $I_{\sigma}$ is its frozen point.
\item The constant ambient vector whose scale function is $\sigma$ is
\[
I_{\Lambda} := n_{\infty} + \frac{\Lambda}{6}\, n_{0},
\]
and it is the only one: $\ip{X(x)}{n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}} = 1 - \lambda Q(x)/2$, which equals $\sigma$ iff $\lambda = \Lambda/6$, and the points $X(x)$ span the ambient space. The vector $n_{0} + \lambda n_{\infty}$, of the same norm, has scale function $\lambda - Q/2$: the inverted chart, not this one.
\item $\ip{I_{\Lambda}}{I_{\Lambda}} = 2 \cdot \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\ip{n_{\infty}}{n_{0}} = \Lambda/3$, in agreement with (1). At $\Lambda = 0$, $I_{\Lambda} = n_{\infty}$: the frozen point of flat space is the point at infinity $n_{\infty}$ of the conformal model (the infinity twistor), and, read through the Klein correspondence as a bivector, it becomes non-simple exactly when $\Lambda \neq 0$.
\end{enumerate}

t12-regenerated.text:
\emph{Hypothesis (S), slot statistics.} Under the slot-module hypothesis (Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}: the composite space $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, a graded $U(2)$ slot module tensored with one pair system, with hypercharge from the centre of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, the slot module generated from a unique vacuum by one doublet of slot creation operators, the chirality a CPT halving that is the grading of the joint Clifford system once the slots are fermionic, and slot and pair operators one Clifford system):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Odd slots.)} If the slot quanta are tower elements of one tower parity $\pi$ whose tower grading $(-1)^{\pi n + k}$ is the chirality, then $\pi = 1$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Slot content.)} $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2}$ as a graded $U(2)$-module, so the composite's state space is the Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W = \Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ of five modes, two slot modes and three pair modes, a state being a set of occupied slots and occupied pairs, on which $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$ acts as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$; its particle half is $(1,1)_{0} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{-2/3} \oplus (2,3)_{1/6} \oplus (2,1)_{-1/2} \oplus (1,1)_{1} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{1/3}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Chirality.)} As in Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves} for the three-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, the chirality of a state is the parity of its total mode number.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Exclusion statistics.)} Every $U(2)$-equivariant slot creation map $a^{\dagger} : \C^{2} \otimes F_{n} \to F_{n+1}$ satisfies $a^{\dagger}(u)a^{\dagger}(u') = -a^{\dagger}(u')a^{\dagger}(u)$ for all $u, u' \in \C^{2}$; in particular $a^{\dagger}(u)^{2} = 0$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(One Clifford system.)} The slots are fermionic modes on the same footing as the pairs: the two slot modes and the three pair modes satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations as one system of five modes, so that, by Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-representation-clifford-algebra-bogoliubov}, their Majorana combinations generate $\Cl(10)$ acting on $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$, its spinor module, whose parity grading is that module's chirality.
\end{enumerate}
Clauses (ii) and (iv) are Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(3) under the premise's generation clause and CPT halving, with no anomaly condition; (v) is the premise's clause (f), applied once (ii) has made the slot module fermionic; (iii) follows from the premise's requirement that the chirality be the grading of the joint Clifford system, which makes it commute with $\Spin(10)$; (i) compares (iii) with a tower grading. The particle half satisfies the four anomaly conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients}, a consequence here and not a premise.

t12-regenerated.title: Commuting copies
t12-regenerated.text:
Inside $T_k$, let $B_k$ be the subalgebra generated by the $2k$ plane generators $e_1, f_1, \dots, e_k, f_k$, and let $A_k$ be the subalgebra generated by the twisted base generators $x^{(k)} := x\,\omega_1 \omega_2 \cdots \omega_k$ for $x$ among the ground generators. Then: $B_k \cong \Cl(k,k) \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$; $A_k \cong \Cl(p,q)$ via $x \mapsto x^{(k)}$ (the twisted generators satisfy the ground Clifford relations); $A_k$ and $B_k$ commute elementwise; and multiplication $A_k \otimes B_k \to T_k$ is an isomorphism of algebras,
\[
\Cl(p{+}k, q{+}k) \;\cong\; \Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\R) \;=\; \Mat_{2^k}(\Cl(p,q)).
\]
The isomorphism is canonical given the ordered planes, and compatible with the tower embeddings up to the twist tracked in the section ``The CAR limit''.

t13-regenerated.title: The mass-weight dictionary
t13-regenerated.text:
Let $\sigma$ be a density of conformal weight $w$ on a vacuum Einstein background with frozen point $I$, and impose the coupling
\[
I \cdot D\sigma = 0.
\]
Then, in the scale of $I$, $\sigma$ obeys the Klein-Gordon equation $(\Box + m^{2})\sigma = 0$ with
\begin{equation}
m^{2} = -\,w(w+n-1)\,Q(I), \qquad\text{in } n = 4:\quad m^{2} = -\,w(w+3)\,\frac{\Lambda}{3} = -\,w(w+3)\,H^{2}.
\end{equation}
The mass of a field is its conformal weight, read in the units the frozen point provides, and every mass in the theory is $\sqrt{\Lambda}$ times a factor fixed by the weight.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lllll@{}}

couplings & factor $3$ of the second family & largest $|M_{\nu}|$ entry & $m_{1}$ & $\Delta$ \\

$10$s, $126$, $120$ & through mixing with the third & $0.04$ GeV & $0.03$ meV & $8$, $11$ \\

t13-regenerated.title: Hypothesis (S): slot statistics, derived from the slot-module hypothesis
t13-regenerated.text:
\emph{Hypothesis (S), slot statistics.} Under the slot-module hypothesis (Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}: the composite space $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, a graded $U(2)$ slot module tensored with one pair system, with hypercharge from the centre of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, the slot module generated from a unique vacuum by one doublet of slot creation operators, the chirality a CPT halving that is the grading of the joint Clifford system once the slots are fermionic, and slot and pair operators one Clifford system):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Odd slots.)} If the slot quanta are tower elements of one tower parity $\pi$ whose tower grading $(-1)^{\pi n + k}$ is the chirality, then $\pi = 1$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Slot content.)} $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2}$ as a graded $U(2)$-module, so the composite's state space is the Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W = \Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ of five modes, two slot modes and three pair modes, a state being a set of occupied slots and occupied pairs, on which $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$ acts as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$; its particle half is $(1,1)_{0} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{-2/3} \oplus (2,3)_{1/6} \oplus (2,1)_{-1/2} \oplus (1,1)_{1} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{1/3}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Chirality.)} As in Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves} for the three-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, the chirality of a state is the parity of its total mode number.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Exclusion statistics.)} Every $U(2)$-equivariant slot creation map $a^{\dagger} : \C^{2} \otimes F_{n} \to F_{n+1}$ satisfies $a^{\dagger}(u)a^{\dagger}(u') = -a^{\dagger}(u')a^{\dagger}(u)$ for all $u, u' \in \C^{2}$; in particular $a^{\dagger}(u)^{2} = 0$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(One Clifford system.)} The slots are fermionic modes on the same footing as the pairs: the two slot modes and the three pair modes satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations as one system of five modes, so that, by Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-representation-clifford-algebra-bogoliubov}, their Majorana combinations generate $\Cl(10)$ acting on $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$, its spinor module, whose parity grading is that module's chirality.
\end{enumerate}
Clauses (ii) and (iv) are Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(3) under the premise's generation clause and CPT halving, with no anomaly condition; (v) is the premise's clause (f), applied once (ii) has made the slot module fermionic; (iii) follows from the premise's requirement that the chirality be the grading of the joint Clifford system, which makes it commute with $\Spin(10)$; (i) compares (iii) with a tower grading. The particle half satisfies the four anomaly conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients}, a consequence here and not a premise.

t13-regenerated.title: Hypercharge from the global form, pair counting, and consistency
t13-regenerated.text:
With $Y$ the hypercharge defined before Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}, and with Hypothesis (S) wherever a doublet at the level of one conformal spinor (a twistor-level doublet) enters:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Under (S).) The one-handed listing keeps the states of even total mode number and conjugates the odd ones, or the reverse; the choice is the particle-antiparticle orientation. Write $(j, k)$ for the component of the five-mode state space with $j$ slot modes and $k$ pair modes occupied (mode counts, not the pair of representation dimensions used elsewhere in this paper, for which see the caption of a figure of the original). In the listing that keeps the quark doublet, the component $(1,1)$, as a particle, the lepton doublet is the full conformal spinor, the component $(1,3)$, $Y_{L} = -1/2$, and the empty conformal spinor, the component $(1,0)$, appears only as its conjugate (here both phrases name doublet components of the one-slot listing; the neutrino paper uses ``empty'' and ``filled conformal spinor'' for the grade-zero and grade-three singlets of the single-spinor sector, different objects, Proposition \claimref{neutrino.empty-twistor}). \item (Unconditional as a computation on the Fock space of a single conformal spinor, like Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(3).) Listed by the handedness of (1), the sector of a single conformal spinor gives the singlet spectrum. Here $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$, the conformal spinor space, and $\CSm{} = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$ are the two chirality halves (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}), and the listing keeping the even grades and conjugating the odd ones gives

(1)_{0} \;\oplus\; (\bar{3})_{-2/3} \;\oplus\; (\bar{3})_{+1/3} \;\oplus\; (1)_{+1},

that is $\nu^{c}$, $u^{c}$, $d^{c}$, $e^{c}$ with hypercharges $0, -\tfrac23, +\tfrac13, +1$: the observed singlet spectrum, with the fourth singlet at hypercharge zero. t13-regenerated.title: The internal symmetry ladder
t13-regenerated.text: For a system of $n$ conformal spinors (an $n$-twistor system) $(Z^{1}, \ldots, Z^{n})$, the linear mixings $Z^{i} \mapsto U^{i}{}_{j} Z^{j}$ that preserve the total momentum $p_{AA'} = \sum_{i} \pi^{i}_{A}\bar\pi^{i}_{A'}$, built from the parts $\pi^{i}$ in the $E = +1$ eigenspace, and the total helicity form $\sum_{i} \bar{Z}^{i} \cdot Z^{i}$, the reversion form $h$ summed over the spinors, for every configuration form exactly the unitary group $U(n)$. t13-regenerated.title: The mass bracket is a charged singlet

Under the $U(2)$ of the two-spinor step (two conformal spinors, mixed by their slot index), the mass bracket transforms by the determinant:

t13-regenerated.title: One vev vector: the $10_{H}$ relations with up-type masses read through the conjugate, the breaking pattern, and the split
t13-regenerated.text:
Under Hypothesis (S), let $c = a\,v_{4} + b\,w_{4}$ be a fixed vector of the rung plane and $M_{c}(\psi, \varphi) = B(\psi, c\varphi)$ the resulting mass form on the sixteen. Then the nonzero entries of $M_{c}$ have magnitude $|a|$ on $(L, 
u^{c})$ and $(Q, u^{c})$ and $|b|$ on $(L, e^{c})$ and $(Q, d^{c})$. The up-type masses, and with them the neutrino's Dirac mass, are read through the conjugate $c^{*} =  ar{b}\,v_{4} +  ar{a}\,w_{4}$ of the tower's conjugation ($v_{j}^{*} = w_{j}$, Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-tower-commuting-copies-fock-module}), as the Standard Model gives up-type masses through the conjugate doublet: they are the entries of $M_{c^{*}}$ on $(Q, u^{c})$ and $(L, 
u^{c})$, the coupling to $c^{*}$, of magnitude $|a(c^{*})| = |b|$ with $a(c^{*})$ the $v_{4}$ coefficient of $c^{*}$, while the down-type and charged-lepton masses are the entries of $M_{c}$. So at tree level $m_{

deposited.statement:
The Standard-Model paper left one absolute bit undetermined, the particle-antiparticle orientation, expected to be fixed by the charge-zero condition. The expectation is refuted by a $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ covariance argument parallel to the trichotomy's rescaling one, on three premises: that CPT conjugation is an isomorphism of every kinematic structure (checked in the proof for the metric, the completion, the pairing and the action; premised for the imported gauge sector and for structures later papers add); Hypothesis (S), under which the Standard-Model paper's chirality proposition, the source of the relative-versus-absolute split, is proved (Fact 2.9); and, for the last step only, the trichotomy's exhaustiveness (Fact 2.8(3)).

Anything the structures determine is conjugation-invariant, and the orientation is not. The charge-zero condition fixes all \emph{relative} structure [ButlerT12, Prop.~5.6]; the absolute bit is kinematically underdetermined, untouched by the CPT-symmetric action, hence initial data, and it is the Witt flag of Proposition 5.1: the open orientation of the content derivation and the arrow of time are one choice, made once.

The descent measure carries two numbers and one bit. The neutrino sector supplies no orientation refutation condition: the identification of $\nu_{R}$ with the hypercharge-zero singlet at grade zero is flag-covariant (the conjugate flag exchanges the singlet grades zero and three), so no completion of the orientation could exclude it [ButlerT15].

This is the seventeenth refutation (the sixteenth is the neutrino paper's [ButlerT15, Prop.~4.1(1)]), in the pattern of the thirteenth and the trichotomy: what the framework cannot determine, it can prove it cannot determine, and locate.
deposited.proof:
CPT conjugation acts on each tower's Clifford bundle as the composition of grade involution, reversal, and the flag conjugate $v_{k} \leftrightarrow w_{k}$ (Definition 2.10); the grade involution negates every vector, the timelike one included (the T; the spatial inversion is the P). Structure by structure: the fibre metric is fixed by grade involution, reversal and the exchange of a null pair, which is an isometry of the completion's hyperbolic plane; the pairing on the Fock module sends the grade-$k$ state to the grade-$(3-k)$ state [ButlerT12, Prop.~5.6], which is exactly what the flag conjugate does; and the action is the frozen point's, built from the metric and the completion. The derived gauge sector (Fact 4.2) is CPT-even by the standard theorem for local Lorentz-invariant actions, but that theorem concerns the antiunitary CPT operator of quantum field theory, whereas the composite here is a real linear $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ automorphism of the kinematic data, which is not that operator (Wigner). The argument uses only the automorphism, which is checked; the gauge sector's CPT-evenness is imported and carried as a premise.

t14-regenerated.title: Introduction
t14-regenerated.text:
The tower paper of this series proves that the (1,1) ascent preserves the signature residue $p - q$ modulo eight, so the transport construction runs in eight parallel towers, one per residue of the real Clifford clock \cite{ButlerT3}. Applied to the matter that gravitates and does not shine, the towers give the mirror's share of it by theorem, prove that the other four shares cannot be derived from the series as it stands, and then, by one geometric rule on three premises of its own, return the whole ratio as a closed form, $(11\pi + 16)/(3\pi) = 5.364$, found by fitting. The paper's level is Tier C: nine premises and a hypothesis, each stated before use, attacked in its own section and carried with its cost, and a falsifiability section that says how each claim would be refuted.

The chain, in outline. A residue fixes no signature, so one must be chosen for each; at the dimension nearest four (Premise P3, with the census of what other choices give) a residue has a single time when the chosen signature has exactly one timelike direction, and two residues fail, $r = 0$ with two times and $r = 4$ with none, the fixed points of the mirror map. Six towers can hold matter, this one and five dark; that they do is a theorem for the mirror (indifference along the reversal orbit) and an inference from the observed remainder for the odd four, since the framework has no other dark candidate (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}). The flag does not refine the sort (Witt's theorem), so the $r = 0$ exclusion rests on a two-time import alone, carried as a fork. The five are dark by superselection: the residue is an invariant of the algebra soldered to the metric, not of the algebra alone ($\Cl(1,3)$ and the sterile tower's $\Cl(0,4)$ are the same algebra, $\Mat(2, \mathbb{H})$), so no operator built from the one metric changes residue, and given the sector decomposition the towers are exactly stable, touching this one only by weight. The descent's one orientation, the flag bit, is the chirality of the pure spinor, and its two halves lie in opposite families only when the tower's dimension is a multiple of four: the odd residues cannot be oriented, the even ones can at their P3 representatives, and the asymmetric dark matter is the mirror tower's alone.

Of the five dark towers this paper derives the contribution of one, the mirror's, by theorem, and gives the other four by a rule:
\begin{gather*}
\frac{\Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}}{\Omega_{b}} \;=\; \underbrace{1}_{\text{mirror, derived, to half a percent}} \;+\; \underbrace{2 \cdot \frac{4}{3} + 2 \cdot \frac{8}{3\pi}}_{\text{four odd towers, the unit-ball rule, fitted}} \;=\; \frac{11\pi + 16}{3\pi} \;=\; 5.364,\\[6pt]
\text{against the survey's}\quad

t14-regenerated.title: The stored asymmetry is a charge, not a number
t14-regenerated.text:
Under the classification of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}, with $\epsilon$ initial data of the descent, inherited rather than generated, and the number $N$ common to the towers under P1 ($N = M_{P}/H$, which fixes the boundary mode count, about $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, without being it: Observation \claimref{standard-model.largeness-number-universes-boundary-modes}; the argument uses only that $N$ is common):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Charge.)} The asymmetry stored in an oriented tower is the charge $Q = \epsilon N$, fixed by the descent's data and independent of the tower's temperature; it is not a thermal number $n - \bar{n} \propto g\,\mu T^{2}$. So the mirror share $f_{2} = 1$ holds at any mirror temperature: a cold mirror carries the same baryon charge as this tower in the same number of baryons, with negligible mirror radiation.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Origin.)} The charge is the descent's and cannot be produced afterwards: the one channel superselection leaves open, gravitational production from the visible plasma (the section ``Seeding by gravity, and why no coupling rule follows''), yields $1.8$ to $2.7 \times 10^{-15}$ mirror quanta per unit entropy at the ceiling reheating against the $8.7 \times 10^{-11}$ baryons per unit entropy that our baryon number requires, more than four orders too few even counting every produced quantum as a baryon. Black holes are a sink for $Q$, not a source (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}(iv), under P5): a mass-preserving rearrangement that erodes each tower's free baryon count and moves no share.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Temperature.)} Taken as a free datum of the descent, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} is an exception to P2 (applied with the reach of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), (v), P2 gives $\xi = 1$, which the record excludes), the mirror's temperature ratio $\xi = T'/T$ is bounded below by the gravitational floor, $\xi$ between $2.8$ and $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$ at the ceiling reheating (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}(ii), the bracket the species-counting ambiguity; four parts in a thousand of this at the bottom of the ceiling range), and above by the $\Neff$ cap at $0.448$; a deposit of each unit of baryon number with energy of order the reheating temperature puts it at $\xi \approx 4 \times 10^{-3}$. The paper carries the whole interval. With $\eta = n_{B}/n_{\gamma} = 6.1 \times 10^{-10}$ here and equal baryon number,
\[
\eta' \;=\; \frac{\eta}{\xi^{3}}
\]
runs from $19$ to $26$ at the floor down to about $0.008$ at the hot deposit, crossing one at $\xi = \eta^{1/3} = 8.5 \times 10^{-4}$: at least $10^{7}$ times ours throughout, with $\Delta\Neff$ eight orders or more below the cap.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The two readings.)} The thermal reading would give $f_{2} \sim \xi_{2}^{3}$ instead, at most $0.090$ under the $\Neff$ cap ($0.448^{3}$) and $10^{-7}$ or less anywhere in the interval; the two readings cannot both hold, and the paper's own classification decides for the charge.
\end{enumerate}
Level: the classification is Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-trichotomy-descents-data}'s; the incompatibility is arithmetic. The mirror's nucleosynthesis, which is not a copy of ours and on which the burning branch of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(i) and the composition caveat of refutation item 6 rest, follows the proof, at assembly level. Caveat (T14c): the proof's thermal up-down ratio at freeze-out fails at the floor, where the mirror is degenerate and, for a copied lepton number $L \leq 0$, ends $96$ to $100$ percent neutrons; it is helium only for $\xi$ between about $3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$, an interval containing the hot-deposit estimate (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}). The burning branch is therefore not the floor's composition.

The yield comparison is Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.seeding-gravity-floor-dark-towers-temperature}'s $Y$ at the ceiling against $\eta$ times the photon-to-entropy ratio $0.1413$; the black-hole clause is Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}(iv), under \claimref{dark-matter.p5-boundary-modes-hold-entropy-not}. \[
\Gamma_{\mathrm{weak}} \;\approx\; G_{F}^{2}T'^{5} \qquad\text{against}\qquad H \;=\; \frac{1.66\sqrt{g_{*}}\,T'^{2}}{\xi^{2}M_{\mathrm{Pl}}}

(non-reduced $M_{\mathrm{Pl}}$) and solves for the crossing at both ends of the interval; it iterates
\[
\frac{B_{D}}{T'} \;=\; \ln\frac{1}{\eta'} + \frac{3}{2}\ln\frac{m_{p}}{T'}

to a fixed point for the bottleneck; and it evaluates the entropy-evolution factor
\[
(g_{\mathrm{mir}}^{\mathrm{seed}}/g_{\mathrm{mir}})^{1/3}(g_{\mathrm{vis}}/g_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\mathrm{seed}})^{1/3},
\]
the photon energy per baryon $2.701\,T'/\eta'$ with the plasma budget $2.75$ times it, the completion-limit reheating factor $(1 + 7.07\ \mathrm{MeV}/E_{\mathrm{plasma}})^{1/4}$, the density and cosmic time at the bottleneck and the Saha recombination temperature, all script-bracketed in decimal arithmetic. Then, for a tower of any dimension, with the extra directions (if any) either co-expanding with the shared scale factor $a$ or static, and with a missing shared direction (the three-dimensional towers, which contain two of the three shared spatial directions) filled by a family of sheets, comoving in the background and displaced with the matter in perturbations (Proposition 7.28), one per unit of comoving length along the missing direction, the projected energy density of non-relativistic matter dilutes as $a^{-3}$ and that of radiation (the zero modes along any static extra direction) as $a^{-4}$, exactly as in this tower. No tower is diluted away or into prominence relative to this one.
deposited.proof:
Let the tower have $D$ spatial directions, $D - 3 = e \geq 0$ of them extra. Co-expanding case: number density per unit $D$-volume scales as $a^{-D}$, and a massless quantum's energy as $a^{-1}$, so the densities per $D$-volume are $a^{-D}$ (matter) and $a^{-(D+1)}$ (radiation); the extra directions have length proportional to $a$, so integrating over them multiplies by $a^{e}$, giving $a^{-3}$ and $a^{-4}$. Static case: the extra directions have fixed length, number density per $D$-volume scales as $a^{-3}$, a massless quantum with no momentum along the static directions redshifts as $a^{-1}$, and integration over the fixed length changes no power: $a^{-3}$ and $a^{-4}$ again (a quantum with momentum along a static direction keeps that momentum and behaves as a massive four-dimensional mode, hence as matter).

For $e < 0$, the three-dimensional towers, the missing shared direction is filled as the hypothesis states, by a comoving family of sheets: the density per unit two-volume within a sheet scales as $a^{-2}$ (matter) or $a^{-3}$ (radiation), and the number of sheets per unit proper length along the missing direction as $a^{-1}$, giving $a^{-3}$ and $a^{-4}$.

The other reading, a single sheet of fixed proper thickness, violates the rule's homogeneity clause and would give $a^{-2}$ and $a^{-3}$, under which the three-dimensional towers would grow relative to everything else; it is named because two of the four odd towers are exactly these. The exponent arithmetic is script-checked as a function of the rule (expanding directions, static extra directions, sheet families) for $D = 2, 3, 4$.

t14-regenerated.title: The radiation audit: what the type-by-residue theorem closes, and what stays open
t14-regenerated.text:
The cosmic microwave background caps extra relativistic energy at $\Delta\Neff \lesssim 0.3$ \cite{Planck2018}, and one massless photon-like species (two polarisations) at the visible temperature contributes $\Delta\Neff = (8/7)(11/4)^{4/3} \approx 4.4$, so five democratically filled sectors with such photons would contribute of order twenty. The audit proceeds tower by tower, at two levels fixed by Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can} and Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.where-flag-defined-what-it-carries}: the \emph{ground} level, where the type decides whether the tower's spinors carry an intrinsic $U(1)$ (exactly at the complex member of each odd pair, $r = 3, 7$ in the paper's convention), and the \emph{rung} level, where every flagged tower carries abelian charges from its ladder pairs.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The mirror tower, $r = 2$.)} Open, by theorem: the mirror's derived content is a copy of ours (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), so it has a massless mirror photon and three light mirror neutrinos. The ground level is closed for the real member of the pair $\{2, 6\}$ (intrinsic group $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$, Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(i); which member depends on the labelling convention, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}) and irrelevant, since the content is not at that level. This is the mirror-matter situation of the literature, costed in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs}.
\item \emph{(The three-dimensional towers, $r = 1, 7$.)} Closed at both levels: vector-like (no chirality in odd dimension), so Dirac masses are unforbidden and generic; with no massless charged matter left, each compact $U(1)$ in three dimensions, the intrinsic one of the complex member of $\{1, 7\}$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(ii)) and the rung-level ones of both, leaves no massless photon. The paper states that every such $U(1)$ confines by monopoles \cite{Polyakov1977}; with the half-integral bare Chern-Simons level that the parity anomaly forces (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.anomalies}(i)), that holds in the confining phase (C) only, and in phase (T) the photon is instead topologically massive (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-phases}); both phases close the channel. The non-abelian factors confine.
\item \emph{(The five-dimensional towers, $r = 3, 5$.)} Open at both levels: the complex member of the pair $\{3, 5\}$ carries an intrinsic $U(1)$ by theorem (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(ii); which member depends on the convention), both carry rung-level ones, no Polyakov mechanism exists in five dimensions, and by Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} a surviving photon dilutes as $a^{-4}$, exactly as ours.
\item \emph{(The Goldstone exposure.)} Confining dark sectors with chiral breaking could leave massless dark pions. The framework supplies its own gap: any tower's accidental global symmetries are broken by its own tower's higher rungs (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}), so the Goldstones are pseudo-Goldstones with masses of order $\Lambda_{\mathrm{conf}}^{2}/M_{\mathrm{rung}}$, the existence input a theorem and the mass estimate dimensional analysis.
\end{enumerate}
Conclusion: the three-dimensional towers are closed by theorem plus Polyakov confinement or, in phase (T), topological mass; the mirror tower is open by theorem, with a known relativistic content, and closes only if it is cold, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} is an exception to P2 (applied with the reach of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), (v), P2 gives $\xi = 1$ and $\Delta\Neff = 7.45$); the five-dimensional towers are open with a content this paper does not derive. By the section ``Seeding by gravity, and why no coupling rule follows'' (proved given the imported rate) every dark tower's temperature is bounded below by gravitational heating at a few parts in ten thousand of the visible temperature at the top of the ceiling range, and above by whatever energy the descent deposited, which the $\Neff$ cap limits to $0.448$ for the mirror and the paper's hot-deposit estimate puts near $4 \times 10^{-3}$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}); across that interval both the mirror's channel and the five-dimensional towers' close by eight orders or more (twelve at the floor; the one case below eight is a nine-vector tower at the hot end, at $7.4$). $\Delta\Neff \approx 0$ is therefore a conditional stance, conditional on the open channels closing by one of the routes of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs} and on the deposit being no hotter than the estimate; so registered, and stated with that cost.

On self-interaction: in the three-dimensional towers it is at composite strength if their matter is the confined charged matter the closure leaves, which the series does not establish (the section ``The composition in galaxy clusters and in the Galaxy''); in the five-dimensional ones it is undetermined; and for the mirror the composite figure is the wrong one, since mirror matter recombines at a visible temperature of order a keV (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}) and enters structure formation as neutral mirror atoms, with an elastic cross-section per mass of order $2 \times 10^{8}$ (hydrogen) or $5 \times 10^{7}$ (helium) $\mathrm{cm^{2}\,g^{-1}}$, and as a plasma once ionised inside a halo: collisional and dissipative like our gas, tested by the collisional-fraction and dark-disk bounds of refutation item 6. The rung-breaking scale of channel (4) is valued in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success}.

(1) is Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(i); the ground-level remark is Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(i). (2) Odd-dimensional towers admit no chirality, so mass terms are unforbidden; Polyakov's theorem is imported at its own level and applies to every compact $U(1)$ once the charged matter is massive, whatever the charge's origin. t14-regenerated.title: The open channels, with their costs
t14-regenerated.text:
\emph{The mirror tower.} Its relativistic content is a copy of ours, so at recombination its radiation is $\rho'_{\mathrm{rad}} = (T'/T_{\gamma})^{4}\,\rho_{\mathrm{rad}}$ with $T'$ the mirror photon temperature and the same internal thermal history; in neutrino units the visible radiation is
\[
\Neff^{\mathrm{tot}} \;=\; \frac{8}{7}\left(\frac{11}{4}\right)^{4/3} + 3.044 \;=\; 7.447, \qquad\text{so}\qquad \Delta\Neff^{\mathrm{mirror}} \;=\; 7.447\left(\frac{T'}{T_{\gamma}}\right)^{4},
\]
and the Planck cap requires $T'/T_{\gamma} < 0.448$ (three relativistic mirror neutrinos; if the heaviest is non-relativistic at recombination, true for $T'/T_{\gamma}$ below about $0.3$ at our masses, the coefficient is $6.40$ and the threshold $0.47$; the paper carries the conservative figure). A copy releases the same entropy as ours at the same epochs, so this ratio is the ratio \emph{seeded at the descent} (the copied history fails at the mirror's nucleosynthesis near the floor, where burning reheats its plasma by $3.0$ to $3.2$, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}; the bound is met on either reading, by eight orders or more up to the hot-deposit point estimate of that Proposition): route (a) below does not arise for the mirror, and the descent must have heated it to less than $0.448$ of the visible temperature, the standard requirement of mirror-matter cosmology \cite{FootMirror2004}. The structure meets it with one datum: after the descent the mirror is heated only through the shared metric (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}), which puts its temperature at a floor of about three parts in ten thousand of ours at the top of the ceiling range (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}(ii); $1.1 \times 10^{-3}$ even for a coefficient of ten, beyond the mirror's content), and above the floor the deposit sets it, near four parts in a thousand on the paper's estimate (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}). A cold mirror with our baryon number is what the framework predicts once that seeded temperature is taken as a free datum of the descent; by Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} this is an exception to P2, which, applied with the reach of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), (v), gives $T'/T_{\gamma} = 1$ and $\Delta\Neff = 7.45$, excluded by the cap above.

\emph{The five-dimensional towers.} A massless abelian species surviving in tower $r$ at temperature $T_{r}$ with $g_{r}$ light polarisations contributes
\[
\Delta\Neff \;=\; g_{r}\,\frac{4}{7}\left(\frac{11}{4}\right)^{4/3}\left(\frac{T_{r}}{T_{\gamma}}\right)^{4} \;\approx\; 2.2\,g_{r}\left(\frac{T_{r}}{T_{\gamma}}\right)^{4}
\]
($g_{r} = 2$ for a four-dimensional photon or a five-dimensional zero mode, $3$ if a fifth component is light). The cap $\Delta\Neff \lesssim 0.3$ is met by one such species if and only if $T_{r}/T_{\gamma} \lesssim (0.3/2.2\,g_{r})^{1/4}$, that is, $0.51$ for $g_{r} = 2$ and $0.46$ for $g_{r} = 3$, and by several jointly if their sum is under the cap.

Three routes close a channel, none proved here. (a) The sector is colder than the photons by a factor of about two, as a sector decoupled and releasing less entropy than ours is: the visible entropy release from the GeV epoch to today heats the photons relative to such a sector by $(g_{*}(\mathrm{GeV})/g_{*}(\mathrm{now}))^{1/3} \approx 2.51$, giving $\Delta\Neff \approx 0.11$ per two-polarisation species, so the two five-dimensional towers sit at $0.22$ with two light polarisations each, under the cap, and at $0.33$ with three, over it; a sector decoupled since the descent is colder still. (b) The abelian factor is Higgsed by the tower's own condensate, whenever that condensate carries the charge (this tower's neutral condensate is the accident that leaves our photon massless). (c) The rung-level charges, or the intrinsic $U(1)$, are not gauged in that tower once its content is derived as this tower's was. Route (a) is a thermal-history computation, (b) and (c) content derivations; all three are successor problem (1).

Observation level; the stance $\Delta\Neff \approx 0$ is registered conditional on them and on the mirror's seeded temperature.
t14-regenerated.proof: The mirror's relativistic content is a copy of ours (by \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), so its total is the photon value plus the three-neutrino value $3.044$ (the record's Standard-Model $\Neff$); the threshold is $(0.3/7.447)^{1/4}$, script-bracketed. The single-species $\Delta\Neff$ formula is the ratio of the species' energy density to one neutrino species', $g_{r}/2$ times the two-polarisation value times $(T_{r}/T_{\gamma})^{4}$; the thresholds are its inversion, script-bracketed. The entropy-release factor is the standard $g_{*}^{1/3}$ scaling, $(61.75/3.91)^{1/3} \approx 2.51$ from the GeV epoch to today, and $4.40 \times 2.51^{-4} \approx 0.11$, script-bracketed. Routes (b) and (c) are stated, not proved. The seeded temperature rests on Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}, which supplies that after the descent the mirror couples to this tower only through the shared metric.

This section states one rule that returns the remainder as a closed form, and says what the rule assumes, what mechanism returns its one length, and what the geometry of the series does and does not fix about it. The rule is a reading of the sourcing rule of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} with three premises added, at observation level throughout; it is not a coupling rule. The standing of the result is Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness} and Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}.

\emph{A note on placement.} The unit-ball rule was proposed by the author after the first version of this paper was complete, and it was added as a section of its own, after the audits, rather than worked through the earlier sections, so that no result numbered in Sections 2 to 6 would move and every citation of them from elsewhere in the series would stay valid. \begin{equation}
\frac{\Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}}{\Omega_{b}} \;=\; 1 + 2 f_{3\mathrm{D}} + 2 f_{5\mathrm{D}}, \qquad f_{3\mathrm{D}} := f_{1} = f_{7}, \quad f_{5\mathrm{D}} := f_{3} = f_{5},
\end{equation}
where in this section $f_{r}$ is the share of the tower of residue $r$, its matter per unit of our volume in units of ours (not the asymmetric tower factor of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}, which vanishes for odd $r$), and the two equalities are P2's audit along the reversal orbit, which exchanges $1$ with $7$ and $3$ with $5$. t14-regenerated.title: A reduced response to gravity needs a supporting stress; the sheets move
t14-regenerated.text:
Let a pressureless component respond to the gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}; the perturbed FLRW field in the conformal Newtonian gauge of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-linear-momentum-equation-traceless-field}, potentials $\psi$, $\phi$) at a fraction $g$ of the full strength, $\theta' = -\mathcal{H}\theta + g\,k^{2}\psi$. Then (i) it carries the anisotropic stress $\sigma = (1 - g)\psi$, and no other value; (ii) that stress enters the field equations, so that with the other components' stresses $\Sigma$,
\[
\psi \;=\; \frac{\phi - 12\pi G a^{2}\Sigma/k^{2}}{1 + 12\pi G a^{2}\rho\,(1 - g)/k^{2}} .
\]
For a three-dimensional tower whose sheets are held fixed, $g = \sin^{2}\theta$ for a wavevector at angle $\theta$ to the missing direction (script: $k_{\perp}^{2}/k^{2}$), $\tfrac{2}{3}$ averaged over orientations, and the stress of (i) is that of a medium holding the sheets in place. The series supplies no such medium: nothing in Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} or in the towers' content gives the sheet family a rigidity along its normal, and the sourcing rule couples the sheets' matter to the one gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ like any other. Hence, on the series as written, the sheets are displaced along their normal by the potential gradient, $g = 1$, and the three-dimensional towers respond to gravity in full at linear order.

The source factor is the projection of the potential gradient onto the sheet, $|\mathbf{k}_{\perp}|^{2}/|\mathbf{k}|^{2}$, whose average over the sphere of directions is $\tfrac{2}{3}$. The last two sentences are a statement about the series' content, at the level of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}: the lemma's sheet family is comoving in the background and carries no stress, so the only consistent reading of it is the one in which the sheets move.

t14-regenerated.title: The sheet family and the linear spectra
t14-regenerated.text: Two readings of the sheet family are excluded, one by symmetry and one by the record. A fixed missing direction gives no clustering along it for $42\%$ of all matter, against the statistical isotropy of the matter power spectrum and the microwave background at the level of a few percent, and it is the uncaused selection P2 refuses. Orientations varying below observed scales give the isotropic average $g = \tfrac{2}{3}$, and that the spectra exclude directly. Computed with a Boltzmann code (a figure of the original; CLASS \cite{CLASS2011}, version 3.4, Planck 2018 parameters otherwise, the three-dimensional towers as a separate pressureless species responding at $g$ with the stress of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.reduced-response-gravity-needs-supporting-stress} carried so that the field equations stay consistent; the patch, inputs and outputs are deposited with the verification materials as a record), $49.7\%$ of the dark matter at $g = \tfrac{2}{3}$ gives $\sigma_{8} = 0.36$ against $0.81$, the lensing-potential spectrum at $28\%$ of the standard model's, and the temperature spectrum $17\%$ high at $\ell = 100$, against measurements at the percent level; the floor's $40.5\%$ and the exchanged assignment's $31.6\%$ give $\sigma_{8} = 0.42$ and $0.49$; and with half the dark matter in the towers a deficit $1 - g$ above about half a percent is excluded by the lensing amplitude alone. Both readings need the stress the series does not have. The reading it does have, $g = 1$, returns in the same code the standard model's temperature, polarisation, lensing and matter power spectra to four decimal places for the rule's composition (the towers as a separate species at full response), so at linear order the rule's dark sector is the standard model's. Within collapsed structures the three-dimensional towers differ from cold dark matter only by what the sheets add beyond collisionless gravity (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.halo-built-collisionless-sheets-cold-dark}): the self-interaction of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem-closes-what}, which is the fraction test of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}(v), with the cross-section read per sheet (at composite strength a fluid, the section ``The composition in galaxy clusters and in the Galaxy''), and, on the deposit branch only, an in-plane free-streaming cutoff. t14-regenerated.title: A halo built from collisionless sheets is a cold-dark-matter halo
t14-regenerated.text: Beyond linear order the question is what the sheets do to a halo, and the answer is an argument, not a simulation. A particle of a three-dimensional tower has two velocities: its motion within its sheet, the tower's own dynamics, and the motion of the sheet, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.reduced-response-gravity-needs-supporting-stress} follows the normal component of gravity pointwise. The one constraint the sheets impose is that at a point of a sheet the normal velocity is single-valued, the sheet being a surface; in-plane velocities are whatever the tower's dynamics allows, and sheets may cross, nothing forbidding it and the sourcing rule already stacking them. Cold dark matter is the same object in all three directions: a single-valued velocity field on a three-dimensional Lagrangian sheet in phase space, multi-streaming only where Lagrangian patches cross. So the sheet family's phase space contains cold dark matter's, one direction treated exactly as cold dark matter treats all three and two directions treated more permissively; with cold initial conditions, which the seeding floor gives (the section ``Seeding by gravity, and why no coupling rule follows''), the in-plane motion is itself a cold single-valued flow and the two phase spaces coincide. The Lagrangian map of the sheet matter is then cold dark matter's at every order in collisionless dynamics, not only at the linear order a figure of the original checks, and a simulation of sheet-labelled particles against plain ones would integrate the same equations. Halo shapes, velocity structure and the pancake, filament and halo sequence are cold dark matter's. What can differ is what the sheets add. First, in-sheet self-interaction: a quantum collides only with quanta of its own sheet, at composite strength on the reading of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem-closes-what}, so the collision rate is set by the surface density within a sheet and the galaxy-cluster bounds on $\sigma/m$ must be re-expressed for a cross-section per sheet before the fraction test of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}(v) is read against them. The companion note T14b does this: per unit of the mass gravity sees, the cross-section is $10^{8}$ to $10^{13}\ \mathrm{cm^{2}\,g^{-1}}$, so at composite strength the sheet matter is a fluid within its sheets, not collisionless, and in simulated galaxy clusters it forms a cored component rounder than cold dark matter (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-composition-simulated}). The conclusion of this remark therefore holds only if the three-dimensional towers' matter is collisionless. Second, on the deposit branch, an in-plane thermal velocity $\sigma_{v}$: free streaming then damps small scales within the plane only, and averaged over orientations the damping is $\langle\exp(-k^{2}\sigma_{v}^{2}\tau^{2}\sin^{2}\theta)\rangle$, milder than isotropic warm dark matter at the same dispersion by the missing normal direction; at the seeding floor $\sigma_{v}$ is of order $10^{-4}$ of our matter's thermal velocity and the cutoff lies far below any observed scale. Structural level: the argument rests on cold initial conditions, on the sheets carrying no stress and on the sheet matter being collisionless.

t14-regenerated.title: What would refute this paper
t14-regenerated.text:
Seven ways, each with its cost. Item 6 is the standing test, where the derivation meets the record and the record is already pressing; item 7 is its gravitational-wave form, unconditional in class and model-dependent in rate; item 2 is an unconditional running experiment; item 4 is bounded by the deposit interval; item 5 is conditional on an unsolved successor problem; items 1 and 3 are theory-internal risks. That the odd towers are empty, or that no consistent value of their relic densities supplies the remainder, does not refute this paper, which does not derive the remainder (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}(iii)); the capstone carries both as conditions on the programme \cite{ButlerT17}. The unit-ball rule's own exposures follow the six and refute the rule, not the paper.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Exhibit caused, tower-distinguishing structure in the pre-descent state, and P2 fails where most depends on it: the mirror's equivalence to this tower and the family ordering fall together (this paper and the families paper share the weakness).
\item Detect dark matter directly or indirectly at any strength above the gravitational floor, and the superselection is breached: Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable} is refuted outright, and with it the exact stability, the gravity-only seeding, and both conditional null stances.
\item Break the superselection argument itself: find a frozen-phase local operator that changes signature. The stability guarantee goes, though not the population count.
\item Exhibit one exactly massless dark species at a temperature above the thresholds of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs}, and the radiation audit fails against the measured $\Neff$. Within the interval of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number} an excess reads first as a deposit hotter than the paper's estimate, the deposit energy being a datum the framework does not fix; it refutes item 2 only above the cap's own limit on the deposit, $T'/T_{\gamma} = 0.448$ for the mirror, where a species must have been heated by something other than gravity.
\item Derive the tower dimensions from the descent and find a window other than P3's, and the count of causal residues moves with the census of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}(iii); the asymmetric share moves only if a new even causal residue appears at a dimension divisible by four (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension}): the windows that make $r = 0$ and $r = 4$ causal do so at $(1,1)$ and $(1,5)$, which carry no bit, so on those windows the asymmetric share is unchanged.
\item \emph{The standing test.} Find the mirror's share other than one. Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one} makes it a theorem, so this refutes P2 for the mirror, the descent's single ceiling, or the charge reading of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}. With the remainder of the ratio underived, this is the one place the paper's derived content meets the record, and the record is already pressing on it.

\emph{Already in tension:} the share is $18.6$ percent of the dark matter in cold, dissipative mirror baryons, and the record's analysis of mirror dark matter's galactic structure allows at most $0.8\,\Omega_{b}$ at low mirror temperature \cite{RouxCline2020}, a fifth below the prediction, which is a quarter above it. That analysis rescales the mirror's baryon-to-photon ratio as $\eta' = \eta\,\beta/x^{3}$ and includes a helium mirror down to $x = T'/T = 10^{-3}$, which covers the hot end of the framework's interval; it does not include the interval's floor, where the framework's mirror, whose $\eta'$ runs from about $0.008$ to $26$, reaches forty billion times ours, and is helium throughout on the expected branch (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}), nor the supernova energy of helium stars, which the companion note T14b finds to be $3.6$ to $7.3$ times ours per unit mass formed \cite{ButlerT14b}.

The dark-disk test runs in two phases. In the \emph{diffuse phase} mirror gas accreted into a halo is shock-heated to the virial temperature and ionised, a fluid with a mean free path of order ten parsecs ($\sigma/m \sim 10^{8}\ \mathrm{cm^{2}\,g^{-1}}$); this is what the Bullet Cluster's bound on the subcluster's mass loss, about $23$ percent and inferred from the mass-to-light ratios, tests \cite{Randall2008}; read as a bound on the dark matter, $18.6$ percent passes, and simulated, a merger in which only the mirror collides gives a mass-to-light change of $0.82$, consistent with the observed $0.84 \pm 0.07$, as cold dark matter's is (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-composition-simulated}(ii)). Its radiative cooling time is of order ten gigayears at the virial radius and a gigayear or less inside the cooling radius, where $n \gtrsim 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, so, as with our baryons, the inner gas radiates its support within a Hubble time and the outer gas does not. In the \emph{settled phase} what cools forms a mirror disk or compact objects of total mass up to $\Omega_{b'} \approx \Omega_{b}$; a thin disk of the visible disk's mass, about $50\ M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ locally, exceeds the Gaia thin-dark-disk bounds of a few $M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ \cite{Schutz2018, Widmark2021} by an order of magnitude, so the settled phase must not be a thin disk. A thick or fragmented component, or mirror feedback holding gas in the diffuse phase, avoids the bound; fragmentation into compact objects is closed by the microlensing limits (compact objects at most $1$ percent of the halo from $1.8 \times 10^{-4}$ to $6.3\ M_{\odot}$ and $10$ percent up to $860\ M_{\odot}$ \cite{Mroz2024}) unless the objects form outside that window. The phase split, the star-formation efficiency, the settled gas's fate and whether helium composition delays settling are the model; the record's mirror-galaxy analysis \cite{RouxCline2020} models them with a rescaled $\eta'$ and a helium mirror at the hot end of the interval, not at its floor; Randall et al.'s mass-to-light ratios \cite{Randall2008} are the observation behind the mass-loss bound, and Clowe et al.'s offset \cite{Clowe2006} behind the lensing test. Model-dependent, so on the burning branch a tension and not an exclusion: this is the framework's one theorem-level dark-matter prediction, and it is at the edge of the record already. The companion note T14b models the settled phase in the Milky Way (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-composition-simulated}(iv)): the proton-only branch is excluded at the Sun, and the burning branch's helium mirror, cooling slowly and with helium-star feedback, is open at the Sun under some normalisations of its gas and in the bulge only if the bulge holds over twice the mirror's proportional share of its dark mass, so that either of two measurements not yet made would decide it. Neither measurement can yet be made from published results. The tightest Gaia bound on a thin dark disk, about $5\ M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ at $95$ percent \cite{Widmark2021}, holds only for scale heights of $50$ pc or less, and at the $100$ to $500$ pc the test needs the bound is weaker; the dynamical models of the bulge \cite{Portail2017} measure its dark mass, about $3.1 \times 10^{9}\ M_{\odot}$, as halo-like, and do not separate a disk-like part from the stars' mass-to-light ratio. The test therefore needs two analyses not yet made: a vertical-dynamics or phase-space-spiral analysis of Gaia data with a dark disk of that thickness, and a bulge model with a disk-like dark component. Until then the Galaxy test is registered, not run.
\item \emph{Dark neutron-star mergers.} The copy theorem makes the mirror sector baryonic, dissipative and at the proton mass, so it forms stars, and its neutron stars have our equation of state: the same maximum mass and the same tidal deformability $\Lambda(M)$. The prediction is a class of compact-binary mergers in the ground-based gravitational-wave band with component masses of one to two solar masses, $\Lambda$ in the range of ordinary neutron stars, and no electromagnetic counterpart at any depth or distance. Nothing in the standard model produces that class, and primordial black holes in the mass range have $\Lambda = 0$. The rate is model-dependent: the mirror sector is helium-dominated on the expected branch (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}) and helium star formation has no calibrated efficiency, so the natural expectation is within an order of magnitude of the visible binary-neutron-star rate, tens to hundreds per cubic gigaparsec per year, and the framework fixes the class and the deformability, not the number. GW190425, with no counterpart and its deformability unconstrained, is the class's example event. Refutation: a large sample of neutron-star-mass mergers whose counterpart fraction is consistent with an all-visible population bounds $\Omega_{b'}$ below $\Omega_{b}$ and refutes Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-assembled} as item 6 does; confirmation is a counterpart fraction well below the visible population's with $\Lambda$ consistent with our equation of state, which third-generation detectors will measure for hundreds of events.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{The unit-ball rule's exposures} (the section ``The dark matter ratio: the unit-ball rule''; these cost the rule and Premises R1 to R3, not the paper). (a) A combined measurement of $\Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}/\Omega_{b}$ settling below the floor $5.255$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}(ii) by more than its error excludes every thickness at once; the ACT DR6 combination's $5.22$ is already there if it holds. (b) A sharper measurement leaving $c = 1$ outside the window of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}(iv) excludes R3 and the mechanism behind it; one leaving both windows excludes the exchanged assignment too and leaves a fitted $c$ with no geometric name. (c) The self-interacting fraction (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}(v)): at composite strength it is about a half at $c = 1$, and simulated, that composition fails the Bullet Cluster and the shapes of galaxy clusters (the section ``The composition in galaxy clusters and in the Galaxy''); with the odd towers' matter collisionless the colliding fraction is the mirror's $18.6$ percent, the composition passes the merger and is not excluded by the shapes, and a colliding fraction measured well away from it excludes that reading whatever the total does. Under that reading the fraction no longer separates the rule from the exchanged assignment (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.equivalent-forms-assignment-not}). Against these stands the caveat of Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}(ii): the closed form is one of fourteen equally simple candidates in the error bar, found by solving for the target, so the value alone is not evidence; the floor is, and the fraction is evidence about the three-dimensional towers' couplings.

t14-regenerated.title: Imported: the massless-graviton production rate
t14-regenerated.text:
Dark matter produced from the Standard-Model plasma by massless graviton exchange has rate per volume
\[
R(T) \;=\; \frac{\alpha\,T^{8}}{M_{P}^{4}}, \qquad M_{P} = 2.435 \times 10^{18}\ \mathrm{GeV},
\]
the reduced Planck mass, with $\alpha = 1.9 \times 10^{-4}$, $1.1 \times 10^{-3}$, $2.3 \times 10^{-3}$ for one scalar, one fermion and one vector \emph{produced} species respectively, the sum over the Standard-Model bath being inside the coefficient, weighted as $4|\mathcal{M}^{0}|^{2} + 45|\mathcal{M}^{1/2}|^{2} + 12|\mathcal{M}^{1}|^{2}$ over its scalar, Weyl-fermion and vector degrees. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Bernal2018}, Eq.~(31), $R^{0}(T) = (3997\pi^{3}/663552000)\,T^{8}/M_{P}^{4}$ for the scalar case, and Table I, the massless-graviton limit of that paper's massive spin-2 mediator. Imported at assembly level: whether the fermion coefficient is per Weyl or per Dirac species is carried as a bracket; the factor between counting particles and pairs, and the mean energy per quantum, are absorbed into a factor of at most $2^{1/4}$ on the temperature ratio below.
t14-regenerated.provenance: N. Bernal, M. Dutra, Y. Mambrini, K. Olive, M. Peloso, and M. Pierre, Spin-2 portal dark matter, Phys. Rev. D 97 (2018), 115020.

t14-regenerated.title: Seeding by gravity: the floor on a dark tower's temperature
t14-regenerated.text:
By exact superselection the towers interact only through the shared metric (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}), so after the descent a dark tower can be heated only gravitationally; what the descent itself deposited in it (its charge, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}, with whatever energy the deposit carried) is a datum, not a computation. Let the descent reheat this tower to $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ and let tower $r$, with $g_{d}$ light degrees of freedom that thermalise among themselves, be heated by graviton-mediated production from the visible plasma at rate per volume $\Gamma = c\,T^{8}/M_{P}^{4}$, with $c$ the sum of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-production-rate}'s per-species coefficients over the tower's light content. Then the produced comoving yield is
\[
Y \;=\; \frac{c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}}{3\,\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3}}, \qquad \kappa_{s} = \sqrt{\frac{\pi^{2}g_{*}}{90}}\;\frac{2\pi^{2}}{45}\,g_{s} \;=\; 145.3 \ \text{at } g_{*} = g_{s} = 100,
\]
its energy fraction at production is $4Y$, and the temperature ratio it alone would give is
\[
\xi_{\mathrm{floor}} \;=\; \Big(4Y\,\frac{g_{*}}{g_{d}}\Big)^{1/4} \;=\; 9.6 \times 10^{-4}\; c^{1/4}\Big(\frac{16}{g_{d}}\Big)^{1/4}\Big(\frac{T_{\mathrm{desc}}}{6 \times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{GeV}}\Big)^{3/4}
\]
for $g_{*} = g_{s} = 100$ at the reheating. This is a floor: the tower's bath cannot be colder, and it is hotter by whatever energy the deposit carried. The ratio thereafter evolves through the two sectors' separate entropy conservation, by
\[
\left(\frac{g_{d}^{\mathrm{seed}}}{g_{d}}\right)^{1/3}\left(\frac{g_{s}}{g_{s}^{\mathrm{seed}}}\right)^{1/3}
\]
at any later epoch. Two inputs are not fixed by the formula: $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$, the ceiling of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success} or below it, so that across that range the floor spans a factor $(3.5 \times 10^{11}/6 \times 10^{14})^{3/4}$, about $4 \times 10^{-3}$ ($3.75 \times 10^{-3}$), the body quoting the top and saying so; and the deposit's energy, which sets the actual ratio above the floor.
t14-regenerated.proof:
With $dt = -dT/(HT)$,
\[
H \;=\; \sqrt{\frac{\pi^{2}g_{*}}{90}}\;\frac{T^{2}}{M_{P}}, \qquad s \;=\; \frac{2\pi^{2}}{45}\,g_{s}T^{3},
\]
in the reduced-mass convention the rate is quoted in (the familiar $1.66\sqrt{g_{*}}\,T^{2}/M_{\mathrm{Pl}}$ with the non-reduced $M_{\mathrm{Pl}} = 1.22 \times 10^{19}$ GeV is the same rate, $1.66 = \sqrt{8\pi}\sqrt{\pi^{2}/90}$), the Boltzmann equation $\dot{n} + 3Hn = \Gamma$, gravitational production being the only source (by \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}), for the comoving yield $Y = n/s$ reads
\[
\frac{dY}{dT} \;=\; -\frac{\Gamma}{HTs} \;=\; -\frac{c\,T^{2}}{\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3}},
\]
which integrates from $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ downward to the stated $Y$, dominated by the top of the range (the script brackets the integral between Riemann sums of that integrand). The energy fraction is $3T\,n/((\pi^{2}/30)g_{*}T^{4}) = 4Y$ for quanta of mean energy $3T$, and $\xi_{\mathrm{floor}}$ follows from $\rho_{d} = (\pi^{2}/30)g_{d}\xi^{4}T^{4}$, which presupposes that the produced quanta thermalise within the tower (true for the mirror's content; assumed for a pure-glue tower). The prefactor, referred to the top of the ceiling range of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success}, is script-evaluated at $c = 0.01, 1, 10$ and at the coefficients of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}, with the two Planck-mass conventions confirmed to give one rate. Level: proved given the imported rate (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-production-rate}) and the standard thermal history (the expansion law, the entropy density, the mean quantum energy and the degree-of-freedom values, listed in the section ``Machine verification'' as assumed).

t14-regenerated.title: The coefficients, the floors they give, and what gravity cannot supply
t14-regenerated.text:
(i) For a five-dimensional tower whose light content is the nine vectors of its $\mathfrak{u}(3)$, eight gluons and the abelian photon, $c = 9 \times 2.3 \times 10^{-3} = 0.021$, $g_{d} = 18$, and $\xi_{\mathrm{floor}} = 3.5 \times 10^{-4}$ at the ceiling reheating; whether those are its light species is part of the coupling question of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}, and the value is the floor for that content, not for the tower.

(ii) For the mirror tower, whose content is the Standard Model's (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), the species sum over four real scalars, forty-five Weyl fermions and twelve vectors gives $c = 0.053$ counting the fermions as $22.5$ Dirac species and $0.078$ counting them singly, with $g_{d} = 4 + 45 \times \tfrac{7}{4} + 24 = 106.75$, hence $\xi_{\mathrm{floor}}$ between $2.8$ and $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$ and, with the charge reading of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}, $\eta'$ between $19$ and $26$ at the floor; the bracket is the counting ambiguity and is carried as such, and $\eta'$ would fall below one at the floor only for a coefficient above about $4$.

(iii) The produced yield at the ceiling, $Y = 1.8$ to $2.7 \times 10^{-15}$ per unit entropy for the mirror, falls short of the $8.7 \times 10^{-11}$ baryons per unit entropy our baryon number requires by a factor of $3$ to $5 \times 10^{4}$; closing the gap would need $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ between $1.9$ and $2.2 \times 10^{16}$ GeV, $31.9$ to $36.2$ times the ceiling, where the floor itself would be $4 \times 10^{-3}$, above the charge-domination crossover and equal to the hot-deposit value of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}, as it must be (the same energy per unit of baryon number either way). Gravity heats the dark towers; it does not populate them with charge, which is the descent's.

(iv) The mirror's contribution to $\Neff$, $7.447\,\xi^{4}$, is below $10^{-13}$ at the floor and below $10^{-8}$ at the hot deposit of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}; a nine-vector tower's, $2.202 \times 18\,\xi^{4}$ for eighteen light polarisations, the coefficient being half the two-polarisation $\Delta\Neff$ bracketed in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem-closes-what}, is below $10^{-12}$ at its floor.
t14-regenerated.proof: Arithmetic on Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.seeding-gravity-floor-dark-towers-temperature} and Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-production-rate}, script-bracketed, with $g_{d}$ counting two polarisations per vector, one per real scalar and $\tfrac{7}{8} \times 2$ per Weyl fermion; the species summed in (ii) are the mirror's Standard Model content (by \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), and the counting ambiguity there is whether the imported fermion coefficient is per Weyl or per Dirac species, and the bracket spans both. (iii): $\eta$ times the photon-to-entropy ratio $n_{\gamma}/s = 0.1413$ against $Y$; the temperature that would make up the shortfall inverts $Y \propto T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}$; the floor at that temperature is $\xi_{\mathrm{floor}} \propto T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3/4}$, and its agreement with the hot-deposit value is the identity $4Y\,g_{*}/g_{d}$ evaluated at $Y = n_{B}/s$ on both sides. (iv): $g_{r}$ light polarisations at $2.2018$ each, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs}.
