t14-regenerated.title: No coupling rule for the odd towers follows from the series
t14-regenerated.text: No rule relating an odd tower's gauge coupling to this tower's follows from the series' premises and theorems, for three independent reasons. (a) In a tower of dimension $d \neq 4$ the gauge coupling is dimensionful, $[g^{2}] = \mathrm{mass}^{4-d}$, so a comparison with this tower's dimensionless coupling needs a length, and in five dimensions that length is the size of the fifth direction, which the sheaf paper's wall construction does not fix \cite{ButlerT4}. (b) No gauge coupling value is derived anywhere in the series (the Standard-Model paper takes $\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}$ and $\alpha_{s}$ from the record \cite[Fact 2.8, Prop.~6.1]{ButlerT12}), so a rule for a dark tower's coupling would be a rule for ours first. (c) Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} cannot supply democracy: the odd towers are inequivalent to this one as soldered algebras (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one}), off the reversal orbit along which alone the audit equates (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv)). Any rule is therefore a premise, and the paper adopts none; structural level, not proved in the sense of \cite{ButlerT1}.
t14-regenerated.proof: (a): under $g \mapsto \lambda^{2}g$ the volume form scales as $\lambda^{d}$ and the two inverse metrics in $\star$ on two-forms as $\lambda^{-4}$, so $\int F \wedge \star F$ scales as $\lambda^{d-4}$ and $1/g^{2}$ carries the compensating dimension. (b) and (c) are as stated, (c) resting on \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference}, which equates along the reversal orbit only, on Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one} for the inequivalence and on Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv) for the reversal orbit.
t14-regenerated.label: Proposition

t14-regenerated.title: Dimmed final evaporation bursts
t14-regenerated.text: Dimmed final evaporation bursts: the hole radiates into every populated tower, so it loses mass faster than the standard expectation (this tower plus gravitons) by the factor $D = \Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}/\Psi_{0}$ of total to standard emission, and the visible burst of its last $\tau$ is the standard burst of its last $D\tau$ divided by $D$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.dimmed-burst-time-rescaled-copy}). Dimming by the full ratio holds for the primary high-energy tail and for the visible fraction of the power at fixed mass; the visible energy in a fixed final window is dimmed by $D^{2/3}$, and the temperature at a fixed time before the end is lowered by $D^{1/3}$. The populated towers are this one and, under P2, the mirror, whose light content copies ours (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), so $D = (2 + g + o)/(1 + g)$, with $g$ and $o$ the gravitational and odd-tower emission relative to this tower's: $D \ge 2$ if and only if $o \ge g$, and $D = 2 - g/(1 + g)$ if the odd towers emit nothing. If the four odd towers hold matter, as Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated} infers from the observed dark remainder, then $o > 0$ and the dimming is larger.

t14-regenerated.title: The trichotomy: what kind of number $N$ is
t14-regenerated.text:
The question the paper ends by pointing at can itself be classified. The classification has four parts, of which the first contains a proved statement and a reading, the second is an import, the third is conditional on the first two, on Observation \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent} and on a decision the fourth names, and the fourth is imported from the action paper; the levels are marked clause by clause.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Kinematic.)} Proved: under $\Lambda \to s^{2}\Lambda$ at fixed $M_{P}$, that is $I \to sI$ on the frozen point with the conformal class unchanged, $H \to sH$ and $N \to N/s$, while every discrete invariant this paper derives (the algebra and its dimension twelve, the global form and its $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$, the dimension four, the content and the hypercharges, and under (S) the ratio $3/8$) is unchanged, since each is computed from the conformal class, the pair structure and the group alone, none of which the rescaling affects. Reading, at observation level: since the conformal class and the pair structure carry no scale, no construction from them alone can fix $N$, which lies in the ratio of the frozen point's norm to the Planck scale; on this reading the kinematic layer determines all discrete invariants and no continuous modulus, and $N$ and the weight spectrum are its only continuous moduli.
\item \emph{(Non-dynamical, imported.)} $\Lambda$ is the norm of the frozen point, and the norm is not a field: it is fixed by a constraint, the fluctuations of the frozen point are pure gauge, and the action carries no equation of motion for it (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-norm-frozen-point-not-field}).
\item \emph{(Initial data, conditional.)} If the alternatives kinematic, dynamical and initial-data are exhaustive, then by (1) and (2) $N$ is initial data, and Observation \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent}(ii) locates the boundary that carries it at the origin. The exhaustiveness is not proved here, and the location is an Observation; the clause is conditional on both, and clause (4) says what the exhaustiveness costs.
\item \emph{(Parameter of the laws, imported.)} The three alternatives are not exhaustive: a conserved quantity that is constant on every solution of a theory but varies across a family of theories indexed by a parameter is a parameter of the laws, and the action paper proves that under the action as written, with $\Lambda$ the value of the Stelle-West constraints fixed before variation, $N$ is exactly that: constant on each solution space $\mathcal{S}_{\Lambda}$ by the rigidity of (2), varying across $\Lambda$, so neither dynamically fixed nor initial data \cite[Prop.~5.8]{ButlerT10}. Clause (3) therefore holds only if the norm is promoted from a fixed number to the value of a Lagrange-multiplier field whose constancy is an equation of motion, the Henneaux-Teitelboim mechanism, which makes $\Lambda$ a label of the solution rather than of the theory; that promotion is a decision for the series, recorded open with both branches stated \cite[Rem.~5.9]{ButlerT10}, and the entropic and null-endpoint effects named below act on a measure over theories or on a measure within one theory according to it.
\end{enumerate}
At observation level, two competing effects are then named without being balanced: an entropic weighting of the freezing by $\exp(S_{\Lambda}) = \exp(\pi N^{2})$, with $S_{\Lambda} = \pi N^{2}$ the cosmological horizon's area-law entropy (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared}), favours large $N$ overwhelmingly (the well-known entropic argument for small $\Lambda$, inherited with every one of its known objections, listed as inherited and not solved), while at the endpoint $\Lambda = 0$ the frozen point is null and the curvature-squared presentation of the action, whose prefactor is $3/\Lambda$, does not exist; the action paper is explicit that this is a boundary of the presentation and not of the action, the Einstein-Cartan functional remaining \cite[Thm.~3.1, Rem.~3.2]{ButlerT10}, so what is lost at $\Lambda = 0$ is the reductive structure and the frozen point's length, not gravity. Large because large boundary mode spaces dominate the measure; nonzero because the descent selects a frozen point of nonzero length; the value is the balance point, and the balance point awaits the descent measure, the one object this framework does not possess. Last, a statement of units only, flagged as such: in the boundary modes' own units, qubits, one per rung of the Fock module (Theorem \claimref{tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung}), the horizon's capacity $S_{\Lambda} = \pi N^{2}$ is $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, about $4.8 \times 10^{122}$ qubits (the mode count of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-mode-count} under the black hole's counting rule), whose base-two logarithm is about $407$; the paper's $R = \log_{2} N^{2} \approx 405$ counts the rungs of a module of dimension $N^{2}$, whose capacity is only $\ln N^{2} = 2\ln N$ nats, not the horizon's. Neither number is a count of turns of the mod-8 clock, which no rung moves: each rung preserves the residue $p - q \pmod 8$ (Theorem \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial}). This is the question in the framework's own coordinates, not an answer to it.

t14-regenerated.title: On the conformal ambient, the field action of CPT conjugation is the pseudoscalar rotor times complex conjugation

Let $\R^{2,4}$ carry the conformal ambient metric, $\Cl(2,4)$ its Clifford algebra with $e_0^2 = e_1^2 = 1$ and $e_2^2 = \dots = e_5^2 = -1$, $I_6 = e_0 e_1 \cdots e_5$ its unit pseudoscalar and $\kappa$ complex conjugation on $\Cl(2,4) \otimes \C$. Let $W \subset \C^6$ be a maximal isotropic subspace with $W \cap \overline W = 0$ (the generic Witt flag of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}), and $\psi_W$ its pure spinor.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The composite of grade involution and reversal is an anti-automorphism of $\Cl(2,4)$, not an automorphism, and acts on vectors as $-1$. Grade involution equals $\mathrm{Ad}(I_6)$, and $I_6 = (e_0e_1)(e_2e_3)(e_4e_5)$ is a rotor of the identity component: each factor squares to $-1$ and is $\exp(\pi B_k/2)$, and $I_6 \widetilde{I_6} = 1$. So the vector action $-1$ lies in $SO_0(2,4)$. In $\Cl(1,3)$, by contrast, $I_4\widetilde{I_4} = -1$.
\item $W$ is the $+i$ eigenspace of an orthogonal complex structure $J$ on $\R^{2,4}$, $W \oplus \overline W = \C^6$, and $I_6\psi_{W} = \pm i\,\psi_{W}$, $I_6 \psi_{\overline W} = \mp i\,\psi_{\overline W}$. So $\overline W$ lies in the other family, and complex conjugation is a flag conjugate. In $\Cl(3,3)$, $I_6^2 = +1$ and conjugation preserves the family.
\item Every real-linear isometry $g$ of $\R^{2,4}$ with $g(W) = \overline W$ has $\det g = -1$, so that $\epsilon(gI, gV, gF, gF) = -\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$ for vectors $I, V$ and bivectors $F$, $g$ acting on bivectors by its outermorphism. The complex-linear Witt exchange $v_k \leftrightarrow w_k$ does not preserve $\R^{2,4}$.
\item $C := \mathrm{Ad}(I_6) \circ \kappa$ is an antilinear involutive automorphism of $\Cl(2,4) \otimes \C$ that is $-1$ on $\R^{2,4}$, fixes the metric, $\epsilon$ and $I_6$, and carries $\psi_W$ to a multiple of $\psi_{\overline W}$. With the flag conjugate realised by $\kappa$, the stored composite $\phi$ (grade involution, reversal, flag conjugate) is reversal composed with $C$: an antilinear anti-automorphism. No realisation of the flag conjugate on $\R^{2,4}$ is both real-linear and orientation-preserving.
\item \emph{Convention.} A (possibly anti-) automorphism $\phi$ acts on fields as a symmetry: on a vector field by its vector part, and on a connection $A$ through the Lie algebra automorphism it induces, $A \mapsto -\phi(A)$ when $\phi$ is an anti-automorphism, so that curvature transforms by the same automorphism; for the stored composite this is the action of $C$. In this convention every action functional of real tensor (multivector) fields on which $C$ acts through its vector part, invariant under constant $SO_0(2,4)$ transformations, in particular the frozen point's $Q(I)^{-1}\int \epsilon(I, V, F, F)$ (\claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}), satisfies $S \circ \phi = S$, while with any real-linear flag conjugate in place of $\kappa$ the same action changes sign. Spinor fields are not covered. If instead $\phi$ is applied to the Clifford integrand $IVFF$ as a whole and the top-grade coefficient taken, both sign statements invert (with $\kappa$ the integrand changes sign, with a real-linear flag conjugate it is preserved), so the conclusion of (5) depends on the convention.

t14-regenerated.title: The dimmed final burst is the standard burst rescaled in time; its primary high-energy tail is dimmed by the full ratio, its energy in a fixed final window only by the two-thirds power
t14-regenerated.text:
Let a black hole of the one metric evaporate in the regime where every populated tower's light species are lighter than its temperature, so that the emission coefficients are constant. Write $\Psi_{\mathrm{vis}}$ for this tower's coefficient in the mass-loss law, $\Psi_{\mathrm{grav}}$ for the gravitational sector's, $\Psi_{\mathrm{odd}}$ for the odd towers', $\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}$ for the total, $g = \Psi_{\mathrm{grav}}/\Psi_{\mathrm{vis}}$, $o = \Psi_{\mathrm{odd}}/\Psi_{\mathrm{vis}}$, and let the standard expectation be the hole with this tower and gravitons only, total coefficient $\Psi_{0} = \Psi_{\mathrm{vis}} + \Psi_{\mathrm{grav}}$. Put $D = \Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}/\Psi_{0}$. Let $\tau$ be the hole's remaining lifetime and $N(E;\tau)$ the number of visible quanta per unit energy emitted in its last $\tau$, $N_{0}$ its standard value.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] Every channel's flux per unit energy depends on $M$ and $E$ only through $ME$ (Theorem \claimref{hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-interface-premise}), so $dM/dt = -\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}/M^{2}$ and $M(\tau)^{3} = 3\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}\tau$; at fixed $M$ the visible power is the same as in the standard case (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}(i)).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Time rescaling.)} For any visible emission $h(E, M)$ per unit time, secondaries included, the same function in every tower configuration because the exterior metric does not record which tower the mass came from,
\[
N(E;\tau) \;=\; \frac{1}{D}\, N_{0}(E;D\tau):
\]
the visible burst of the last $\tau$ is the standard burst of the last $D\tau$, divided by $D$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Three dimming laws.)} Consequently, at fixed remaining lifetime: the visible energy emitted in the last $\tau$ is $D^{-2/3}$ times its standard value; the hole's temperature is $D^{-1/3}$ times its standard value; and for primary emission, whose flux depends on $E$ and $M$ only through $ME$, the high-energy tail $N(E;\tau) \to C\,E^{-3}/(\Psi_{0}D)$ for $E\,M(\tau)$ large, which does not depend on $\tau$, is $1/D$ times its standard value. \item[(iv)] \emph{(Floor.)} The mirror's light content copies ours (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), so $D = (2 + g + o)/(1 + g) = 2 + (o - g)/(1 + g)$: $D \ge 2$ if and only if $o \ge g$, and with $o = 0$, $D = 2 - g/(1 + g)$. The factors of (iii) are $D$, $D^{2/3}$ and $D^{1/3}$.

deposited.proof:
Constraints: $\delta\ip{I}{I} = 2\ip{\delta I}{I} = 0$, $\delta\ip{V}{I} = \ip{\delta V}{I} + \ip{V}{\delta I} = 0$, $\delta\ip{V}{V} = 2\ip{\delta V}{V} = 0$: three independent linear conditions on the twelve components of $(\delta I, \delta V)$ (independent because $I$ and $V$ are non-null and orthogonal), leaving nine. Stabiliser: a bivector annihilating both $I$ and $V$ is a bivector of $\{I,V\}^\perp$, which has signature $(1,3)$ (Theorem 3.1(ii)), so the stabiliser algebra is $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$, of dimension six, and the broken complement has dimension nine. The map $\xi \mapsto (\xi\cdot I, \xi\cdot V)$ maps into the constrained space, since $\ip{\xi\cdot I}{I} = 0$, $\ip{\xi\cdot V}{V} = 0$ and $\ip{\xi\cdot V}{I} + \ip{V}{\xi\cdot I} = 0$ by antisymmetry of $\xi$; restricted to the broken complement it is injective, because a $\xi$ in the complement with $\xi\cdot I = \xi\cdot V = 0$ lies in the stabiliser; by equal dimensions it is bijective. Any constrained $(\delta I, \delta V)$ is thus $(\xi\cdot I, \xi\cdot V)$ for a unique broken $\xi$, and the gauge transformation by $-\xi$, acting simultaneously on $
abla$, $I$ and $V$, removes it while shifting $\delta
abla$: the Goldstone eating. In the resulting gauge the second variation is a quadratic form in $\delta
abla$ alone. Invariance of the functional: a gauge transformation is a section $g$ of the ambient group bundle, acting on the fibre by $g(x) \in SO(2,4)$ at each point; it acts on the connection by $
abla \mapsto g
abla g^{-1}$, so that the curvature, $F = 
abla^2$, transforms by $F \mapsto gFg^{-1}$, that is, its bivector value at each point is carried by $g(x)$ (a bivector $a\wedge b$ goes to $ga\wedge gb$, since $g$ is an isometry), and on $I$ and $V$ by $I \mapsto gI$, $V \mapsto gV$. The volume form of a six-dimensional fibre with a nondegenerate form is invariant under its special orthogonal group, so at each point $\epsilon(gI, gV, gF, gF) = \det(g)\,\epsilon(I, V, F, F) = \epsilon(I, V, F, F)$; the prefactor $1/\ip{I}{I}$ and the three constraints $\ip{I}{I} = \Lambda/3$, $\ip{V}{I} = 0$, $\ip{V}{V} = -3/\Lambda$ are preserved because $g(x)$ is an isometry of the fibre; and a pointwise identity between integrands is an identity between the integrals. The functional is therefore invariant, and the constraint surface is carried to itself, under the ambient gauge group acting on all three arguments. The script confirms the fibrewise identity on rational elements of $SO(2,4)$ (a boost, a rotation, and their product, each confirmed an isometry). abla$ and $I$ while holding $X$ fixed changes the integrand by minus itself, not by zero. The singular locus of a black hole is an inter-tower event for energy, as it already was for weight, and never for the residue of any quantum: energy crosses at the wall, the residue does not (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}).
\end{enumerate}
One residue is flagged at observation level: dark-tower matter crossing this tower's horizons carries superselected charge the four-dimensional boundary mode space cannot hold, which routes it into the tower-wise run of the singularity paper's ascend-then-descend structure \cite{ButlerT5}; the computation of that routing, with the mass range of its Gauss-law clause, is Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}.

t14a-regenerated.title: Towers are residues, and the single-clock filter
t14a-regenerated.text:
The residue $r = p - q \pmod 8$ is invariant along every tower: the eight parallel towers are the eight residues, their parallelism derived rather than described. Call a signature $(p,q)$ \emph{causal} if $\min(p,q) = 1$: exactly one direction of the minority sign, the timelike one, whichever sign convention carries time. Labelling this world $(1,3)$, residue $6$, fixes the convention time $=$ plus, and the mirror residue $2$ reads $(3,1)$; under the opposite convention the two labels swap and the causal sort is unchanged, but every attribution of a Clifford type to a member of the reversal pair passes to the other member, since $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat(2,\mathbb{H})$ and $\Cl(3,1) \cong \Mat(4,\R)$ are not isomorphic. That attribution is fixed by a labelling convention Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} declares indexical, and is so read below. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Census; proved.)} Every residue contains causal signatures once the dimension is free: the lowest are $(1,1)$ at $r = 0$, $(2,1)$ at $r = 1$, $(3,1)$ at $r = 2$, $(4,1)$ at $r = 3$, $(1,5)$ or $(5,1)$ at $r = 4$, $(1,4)$ at $r = 5$, $(1,3)$ at $r = 6$, $(1,2)$ at $r = 7$. The residue alone therefore sorts nothing; a representative must be chosen.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The sort under P3; proved given the premise.)} Under Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} the representatives are $(1,3)$ at $r = 6$, this world; $(3,1)$ at $r = 2$, a mirror Minkowski with real (Majorana-type) spinors; $(2,2)$ at $r = 0$, two times; $(4,0)$ or $(0,4)$ at $r = 4$, none; $(2,1)$ and $(1,2)$ at $r = 1, 7$, three-dimensional; $(4,1)$ and $(1,4)$ at $r = 3, 5$, five-dimensional. Exactly two are sterile, $r = 0$ and $r = 4$ (a figure of the original), and they are the fixed points of the mirror map $r \mapsto -r$: under P3 the towers without a single time are the towers that are their own mirrors.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Sensitivity; proved.)} The sterile set is a function of the window. With any dimension up to five allowed, only $r = 4$ is sterile ($(1,1)$ is a causal signature for $r = 0$); with dimensions three to six, only $r = 0$ ($(1,5)$ is one for $r = 4$); with the upper bound removed, nothing is ($(1,9)$ is one for $r = 0$ at ten); and the literal lowest-dimensional representative of every residue, with no lower bound, is definite for $r = 6$ itself, namely $(0,2)$: without a lower bound the criterion would sterilise this world.
\end{enumerate}
Six admit matter: this one and five dark. Which of the six the descent populated is a further question, answered for the mirror by P2 and for the odd towers only by the record (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}). Structural level given P3; the two-time exclusion at $r = 0$ imports the standard instability of two-time dynamics, flagged, and the flag does not remove it (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.flag-insensitive-residue-no-flag-level}).

t14a-regenerated.title: The degeneration sheaf
t14a-regenerated.text:
Let $(M, G)$ be a tame corank-one degeneration (Hypotheses \claimref{sheaf.tameness}), $\shA = \Cl(T^*M, G)$, and write $A(x)$ for the fibre at $x$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Over $\Mo$, each fibre $A(x)$ is isomorphic to the nondegenerate Clifford algebra of the local signature; on the interior of $\Mp$ this is $\Cl(p,q)$, on the far side $\Cl(p{-}1,q{+}1)$. In the physical case these are $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat_2(\HH)$ and $\Cl(0,4) \cong \Mat_2(\HH)$.
\item Over $x \in \Sig$, the two-sided ideal $J(x)$ of $A(x)$ generated by the radical line $\shL(x)$ is
\[
J(x) \;=\; A(x)\,k \;=\; k\,A(x), \qquad J(x)^2 = 0, \qquad \dim_\R J(x) = 2^{n-1},
\]
for any spanning $k \in \shL(x)$, and the quotient is canonically the Clifford algebra of the induced form:
\[
A(x)/J(x) \;\cong\; \Cl\bigl(T^*_xM / \shL(x),\ \overline{G}_x\bigr),
\]
where $\overline{G}_x$ is nondegenerate of rank $n-1$ and signature $(p{-}1, q)$.
\item The fibrewise ideals assemble: the multiplication map $\shA|_\Sig \otimes \shL \to \shA|_\Sig$ has image a smooth subbundle $\shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL$ of rank $2^{n-1}$, and its pushforward
\[
\shJ \;:=\; i_*\bigl(\shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL\bigr) \qquad (i : \Sig \hookrightarrow M)
\]
is a finitely presented sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_M$-modules and of $\shA$-bimodules, supported exactly on $\Sig$, with fibre $J(x)$ at $x \in \Sig$ and fibre $0$ elsewhere. The associated ideal sheaf of $\shA$ is the kernel
\[
\shK \;:=\; \ker\bigl(\shA \longrightarrow i_*\bigl(\shA|_\Sig \,/\, \shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL\bigr)\bigr),
\]
a sheaf of two-sided ideals of $\shA$ whose restriction to $\Sig$ realises $J(x)$ fibrewise and whose quotient $\shA/\shK$ is the pushforward of the quotient bundle of (2).
\end{enumerate}

At a tame wall the physical metric (the inverse cometric) has a canonical simple pole: for any defining function $\tau$ of $\Sig$,

t14a-regenerated.title: Imported: the frozen point and the dictionary
t14a-regenerated.text:
On the Einstein region with $\Lambda \neq 0$ of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), the frozen point $I$ is the scale tractor parallel for the tractor gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}, of squared norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3 = H^{2}$, and in the flat chart of the conformal model (the flat twistor chart, the flat background itself) its frozen point is $I_{\Lambda} = n_{\infty} + (\Lambda/6)\,n_{0}$. Mass is conformal weight read against it: a density of weight $w$ coupled to the frozen point obeys the Klein-Gordon equation with
\[
m^{2} = -\,w(w+3)\,\frac{\Lambda}{3} = \Delta(3-\Delta)\,H^{2}, \qquad \Delta = -w,
\]
so a real weight gives $m^{2} \ge 0$ only on $w \in [-3, 0]$, where $m \le 3H/2$, and every heavier field has complex weight $w = -\tfrac32 \pm i\nu$ with $\nu \approx m/H$. In particular the weight of the Planck mass is complex, and its imaginary part is
\[
N := \operatorname{Im} w(M_{P}) \approx M_{P}/H, \qquad\text{about } 1.0 \times 10^{61}.
\]
Throughout this paper $N$ means $M_{P}/H$, the number the dictionary attaches to the Planck mass. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thms.~4.5, 4.7]{ButlerT6} for the frozen point and its norm; \cite[Thm.~3.1, Cor.~3.2]{ButlerT11} for the dictionary and the complex weights; \cite[Lem.~5.1]{ButlerT11} for the chart form of $I_{\Lambda}$. The value, about $1.0 \times 10^{61}$ for $G = M_{P}^{-2}$, is the measured ratio $M_{P}/H$ and carries the record's status \cite{PDG2024}.

t14b-regenerated.text: The dark-matter paper T14 fixes how much matter each dark tower holds. By its unit-ball rule the mirror carries 18.6 percent of the dark matter, the three-dimensional towers 49.7 percent and the five-dimensional towers 31.6 percent. This note sets out the assumptions, equations, code and results of the tests of those amounts. Quanta confined to a sheet scatter in two dimensions; per unit of the mass gravity sees, their cross-section is a length times the sheet spacing. At composite strength the three-dimensional towers' matter is a fluid, eight to thirteen orders of magnitude above the cluster bound, whatever its confinement scale. A tree-gravity, multi-species smoothed-particle code, with the sheet fluid's pressure confined to its planes, follows a Bullet-like merger and a cluster's assembly. As T14 writes it, the composition fails both tests: 68 percent of the dark matter collides, with randomly oriented sheets the subcluster dissolves from the lensing map, and halos reach about 0.4 of the cold-dark-matter ellipticity. If the odd towers' matter is collisionless, only the mirror collides; the subcluster keeps a lensing peak on its galaxies, its gas trailing, at the cost of a puffier subcluster and halos about 0.8 as elliptical. A semi-analytic Milky Way model with helium-star feedback excludes the mirror's proton-only branch; its helium branch fits at the Sun under some normalisations, and in the bulge only if the bulge holds over twice the mirror's proportional share of its dark mass. Two films, the code and a verification script accompany the note.

t14b-regenerated.title: Introduction
t14b-regenerated.text:
The dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14} derives eight towers of the Clifford clock, proves that matter in the five populated dark towers gravitates on our metric and does nothing else, and by one geometric rule, the unit-ball rule, returns the ratio of dark to visible matter as $(11\pi + 16)/(3\pi) = 5.364$. The Clifford clock is the mod-$8$ periodicity of the real Clifford algebras, read as a ladder of spacetimes of different dimension, ours among them. The rule was found by fitting one length, so the total is not a test of it. What the rule also fixes, and what can be tested, is the composition: which towers hold how much, and therefore what that matter does when halos collide, when clusters assemble and when gas settles into a galaxy.

Tower dimensions count time. A three-dimensional tower has two space dimensions, so its matter lives on sheets, one direction short of ours; a five-dimensional tower has four, one more. There are two of each, and these four are the odd towers; with the mirror, a copy of ours, they are the five populated dark towers. The share of a tower is the ratio of unit-ball volumes, $V_{3}/V_{D}$ for a tower whose space has $D$ dimensions, which gives $V_{3}/V_{2} = 4/3$ for each three-dimensional tower (Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-unit-ball-rule-family}).

This note collects everything that was done to test the composition. It is a methods note: each section states its premises, the equations it uses, how the code implements them, and what came out. Nothing here changes a derived result of T14. Where the tests disagree with a physical statement of T14, the note says which statement and what was found, and T14 records the outcome in its Section 7.7.

t14b-regenerated.title: The effective cross-section of sheet matter
t14b-regenerated.text:
Let the sheets carry $n_{2}$ quanta per unit area, be stacked a distance $s$ apart, and let each quantum have in-sheet cross-section $\lambda$. Then the collision rate of a quantum moving at speed $v$ equals that of a three-dimensional gas of number density $n_{3} = n_{2}/s$ with cross-section
\[
\sigma_{\mathrm{eff}} \;=\; \lambda\, s ,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad
\frac{\sigma_{\mathrm{eff}}}{m} \;=\; \frac{\lambda s}{m}.
\]
In a halo region of overdensity $\Delta$ at redshift $z$ the spacing lies between $d_{b}\Delta^{-1}/(1+z)$ (all compression along the normal) and $d_{b}/(1+z)$ (all compression in the plane), and is $s = d_{b}\Delta^{-1/3}/(1+z)$ for isotropic compression.
t14b-regenerated.proof: The in-sheet collision rate is $n_{2}\lambda v$, and $n_{2}\lambda v = (n_{2}/s)(\lambda s)v = n_{3}\sigma_{\mathrm{eff}}v$. By R3 (\claimref{dark-matter.r3-one-cell-per-unshared-direction}) the sheets are $d_{b}$ apart in the mean, comoving \cite[Prem.~7.4]{ButlerT14}. A region compressed by $\Delta$ in volume has its comoving lengths reduced by $\Delta$ along one direction, by $\Delta^{1/3}$ along each for isotropic compression, or not at all along the normal if the compression is in the plane; the physical spacing carries the further factor $1/(1+z)$.

t14b-regenerated.title: Gravity
t14b-regenerated.text:
Gravity is computed with a Barnes-Hut octree \cite{BarnesHut1986}. A node of side $\ell$ at distance $r$ from its centre of mass is opened if $\ell^{2} > \theta^{2}r^{2}$ or if the particle lies inside it, with $\theta = 0.7$. Forces use Plummer softening,
\[
\mathbf{a}_{i} \;=\; \sum_{j} G\,m_{j}\,\frac{\mathbf{r}_{j} - \mathbf{r}_{i}}{\bigl(|\mathbf{r}_{j} - \mathbf{r}_{i}|^{2} + \epsilon^{2}\bigr)^{3/2}},
\qquad \epsilon = 15\ \kpc ,
\]
with nodes standing in for the particles they contain.
t14b-regenerated.label: note

t14b-regenerated.title: Smoothed-particle hydrodynamics
t14b-regenerated.text:
Each fluid species has its own tree. The kernel is the cubic spline of support $2h$ \cite{MonaghanLattanzio1985},
\[
W(r, h) = \frac{1}{\pi h^{3}}
\begin{cases}
1 - \tfrac{3}{2}q^{2} + \tfrac{3}{4}q^{3}, & 0 \le q < 1,\\[2pt]
\tfrac{1}{4}(2 - q)^{3}, & 1 \le q < 2,\\[2pt]
0, & q \ge 2,
\end{cases}
\qquad q = r/h ,
\]
normalised so that $\int W\,d^{3}r = 1$. Density is gathered at each particle's own smoothing length, $\rho_{i} = \sum_{j} m_{j}W(r_{ij}, h_{i})$; pressure and sound speed are $P_{i} = (\gamma - 1)\rho_{i}u_{i}$ and $c_{i} = \sqrt{\gamma(\gamma - 1)u_{i}}$. The next smoothing length is
\[
h_{i} = \tfrac{1}{2}\Bigl(\frac{3N_{\mathrm{ngb}}m_{i}}{4\pi\rho_{i}}\Bigr)^{1/3}, \qquad N_{\mathrm{ngb}} = 40,
\]
limited to a change between $0.8$ and $1.25$ per step, floored at $h_{\min} = 10\ \kpc$, and cut to $0.7h_{i}$ if a particle's neighbour list reaches its cap of $2000$.

The equations of motion are the symmetric form \cite{Monaghan1992},
\begin{align*}
\frac{d\mathbf{v}_{i}}{dt} &= -\sum_{j} m_{j}\Bigl(\frac{P_{i}}{\rho_{i}^{2}} + \frac{P_{j}}{\rho_{j}^{2}} + \Pi_{ij}\Bigr)\,\mathbf{g}_{ij},
\\
\frac{du_{i}}{dt} &= \sum_{j} m_{j}\Bigl(\frac{P_{i}}{\rho_{i}^{2}} + \tfrac{1}{2}\Pi_{ij}\Bigr)\,\mathbf{v}_{ij}\cdot\mathbf{g}_{ij},
\end{align*}
with the kernel gradient averaged over the two smoothing lengths, $\mathbf{g}_{ij} = \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(\nabla_{i}W(r_{ij}, h_{i}) + \nabla_{i}W(r_{ij}, h_{j})\bigr)$, and $\mathbf{v}_{ij} = \mathbf{v}_{i} - \mathbf{v}_{j}$. The artificial viscosity acts on approaching pairs \cite{MonaghanGingold1983}:
\[
\Pi_{ij} = \frac{-\alpha\,\bar{c}_{ij}\mu_{ij} + \beta\mu_{ij}^{2}}{\bar{\rho}_{ij}}, \qquad
\mu_{ij} = \frac{\bar{h}_{ij}\,\mathbf{v}_{ij}\cdot\mathbf{r}_{ij}}{r_{ij}^{2} + 0.01\bar{h}_{ij}^{2}} \quad (\mathbf{v}_{ij}\cdot\mathbf{r}_{ij} < 0),
\]
with $\alpha = 1$, $\beta = 2$ and bars denoting pair means. Internal energy is floored at $u_{\mathrm{floor}} = u(10^{4}\ \mathrm{K})$ for mean particle mass $0.6\,m_{p}$.
t14b-regenerated.label: note

t14b-regenerated.title: The sheet fluid
t14b-regenerated.text:
Premise S2 is implemented by contracting both the kernel gradient and the separation vector of every pair of sheet-fluid particles with an averaged pair operator before they enter the equations above. With $\mathbf{n}_{i}$ and $\mathbf{n}_{j}$ the unit normals of the two particles' sheets,
\begin{equation}
P_{ij} \;=\; I - \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(\mathbf{n}_{i}\mathbf{n}_{i}^{\mathsf T} + \mathbf{n}_{j}\mathbf{n}_{j}^{\mathsf T}\bigr),
\qquad
\mathbf{g}_{ij} \mapsto P_{ij}\mathbf{g}_{ij}, \quad \mathbf{r}_{ij} \mapsto P_{ij}\mathbf{r}_{ij}.
\end{equation}
$P_{ij}$ is the mean of the two in-plane projectors $I - \mathbf{n}_{i}\mathbf{n}_{i}^{\mathsf T}$ and $I - \mathbf{n}_{j}\mathbf{n}_{j}^{\mathsf T}$. When all normals are parallel it is the projection onto the common sheet, nothing acts along the normal except gravity, and motion along it is ballistic; for differently oriented normals it is not a projection and keeps part of each normal component (Lemma \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator}(iii)). Each particle's normal is fixed at its initial value, random per particle or common to all (the section ``Initial conditions'').

t14b-regenerated.title: Halos
t14b-regenerated.text:
A halo of mass $M_{200}$ and concentration $c$ is a Hernquist sphere of the same mass inside $r_{200}$, with the scale length that matches the Navarro-Frenk-White inner profile \cite{Hernquist1990, NFW1997, SpringelDiMatteoHernquist2005}:
\[
r_{200} = \Bigl(\frac{GM_{200}}{100H_{0}^{2}}\Bigr)^{1/3},\qquad
a = \frac{r_{200}}{c}\sqrt{2\Bigl[\ln(1 + c) - \frac{c}{1 + c}\Bigr]},\qquad
M_{H} = M_{200}\Bigl(1 + \frac{a}{r_{200}}\Bigr)^{2},
\]
with $H_{0} = 70$ km/s/Mpc; the first is the radius inside which the mean density is $200$ times critical, and the last makes the Hernquist enclosed mass $M_{H}r^{2}/(r + a)^{2}$ equal $M_{200}$ at $r_{200}$. The sphere is truncated at $15a$, keeping $225/256$ of $M_{H}$. Positions are drawn from the enclosed-mass profile; each particle is then assigned a species at random in proportion to the species' mass fraction (Premise S5).

Collisionless particles take speeds from the isotropic Hernquist distribution function $f(E)$ \cite{Hernquist1990} by rejection sampling up to the escape speed, with random directions. Fluid particles start at rest with $u = \sigma_{r}^{2}/(\gamma - 1)$, so that $P = \rho\sigma_{r}^{2}$ and the gas is in hydrostatic equilibrium with the isotropic Jeans dispersion
\[
\sigma_{r}^{2}(r) = \frac{GM_{H}}{12a}\Bigl[12x(1 + x)^{3}\ln\frac{1 + x}{x} - \frac{x}{1 + x}\bigl(25 + 52x + 42x^{2} + 12x^{3}\bigr)\Bigr], \qquad x = r/a ,
\]
which solves $d(\rho\sigma_{r}^{2})/dr = -\rho\,GM(r)/r^{2}$ for the Hernquist density. The sheet fluid has no pressure along its normal, so it also carries a Gaussian velocity of dispersion $\sigma_{r}$ along the normal.

In reading (W) the subcluster's sheet fluid and mirror gas are held back with its gas, $71$ percent of its mass ($56$ percent in the mixed count). The mixed count fails in the same way. With the mirror collisionless from the start, so that only the sheet fluid collides, the subcluster keeps a weaker peak (contrast $2.69$ in the mixed count, $3.78$ with one three-dimensional tower colliding) and $0.44$ to $0.55$ of CDM's own mass: with a quarter to a third of the dark matter as sheet fluid, the sheet fluid alone costs about half the subcluster's central mass.

Its own mass inside $150$ kpc of its galaxies is $0.57$ of CDM's, a deficit larger than the $23$ percent bound, because its halo puffs more than it strips. Its galaxies spread with it: the galaxy mass within $150$ kpc of the galaxy peak is $0.83$ of its start, where CDM's is compressed to $1.31$. t14b-regenerated.title: The model
t14b-regenerated.text:
One Milky Way halo is shared by both sectors: the same growth, potential and spin. Its growth follows the Fakhouri-Ma-Boylan-Kolchin rate \cite{Fakhouri2010},
\[
\frac{dM}{dt} = A\Bigl(\frac{M}{10^{12}\Msun}\Bigr)^{1.1}(1 + bz)\sqrt{\Omega_{m}(1+z)^{3} + \Omega_{\Lambda}},
\]
with $(A, b) = (46.1\ \Msun/\mathrm{yr}, 1.11)$ (mean) or $(25.3, 1.65)$ (median). Each sector accretes its baryon share $f_{b}\,dM$ ($f_{b} = \Omega_{b}/\Omega_{m} = 0.1565$) into a hot halo, an isothermal sphere $\rho_{g}(r) = m_{\mathrm{hot}}/(4\pi Rr^{2})$ at the virial temperature $T = \mu m_{p}V^{2}/2k$ of its own composition. Following Croton et al.\ \cite{Croton2006}, with their parameter values, and with $R$ and $V$ the halo's virial radius and circular velocity, $m_{\mathrm{hot}}$ and $m_{\mathrm{cold}}$ the hot and cold gas masses, $r_{\mathrm{cool}}$ the radius at which the cooling time equals the reference time, and $\lambda$ the spin parameter:
\begin{align*}
t_{\mathrm{cool}}(r_{\mathrm{cool}}) &= t_{\mathrm{dyn}} = R/V \quad (\text{or the cosmic time}),\\
\dot m_{\mathrm{cool}} &= \tfrac{1}{2}m_{\mathrm{hot}}\frac{r_{\mathrm{cool}}}{R}\frac{V}{R} \quad (\text{all hot gas per } t_{\mathrm{dyn}} \text{ if } r_{\mathrm{cool}} > R),\\
\dot m_{*} &= \alpha\,\frac{m_{\mathrm{cold}} - m_{\mathrm{crit}}}{t_{\mathrm{disk}}}, \qquad
m_{\mathrm{crit}} = 3.8 \times 10^{9}\Msun\,\frac{V}{200\ \mathrm{km/s}}\,\frac{3R_{d}}{10\ \kpc},\\
\Delta m_{\mathrm{reheat}} &= \epsilon_{\mathrm{disk}}F\,\Delta m_{*}, \qquad
\Delta E = \tfrac{1}{2}\epsilon_{\mathrm{halo}}F\,\Delta m_{*}V_{\mathrm{SN}}^{2},\\
\Delta m_{\mathrm{eject}} &= \frac{\Delta E - \tfrac{1}{2}\Delta m_{\mathrm{reheat}}V^{2}}{\tfrac{1}{2}V^{2}}, \qquad
\dot m_{\mathrm{return}} = \gamma_{\mathrm{ej}}\,m_{\mathrm{ej}}/t_{\mathrm{dyn}},
\end{align*}
with $\alpha = 0.07$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{disk}} = 3.5$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{halo}} = 0.35$, $V_{\mathrm{SN}} = 630$ km/s, $\gamma_{\mathrm{ej}} = 0.5$, recycled fraction $0.43$, $R_{d} = \lambda R/\sqrt{2}$ and $t_{\mathrm{disk}} = 3R_{d}/V$. Metals are followed in each sector from a metal-free start: a yield $y = 0.03$ per unit of stars formed enters the cold gas and is carried by every flow, and each hot halo cools at its own metallicity. The feedback factor $F$ multiplies the supernova energy and mass loading per unit stellar mass; for our sector it is a calibrated number $F_{\mathrm{cal}}$, and the mirror's is $F$ times that.

t14b-regenerated.title: The model
t14b-regenerated.text:
\textbf{Calibration and normalisation.} In each set-up our sector's $F_{\mathrm{cal}}$ is tuned so that its settled mass, stars plus cold gas, is the observed $6.0 \times 10^{10}\ \Msun$. The mirror, at $\Omega_{b'} = 0.995\,\Omega_{b}$, then runs in the same halo with feedback $F\,F_{\mathrm{cal}}$ and with yield $yF$ (its extra feedback comes from extra supernovae, which also make metals; the consistent choice) or, for comparison, $y$. Its surface density at the Sun is normalised to ours, either in total,
\[
\Sigma'_{x} = 47.1\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}\times\frac{m'_{x}}{6.0 \times 10^{10}\ \Msun},
\]
or with gas and stars scaled separately to our observed $13.7$ and $33.4$ (component normalisation). The mass the mirror puts in the bulge volume is taken as a quarter of its settled mass, the fraction of ours the bulge volume holds. There are $24$ set-ups: $M_{200} = 1.0$, $1.2$ and $1.5 \times 10^{12}\ \Msun$; mean or median growth; $t_{\mathrm{dyn}}$ or cosmic time as cooling reference; and a star-formation-threshold disk of $5.6$ kpc ($\lambda = 0.035$) or $2.6$ kpc ($\lambda = 0.0163$, the Milky Way's). Points with $F\,F_{\mathrm{cal}}$ above $12$ are dropped as not converged.

So with the consistent yield the Galaxy test would be decided by either of two measurements not yet made: a $2\sigma$ limit below $5\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ on extra disk-like mass at the Sun with scale height $100$ to $500$ pc (the room is $4.6 \pm 5$, the dynamical stellar surface density less the counted one, Fact \claimref{simulations.imported-milky-ways-mass-budget}), or a limit below $1.7 \times 10^{9}\ \Msun$ on disk-like dark mass in the bulge volume, which would bound the mirror's mass there directly, whatever reading of the room is taken. t14b-regenerated.title: What the tests decide, and what they cost
t14b-regenerated.text: \textbf{What the tests decide.} Read as T14 writes it, the composition fails the merger and the halo shapes, and it fails them because of the three-dimensional towers' self-interaction, not because of the amounts. Read with the odd towers collisionless, the same amounts keep a lensing peak on the subcluster's galaxies with its gas behind and a mass-to-light change consistent with the observed ratio (as CDM's is; the measure does not discriminate), and come within a quarter of CDM on halo shapes. The remaining exposure is the mirror in the Galaxy, the same in both readings: its helium branch is open at the Sun, at the $2\sigma$ room, under some normalisations of the mirror's gas and, in the bulge, only if the bulge holds over twice the mirror's proportional share of its dark mass.

t14b-regenerated.title: What the tests decide, and what they cost
t14b-regenerated.text:
\textbf{Statements of T14 the tests bear on.} T14 records the outcome in its Section 7.7 and at each place cited below \cite[Fact~7.32]{ButlerT14}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item At composite strength the three-dimensional towers' self-interaction is $10^{8}$ to $10^{13}\ \cmg$ (Proposition \claimref{simulations.effective-cross-section-sheet-matter}), far above the cluster bounds \cite[Prop.~6.2]{ButlerT14}.
\item ``A halo built from collisionless sheets is a cold-dark-matter halo'' \cite[Rem.~7.30]{ButlerT14} needs the sheet matter collisionless; as a fluid it is cored, rounder and less concentrated than collisionless matter (Observation \claimref{simulations.halo-shapes}).
\item The self-interacting fraction, counted as all colliding dark matter, is $68$ percent in reading (W) and $19$ percent in reading (C); T14's Proposition 7.15(v) counts the three-dimensional towers alone (about half); for the merger bound its Section 7.7 adds the mirror, as here \cite[Prop.~7.15(v), \S7.7]{ButlerT14}. The Bullet bound on mass loss is about $23$ percent \cite{Randall2008}, inferred from the mass-to-light ratio.
\item The mirror analysis T14 cites \cite[\S 8, refutation item 6]{ButlerT14} rescales $\eta$ and includes a helium mirror down to $T'/T = 10^{-3}$ \cite{RouxCline2020}; it covers the hot end of T14's interval, not its floor.
\item For the helium branch with stars the excess over the Galaxy's room at the Sun is a factor of $1.5$ to $2.8$ over the $2\sigma$ room of $15\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ at equal feedback, and at the helium-star feedback it falls within the $2\sigma$ room at the Sun in most set-ups in total normalisation (all of them at the best-shifted IMF) and persists in the bulge unless the bulge holds over twice the mirror's proportional share of its dark mass (Observation \claimref{simulations.mirror-galaxy}). The order-of-magnitude excess holds for the proton-only branch and for a mirror that forms no stars \cite[\S 8, refutation item 6]{ButlerT14}.
\item The current bounds on the settled phase are the thin-disk bound of Widmark et al.\ \cite{Widmark2021} and the microlensing bound of Mr\'oz et al.\ (compact objects at most $1$ percent of the halo from $1.8 \times 10^{-4}$ to $6.3\ \Msun$ and $10$ percent up to $860\ \Msun$ \cite{Mroz2024}), which T14's refutation item 6 uses. The thin-disk bound, about $5\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ at $95$ percent, holds for scale heights of $50$ pc or less; it does not reach the $5\ \Msun\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ at $100$ to $500$ pc that would decide the helium branch, and the bulge models \cite{Portail2017} do not separate a disk-like part of the bulge's dark mass, so the Galaxy test is not yet decidable.
\end{enumerate}

t14b-regenerated.title: Position in the series
t14b-regenerated.text: This paper is T14b of the series, a companion to the dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14}. It is downstream of T14's Proposition 4.1 (superselection), Theorem 4.3 and Proposition 4.6 (the mirror), Proposition 6.2 (the radiation audit and its self-interaction statement) and Section 7 (the unit-ball rule, its premises R1 to R3, the thickness family and the moving sheets), and it tests the composition T14's Section 7 fixes against the record. Remark \claimref{note.simulations.what-premise-c-needs} refers to the Standard-Model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} for the gauge charges of the four-dimensional minimal massive composite. It proves nothing about the series' algebra and changes no derived result of T14; it says which of T14's physical statements the simulations and the Galaxy model support and which they do not (the section ``What the tests decide, and what they cost''). The capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17} should carry the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.mirror-galaxy} beside T14's ledger entry, Premise C as the condition under which the rule's composition meets the cluster record, and the two measurements of the section ``The mirror in the Galaxy'' that would decide the mirror's helium branch.

t14b-regenerated.title: Machine verification
t14b-regenerated.text:
\textbf{The script.} \file{verify\_T14b.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT14b} imports the series' shared library \file{GA.py} and checks the note's computational identities and derived numbers: $60$ checks, all passing, in eight parts. A few are arithmetic restatements of a quoted number rather than tests of a claim (D4, F3, R4, R7). Algebraic identities are checked in exact rational arithmetic; evaluations with physical constants, transcendental functions and integrals in double precision, with the tolerance stated beside each check.

\emph{Part A: composition.} $T(1) = (11\pi + 16)/(3\pi)$ between rational bounds; $T(\pi/2) = T(1)$; the three shares and their sum; the baryon, galaxy and gas fractions of every halo; the three colliding shares and their order against the bounds.

\emph{Part B: self-interaction.} Proposition \claimref{simulations.effective-cross-section-sheet-matter} as an exact identity; $n_{b}$ and $d_{b}$; the ratio $V_{3}/V_{2} = 4/3$ from the unit-ball volumes; the range of the table accompanying \claimref{simulations.effective-cross-section-sheet-matter}; the bound on $\lambda$; Computation \claimref{simulations.cluster-bound-two-dimensions}, with Bessel functions by their series; the five-dimensional range; the mean free path.

\emph{Part C: the code's algebra.} The kernel's normalisation, derivative and continuity, exactly; Lemma \claimref{simulations.averaged-pair-operator}(ii) in the blade engine of $\Cl(3,0)$, (iii) in exact rationals, including $P_{ij}^{2} \ne P_{ij}$ for orthogonal normals, and (i) on a rational instance with distinct normals and viscosity; the cooling update as a polynomial identity; the units; the settling threshold at $\mu = 0.6$ and its temperature for the helium plasma, from the code's $u(T)$ formula and constants; the algebra of the bremsstrahlung coefficient (the electron and ion densities and $T(u)$ for He$^{++}$) against $du/dt = -\varepsilon/\rho$, with the code's constants.

\emph{Part D: initial conditions.} The Hernquist matching and $r_{200}$, exactly; the Jeans equation for $\sigma_{r}^{2}$ at three radii; the truncation fraction; the merger geometry, exactly.

\emph{Part E: the mirror's composition.} Freeze-out temperatures, $Y'$, $\eta'$, the recombination temperature and $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}}$.

\emph{Part F: cooling.} The metal-free $\Lambda_{N}$ at three temperatures; the cooling-time ratios of helium to our gas; the Tozzi-Norman conversion.

\emph{Part G: supernova energy.} The continuity of the IMF; our energy per unit mass; $F$ for our IMF's shape and the best shifted IMF.

\emph{Part R: recorded outputs.} Selected simulation and model outputs, carried as constants from the run summaries, and the comparisons the text draws from them: the mass-to-light change, ratio and sampling error; the merger separations; the halo ratios, with their seed-paired values; the Galaxy floors against the decisive limits and the three readings of the bulge room. The outputs themselves are reproduced by the deposited scripts, not by this one: Part R does not read \file{outputs/}, so a change to a deposited output would not fail the script.

\emph{What the script does not check:} the simulations and the Galaxy model themselves, which the section ``Running the code'' shows how to rerun, and the imported Facts and published bounds.

Open the supplement's top folder, \file{T14b\_supplement}, as the project in the IDE and keep its layout:
{ \begin{verbatim}
T14b_supplement/          open this folder as the project
  README.md
  requirements.txt
  code/                   every script and library; nothing is run from here
  outputs/                the deposited results the note quotes
  films/                  the deposited films
  work/                   created by reproduce.py
    bin/tpsim               the compiled simulation code
    tests/                  the two code tests

Two rules follow from how the scripts are written. First, every file in \file{code/} must stay in that one folder: the scripts import one another by module name (\file{ics}, \file{render\_lib}, \file{sam2} and so on), and Python finds them because they sit beside the script being run. Second, the working directory matters. t14b-regenerated.title: The mirror share is one, and how fragile that is
t14b-regenerated.text:
Write $m_{r} = c_{r}\Lambda_{r}$, with $\Lambda_{r}$ the confinement scale of tower $r$'s non-abelian sector and $c_{r}$ the constituent factor of its lightest charge-carrying composite.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The mirror.)} By Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iii), $\Lambda_{2} = \Lambda_{6}$ and $c_{2} = c_{6}$ exactly, hence $f_{2} = 1$ under P4, which Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v) discharges for the mirror, an isomorphism of theories rather than a one-loop statement. As a ratio of mass densities it is a ratio of mean mass per baryon: ours is about $936.7$ MeV after helium, a mirror burnt entirely to helium (the completion limit of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}'s burning branch) gives $931.8$ MeV, so $f_{2}$ is $0.995$ in that limit and $1$ on the proton-only branch, a one-sided systematic of half a percent at assembly level. Caveat (T14c): the two branches bracket the share where the mirror is helium or protons; at the gravitational floor the mirror is degenerate and, for a copied lepton number $L \leq 0$, ends $96$ to $100$ percent neutrons, a composition neither branch describes, and it is helium only for $\xi$ between about $3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$ (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}); the half-percent bracket is established there and not at the floor.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Fragility.)} The equality is unstable to any departure from the copy. Suppose the two towers shared a ceiling $M$ and coupling but differed in light content by $\Delta b$ over the running range, with $b_{6} \leq 11$; then at one loop
\[
\ln\frac{\Lambda_{2}}{\Lambda_{6}} \;\geq\; \frac{\Delta b}{b_{6} + \Delta b}\,\ln\frac{M}{\Lambda_{6}}.
\]
One Dirac flavour is $\Delta b = 2/3$, which with $\Lambda_{6} = 0.3$ GeV moves the mirror share by a factor between $4.89$ (bottom of the ceiling range, $b_{6} = 11$) and $21.4$ (top, $b_{6} = 7$), past the observed $5.364$ everywhere except at the bottom of the range on the most conservative branch. A coupling departure $\delta = \alpha_{2}(M)^{-1} - \alpha_{6}(M)^{-1}$ at the ceiling with identical content moves $\Lambda_{2}/\Lambda_{6}$ by $e^{-2\pi\delta/b}$, a factor $2.45$ per unit at $b = 7$, so the share stays within ten percent of one only for $|\delta| < 0.106$. So $f_{2} = 1$ is exact, P2-protected, and fragile.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The odd towers.)} In three and five dimensions the gauge coupling is dimensionful and the confinement scale is set by the coupling itself ($\Lambda_{3} \sim g_{3}^{2}N$, $\Lambda_{5} \sim 1/g_{5}^{2}$), so nothing about $\Lambda_{1,7,3,5}$ follows without a rule the series does not derive (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}); the unit-ball rule of the section ``The dark matter ratio: the unit-ball rule'' constrains that rule, as shares per unit of our volume, without supplying it.
\end{enumerate}
Level: (i) is Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}; (ii) is one-loop arithmetic under its stated assumptions, flagged; (iii) is a scope statement.

t14b-regenerated.title: The radiation audit: what the type-by-residue theorem closes, and what stays open
t14b-regenerated.text:
The cosmic microwave background caps extra relativistic energy at $\Delta\Neff \lesssim 0.3$ \cite{Planck2018}, and one massless photon-like species (two polarisations) at the visible temperature contributes $\Delta\Neff = (8/7)(11/4)^{4/3} \approx 4.4$, so five democratically filled sectors with such photons would contribute of order twenty. The audit proceeds tower by tower, at two levels fixed by Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can} and Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.where-flag-defined-what-it-carries}: the \emph{ground} level, where the type decides whether the tower's spinors carry an intrinsic $U(1)$ (exactly at the complex member of each odd pair, $r = 3, 7$ in the paper's convention), and the \emph{rung} level, where every flagged tower carries abelian charges from its ladder pairs.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The mirror tower, $r = 2$.)} Open, by theorem: the mirror's derived content is a copy of ours (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), so it has a massless mirror photon and three light mirror neutrinos. This is the mirror-matter situation of the literature, costed in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs}.
\item \emph{(The three-dimensional towers, $r = 1, 7$.)} Closed at both levels: vector-like (no chirality in odd dimension), so Dirac masses are unforbidden and generic; with no massless charged matter left, each compact $U(1)$ in three dimensions, the intrinsic one of the complex member of $\{1, 7\}$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(ii)) and the rung-level ones of both, leaves no massless photon. The paper states that every such $U(1)$ confines by monopoles \cite{Polyakov1977}; with the half-integral bare Chern-Simons level that the parity anomaly forces (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.anomalies}(i)), that holds in the confining phase (C) only, and in phase (T) the photon is instead topologically massive (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-phases}); both phases close the channel. t14b-regenerated.title: The stored asymmetry is a charge, not a number

\item[(i)] \emph{(Charge.)} The asymmetry stored in an oriented tower is the charge $Q = \epsilon N$, fixed by the descent's data and independent of the tower's temperature; it is not a thermal number $n - \bar{n} \propto g\,\mu T^{2}$. runs from $19$ to $26$ at the floor down to about $0.008$ at the hot deposit, crossing one at $\xi = \eta^{1/3} = 8.5 \times 10^{-4}$: at least $10^{7}$ times ours throughout, with $\Delta\Neff$ eight orders or more below the cap.

t14b-regenerated.title: Superselected, hence dark and exactly stable
t14b-regenerated.text:
By Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} and the acoustic programme (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-gravity-only-coupling}, the series' acoustic no-go, at its mixed level: within the s-wave current algebra, with the sphere step conditional on the Indifference premise and the thermal state on premise (Q)), matter in a neighbouring tower gravitates on this metric and does nothing else observable at first order: dark by structural necessity, at that level. \item The tower charge $r$ is superselected in the frozen phase: frozen-phase operators are built from the one soldering and preserve its signature (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one}), so portal matrix elements between residues vanish identically away from walls.

t14c-regenerated.title: Introduction
t14c-regenerated.text:
The dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14} derives eight parallel towers, one per residue $r = p - q \bmod 8$ of the real Clifford algebras, and finds that six can hold matter: this one ($r = 6$, signature $(1,3)$), its mirror ($r = 2$, $(3,1)$), two three-dimensional towers ($r = 1, 7$) and two five-dimensional towers ($r = 3, 5$). The towers touch only through the one shared metric. By its unit-ball rule the five dark towers hold, relative to our baryons, the shares $1$, $4/3$, $4/3$, $8/(3\pi)$ and $8/(3\pi)$, whose sum $(11\pi + 16)/(3\pi) = 5.364$ is the observed ratio of dark to visible matter. This note answers that question by doing in each tower what the Standard-Model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} does in ours. T12's chain is: a constituent; the number of constituents at which mass begins; the mixings that preserve total momentum; the automorphisms of the smallest massive composite, identified with the gauge algebra; the content and its charges; then, with imported physics, hadrons, atoms and a stable relic. \[
e_{K}^{\dagger} = e_{t}\rev{e_{K}}e_{t}^{-1} = (-1)^{|K|}\rev{e_{K}}, \qquad e_{K}\rev{e_{K}} = \bigl(-Q(e_{t})\bigr)^{|K|},
\]
so $e_{K}e_{K}^{\dagger} = (-1)^{|K|}\bigl(-Q(e_{t})\bigr)^{|K|} = Q(e_{t})^{|K|}$.

If $e_{K} = e_{t}e_{K'}$, then $\rev{e_{K}} = \rev{e_{K'}}e_{t}$, and
\begin{align*}
e_{K}^{\dagger} &= e_{t}\rev{e_{K'}} = (-1)^{|K'|}\,\rev{e_{K'}}\,e_{t}, \\
e_{K}e_{K}^{\dagger} &= (-1)^{|K'|}\,e_{t}\bigl(e_{K'}\rev{e_{K'}}\bigr)e_{t} = (-1)^{|K'|}\bigl(-Q(e_{t})\bigr)^{|K'|}\,Q(e_{t}) = Q(e_{t})^{|K|}.
\end{align*}
For $K \neq L$, $e_{K}e_{L}^{\dagger}$ is a multiple of $e_{K \triangle L}$, which has no scalar part. Hence for even $x = \sum_{K}x_{K}e_{K}$,
\[
\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0} \;=\; \sum_{K,L}x_{K}x_{L}\,\ip{e_{K}e_{L}^{\dagger}}_{0} \;=\; \sum_{K}x_{K}^{2} \qquad \text{(check B0)}.
\]



\emph{(ii) The corner and its conjugation.}  With $f = \tfrac{1}{2}(1 + e_{t}e_{a})$ and $\rev{(e_{t}e_{a})} = e_{a}e_{t}$,
\[
f^{\dagger} = \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(1 + e_{t}\,e_{a}e_{t}\,e_{t}^{-1}\bigr) = \tfrac{1}{2}(1 + e_{t}e_{a}) = f.
\]
The corner $\F = f\Cl^{0}f$ is a division algebra $\R$, $\C$ or $\HH$ with unit $f$ (Fact \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-structure}(iii)). It is closed under $\dagger$, since $(fxf)^{\dagger} = fx^{\dagger}f$, and $\dagger$ is an anti-involution of it with $\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0} > 0$ for $x \neq 0$ by (i).

The standard conjugation is the only anti-involution with that positivity. Every other candidate has an element with $xx^{\dagger} = -f$, whose scalar part is $-\tfrac{1}{2}$:
\begin{itemize}
\item on $\C$ the other candidate is the identity, and a unit square root $x$ of $-f$ gives $xx^{\dagger} = xx = -f$;
\item on $\HH$ every other anti-involution is $x \mapsto u\bar{x}u^{-1}$ for a unit imaginary $u$, and a unit imaginary $v$ anticommuting with $u$ gives $v\,u\bar{v}u^{-1} = v^{2} = -f$.
\end{itemize}
So $\dagger$ is the standard conjugation, and
\[
x^{\dagger}x \;=\; xx^{\dagger} \;=\; N(x)\,f

\[
\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0} \;=\; N(x)\,\ip{f}_{0} \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\,N(x),
\]

\psi x\,e_{t}\,\rev{(\psi x)} &= \psi\,\bigl(x e_{t}\rev{x}\bigr)\,\rev{\psi} \\
&= \psi\,\bigl(xx^{\dagger}\bigr)\,e_{t}\rev{\psi} \\
&= N(x)\,\psi f\,e_{t}\rev{\psi} \\

\end{align*}

t14c-regenerated.title: Where mass begins in each causal tower
t14c-regenerated.text:
Let $\psi, \psi_{1}, \psi_{2} \in S$ in a causal tower of dimension $n$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For $n = 3$ and $n = 4$ the reversion pairing is alternating, $\rev{\psi}\psi = 0$, every single constituent's momentum is null, and
\[
m^{2}\bigl(j(\psi_{1}) + j(\psi_{2})\bigr) \;=\; 2\,\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0}, \qquad x = \rev{\psi}_{1}\psi_{2}.
\]
Mass begins at two constituents; it vanishes exactly when $\rev{\psi}_{1}\psi_{2} = 0$.
\item[(ii)] For $n = 5$ the reversion pairing is not alternating, and
\[
m^{2}\bigl(j(\psi)\bigr) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\,\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0}, \qquad x = \rev{\psi}\psi,
\]
which vanishes on a nonzero proper cone in $S$. Mass begins at one constituent.
\end{enumerate}
In every causal tower the total momentum of any number of constituents is timelike or null, never spacelike.
t14c-regenerated.proof:
\textit{The pairing as a sandwich.}\enspace Write $\psi = \phi f$ with $\phi \in \Cl^{0}(V)$ and $f = \tfrac{1}{2}(1 + b)$, $b$ a bivector of square $+1$. Then $\rev{b} = -b$, so $\rev{f} = 1 - f$ and
\[
\rev{\psi}\psi \;=\; (1 - f)\;\rev{\phi}\phi\;f.
\]
The element $\rev{\phi}\phi$ is even and reversion-invariant, so it has grades $0$ and $4$ only:
\[
\rev{\phi}\phi = s + F, \qquad s = \ip{\rev{\phi}\phi}_{0}, \quad F = \ip{\rev{\phi}\phi}_{4}.
\]
Since $(1 - f)f = 0$, every part of $\rev{\phi}\phi$ that commutes with $b$ drops out of the sandwich:
\[
(1 - f)\,c\,f \;=\; c\,(1 - f)f \;=\; 0 \qquad \text{whenever } cb = bc.
\]



\emph{Dimensions three and four.}  In dimension three $F = 0$. In dimension four $F = uI$ is a multiple of the pseudoscalar, which commutes with every even element and in particular with $b$. In both cases all of $\rev{\phi}\phi$ commutes with $b$, so $\rev{\psi}\psi = 0$. This is the alternation in (i).

t14c-regenerated.text: This paper is T14c of the series, a companion to the dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14}, downstream of its Theorem 3.4 (types by residue), Proposition 4.1 (superselection), Theorem 4.3 (the mirror copy), Theorem 3.10 (no orientation bit in odd dimension) and its unit-ball rule (Section 7). It runs the construction of the Standard-Model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} in each tower, using the mass formula of the mass paper T11 \cite{ButlerT11}, the rungs and canonical relations of the tower paper T3 \cite{ButlerT3}, and, for comparison only, the families of T13 \cite{ButlerT13} and the neutrino sector of T15 \cite{ButlerT15}. Its physical tests take the simulations of the companion note T14b \cite{ButlerT14b} as given; the companion note T14a \cite{ButlerT14a} is upstream of nothing here. The cone fact for signature $(2,2)$ is the foundations paper T16's \cite{ButlerT16}. The capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17} records T14's predictions; the section ``What this note depends on, and what would refute it'' lists what this note adds to them.

t14c-regenerated.text:
The script \file{verify\_T14c.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT14c} imports the series library \file{GA.py} and checks the computational statements of Sections 3 to 10 in exact arithmetic: rational numbers, and a small polynomial ring over $\mathbb{Q}$ in which the identities of Lemma \claimref{dark-tower-matter.adjoint-norm} and Theorems \claimref{dark-tower-matter.where-mass-begins} and \claimref{dark-tower-matter.ladder} are verified as polynomial identities in the spinors' coordinates rather than on samples. Part K alone is decimal and labelled. Without the supplementary scripts it runs $57$ checks, all passing:

\begin{center} \begin{tabular}{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule
Part & statements & checks \\
\midrule
A & Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field} & A1 to A5 \\
B & Lemma \claimref{dark-tower-matter.adjoint-norm}, Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.where-mass-begins} & B0 to B7 \\
C & Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.ladder} & C1, C2 \\
D & Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.pairs}, Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.third-pairs-unit-five-dimensions} & D1a, D1b, D2 to D12 \\
E & Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.gauge-algebras}, Remark \claimref{note.dark-tower-matter.kleinian-algebra} & E1 to E5 \\
F & Propositions \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-content}, \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-content} & F1 to F4 \\
G & Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.anomalies} & G1 to G3 \\
H & Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.residue-seven-unit} & H1 to H4 \\
I & Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirror-algebra} & I1 to I3 \\
J & Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.sterile-kinematics} & J1 to J3 \\
K & Propositions \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2}, \claimref{dark-tower-matter.survival-sheets}, \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-towers}; Fact \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-unit-ball-rule} (decimal) & K1 to K7 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Part L runs the supplementary derivation scripts deposited with the paper in the folders \file{MIR}, \file{D3R}, \file{D3C}, \file{D5C}, \file{D5Q}, \file{STE} (one per tower: $24$, $61$, $78$, $86$, $106$ and $68$ checks) and two independent checks, \file{CHECK\_ALG} ($50$ exact checks) and \file{CHECK\_COS} (decimal), and requires each to be present and to run clean, twelve further checks ($69$ in all). The paper cites them for the decimal composition of the mirror (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}), the five-dimensional binding, scattering and plasma estimates (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-towers}), the invariant forms of Corollary \claimref{dark-tower-matter.same-kind-matter}, the branches of Remark \claimref{note.dark-tower-matter.branches-break-u-what-they-give}, the Kleinian ladder of Remark \claimref{note.dark-tower-matter.kleinian-algebra}, the transported weights of Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-content}(iii) and the sheet radiation of Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-phases}. What no script checks: the statement after Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.gauge-algebras} about the mirror (T14's), the imported physics (Redlich's shift, Polyakov, topological mass, flux attachment, five-dimensional Chern-Simons quantisation, plasma instabilities) and the galaxy modelling of T14b.

t14c-regenerated.title: The flag bit exists exactly at tower dimension $0 \bmod 4$
t14c-regenerated.text: Let a tower have dimension $n$ and conformal completion with ambient $V$ of dimension $n + 2$, and let $W, W' \subset V_{\C}$ be a Witt pair, the two halves of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag} taken coherently across the pairs, with pure spinors the null blade $f$ and the top state (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.null-blades-fock-ideal-chirality}). Then the choice between $W$ and $W'$ is a discrete invariant of the connected conformal spin group, a \emph{bit}, if and only if $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ (ambient dimension $2m$ with $m$ odd), and the bit is the chirality of the pure spinor, that is, the parity of the Fock grade of the complementary half's pure spinor ($0$ for $f$, $m$ for the top state). (i) The odd residues are odd-dimensional for every signature in the class, so the ambient is odd-dimensional, the pseudoscalar central, an even versor carries $W$ to $W'$, and the spin algebra mixes the Fock grades: no bit, on any window. (ii) The even residues carry the bit exactly at tower dimension $0 \bmod 4$: under Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} all four are at dimension four and carry it; the causal representatives of the alternative windows of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}(iii), $(1,1)$ of $r = 0$ and $(1,5)$ of $r = 4$, do not. So the towers that can be oriented are the even residues $\{0, 2, 4, 6\}$ given P3, and the odd residues cannot be, given nothing.

t14c-regenerated.title: The mirror share is one, and how fragile that is
t14c-regenerated.text:
Write $m_{r} = c_{r}\Lambda_{r}$, with $\Lambda_{r}$ the confinement scale of tower $r$'s non-abelian sector and $c_{r}$ the constituent factor of its lightest charge-carrying composite.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The mirror.)} By Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iii), $\Lambda_{2} = \Lambda_{6}$ and $c_{2} = c_{6}$ exactly, hence $f_{2} = 1$ under P4, which Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v) discharges for the mirror, an isomorphism of theories rather than a one-loop statement. As a ratio of mass densities it is a ratio of mean mass per baryon: ours is about $936.7$ MeV after helium, a mirror burnt entirely to helium (the completion limit of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}'s burning branch) gives $931.8$ MeV, so $f_{2}$ is $0.995$ in that limit and $1$ on the proton-only branch, a one-sided systematic of half a percent at assembly level. Caveat (T14c): the two branches bracket the share where the mirror is helium or protons; at the gravitational floor the mirror is degenerate and, for a copied lepton number $L \leq 0$, ends $96$ to $100$ percent neutrons, a composition neither branch describes, and it is helium only for $\xi$ between about $3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$ (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}); the half-percent bracket is established there and not at the floor.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Fragility.)} The equality is unstable to any departure from the copy. Suppose the two towers shared a ceiling $M$ and coupling but differed in light content by $\Delta b$ over the running range, with $b_{6} \leq 11$; then at one loop
\[
\ln\frac{\Lambda_{2}}{\Lambda_{6}} \;\geq\; \frac{\Delta b}{b_{6} + \Delta b}\,\ln\frac{M}{\Lambda_{6}}.
\]
One Dirac flavour is $\Delta b = 2/3$, which with $\Lambda_{6} = 0.3$ GeV moves the mirror share by a factor between $4.89$ (bottom of the ceiling range, $b_{6} = 11$) and $21.4$ (top, $b_{6} = 7$), past the observed $5.364$ everywhere except at the bottom of the range on the most conservative branch. A coupling departure $\delta = \alpha_{2}(M)^{-1} - \alpha_{6}(M)^{-1}$ at the ceiling with identical content moves $\Lambda_{2}/\Lambda_{6}$ by $e^{-2\pi\delta/b}$, a factor $2.45$ per unit at $b = 7$, so the share stays within ten percent of one only for $|\delta| < 0.106$. So $f_{2} = 1$ is exact, P2-protected, and fragile.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The odd towers.)} In three and five dimensions the gauge coupling is dimensionful and the confinement scale is set by the coupling itself ($\Lambda_{3} \sim g_{3}^{2}N$, $\Lambda_{5} \sim 1/g_{5}^{2}$), so nothing about $\Lambda_{1,7,3,5}$ follows without a rule the series does not derive (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}); the unit-ball rule of the section ``The dark matter ratio: the unit-ball rule'' constrains that rule, as shares per unit of our volume, without supplying it.
\end{enumerate}
Level: (i) is Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}; (ii) is one-loop arithmetic under its stated assumptions, flagged; (iii) is a scope statement.
