t14c-regenerated.title: Seeding by gravity: the floor on a dark tower's temperature
t14c-regenerated.text:
By exact superselection the towers interact only through the shared metric (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}), so after the descent a dark tower can be heated only gravitationally; what the descent itself deposited in it (its charge, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}, with whatever energy the deposit carried) is a datum, not a computation. Let the descent reheat this tower to $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ and let tower $r$, with $g_{d}$ light degrees of freedom that thermalise among themselves, be heated by graviton-mediated production from the visible plasma at rate per volume $\Gamma = c\,T^{8}/M_{P}^{4}$, with $c$ the sum of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-production-rate}'s per-species coefficients over the tower's light content. Then the produced comoving yield is
\[
Y \;=\; \frac{c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}}{3\,\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3}}, \qquad \kappa_{s} = \sqrt{\frac{\pi^{2}g_{*}}{90}}\;\frac{2\pi^{2}}{45}\,g_{s} \;=\; 145.3 \ \text{at } g_{*} = g_{s} = 100,
\]
its energy fraction at production is $4Y$, and the temperature ratio it alone would give is
\[
\xi_{\mathrm{floor}} \;=\; \Big(4Y\,\frac{g_{*}}{g_{d}}\Big)^{1/4} \;=\; 9.6 \times 10^{-4}\; c^{1/4}\Big(\frac{16}{g_{d}}\Big)^{1/4}\Big(\frac{T_{\mathrm{desc}}}{6 \times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{GeV}}\Big)^{3/4}
\]
for $g_{*} = g_{s} = 100$ at the reheating. This is a floor: the tower's bath cannot be colder, and it is hotter by whatever energy the deposit carried. The ratio thereafter evolves through the two sectors' separate entropy conservation, by
\[
\left(\frac{g_{d}^{\mathrm{seed}}}{g_{d}}\right)^{1/3}\left(\frac{g_{s}}{g_{s}^{\mathrm{seed}}}\right)^{1/3}
\]
at any later epoch. Two inputs are not fixed by the formula: $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$, the ceiling of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success} or below it, so that across that range the floor spans a factor $(3.5 \times 10^{11}/6 \times 10^{14})^{3/4}$, about $4 \times 10^{-3}$ ($3.75 \times 10^{-3}$), the body quoting the top and saying so; and the deposit's energy, which sets the actual ratio above the floor.
t14c-regenerated.provenance: Transport Lab claim dark-matter.seeding-gravity-floor-dark-towers-temperature, version 4 (T14 Prop A.2)
t14c-regenerated.label: Fact (imported)

t14c-regenerated.title: The stored asymmetry is a charge, not a number
t14c-regenerated.text:
Under the classification of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}, with $\epsilon$ initial data of the descent, inherited rather than generated, and the number $N$ common to the towers under P1 ($N = M_{P}/H$, which fixes the boundary mode count, about $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, without being it: Observation \claimref{standard-model.largeness-number-universes-boundary-modes}; the argument uses only that $N$ is common):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Charge.)} The asymmetry stored in an oriented tower is the charge $Q = \epsilon N$, fixed by the descent's data and independent of the tower's temperature; it is not a thermal number $n - \bar{n} \propto g\,\mu T^{2}$. So the mirror share $f_{2} = 1$ holds at any mirror temperature: a cold mirror carries the same baryon charge as this tower in the same number of baryons, with negligible mirror radiation.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Origin.)} The charge is the descent's and cannot be produced afterwards: the one channel superselection leaves open, gravitational production from the visible plasma (the section ``Seeding by gravity, and why no coupling rule follows''), yields $1.8$ to $2.7 \times 10^{-15}$ mirror quanta per unit entropy at the ceiling reheating against the $8.7 \times 10^{-11}$ baryons per unit entropy that our baryon number requires, more than four orders too few even counting every produced quantum as a baryon. Black holes are a sink for $Q$, not a source (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}(iv), under P5): a mass-preserving rearrangement that erodes each tower's free baryon count and moves no share.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Temperature.)} Taken as a free datum of the descent, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} is an exception to P2 (applied with the reach of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), (v), P2 gives $\xi = 1$, which the record excludes), the mirror's temperature ratio $\xi = T'/T$ is bounded below by the gravitational floor, $\xi$ between $2.8$ and $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$ at the ceiling reheating (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}(ii), the bracket the species-counting ambiguity; four parts in a thousand of this at the bottom of the ceiling range), and above by the $\Neff$ cap at $0.448$; a deposit of each unit of baryon number with energy of order the reheating temperature puts it at $\xi \approx 4 \times 10^{-3}$. The paper carries the whole interval. With $\eta = n_{B}/n_{\gamma} = 6.1 \times 10^{-10}$ here and equal baryon number,
\[
\eta' \;=\; \frac{\eta}{\xi^{3}}
\]
runs from $19$ to $26$ at the floor down to about $0.008$ at the hot deposit, crossing one at $\xi = \eta^{1/3} = 8.5 \times 10^{-4}$: at least $10^{7}$ times ours throughout, with $\Delta\Neff$ eight orders or more below the cap.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The two readings.)} The thermal reading would give $f_{2} \sim \xi_{2}^{3}$ instead, at most $0.090$ under the $\Neff$ cap ($0.448^{3}$) and $10^{-7}$ or less anywhere in the interval; the two readings cannot both hold, and the paper's own classification decides for the charge.
\end{enumerate}
Level: the classification is Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-trichotomy-descents-data}'s; the incompatibility is arithmetic. The mirror's nucleosynthesis, which is not a copy of ours and on which the burning branch of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(i) and the composition caveat of refutation item 6 rest, follows the proof, at assembly level. Caveat (T14c): the proof's thermal up-down ratio at freeze-out fails at the floor, where the mirror is degenerate and, for a copied lepton number $L \leq 0$, ends $96$ to $100$ percent neutrons; it is helium only for $\xi$ between about $3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$, an interval containing the hot-deposit estimate (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}). The burning branch is therefore not the floor's composition.
t14c-regenerated.provenance: Transport Lab claim dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number, version 7 (T14 Prop 4.6)
t14c-regenerated.label: Fact (imported)

t14c-regenerated.title: Superselected, hence dark and exactly stable
t14c-regenerated.text:
By Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} and the acoustic programme (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-gravity-only-coupling}, the series' acoustic no-go, at its mixed level: within the s-wave current algebra, with the sphere step conditional on the Indifference premise and the thermal state on premise (Q)), matter in a neighbouring tower gravitates on this metric and does nothing else observable at first order: dark by structural necessity, at that level. Stability is then not suppressed but exact, in three steps, the first of which is proved given the sector decomposition of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.frozen-phase-operators}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The tower charge $r$ is superselected in the frozen phase: frozen-phase operators are built from the one soldering and preserve its signature (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one}), so portal matrix elements between residues vanish identically away from walls.
\item The walls are unreachable: singular loci ascend within-tower, since the completion adjoins exactly $(1,1)$ and preserves the residue (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}), while the mod-8 shadow walls that separate residues are displaced successively away from the physical region, by the wall-sequence theorem of the sheaf paper \cite[\S5]{ButlerT4}, under that theorem's hypotheses (a compact base and good couplings at every stage), carried here.
\item Therefore the only inter-tower event in the universe's history is the descent itself: the towers communicated once, at the origin, and have been in absolute mutual darkness but for weight ever since. The singular locus of a black hole is an inter-tower event for energy, as it already was for weight, and never for the residue of any quantum: energy crosses at the wall, the residue does not (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}).
\end{enumerate}
One residue is flagged at observation level: dark-tower matter crossing this tower's horizons carries superselected charge the four-dimensional boundary mode space cannot hold, which routes it into the tower-wise run of the singularity paper's ascend-then-descend structure \cite{ButlerT5}; the computation of that routing, with the mass range of its Gauss-law clause, is Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}.
t14c-regenerated.provenance: Transport Lab claim dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable, version 5 (T14 Prop 4.1)
t14c-regenerated.label: Fact (imported)

t14c-regenerated.title: Towers are residues, and the single-clock filter
t14c-regenerated.text:
The residue $r = p - q \pmod 8$ is invariant along every tower: the eight parallel towers are the eight residues, their parallelism derived rather than described. Call a signature $(p,q)$ \emph{causal} if $\min(p,q) = 1$: exactly one direction of the minority sign, the timelike one, whichever sign convention carries time. Labelling this world $(1,3)$, residue $6$, fixes the convention time $=$ plus, and the mirror residue $2$ reads $(3,1)$; under the opposite convention the two labels swap and the causal sort is unchanged, but every attribution of a Clifford type to a member of the reversal pair passes to the other member, since $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat(2,\mathbb{H})$ and $\Cl(3,1) \cong \Mat(4,\R)$ are not isomorphic. That attribution is fixed by a labelling convention Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} declares indexical, and is so read below. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Census; proved.)} Every residue contains causal signatures once the dimension is free: the lowest are $(1,1)$ at $r = 0$, $(2,1)$ at $r = 1$, $(3,1)$ at $r = 2$, $(4,1)$ at $r = 3$, $(1,5)$ or $(5,1)$ at $r = 4$, $(1,4)$ at $r = 5$, $(1,3)$ at $r = 6$, $(1,2)$ at $r = 7$. The residue alone therefore sorts nothing; a representative must be chosen.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The sort under P3; proved given the premise.)} Under Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} the representatives are $(1,3)$ at $r = 6$, this world; $(3,1)$ at $r = 2$, a mirror Minkowski with real (Majorana-type) spinors; $(2,2)$ at $r = 0$, two times; $(4,0)$ or $(0,4)$ at $r = 4$, none; $(2,1)$ and $(1,2)$ at $r = 1, 7$, three-dimensional; $(4,1)$ and $(1,4)$ at $r = 3, 5$, five-dimensional. Exactly two are sterile, $r = 0$ and $r = 4$ (a figure of the original), and they are the fixed points of the mirror map $r \mapsto -r$: under P3 the towers without a single time are the towers that are their own mirrors.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Sensitivity; proved.)} The sterile set is a function of the window. With any dimension up to five allowed, only $r = 4$ is sterile ($(1,1)$ is a causal signature for $r = 0$); with dimensions three to six, only $r = 0$ ($(1,5)$ is one for $r = 4$); with the upper bound removed, nothing is ($(1,9)$ is one for $r = 0$ at ten); and the literal lowest-dimensional representative of every residue, with no lower bound, is definite for $r = 6$ itself, namely $(0,2)$: without a lower bound the criterion would sterilise this world.
\end{enumerate}
Six admit matter: this one and five dark. Which of the six the descent populated is a further question, answered for the mirror by P2 and for the odd towers only by the record (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}). Structural level given P3; the two-time exclusion at $r = 0$ imports the standard instability of two-time dynamics, flagged, and the flag does not remove it (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.flag-insensitive-residue-no-flag-level}).

t14c-regenerated.label: Fact (imported)

t14c-regenerated.title: The unit-ball rule
t14c-regenerated.text:
Under R1 to R3, the share of a tower whose space has $D$ dimensions is $f = \tfrac{V_{3}}{V_{D}}$, and
\[
\frac{\Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}}{\Omega_{b}} \;=\; V_{3}\sum_{\text{dark }r}\frac{1}{V_{D_{r}}}
\;=\; \frac{V_{3}}{V_{3}} + 2\,\frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}} + 2\,\frac{V_{3}}{V_{4}}
\;=\; 1 + \frac{8}{3} + \frac{16}{3\pi} \;=\; \frac{11\pi + 16}{3\pi} \;=\; 5.36432\ldots
\]
against the observed $5.364 \pm 0.065$. The agreement is built in, not predicted: the relation was found by solving for the observed value, and its clauses were chosen with it known, and the closed form is one of fourteen equally simple candidates within the error bar (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}).

t14c-regenerated.title: Imported: the five-dimensional Chern-Simons shift

t14c-regenerated.title: Hypercharge from the global form, pair counting, and consistency
t14c-regenerated.text:
With $Y$ the hypercharge defined before Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}, and with Hypothesis (S) wherever a doublet at the level of one conformal spinor (a twistor-level doublet) enters:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Under (S).) The one-handed listing keeps the states of even total mode number and conjugates the odd ones, or the reverse; the choice is the particle-antiparticle orientation. Write $(j, k)$ for the component of the five-mode state space with $j$ slot modes and $k$ pair modes occupied (mode counts, not the pair of representation dimensions used elsewhere in this paper, for which see the caption of a figure of the original). In the listing that keeps the quark doublet, the component $(1,1)$, as a particle, the lepton doublet is the full conformal spinor, the component $(1,3)$, $Y_{L} = -1/2$, and the empty conformal spinor, the component $(1,0)$, appears only as its conjugate (here both phrases name doublet components of the one-slot listing; the neutrino paper uses ``empty'' and ``filled conformal spinor'' for the grade-zero and grade-three singlets of the single-spinor sector, different objects, Proposition \claimref{neutrino.empty-twistor}). The $[SU(2)]^{2}U(1)$ anomaly coefficient of the two doublets, $3Y_{Q} + Y_{L}$ with the three the colour multiplicity, is then the identity $3 \cdot \tfrac16 - \tfrac12 = 0$; it would equal $1$ if the empty conformal spinor were listed as the particle instead, so the anomaly confirms the orientation the listing fixed. Pair counting fixes $|Y_{L}/Y_{Q}| = 3$; the parity fixes the sign.
\item (Unconditional as a computation on the Fock space of a single conformal spinor, like Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(3).) Listed by the handedness of (1), the sector of a single conformal spinor gives the singlet spectrum. Here $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$, the conformal spinor space, and $\CSm{} = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$ are the two chirality halves (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}), and the listing keeping the even grades and conjugating the odd ones gives
\[
(1)_{0} \;\oplus\; (\bar{3})_{-2/3} \;\oplus\; (\bar{3})_{+1/3} \;\oplus\; (1)_{+1},
\]
that is $\nu^{c}$, $u^{c}$, $d^{c}$, $e^{c}$ with hypercharges $0, -\tfrac23, +\tfrac13, +1$: the observed singlet spectrum, with the fourth singlet at hypercharge zero. (The listing by the opposite handedness is the conjugate of this one, the same spectrum in the opposite convention.) Under (S) the grade-$k$ states of a single conformal spinor are the $(0, k)$ components, the states with no slot mode and $k$ pair modes occupied (their content $\Lambda^{k}\C^{3}$ and weight $-2k$ match, and irreducibles are determined by content and weight), so their parity is the total parity and this listing is the same listing as in (1).
\item (Consistency, and uniqueness given the content; under (S) for the doublets.) With the content of (1) and (2), all four anomaly conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients} hold. Conversely, for the field content $Q = (2,3)$, $L = (2,1)$, $u^{c} = (1,\bar{3})$, $d^{c} = (1,\bar{3})$, $e^{c} = (1,1)$, all listed in one handedness, together with a fourth singlet of hypercharge zero or no fourth singlet, and $Y_{Q} = 1/6$ as the normalisation, the four conditions determine $Y_{L}$, $Y(e^{c})$ and $\{Y(u^{c}), Y(d^{c})\}$ uniquely, and the solution is the spectrum of (1) and (2). Both hypotheses are necessary: with a fourth singlet of unconstrained hypercharge the conditions admit a one-parameter family, and if the doublets were listed in the opposite handedness from the singlets the $[SU(3)]^{2}U(1)$ and cubic sums would be $-\tfrac23$ and $+\tfrac49$ rather than zero.
\end{enumerate}

t14c-regenerated.title: Imported: the pair systems and the two chirality halves
t14c-regenerated.text: Let $W$ be a maximal isotropic (three-dimensional) subspace of $V_{\C}$ with a dual isotropic complement. The complexified ascended algebra acts irreducibly on $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, and its two chirality halves are $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ and $\CSm = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$, each of dimension four. Every nonzero conformal spinor (twistor) $u \in \CS$ is a pure spinor: it is the Fock vacuum of the system of three fermionic ladder pairs built on its own annihilator space $W_{u}$, every state of the module is generated from $u$ by those pair operators, and $\CS$ (respectively $\CSm$) is what the even (respectively odd) products generate. Conformal spinors are states of the pair algebra, not its operators. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thm.~3.1]{ButlerT9} for the Fock model and the chirality halves; \cite[Thm.~5.3]{ButlerT9} for the pure-spinor and Fock-vacuum statements; the tower paper \cite[Thms.~4.2, 4.3]{ButlerT3} for the iterated pair structure (one qubit per rung, Witt index as capacity) within which this sits.

t14c-regenerated.title: The internal symmetry ladder
t14c-regenerated.text: For a system of $n$ conformal spinors (an $n$-twistor system) $(Z^{1}, \ldots, Z^{n})$, the linear mixings $Z^{i} \mapsto U^{i}{}_{j} Z^{j}$ that preserve the total momentum $p_{AA'} = \sum_{i} \pi^{i}_{A}\bar\pi^{i}_{A'}$, built from the parts $\pi^{i}$ in the $E = +1$ eigenspace, and the total helicity form $\sum_{i} \bar{Z}^{i} \cdot Z^{i}$, the reversion form $h$ summed over the spinors, for every configuration form exactly the unitary group $U(n)$. The ladder therefore reads: one conformal spinor, massless, internal group $U(1)$; two, the first massive step, internal group $U(2)$, with Lie algebra $\su(2) \oplus \uu(1)$; three, internal group $U(3)$, with Lie algebra $\su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$. (The groups are $U(n)$ themselves, not products: the map $SU(n) \times U(1) \to U(n)$, $(a, \mu) \mapsto \mu a$, is onto, and its kernel is $\{(\mu^{-1}I_{n}, \mu) : \mu^{n} = 1\} \cong \mathbb{Z}_{n}$ by the determinant, so $U(n) = (SU(n) \times U(1))/\mathbb{Z}_{n}$; the distinction is treated in the section ``The gauge algebra and the global form''.)

t14c-regenerated.title: Orthogonal bases and the law of inertia
t14c-regenerated.text: Every real quadratic space $(V, Q)$ of dimension $n$ has an orthogonal basis $e_1, \dots, e_n$ with $Q(e_i) \in \{1, -1, 0\}$. The numbers $p$, $q$ and $r$ of basis vectors with $Q(e_i) = 1$, $-1$ and $0$ do not depend on the basis (Sylvester's law of inertia). Moreover $r = \dim \operatorname{rad} V$, and $p + q$ is the rank of any Gram matrix of $B$. Two real quadratic spaces are isometric if and only if they have the same $(p, q, r)$.

t15-regenerated.title: CPT covariance of the kinematic structures and of every action
t15-regenerated.text:
\emph{CPT covariance.} CPT conjugation is an isomorphism of every kinematic structure and leaves every action functional invariant (T14, Proposition 5.2, its first premise: ``checked in the proof for the metric, the completion, the pairing and the action; premised for the imported gauge sector and for structures later papers add'').

\emph{The conjugation.} CPT conjugation $\phi$ is the composite of grade involution, reversal and the flag conjugate exchanging the two families of maximal isotropic subspaces (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}). Because of the reversal, $\phi$ is an anti-automorphism of the Clifford algebra.

\emph{Convention (field action).} $\phi$ acts on fields as a symmetry: on a vector field by its vector part, and on a connection $A$ through the Lie algebra automorphism it induces, $A \mapsto -\phi(A)$, so that curvature is carried by that automorphism. In this convention $\phi$ acts on fields as $C = \mathrm{Ad}(I_{6}) \circ \kappa$, with $\kappa$ complex conjugation on $\Cl(2,4) \otimes \C$: its vector part $-1$ is the rotor $I_{6}$ of the identity component, and the flag conjugate that preserves the frozen point's action is complex conjugation, a real-linear one reversing that action (\claimref{synthesis.cpt-conjugation-pseudoscalar-rotor-times-complex-conjugation}). So CPT conjugation is antilinear on the complexified ambient and on the Fock module, of Wigner's antiunitary type (argued there, not proved).

\emph{Action clause.} For every action functional $S_{\mu}$ of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape}, the gauge couplings among its parameters $\mu$ included, $S_{\mu} \circ C = S_{\mu}$; in particular $C$ does not move $\mu$.

\emph{What is checked and what is premised.} Checked: the fibre metric, the completion, the pairing on the Fock module, and the frozen point's action, which with every functional of real tensor fields invariant under constant $SO_{0}(2,4)$ satisfies the action clause in this convention by the cited result's clause (5). Premised: the imported gauge sector, spinor and fermion fields, and structures later papers add. For the gauge sector the standard CPT theorem for local Lorentz-invariant actions concerns the antiunitary CPT operator of quantum field theory; that this conjugation realises that operator is argued, not proved, so the gauge sector's invariance ``is imported and carried as a premise''.

t15-regenerated.title: Introduction
t15-regenerated.text:
The neutrino was the largest gap in the framework's derived content. This paper addresses it using only parts already present in the series, and ends by registering the framework's most precise and most exposed prediction: this is, by design and by declaration, the series' fastest-falsifiable paper, published while the prediction is still open.

The chain. The Standard-Model paper T12's derived content always contained a fourth colour singlet: the single-twistor sector carries \emph{two} singlets, at grades zero and three of $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{3}$, and the observed comparison column always had two. The right-handed neutrino is the grade-zero state, the \emph{empty twistor}, the pair system with no rung occupied, whose hypercharge the weight rule computes as zero. Anomaly cancellation could not have fixed it: with a fourth singlet of free hypercharge and $Y_{Q} \neq 0$ the anomaly-free spectra are exactly the two-dimensional span of the derived spectrum and $B - L$, a fact we prove in closed form, so the zero is a computation of the content derivation and not a consistency condition, and the Standard Model's ambivalence about $\nu_{R}$ is the ambivalence of a bottom-up construction that has only anomalies to go on. The natural small-mass mechanism is refuted first (the sixteenth refutation): the cosmological term of the mass paper T11's deformed bracket lies below the flat term by $\Lambda l^{2}/6$ for a composite of extent $l$, and can dominate only at horizon size. t15-regenerated.title: The asymmetry: the arrow counted, and the fifteenth refutation
t15-regenerated.text:
The framework does not generate its asymmetry; it inherits it.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Sakharov.)} The Sakharov conditions are for generating an asymmetry dynamically from a symmetric state; a universe whose asymmetry is initial data does not need them. The descent supplies the reason the initial data need not be symmetric: it is irreversible (the lossy projection of the taxonomy paper's descent theorem \cite{ButlerT1}), it creates the tower charges, and it makes one orientation choice, the Witt flag, which is what particle-versus-antiparticle means (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-flag}). Each matches a Sakharov condition in name; none is a mechanism producing a number.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The fifteenth refutation.)} A pre-descent $\theta$-term would source asymmetry through the topology of gauge bundles; but it integrates a characteristic class, of even degree, so the odd-dimensional towers carry no continuous $\theta$, and at the P3 representatives a $\theta$-term exists exactly where a flag bit does. In this tower it is excluded empirically: a $\theta$-routed asymmetry needs an angle of order one at the descent that does not relax before it acts, and the neutron dipole bound $|d_{n}| < 1.8 \times 10^{-26}\,e\,$cm \cite{Abel2020} gives $|\theta| \lesssim 10^{-10}$ today (through a hadronic matrix element with its own uncertainty). Not excluded, and not claimed: an angle that relaxes or rolls; and the mirror's angle, which equals ours only by P2 along the reversal orbit (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv)), the copy being of the functional, not its coefficient. Internally the paper says only that the orientation is the one mechanism the framework itself supplies; that locates the mechanism and does not refute the alternative.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Confinement and universality.)} The orientation route is one bit spent once (uniqueness among all conceivable mechanisms is not claimed). A flag exists on every rung of every tower (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.where-flag-defined-what-it-carries}), but the flag \emph{bit} only in the even residues at their P3 representatives (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension}), so the asymmetry is confined to the oriented causal towers, this one and the mirror, and the odd towers carry none by either route. Universality of the value is Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p4-democracy-asymmetry-over-oriented-towers}, a theorem for the mirror (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v)) and not extendable to inequivalent towers, the asymmetry per mode depending on the tower's own charge structure.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The value, a stance.)} $\epsilon$ is not derived here and not classified. The trichotomy's kinematic clause runs for it as for $N$ ($\epsilon$ is continuous), at that Fact's observation level; the dynamical clause does not, since generating an asymmetry from CPT-invariant dynamics is exactly what the Sakharov mechanism does. \emph{Stance, flagged and attacked in the section ``The premises attacked, and what would refute this paper'':} the framework inherits its asymmetry, and $\epsilon$ is initial data of the descent, refuted by any in-framework calculation that produces $\epsilon$ dynamically. The count uses only the equality of $\epsilon$ across the reversal orbit (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v)), not its provenance. On the stance the unexplained numbers are two, $N$ and $\epsilon$, with the orientation bit of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeenth-refutation} a third datum of the same event.
\end{enumerate}

t15-regenerated.title: The ceiling valued, and an inherited success
t15-regenerated.text:
The families paper's alignment gives, within each sector, one vacuum direction and hence one rank-one Dirac mass at leading order \cite[Prop.~4.3]{ButlerT13}; it never equates magnitudes across sectors. This paper adds its own hypothesis, attacked below: \emph{Hypothesis (U)}, that the rank-one eigenvalues of the different sectors coincide at the ceiling, so that the neutrino's Dirac eigenvalue $m_{D}$ there is the common leading-order value, which the top retains and the second-order breaking splits for the down-type and charged-lepton sectors. With $m_{3}$ the heaviest light neutrino mass, the seesaw $m_{3} = m_{D}^{2}/M_{R}$ then values the scale on which two results depend, in a range whose ends are the two readings of (U):
\[
\frac{m_{b}^{2}}{m_{3}} \;\approx\; 3.5 \times 10^{11}\ \mathrm{GeV} \;\lesssim\; M_{\mathrm{rung}} \;=\; M_{R} \;=\; \frac{m_{D}^{2}}{m_{3}} \;\lesssim\; \frac{m_{t}^{2}}{m_{3}} \;\approx\; 6 \times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{GeV},
\]
the upper end if the neutrino's Dirac mass is retained unbroken like the top's, the lower if it is split like the bottom's, with (U) read at a common low scale (read at the ceiling, the running of $m_{t}$ and $m_{b}$ lowers both ends by about an order of magnitude, a systematic the range does not include); the ends differ by $(m_{t}/m_{b})^{2} \approx 1.7 \times 10^{3}$, and which applies is a condensate-component question the families paper leaves open. Conditional on (U) and flagged so; (U) is used in two results, the $M$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(ii) and the rung scale of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem-closes-what}(4). t15-regenerated.title: The orientation is the arrow: the seventeenth refutation
t15-regenerated.text:
The Standard-Model paper left one absolute bit undetermined, the particle-antiparticle orientation, expected to be fixed by the charge-zero condition. The expectation is refuted by a $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ covariance argument parallel to the trichotomy's rescaling one, on three premises: that CPT conjugation $C$ is an isomorphism of every kinematic structure and leaves every action functional $S_{\mu}$ of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape} invariant, $S_{\mu}\circ C = S_{\mu}$, the gauge couplings included (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-cpt-covariance}; checked in the proof for the metric, the completion, the pairing and the action; premised for the imported gauge sector and for structures later papers add); Hypothesis (S), under which the Standard-Model paper's chirality proposition, the source of the relative-versus-absolute split, is proved (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-flag}); and that the orientation flag is a datum of each solution, the sign of its complex structure relative to the Fock module's unit planted by the descent and not part of the kinematic structure (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-flag-as-datum}; were it kinematic, the bit would be constant on every solution space, hence dynamically fixed within each of two isomorphic theories, and the conclusion below would fail). Here $C$ is the composite of grade involution, reversal and the flag conjugate, an anti-automorphism; acting on fields as a symmetry does (vectors by its vector part, connections through the induced Lie algebra automorphism), it is $\mathrm{Ad}(I_{6}) \circ \kappa$, with $\kappa$ complex conjugation, so it is antilinear (\claimref{synthesis.cpt-conjugation-pseudoscalar-rotor-times-complex-conjugation}).

Anything the structures determine is conjugation-invariant, and the orientation is not. The charge-zero condition fixes all \emph{relative} structure \cite[Prop.~5.6]{ButlerT12}; under that reading the absolute bit is not kinematic, and since conjugation maps each solution space onto itself and exchanges the two orientations, the bit takes both values on every nonempty solution space: it is initial data in the sense of clause (I) of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape}, and so neither dynamically fixed nor a parameter of the laws (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.four-alternatives-are-exhaustive-three-are}). No exhaustiveness of the kinematic, dynamical and initial-data alternatives is used. It is the Witt flag of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}: the open orientation of the content derivation and the arrow of time are one choice, made once.

The descent measure carries two numbers and one bit. The neutrino sector supplies no orientation refutation condition: the identification of $\nu_{R}$ with the hypercharge-zero singlet at grade zero is flag-covariant (the conjugate flag exchanges the singlet grades zero and three), so no completion of the orientation could exclude it \cite{ButlerT15}.

This is the seventeenth refutation (the sixteenth is the neutrino paper's \cite[Prop.~4.1(1)]{ButlerT15}), in the pattern of the thirteenth and the trichotomy: what the framework cannot determine, it can prove it cannot determine, and locate.

Writing $P = \alpha n_{\infty} + \beta n_{0} + v$ with $v$ in the $x$-slot, $\alpha = \ip{P}{n_{0}} = -d$, $\beta = \ip{P}{n_{\infty}} = \lambda d$, and $\ip{v}{x} = p(x) + \lambda k(x)$ for all $x$. Hence
\[
\ip{P}{P} = 2\alpha\beta + \ip{v}{v} = -2\lambda d^{2} + p\cdot p + 2\lambda\, p\cdot k + \lambda^{2}\, k\cdot k,
\]
where $f \cdot g$ denotes the dual metric on linear forms on the $x$-slot. By Remark 5.2 the metric matrix on the $x$-slot, in the components $x^{aa'}$, is $G = -\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon$; since $\varepsilon^{2} = -1$, $G^{2} = (\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)^{2} = \varepsilon^{2}\otimes\varepsilon^{2} = 1$, so $G^{-1} = G$ and $f\cdot g = -\varepsilon_{ab}\varepsilon_{a'b'}f_{aa'}g_{bb'}$ with the same numerical symbols. \emph{Hypothesis (S), slot statistics.} Under the slot-module hypothesis (Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}: the composite space $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, a graded $U(2)$ slot module tensored with one pair system, with hypercharge from the centre of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, the slot module generated from a unique vacuum by one doublet of slot creation operators, the chirality a CPT halving that is the grading of the joint Clifford system once the slots are fermionic, and slot and pair operators one Clifford system):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Odd slots.)} If the slot quanta are tower elements of one tower parity $\pi$ whose tower grading $(-1)^{\pi n + k}$ is the chirality, then $\pi = 1$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Slot content.)} $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2}$ as a graded $U(2)$-module, so the composite's state space is the Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W = \Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ of five modes, two slot modes and three pair modes, a state being a set of occupied slots and occupied pairs, on which $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$ acts as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$; its particle half is $(1,1)_{0} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{-2/3} \oplus (2,3)_{1/6} \oplus (2,1)_{-1/2} \oplus (1,1)_{1} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{1/3}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Chirality.)} As in Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves} for the three-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, the chirality of a state is the parity of its total mode number.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Exclusion statistics.)} Every $U(2)$-equivariant slot creation map $a^{\dagger} : \C^{2} \otimes F_{n} \to F_{n+1}$ satisfies $a^{\dagger}(u)a^{\dagger}(u') = -a^{\dagger}(u')a^{\dagger}(u)$ for all $u, u' \in \C^{2}$; in particular $a^{\dagger}(u)^{2} = 0$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(One Clifford system.)} The slots are fermionic modes on the same footing as the pairs: the two slot modes and the three pair modes satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations as one system of five modes, so that, by Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-representation-clifford-algebra-bogoliubov}, their Majorana combinations generate $\Cl(10)$ acting on $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$, its spinor module, whose parity grading is that module's chirality.
\end{enumerate}
Clauses (ii) and (iv) are Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(3) under the premise's generation clause and CPT halving, with no anomaly condition; (v) is the premise's clause (f), applied once (ii) has made the slot module fermionic; (iii) follows from the premise's requirement that the chirality be the grading of the joint Clifford system, which makes it commute with $\Spin(10)$; (i) compares (iii) with a tower grading. The particle half satisfies the four anomaly conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients}, a consequence here and not a premise.

t16-regenerated.title: The two presentations
t16-regenerated.text:
The defining relation of a Clifford algebra, $\{e_{a}, e_{b}\} = 2g_{ab}\mathbf{1}$, carries both theories as its two canonical presentations. On an orthogonal basis the relation displays a metric: the geometric reading, which the geometry paper carries to the vacuum Einstein equations and proves there equivalent to parallelism of the scale tractor \cite[Thm.~4.5]{ButlerT6}. On a Witt basis, a maximal isotropic decomposition $V_{\C} = W \oplus \bar{W}$ with the cross pairing normalised to $\ip{w_{i}}{\bar{w}_{j}} = \tfrac12\delta_{ij}$, the same relation reads
\[
\{c(w_{i}), c(w_{j})\} = 0, \qquad \{c(w_{i}), c(\bar{w}_{j})\} = \delta_{ij},
\]
verbatim the canonical anticommutation relations of $\dim W$ fermionic modes, with the Fock module supplied by the pure-spinor construction (Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-pure-spinors-incidence-chart}). Over $\R$ the same reading is available on the real null pairs alone, and Fact \claimref{tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity} counts them. The metric is the anticommutator and the anticommutator is the metric; geometric versus quantum is a choice of chart on one object, not a choice of object. The claim is kinematic: it identifies the metric datum with the CAR algebra, and says nothing about dynamics, states, and measurement, which carry their own levels below.
t16-regenerated.proof: The orthogonal reading is definitional. For the Witt reading, let $V_{\C} = W \oplus \bar{W}$ be a maximal isotropic decomposition with the cross pairing normalised as stated (a dual basis of $\bar{W}$ exists because the form is nondegenerate and $W$ is isotropic, so $\ip{w_{i}}{\cdot}$ restricted to $\bar{W}$ are independent functionals). For $w_{i}, w_{j} \in W$ isotropy gives $g(w_{i}, w_{j}) = 0$, so $\{c(w_{i}), c(w_{j})\} = 2g(w_{i}, w_{j}) = 0$ (\claimref{std-algebra.vector-squares}) (with $c$ the action on the Fock module of \claimref{one-relation.imported-pure-spinors-incidence-chart}), likewise on $\bar{W}$; for the cross terms the normalised pairing gives $\{c(w_{i}), c(\bar{w}_{j})\} = 2g(w_{i}, \bar{w}_{j}) = \delta_{ij}$, the CAR of a Witt basis (\claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car}). Both bases generate the same algebra, since a Witt basis is a linear change of basis of an orthogonal one over $\C$. The script exhibits the bases explicitly: the real null pair of $\Cl(1,1)$; for $\Cl(1,3)_{\C}$ the real pair $(e_{0} \pm e_{1})/2$ on the boost plane and the complex pair $(e_{2} + ie_{3})/2$, $-(e_{2} - ie_{3})/2$ on the anisotropic kernel; for $\Cl(2,4)_{\C}$ two real pairs and one complex pair; and verifies every anticommutator and the invertibility of the change of basis over the Gaussian rationals.

The defining relation of a Clifford algebra, $\{e_{a}, e_{b}\} = 2g_{ab}\mathbf{1}$, carries both theories as its two canonical presentations. On an orthogonal basis the relation displays a metric: the geometric reading, which the geometry paper carries to the vacuum Einstein equations and proves there equivalent to parallelism of the scale tractor [ButlerT6, Thm.~4.5]. On a Witt basis, a maximal isotropic decomposition $V_{\C} = W \oplus \bar{W}$ with the cross pairing normalised to $\ip{w_{i}}{\bar{w}_{j}} = \tfrac12\delta_{ij}$, the same relation reads
\[
\{c(w_{i}), c(w_{j})\} = 0, \qquad \{c(w_{i}), c(\bar{w}_{j})\} = \delta_{ij},
\]
verbatim the canonical anticommutation relations of $\dim W$ fermionic modes, with the Fock module supplied by the pure-spinor construction (Fact 2.3). Over $\R$ the same reading is available on the real null pairs alone, and Fact 2.2 counts them. The metric is the anticommutator and the anticommutator is the metric; geometric versus quantum is a choice of chart on one object, not a choice of object. The claim is kinematic: it identifies the metric datum with the CAR algebra, and says nothing about dynamics, states, and measurement, which carry their own levels below.

For the Witt reading, let $V_{\C} = W \oplus \bar{W}$ be a maximal isotropic decomposition with the cross pairing normalised as stated (a dual basis of $\bar{W}$ exists because the form is nondegenerate and $W$ is isotropic, so $\ip{w_{i}}{\cdot}$ restricted to $\bar{W}$ are independent functionals). For $w_{i}, w_{j} \in W$ isotropy gives $g(w_{i}, w_{j}) = 0$, so $\{c(w_{i}), c(w_{j})\} = 2g(w_{i}, w_{j}) = 0$, likewise on $\bar{W}$; for the cross terms the normalised pairing gives $\{c(w_{i}), c(\bar{w}_{j})\} = 2g(w_{i}, \bar{w}_{j}) = \delta_{ij}$. Both bases generate the same algebra, since a Witt basis is a linear change of basis of an orthogonal one over $\C$. The script exhibits the bases explicitly: the real null pair of $\Cl(1,1)$; for $\Cl(1,3)_{\C}$ the real pair $(e_{0} \pm e_{1})/2$ on the boost plane and the complex pair $(e_{2} + ie_{3})/2$, $-(e_{2} - ie_{3})/2$ on the anisotropic kernel; for $\Cl(2,4)_{\C}$ two real pairs and one complex pair; and verifies every anticommutator and the invertibility of the change of basis over the Gaussian rationals.

Let $(V,Q)$ be real, nondegenerate, of signature $(p,q)$, $d = p+q$. The quantum presentation of Proposition \claimref{one-relation.two-presentations} supports two mode counts, which differ in general and must not be conflated:
\[
r_{\R}(p,q) = \min(p,q), \qquad r_{\C}(p,q) = \lfloor d/2 \rfloor,
\]
the \emph{real capacity}, the number of modes realisable by real null vectors (Fact \claimref{tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity}), and the \emph{complex capacity}, the maximal isotropic dimension of $V_{\C}$, the number of modes of the complexified reading. They agree exactly when $|p - q| \leq 1$, in particular on the split signatures $(k,k)$; for $(1,3)$ they are $1$ and $2$, for $(2,4)$ they are $2$ and $3$. Three consequences, each labelled with the capacity it uses.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The boost qubit; real.)} $r_{\R}(1,3) = 1$: Lorentzian signature has one real hyperbolic plane, unique up to an isometry of the whole space (all such planes are conjugate under $O(1,3)$), and the anisotropic complement is definite, so pre-ascent spacetime natively supports exactly one \emph{real} quantum mode, the boost qubit. The complex capacity is two, which is the Dirac spinor of $\Cl(1,3)_{\C}$ as a two-mode Fock space of dimension $2^{2} = 4$. This clause counts the modes of $(1,3)$ and says nothing about the single-mode thermality theorem, whose mode is the ladder pair of the ascent and is counted by neither $r_{\R}(1,3)$ nor $r_{\C}(1,3)$; what is said about that theorem is a reading, Proposition \claimref{one-relation.overlap-table-sorted}(iii).
\item \emph{(Transport is capacity increment; both capacities.)} Each $(1,1)$ ascent adjoins one hyperbolic plane, hence one real null pair, hence one mode in either count: $r_{\R}$ and $r_{\C}$ each rise by exactly one per rung. \item \emph{(The ascended capacity is three; complex.)} $r_{\C}(2,4) = 3$: the complexified ascended $\C^{6}$ has maximal isotropic dimension three, which is the Standard-Model paper's pair count $(n+2)/2$ at spacetime dimension $n = 4$, the ambient signature being $(2,n)$, so that $d = n + 2$ and, for $n$ even, $\lfloor d/2 \rfloor = (n+2)/2$ \cite[Lem.~2.12]{ButlerT12}. t16-regenerated.title: Spacetime as the manifold of vacuum lines
t16-regenerated.text:
Four clauses.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Every point is null.)} Under the embedding of Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-pure-spinors-incidence-chart}, $Q(X(x)) = 0$ identically: every point of spacetime is a non-invertible element of the algebra. Division by zero is not confined to special loci but is the condition of every point. The embedding needs $Q(x) = c^{2}t^{2} - |\mathbf{x}|^{2}$ dimensionally homogeneous, so the null embedding is where the third constant first enters the series (Lemma \claimref{one-relation.third-constant-conversion-constant-between-charts}).
\item \emph{(Every point is a projective line of vacua.)} The point's null vector acts on the Fock module of Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-pure-spinors-incidence-chart} as a nilpotent, $c(X(x))^{2} = Q(X(x)) = 0$, whose kernel has dimension four on the eight-dimensional module and exactly two on the conformal spinor half $\CS$ (twistor space): that two-dimensional kernel is the point's incidence line $L_{x}$. Every conformal spinor $u$ on $L_{x}$ is the Fock vacuum of its own three-pair system $W_{u}$, and $X(x) \in W_{u}$ for each of them: a point is not one vacuum but a projective line of distinct vacua, all of whose isotropic systems contain its null vector. Complexified compactified spacetime is the manifold of such lines, the Klein quadric of lines in $\PCS = \mathbb{P}(\CS)$, of which the real compactified spacetime is the real slice (double covered by the completion's fibre quadric, Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-pure-spinors-incidence-chart}); it is not the pure-spinor variety $\PCS$, which has one dimension fewer. Two points are null-separated exactly when their incidence lines share a vacuum: $\ip{X(x)}{X(y)} = -\tfrac12 Q(x - y)$.
\item \emph{(The location of each theory.)} The two theories then read: general relativity is the dynamics \emph{of} the vacua, how the vacuum family varies from point to point, carried by the connection; quantum mechanics is the dynamics \emph{above} a vacuum, excitations over a chosen vacuum obeying the CAR of Proposition \claimref{one-relation.two-presentations}. The choice of a vacuum on a point's incidence line is an extra datum, a null direction at the point, which the reading must supply and the point does not.
\item \emph{(Ubiquity, and what a singularity is.)} Quantum mechanics holds everywhere because every point carries its incidence line of vacua; a singularity is where the vacuum family degenerates, where the choice of vacuum itself becomes operator-valued, which is the sheaf paper's localisation theorem, in the Schwarzschild form the singularity paper carries, read in this language \cite[Thm.~4.4, Cor.~4.5, Thm.~8.12]{ButlerT4}, \cite[App.~B]{ButlerT5}.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{The connection in words.} Gravity enters when the same construction is made at every point. The relation holds everywhere, so every point has its own light rays, its own bivector $\sigma$, and its own mode. That raises a question the relation cannot answer on its own: given the mode here, which mode over there is the same one? The answer can depend on the path. Carry $\sigma$ from here to there by one route and back by another, and it need not come home as the $\sigma$ you started with; it comes back tilted. \begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Existence and finiteness.)} A finite invariant ratio of length to time exists if and only if $Q$ is nondegenerate and mixed, $pq \neq 0$: the null cone is that invariant ratio, preserved by every isometry, and it is nonempty exactly when the signature is mixed; dividing $Q$ by $c^{2}$ and letting $c \to \infty$ degenerates $Q$ to the rank-one form $t^{2}$, whose zero set is the simultaneity hyperplane, the Galilean case the root paper sets aside. The word \emph{speed} is reserved for the case of clause (iv). Two of the three standing hypotheses of the root paper's no-go theorem \cite[Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT1}, nondegenerate and mixed, are jointly the existence of a finite invariant ratio; the third, $n \geq 3$, is not needed here and enters only through Zeeman's theorem below.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(One number.)} The invariant ratio is a property of a hyperbolic plane, and the isometry group is transitive on the hyperbolic planes of $(V, Q)$ (Witt's extension theorem, Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-witts-extension-theorem}), so every hyperbolic plane carries the same $c$. This is the Witt fact of Proposition \claimref{one-relation.two-capacities-three-consequences}(1): the uniqueness of the boost qubit and the uniqueness of the invariant ratio are one statement.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Invisible in the Witt chart, fixed in the metric chart.)} On a hyperbolic plane with orthonormal pair $e_{0}, e_{1}$, $e_{0}^{2} = 1$, $e_{1}^{2} = -1$, the Witt chart $f_{\pm} = \tfrac12(e_{0} \pm e_{1})$, $f_{+} \cdot f_{-} = \tfrac12$, has a one-parameter freedom the metric chart does not show, $f_{+} \to \lambda f_{+}$, $f_{-} \to f_{-}/\lambda$, $\lambda > 0$; that rescaling is exactly the boost rotor of rapidity $\eta = \log\lambda$ acting on the orthonormal frame, $R = \cosh(\eta/2) - \sinh(\eta/2)\,e_{0}e_{1}$, with $R e_{0}\tilde{R} = \cosh\eta\, e_{0} + \sinh\eta\, e_{1}$ and $R f_{+}\tilde{R} = e^{\eta}f_{+}$, and the coordinate velocity of the boosted time axis is $c\tanh\eta$. The Witt chart contains rapidity, a dimensionless number, and no other quantity; the metric chart contains time and length separately; the transition from one to the other is what requires the conversion constant $c$. That the algebra fixes orbits and not speeds, as the entropy paper states \cite[Fact~2.2]{ButlerT8}, is this clause: the Witt chart is scale-free, and the geometric normalisation that converts rapidity to time is the chart transition.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(A speed with an arrow.)} The set $\{Q > 0\}$ retracts onto the unit sphere of the positive part and has the components of $S^{p-1}$: two when $p = 1$, one when $p \geq 2$, none when $p = 0$; symmetrically $\{Q < 0\}$ splits exactly when $q = 1$. Hence a nondegenerate form admits a future/past split, a $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ of time orientation, if and only if $\min(p, q) = 1$. The dark-matter paper's causal criterion \cite[Prop.~3.1]{ButlerT14}, stated there as a definition, is thereby a theorem about the cone: a signature has a single time if and only if its timelike set is disconnected. $c$ is a speed, a length over one time, precisely in the causal signatures; in $(2,2)$ the null cone exists and determines the form, so an invariant ratio exists, but there is no single time to divide by and no arrow, and the invariant is not a speed.

t16-regenerated.title: The Dirac current is the conserved density
t16-regenerated.text: Let $\psi$ range over solutions of the Dirac equation $(i\gamma^{\mu}\partial_{\mu} - m)\psi = 0$ with $m > 0$, in a matrix representation with $\{\gamma^{\mu}, \gamma^{\nu}\} = 2\eta^{\mu\nu}$, $\gamma^{0}$ Hermitian and $\gamma^{k}$ anti-Hermitian, and let $\bar{\psi} = \psi^{\dagger}\gamma^{0}$. Among the constant sesquilinear currents $J^{\mu}_{\Gamma} = \bar{\psi}\,\Gamma^{\mu}\psi$, $\Gamma^{\mu} \in \Mat(4, \C)$ constant, those conserved on every solution ($\partial_{\mu}J^{\mu}_{\Gamma} = 0$) form the one-dimensional space spanned by $\Gamma^{\mu} = \gamma^{\mu}$. For a finite superposition $\psi = \sum_{k} u_{k}e^{-ip_{k}\cdot x}$ one has $\partial_{\mu}J^{\mu}_{\Gamma} = i\sum_{k,l}(p_{k} - p_{l})_{\mu}\,\bar{u}_{k}\Gamma^{\mu}u_{l}\,e^{i(p_{k} - p_{l})\cdot x}$, the diagonal terms vanishing identically; for a two-term superposition the two cross terms carry the distinct nonzero exponents $\pm i(p_{1} - p_{2})\cdot x$, which are linearly independent functions, so conservation on every solution is equivalent to
\[
(p - p')_{\mu}\,\bar{u}\,\Gamma^{\mu}\,v = 0 \qquad \text{for all mass-shell } p, p',\ u \in \ker(\slashed{p} - m),\ v \in \ker(\slashed{p}' - m),
\]

t16-regenerated.text:
Grant Premise \claimref{one-relation.supervenience-stated-so-it-can-be}. Three statements follow about what any such subject must be like.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Singleness.)} A record chain reads only its own records, by the superselection of Remark \claimref{note.one-relation.measurement-recording-open-remainder} under Premise \claimref{one-relation.recording-irreversible-stated-so-it-can}, so no self can find, remember, or feel a sibling branch: experience must present as a single history however many the branches.
\item \emph{(Flow.)} A record chain writes in one direction on the modular period and never unwrites (Premise \claimref{one-relation.recording-irreversible-stated-so-it-can}), so experience must present as passage; and the direction of the felt passage is the flag itself. The arrow one experiences is the orientation bit of Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-flag-arrow-superselection}, read from inside, under Hypothesis (S) as that Fact records.
\item \emph{(The question dissolves.)} ``Why am I in this branch'' presupposes a branch-transcendent self that could have been located elsewhere, and no such object exists in the record structure: the self is individuated by the very records that constitute the branch, so each branch's subject asks the question and each is correct that this one is theirs. The question does not go unanswered; it goes unasked by anything real. This is the self-location analysis standard in the Everett literature \cite{Saunders2010, Wallace2012}, arrived at here from the record chain rather than postulated alongside it.
\end{enumerate}

On this the framework asserts nothing and derives nothing, and observes only that the question is invariant across every branch, every tower, and every physical theory yet written; it is not a residue of this framework but of physics. Structural level, conditional on Premises \claimref{one-relation.supervenience-stated-so-it-can-be} and \claimref{one-relation.recording-irreversible-stated-so-it-can}; refutation condition: exhibit experiential access to a sibling branch, or a felt arrow decoupled from the recording direction, and the identification fails.

c(w) := \sqrt2\; w \wedge (\cdot) \quad (w \in W),

Fix bases $\pi_1, \pi_2$ of $\Spi$ and $e_1, e_2$ of $\Som$ with $\pi_1\wedge\pi_2 = N_0$ and $e_1 \wedge e_2 = N_\infty$. For a linear map $A: \Spi \to \Som$ let $L_A := \{A\pi + \pi : \pi \in \Spi\}$ be its graph line and
\[
P(A) \;:=\; (A\pi_1 + \pi_1)\wedge(A\pi_2 + \pi_2) \;\in\; \Lambda^2\CS
\]
its Pl\"ucker bivector, normalised by $P(0) = N_0$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Expansion.)} $P(A) = N_0 + \varphi(A) + (\det A)\, N_\infty$, where $\varphi(A) := A\pi_1\wedge\pi_2 + \pi_1\wedge A\pi_2$ lies in the mixed slot $\Som\wedge\Spi$ and $\det$ is taken in the chosen bases.
\item \emph{(The chart, term by term.)} $\varphi$ is a linear isomorphism onto the mixed slot $= \{\nO,\nInf\}^\perp \otimes \C$, and satisfies $Q(\varphi(A)) = -2\det A$. \[
P(A) \;=\; \nO \,+\, m(A)\,-\,\tfrac12\,Q(m(A))\,\nInf \;=\; X\bigl(m(A)\bigr).
\]
In particular every $P(A)$ is null, as a Pl\"ucker bivector must be, and the nullity of $P(A)$ is equivalent to the identity $\det A = -\tfrac12Q(m(A))$: the quadratic term of the chart is a determinant.
\item \emph{(Coverage.)} $A \mapsto L_A$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}(\Spi, \Som)$ onto the lines of $\PCS$ skew to $L_\infty$, and $[P(A)]$ ranges exactly over the points of the Klein quadric with $\ip{P}{\nInf} \neq 0$: the affine chart of the complexified conformal compactification, with the lines meeting $L_\infty$ as the points at infinity; the real locus is cut out in Proposition \claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor}(5).

t16-regenerated.text:
\emph{Hypothesis (S), slot statistics.} Under the slot-module hypothesis (Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}: the composite space $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, a graded $U(2)$ slot module tensored with one pair system, with hypercharge from the centre of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, the slot module generated from a unique vacuum by one doublet of slot creation operators, the chirality a CPT halving that is the grading of the joint Clifford system once the slots are fermionic, and slot and pair operators one Clifford system):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Odd slots.)} If the slot quanta are tower elements of one tower parity $\pi$ whose tower grading $(-1)^{\pi n + k}$ is the chirality, then $\pi = 1$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Slot content.)} $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2}$ as a graded $U(2)$-module, so the composite's state space is the Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W = \Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ of five modes, two slot modes and three pair modes, a state being a set of occupied slots and occupied pairs, on which $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$ acts as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$; its particle half is $(1,1)_{0} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{-2/3} \oplus (2,3)_{1/6} \oplus (2,1)_{-1/2} \oplus (1,1)_{1} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{1/3}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Chirality.)} As in Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves} for the three-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, the chirality of a state is the parity of its total mode number.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Exclusion statistics.)} Every $U(2)$-equivariant slot creation map $a^{\dagger} : \C^{2} \otimes F_{n} \to F_{n+1}$ satisfies $a^{\dagger}(u)a^{\dagger}(u') = -a^{\dagger}(u')a^{\dagger}(u)$ for all $u, u' \in \C^{2}$; in particular $a^{\dagger}(u)^{2} = 0$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(One Clifford system.)} The slots are fermionic modes on the same footing as the pairs: the two slot modes and the three pair modes satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations as one system of five modes, so that, by Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-representation-clifford-algebra-bogoliubov}, their Majorana combinations generate $\Cl(10)$ acting on $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$, its spinor module, whose parity grading is that module's chirality.
\end{enumerate}
Clauses (ii) and (iv) are Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(3) under the premise's generation clause and CPT halving, with no anomaly condition; (v) is the premise's clause (f), applied once (ii) has made the slot module fermionic; (iii) follows from the premise's requirement that the chirality be the grading of the joint Clifford system, which makes it commute with $\Spin(10)$; (i) compares (iii) with a tower grading. t16-regenerated.title: The trichotomy: what kind of number $N$ is
t16-regenerated.text:
The question the paper ends by pointing at can itself be classified. The classification has four parts, of which the first contains a proved statement and a reading, the second is an import, the third is conditional on the first two, on Observation \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent} and on a decision the fourth names, and the fourth is imported from the action paper; the levels are marked clause by clause.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Kinematic.)} Proved: under $\Lambda \to s^{2}\Lambda$ at fixed $M_{P}$, that is $I \to sI$ on the frozen point with the conformal class unchanged, $H \to sH$ and $N \to N/s$, while every discrete invariant this paper derives (the algebra and its dimension twelve, the global form and its $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$, the dimension four, the content and the hypercharges, and under (S) the ratio $3/8$) is unchanged, since each is computed from the conformal class, the pair structure and the group alone, none of which the rescaling affects. Reading, at observation level: since the conformal class and the pair structure carry no scale, no construction from them alone can fix $N$, which lies in the ratio of the frozen point's norm to the Planck scale; on this reading the kinematic layer determines all discrete invariants and no continuous modulus, and $N$ and the weight spectrum are its only continuous moduli.
\item \emph{(Non-dynamical, imported.)} $\Lambda$ is the norm of the frozen point, and the norm is not a field: it is fixed by a constraint, the fluctuations of the frozen point are pure gauge, and the action carries no equation of motion for it (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-norm-frozen-point-not-field}).
\item \emph{(Initial data, conditional.)} If the alternatives kinematic, dynamical and initial-data are exhaustive, then by (1) and (2) $N$ is initial data, and Observation \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent}(ii) locates the boundary that carries it at the origin. The exhaustiveness is not proved here, and the location is an Observation; the clause is conditional on both, and clause (4) says what the exhaustiveness costs.
\item \emph{(Parameter of the laws, imported.)} The three alternatives are not exhaustive: a conserved quantity that is constant on every solution of a theory but varies across a family of theories indexed by a parameter is a parameter of the laws, and the action paper proves that under the action as written, with $\Lambda$ the value of the Stelle-West constraints fixed before variation, $N$ is exactly that: constant on each solution space $\mathcal{S}_{\Lambda}$ by the rigidity of (2), varying across $\Lambda$, so neither dynamically fixed nor initial data \cite[Prop.~5.8]{ButlerT10}. Clause (3) therefore holds only if the norm is promoted from a fixed number to the value of a Lagrange-multiplier field whose constancy is an equation of motion, the Henneaux-Teitelboim mechanism, which makes $\Lambda$ a label of the solution rather than of the theory; that promotion is a decision for the series, recorded open with both branches stated \cite[Rem.~5.9]{ButlerT10}, and the entropic and null-endpoint effects named below act on a measure over theories or on a measure within one theory according to it.
\end{enumerate}
At observation level, two competing effects are then named without being balanced: an entropic weighting of the freezing by $\exp(S_{\Lambda}) = \exp(\pi N^{2})$, with $S_{\Lambda} = \pi N^{2}$ the cosmological horizon's area-law entropy (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared}), favours large $N$ overwhelmingly (the well-known entropic argument for small $\Lambda$, inherited with every one of its known objections, listed as inherited and not solved), while at the endpoint $\Lambda = 0$ the frozen point is null and the curvature-squared presentation of the action, whose prefactor is $3/\Lambda$, does not exist; the action paper is explicit that this is a boundary of the presentation and not of the action, the Einstein-Cartan functional remaining \cite[Thm.~3.1, Rem.~3.2]{ButlerT10}, so what is lost at $\Lambda = 0$ is the reductive structure and the frozen point's length, not gravity. Large because large boundary mode spaces dominate the measure; nonzero because the descent selects a frozen point of nonzero length; the value is the balance point, and the balance point awaits the descent measure, the one object this framework does not possess. Last, a statement of units only, flagged as such: in the boundary modes' own units, qubits, one per rung of the Fock module (Theorem \claimref{tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung}), the horizon's capacity $S_{\Lambda} = \pi N^{2}$ is $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, about $4.8 \times 10^{122}$ qubits (the mode count of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-mode-count} under the black hole's counting rule), whose base-two logarithm is about $407$; the paper's $R = \log_{2} N^{2} \approx 405$ counts the rungs of a module of dimension $N^{2}$, whose capacity is only $\ln N^{2} = 2\ln N$ nats, not the horizon's. Neither number is a count of turns of the mod-8 clock, which no rung moves: each rung preserves the residue $p - q \pmod 8$ (Theorem \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial}). This is the question in the framework's own coordinates, not an answer to it.

deposited.statement: For any nondegenerate real quadratic space $(V, Q)$, the maximal number of pairwise-anticommuting fermionic mode pairs realisable by \emph{vectors} of $\Cl(V, Q)$ (families $(a_i, b_i)$ of vectors satisfying the displayed CAR of Proposition 4.1) is exactly the Witt index $\min(p,q)$ of $Q$. Along the tower the Witt index is $\min(p,q) + k$: each rung raises the algebra's mode capacity by exactly one, and by no more.
deposited.proof:
\emph{Upper bound.} Let $(a_i, b_i)_{i \leq m}$ be vectors satisfying the CAR. Reading the relations through the Clifford relation on vectors: $\langle a_i, a_j \rangle = 0$ for all $i, j$ (including $i = j$), and $\langle a_i, b_j \rangle = \tfrac12 \delta_{ij}$. The span of the $a_i$ is therefore totally isotropic, and the $a_i$ are independent: a vanishing combination $\sum c_i a_i = 0$ pairs against $b_j$ to give $c_j/2 = 0$. So $m \leq$ the maximal totally isotropic dimension, which for a nondegenerate real form of signature $(p,q)$ is $\min(p,q)$: diagonalise, $V = P \perp N$ with $P$ positive definite of dimension $p$ and $N$ negative definite of dimension $q$; a totally isotropic $U$ meets $P$ trivially (a nonzero $v \in U \cap P$ would have $Q(v,v) > 0$ and $Q(v,v) = 0$ at once), so the projection $U \to N$ along $P$ is injective and $\dim U \leq q$; symmetrically $\dim U \leq p$; and $\min(p,q)$ is attained by the null spans of $\min(p,q)$ hyperbolic pairs (the classical bound, cf.\ [Lam2005, Ch.~I]).

\emph{Attainment.} Split off $\min(p,q)$ orthogonal hyperbolic planes from $(V, Q)$ (Witt decomposition) and take their normalised null pairs, as in Proposition 4.1. Along the tower, the form of signature $(p{+}k, q{+}k)$ has Witt index $\min(p,q) + k$, and each rung contributes its own plane to the attaining family.

t16-regenerated.title: Minimality
t16-regenerated.text:
Let $(\mathbb{W}, f)$ be any null-lift completion of $(\mathbb{V}, Q)$. t16-regenerated.title: The pinching, and its kernel
t16-regenerated.text:
Define the pinching $E : B \to B$, $E(x) = PxP + (1-P)x(1-P)$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ is an idempotent linear map whose image is the commutant $C = \{x \in B : xP = Px\} = A \oplus A\,ff^*$, on which it restricts to the identity, and $E$ is a $C$-bimodule map: $E(cxc') = c\,E(x)\,c'$ for $c, c' \in C$, with $E(1) = 1$: a conditional expectation onto $C$.
\item Its kernel is exactly the adjoined ladder sector:
\[
\ker E \;=\; PB(1-P) \,\oplus\, (1-P)BP \;=\; A f^* \,\oplus\, A f .
\]
In particular $E(f) = E(f^*) = 0$: the pinching erases precisely the pair the ascent adjoined, and nothing else.
\item The round trip is exact on transported elements: for $a \in A$, $E(a) = a$, and the corner read-out $D(x) = PxP$, identified with an $A$-valued map through the natural corner isomorphism $E_{22}BE_{22} = A\,f^*f \cong A$ ($a \mapsto a\,f^*f$), satisfies $D(a) = a$: ascent-then-descent is the \emph{identity} on the base. (In the Peirce coordinates of Theorem \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial}, which identify the $(2,2)$ block with the $(1,1)$ corner by conjugating with $E_{12} = f$, the same round trip reads as the grade involution $\hat{a}$; the two corner identifications differ by exactly the grade twist of the embedding $a \mapsto \mathrm{diag}(a,\hat a)$, and either way the map is an automorphism, faithful.) The multiplicative defect of $D$ on general elements is the exact interposition formula
\[
D(xy) - D(x)D(y) \;=\; P\,x\,(1-P)\,y\,P .
\]
\end{enumerate}

t17-regenerated.title: Introduction
t17-regenerated.text:
A single question opens the series: what happens where division fails. In a Clifford algebra the failure is a geometric object, the null vector on its cone, and the series' founding principle treats the failure as prescribing the next step. Division by an isotropic vector is impossible at the level of elements, provably, in every mixed-signature algebra of dimension at least three (the hyperbolic plane is the one exception, and the idempotent type needs no repair at all); it becomes possible, uniquely and minimally, at the level of the space, by adjoining one hyperbolic plane and letting the undefined values be taken at the adjoined ideal points. The inverse operation never appears. That one principle, pursued mechanically through seventeen natural conjectures, sixteen of them refuted, generates the series this paper surveys: eighteen papers running from pure algebra to the black hole, the Standard Model, the dark sector, and the foundations of quantum mechanics.

This capstone is the one paper of the series whose subject is the series. It does three things that no companion paper can do for itself. It states the \emph{method}: the refutation discipline, the three epistemic tiers, and the house rules that hold every paper to them (the section ``The method''); the roadmap of the series reserves this narrative for the capstone alone, so the companion papers state their results neutrally and cite here. It records the \emph{status}: one table carrying every paper's payload, tier, and machine-verified check count, so that a reader can see in one place what has been proved, at what standard, and what remains (the section ``The series, paper by paper''). And it gathers the \emph{falsifiable claims}: every registered stance in one place with its dataset, its current confrontation date-stamped, and the measurement that would refute it, together with the descent measure the whole framework leaves unexplained: two numbers and one bit (the section ``The falsifiable claims'' and the section ``The measure: two numbers and one bit''). The closing sections carry the series' open directions, each item with the paper it is now assigned to, and the thesis the whole programme argues for: a theory of singularities in which a singularity is not a wall but an interface (the section ``The open directions'' and the section ``The successor programme: a theory of singularities'').

One property of this paper is structural and is declared up front: it is \emph{kept current}. Every status line here depends on results that are, at this writing, under review; when review changes a source paper, the corresponding line here changes. The paper is therefore built to be mechanically refreshable: its tables are compiled from the series' own verified numbers, and its verification script audits the page counts quoted here against the companion PDFs, the check counts against the counts the companion papers record (or, on request, against a fresh run of every companion script), and the tables against one another, so that a stale quotation is a failing check rather than a silent error. t17-regenerated.title: The three tiers
t17-regenerated.text: Every paper in the series is assigned one of three epistemic tiers, and every result inside a paper declares its own level, so that typography matches epistemic content everywhere. Where a paper declares its tier itself, in its abstract or its introduction, the status table of the section ``The series, paper by paper'' records that declaration; where it does not, the tier in the table is this survey's assignment. Tier A papers (the algebra arc) are theorem papers: complete proofs at journal-mathematics standard, nothing conditional. Tier B papers (the geometric and quantum companions) are assembly papers: their proofs rest on named established theorems (Bisognano-Wichmann, MacDowell-Mansouri, Kostant, Araki, the Penrose transform), with the assembly steps itemised so a reader can see exactly which steps the paper proves and which it imports. Tier C papers (the programme papers of the matter arc and the foundations) derive from flagged structural premises, with the premises stated in their own environments, attacked in their own subsections where the roadmap demands it, and quantified by registered predictions with named refutation conditions. The tiers are the declared shape of a programme that runs from pure algebra to cosmology. A Tier C paper that states five ways it could be refuted is doing its job as well as a Tier A paper that proves its theorems.
